title: P0.3: Unify connector tags — centralize canonical tag mapping and remove ad-hoc runtime tags
description:
## Context

The runtime (`gossip-scanner-runtime`) and the connectors (`gossip-connectors`)
use different tag values for the same connector kinds. The connectors define
canonical tags (`b"fslocal"`, `b"gitlocal"`), but the runtime hardcodes ad-hoc
tags (`b"fs"`, `b"git"`, `b"inmem"`). Two tag registries means two identity
spaces — any code path that crosses the boundary derives different `StableItemId`
values for the same logical item.

After P0.2 lands (adding `stable_item_id` to `ItemMeta` and removing
`connector_tag` from `DurableCommitSink`), the runtime may no longer need
connector tags for commit-path identity derivation. But the ad-hoc mapping
in `distributed.rs` still exists and may be used by other callers. It must
be replaced with a single canonical source of truth.

## Current State

### Connector-defined canonical tags

```rust
// crates/gossip-connectors/src/filesystem.rs:119
pub const FILESYSTEM_CONNECTOR_TAG: ConnectorTag = ConnectorTag::from_ascii(b"fslocal");

// crates/gossip-connectors/src/git.rs:78
pub const GIT_CONNECTOR_TAG: ConnectorTag = ConnectorTag::from_ascii(b"gitlocal");
```

The in-memory connector has no canonical tag constant — it takes one as a
constructor parameter:

```rust
// crates/gossip-connectors/src/in_memory.rs:215
pub fn new(connector_tag: ConnectorTag, mut items: Vec<MemItem>) -> Self {
```

### Runtime ad-hoc tags

```rust
// crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/distributed.rs:174-180
fn connector_tag_for_kind(kind: ConnectorKind) -> ConnectorTag {
    match kind {
        ConnectorKind::Filesystem => ConnectorTag::from_ascii(b"fs"),
        ConnectorKind::Git => ConnectorTag::from_ascii(b"git"),
        ConnectorKind::InMemory => ConnectorTag::from_ascii(b"inmem"),
    }
}
```

Tag mismatch:
- Runtime uses `b"fs"` (2 bytes, null-padded to 8) vs connector uses `b"fslocal"` (7 bytes, null-padded to 8)
- Runtime uses `b"git"` (3 bytes, null-padded to 8) vs connector uses `b"gitlocal"` (8 bytes)
- Runtime uses `b"inmem"` (5 bytes) vs connector has no canonical tag

### ConnectorKind enum

```rust
// crates/gossip-scan-driver/src/lib.rs:95-103
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum ConnectorKind {
    Filesystem,
    Git,
    InMemory,
}
```

### Current re-exports from gossip-connectors

```rust
// crates/gossip-connectors/src/lib.rs:24-31
pub use common::path_buf_from_bytes;
pub use filesystem::{FILESYSTEM_CONNECTOR_TAG, FilesystemConnector};
pub use git::{GIT_CONNECTOR_TAG, GitConnector};
pub use in_memory::{InMemoryDeterministicConnector, MemItem};
pub use scan_driver::{...};
```

`FILESYSTEM_CONNECTOR_TAG` and `GIT_CONNECTOR_TAG` are already exported.
`IN_MEMORY_CONNECTOR_TAG` does not exist. `connector_tag_for_kind()` does
not exist in `gossip-connectors`.

## Desired State

A single canonical `connector_tag_for_kind()` function exported from
`gossip-connectors`, plus a canonical `IN_MEMORY_CONNECTOR_TAG` constant.
The ad-hoc mapping in `distributed.rs` is replaced by an import.

### New exports from gossip-connectors

```rust
pub const IN_MEMORY_CONNECTOR_TAG: ConnectorTag = ConnectorTag::from_ascii(b"inmem");

pub fn connector_tag_for_kind(kind: ConnectorKind) -> ConnectorTag {
    match kind {
        ConnectorKind::Filesystem => FILESYSTEM_CONNECTOR_TAG,
        ConnectorKind::Git => GIT_CONNECTOR_TAG,
        ConnectorKind::InMemory => IN_MEMORY_CONNECTOR_TAG,
    }
}
```

### Runtime change

`distributed.rs` replaces its local `connector_tag_for_kind` with the import
from `gossip_connectors::connector_tag_for_kind`.

## Implementation Guidance

### Files to Modify

| File | Change | Rationale |
|------|--------|-----------|
| `crates/gossip-connectors/src/in_memory.rs` | Add `pub const IN_MEMORY_CONNECTOR_TAG` | Canonical tag for in-memory connector |
| `crates/gossip-connectors/src/lib.rs` | Add `connector_tag_for_kind()` function, export `IN_MEMORY_CONNECTOR_TAG` | Centralized mapping |
| `crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/distributed.rs` | Remove local `connector_tag_for_kind`, import from `gossip_connectors` | Eliminate duplication |

### Patterns to Follow

Follow the existing connector tag constant pattern:

```rust
// crates/gossip-connectors/src/filesystem.rs:119
pub const FILESYSTEM_CONNECTOR_TAG: ConnectorTag = ConnectorTag::from_ascii(b"fslocal");
```

The `connector_tag_for_kind` function should be a simple exhaustive match that
uses the existing constants. It belongs in `gossip-connectors/src/lib.rs`
since it maps `ConnectorKind` (from `gossip-scan-driver`) to `ConnectorTag`
(from `gossip-contracts`).

### Utilities to Reuse

| Utility | Location | How to Reuse |
|---------|----------|-------------|
| `ConnectorTag::from_ascii` | `gossip-contracts/src/identity/item.rs:184` | For `IN_MEMORY_CONNECTOR_TAG` const |
| `FILESYSTEM_CONNECTOR_TAG` | `gossip-connectors/src/filesystem.rs:119` | Already exists, use in match |
| `GIT_CONNECTOR_TAG` | `gossip-connectors/src/git.rs:78` | Already exists, use in match |

### Blast Radius

| Caller/Dependent | File | Relationship |
|-----------------|------|-------------|
| `distributed.rs::connector_tag_for_kind` | `gossip-scanner-runtime/src/distributed.rs:174` | Replaced by import |
| `DurableCommitSink::new` call site | `gossip-scanner-runtime/src/distributed.rs:140` | Uses tag from mapping |
| `commit_sink.rs` tests | `gossip-scanner-runtime/src/commit_sink.rs:226` | Test fixture uses `b"fs"` |

After P0.2 lands, `DurableCommitSink` will no longer have a `connector_tag`
field, so the `distributed.rs` call site may not need the tag for commit
purposes. However, the canonical mapping should still exist for any remaining
callers (logging, metrics, assignment routing).

If P0.3 is implemented *before* P0.2, the `DurableCommitSink` constructor
still takes `connector_tag`, and the fix is to pass the canonical tag instead
of the ad-hoc one. If P0.3 is implemented *after* P0.2, the `connector_tag`
parameter may already be gone, and this task reduces to adding
`IN_MEMORY_CONNECTOR_TAG`, the centralized mapping function, and cleanup.

## Code References

```rust
// crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/distributed.rs:174-180 — ad-hoc mapping to remove
fn connector_tag_for_kind(kind: ConnectorKind) -> ConnectorTag {
    match kind {
        ConnectorKind::Filesystem => ConnectorTag::from_ascii(b"fs"),
        ConnectorKind::Git => ConnectorTag::from_ascii(b"git"),
        ConnectorKind::InMemory => ConnectorTag::from_ascii(b"inmem"),
    }
}
```

```rust
// crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/distributed.rs:138-145 — usage site
let commit = DurableCommitSink::new(
    Arc::clone(&recorder),
    lease.shard_id.clone(),
    lease.tenant_id,
    lease.tenant_secret_key,
    connector_tag_for_kind(lease.assignment.connector_kind),
);
```

```rust
// crates/gossip-connectors/src/lib.rs:24-31 — current exports
pub use common::path_buf_from_bytes;
pub use filesystem::{FILESYSTEM_CONNECTOR_TAG, FilesystemConnector};
pub use git::{GIT_CONNECTOR_TAG, GitConnector};
pub use in_memory::{InMemoryDeterministicConnector, MemItem};
```

## Testing Strategy

Add to `gossip-connectors` (unit tests):
- `canonical_tag_mapping_matches_constants` — `connector_tag_for_kind(Filesystem)` == `FILESYSTEM_CONNECTOR_TAG`, etc.
- `no_duplicate_canonical_tags` — all 3 tags are distinct

Add to `gossip-scanner-runtime` (or update existing):
- Verify that the runtime's tag usage matches the canonical constants (this
  may already be covered if `distributed.rs` just imports the function)

## Related Work

| Task ID | Title | Relationship |
|---------|-------|-------------|
| None found | | |

This task is logically downstream of P0.2 (connector identity collisions). If
P0.2 removes `connector_tag` from `DurableCommitSink`, the blast radius of
P0.3 shrinks. Either ordering works, but implementing P0.2 first is cleaner.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `IN_MEMORY_CONNECTOR_TAG` constant exists in `gossip-connectors/src/in_memory.rs` with value `ConnectorTag::from_ascii(b"inmem")`
- [ ] `connector_tag_for_kind(kind: ConnectorKind) -> ConnectorTag` exists in `gossip-connectors/src/lib.rs`
- [ ] `connector_tag_for_kind` uses `FILESYSTEM_CONNECTOR_TAG`, `GIT_CONNECTOR_TAG`, `IN_MEMORY_CONNECTOR_TAG` — no inline `from_ascii` calls
- [ ] `connector_tag_for_kind` and `IN_MEMORY_CONNECTOR_TAG` are re-exported from `gossip-connectors/src/lib.rs`
- [ ] `distributed.rs` local `connector_tag_for_kind` is removed
- [ ] `distributed.rs` imports `connector_tag_for_kind` from `gossip_connectors`
- [ ] Any test fixtures using `b"fs"` or `b"git"` as connector tags are updated to use canonical constants
- [ ] Test: canonical mapping matches connector constants
- [ ] Test: no duplicate canonical tags across connector kinds
- [ ] All existing tests pass: `cargo test`
- [ ] Code compiles clean: `cargo fmt --all && cargo check && cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`
- [ ] No version bumps — all code remains V0

## Pointers

- `ConnectorTag::from_ascii` implementation: `gossip-contracts/src/identity/item.rs:184-211` — the const function panics on >8 bytes or non-ASCII
- `ConnectorKind` definition: `gossip-scan-driver/src/lib.rs:95-103` — this is the enum that the mapping function takes as input
- Check if `gossip-connectors` already depends on `gossip-scan-driver` (for `ConnectorKind`) — if not, you need to add it to `Cargo.toml` or move the function
close_reason: Implemented canonical connector tag mapping and unified in-memory tag namespace

title: Consider derive macro for CanonicalBytes field-order enforcement
description:
## Context

Review finding F3 from refactor/persistence-prep PR review. The CanonicalBytes trait
implementations are repetitive boilerplate that manually feeds struct fields to a hasher
in declaration order. This is error-prone: reordering struct fields without updating the
impl silently changes all derived IDs.

## Current State

Each identity input struct (FindingIdInputs, OccurrenceIdInputs, ObservationIdInputs) in
`crates/gossip-contracts/src/identity/finding.rs` has a hand-written `CanonicalBytes` impl
that calls `write_canonical` on each field sequentially. Field-order invariants are
documented in comments but not enforced mechanically.

## Desired State

Consider a derive macro for `CanonicalBytes` that automatically generates the impl by
iterating over struct fields in declaration order. This would:
- Eliminate repetitive boilerplate
- Mechanically enforce field-order = hash-order invariant
- Prevent silent ID breakage from field reordering

title: Boundary 5 — Persistence contracts, backends, and commit protocol
description:
## Context

The persistence boundary is the rightmost module in the gossip-rs acyclic boundary graph. It owns the done-ledger (tracking which object-versions have been scanned under which policies), the findings sink (durable storage for detection results at three layers: findings, occurrences, observations), and the commit protocol typestate that enforces correct ordering of persistence operations at compile time.

## Architecture: Contracts vs Implementations

**gossip-contracts::persistence** defines the API surface only — traits, types, contracts, and the conformance harness that backends must pass. No concrete implementations live here.

**Backend implementations** live in separate crates, each implementing the contract traits:

| Crate | Purpose | Status |
|-------|---------|--------|
| `gossip-persistence-inmemory` | Reference/test backends for simulation | Planned (gossip-8961) — currently in contracts, being extracted |
| `gossip-persistence-postgres` | MVP production done-ledger + findings | Future |
| `gossip-persistence-scylla` | Scale-path done-ledger | Future |

This mirrors the coordination boundary where:
- Traits live in `gossip-contracts::coordination`
- In-memory implementation lives in `gossip-coordination`
- Future etcd backend would live in `gossip-coordination-etcd`

## Current State

Phase 1 contracts are complete (A1-A4 closed). The in-memory reference backends were initially placed in `gossip-contracts` behind a `test-support` feature gate. Task gossip-8961 extracts them into `gossip-persistence-inmemory` to enforce the contracts-only boundary.

Remaining Phase 1 work:
- A5 (gossip-8951.5): Backend-agnostic conformance test harness — blocked on gossip-8961
- gossip-8961: Extract in-memory backends to `gossip-persistence-inmemory`

## Desired State

A complete persistence boundary with:
1. Contract types and backend-neutral traits in `gossip-contracts::persistence`
2. Commit protocol typestate machine enforcing write ordering at compile time
3. Backend-agnostic conformance test harness in `gossip-contracts::persistence::conformance`
4. In-memory reference backends in `gossip-persistence-inmemory` (separate crate)
5. Production backend implementations in their own crates (future phases)
6. Worker integration enforcing durable commit ordering before cursor checkpoint advancement

## Planned Phases

| Phase | Scope | Status |
|-------|-------|--------|
| Phase 1 — A1 | Core types and backend-neutral traits (`DoneLedger`, `FindingsSink`) | Done |
| Phase 1 — A2 | Commit receipts / commit-handle typestate | Done |
| Phase 1 — A3 | Canonical ObservationId derivation | Done |
| Phase 1 — A4 | In-memory reference backends | Done (needs extraction to own crate — gossip-8961) |
| Phase 1 — A5 | Backend-agnostic conformance harness | Open (blocked on gossip-8961) |
| Phase 2 — Extraction | Move in-memory impls to `gossip-persistence-inmemory` | gossip-8961 |
| Phase 3+ | Production backends (Postgres, ScyllaDB), worker integration, commit pipeline | Future |

## Implementation Guidance

### Module Organization (gossip-contracts::persistence)

The persistence module follows the same pattern as other gossip-contracts boundaries:
- `mod.rs` contains only module-level docs and `pub use` re-exports
- Submodule files are named by domain concern (not `types.rs`)
- Each submodule is self-contained with its own imports
- Conformance harness is a public module (not behind feature gate) so external crates can use it
- **No concrete implementations** — those live in backend crates

### Backend Crate Organization

Each backend crate:
- Depends on `gossip-contracts` for trait definitions
- Implements `DoneLedger` and/or `FindingsSink`
- Implements `FindingsConformanceProbe` (from conformance harness) in test code
- Runs the conformance suite as integration tests

### Patterns to Follow
- Do not checkpoint cursor before durable done-ledger/findings commit
- Use deterministic IDs and idempotent upsert semantics
- Maintain tenant isolation and no raw-secret storage guarantees
- Secret-derived fields use fixed-width hash newtypes with redacted Debug
- Free-form strings are bounded and validated at construction

### Utilities to Reuse
- `gossip_contracts::identity` — deterministic hashes/IDs, `CanonicalBytes`, `define_id_32!`
- `gossip_contracts::connector` — `Location`, `VersionId` types
- Coordination op-id/fence patterns for consistency with control plane

## Code References

- Persistence contracts: `crates/gossip-contracts/src/persistence/`
- Module declaration: `crates/gossip-contracts/src/lib.rs:59-62`
- Identity prerequisites: `crates/gossip-contracts/src/identity/`
- Connector prerequisites: `crates/gossip-contracts/src/connector/types.rs`
- Architecture doc: `docs/gossip-contracts/boundary-5-persistence.md`
- Implementation artifacts: `tmp/gossip-project-artifacts/b5_persistence/`
- Coordination pattern (reference): `crates/gossip-coordination/src/in_memory.rs`

## Related Work

| Task ID | Title | Relationship |
|---------|-------|-------------|
| gossip-rs-8r9.10 (closed) | Phase 5B: done-ledger and findings persistence backends | Predecessor, deferred — this epic supersedes |
| gossip-rs-8r9.9 (closed) | Phase 5A: durable coordination backend | Completed prerequisite |
| gossip-8936.6 | Done-ledger key-range skip-ahead for filesystem rescans | Depends on persistence contracts |
| gossip-rs-8r9 | Consolidate scanner-rs into gossip-rs | Parent consolidation stream (completed milestone) |
| gossip-8961 | Extract in-memory persistence into gossip-persistence-inmemory | Enforces contracts-only boundary |

## Risk Analysis

- Ordering mistakes can acknowledge progress before durable writes
- Backend schema drift can break deterministic dedupe assumptions
- Scope risk: persistence touches correctness-critical paths (duplicate findings, missing findings, false completion signals)
- Mitigation: typestate/explicit sequencing APIs, conformance harness, integration tests with retries/replays, failure injection

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Downstream crates can compile using persistence traits without touching backend crates
- [ ] Done-ledger and findings-sink contracts are backend-neutral and storage-agnostic
- [ ] No raw secret bytes in any public record shape
- [ ] Commit protocol typestate prevents misordered persistence operations at compile time

title: A1 — Implement gossip-contracts::persistence core types and backend-neutral traits
description:
## Context

This is the foundation task for the persistence boundary (Boundary 5). It replaces the documentation-only stub in `gossip-contracts::persistence` with actual types and traits that downstream crates can compile against. No backend implementations, no commit protocol typestate, no in-memory test doubles — just the data model and trait surface.

The "no secret bytes by construction" invariant is central: secret material only appears as fixed-width hashes with redacted `Debug`, and no free-form `String` fields are sourced from content unless explicitly marked safe/bounded.

## Current State

```rust
// crates/gossip-contracts/src/persistence/mod.rs (entire file — 24 lines)
//! Done-ledger, findings-sink traits, and the commit protocol typestate machine.
//!
//! Owns the persistence boundary: the `DoneLedger` trait for
//! recording completed work (`DoneLedgerKey`, `OvidHash`), the `FindingsSink`
//! trait for emitting detection results (`FindingRecord`, `OccurrenceRecord`,
//! `FindingsUpsertBatch`), and the `PageCommit<S>` typestate machine that
//! enforces the commit protocol at compile time — ensuring that a page's
//! done-ledger writes, findings upserts, and cursor checkpoint happen in the
//! correct order and exactly once.
// (doc comments only, zero code)
```

The module is declared `pub mod persistence;` at `crates/gossip-contracts/src/lib.rs:59-60` but exports nothing.

All prerequisite types exist and are exported:
- Identity: `FindingId`, `ObservationId`, `OccurrenceId`, `ObjectVersionId`, `SecretHash`, `RuleFingerprint`, `LogicalTime`, `FenceEpoch`, `TenantId`, `PolicyHash`, `StableItemId`, `RunId`, `ShardId`
- Connector: `Location`, `VersionId`
- Infrastructure: `define_id_32!` macro, `CanonicalBytes` trait, `identity::domain::OVID_V1`, `blake3` dependency

## Desired State

The persistence module is split into four domain-named submodules plus a minimal re-export hub:

### `persistence/ovid.rs` (~80 lines)
- `OvidHash` (32B) — BLAKE3-derived object-version identity hash, via `define_id_32!`
- `OvidHashInputs` — structured inputs: `StableItemId` + `VersionId`
- `derive_ovid_hash()` — deterministic derivation using cached `OVID_HASHER` (BLAKE3 derive-key with `identity::domain::OVID_V1`)
- `OVID_HASHER` — `LazyLock<Hasher>` for derive-key context reuse
- `write_version_id_canonical()` — canonical encoding of `VersionId::Strong`/`Weak` discriminant

### `persistence/done_ledger.rs` (~370 lines)
- `MAX_DONE_LEDGER_ERROR_CODE_SIZE` (128) — byte limit for error codes
- `DoneLedgerKey` — tenant + policy + ovid composite key with `CanonicalBytes`
- `DoneLedgerStatus` — monotonic result lattice enum:
  - `FailedRetryable(1) < FailedPermanent(2) < Skipped(3) < ScannedClean(10) < ScannedWithFindings(11)`
  - `merge()` returns the higher-ranked status
  - `is_scanned()` and `is_failure()` classification helpers
- `DoneLedgerErrorCode` — bounded safe string (max 128 bytes, ASCII alphanumeric + `_-.:/ `)
- `DoneLedgerProvenance` — run/shard/fence/timing metadata
- `DoneLedgerRecord` — complete durable done-ledger row
- `DoneLedger` trait — `batch_get` + `batch_upsert` with monotonic merge and idempotent upsert contracts

### `persistence/findings.rs` (~350 lines)
- `FindingRecord` — stable finding identity (tenant, finding_id, stable_item_id, rule_fingerprint, secret_hash)
- `OccurrenceRecord` — version-specific occurrence (with `NonZeroU64` span length, `try_new` fallible constructor)
- `ObservationRecord` — policy-scoped observation (includes policy_hash, run_id, shard_id, fence_epoch, seen_at, optional `Location`)
- `FindingsUpsertBatch<'a>` — borrowed batch view for sink upserts
- `FindingsSink` trait — `upsert_batch` with idempotent upsert + referential integrity contract

### `persistence/error.rs` (~50 lines)
- `PersistenceInputError` — validation error enum shared by done-ledger and findings:
  - `Empty { field }` — bounded string field was empty

title: A2 — Implement commit-handle/receipt boundary and page-commit typestate machine
description:
## Context

This is the second foundation task for the persistence boundary. It builds on A1 (core types and backend-neutral traits) by adding the acknowledgement protocol and commit-ordering typestate machine. The key design principle is that **submission and durability are separated**: a sink method returning `Ok(handle)` means the backend accepted the write request, but durability is not established until `handle.wait()` returns a receipt. The `PageCommit<S>` typestate machine then enforces the correct ordering (findings → done-ledger → checkpoint) at compile time, making misordered persistence operations a type error.

This task depends on A1 (`gossip-8951.1`) being complete because it modifies the `DoneLedger` and `FindingsSink` traits introduced there, and the receipt types reference A1 record types.

## Current State

After A1 is complete, the persistence module will have four submodules:
- `ovid.rs` — `OvidHash` derivation
- `done_ledger.rs` — done-ledger types + `DoneLedger` trait (returns `Result<(), Self::Error>` from `batch_upsert`)
- `findings.rs` — findings types + `FindingsSink` trait (returns `Result<(), Self::Error>` from `upsert_batch`)
- `error.rs` — `PersistenceInputError` shared validation errors
- `mod.rs` — re-exports

The A1 traits have no concept of deferred durability — `batch_upsert` and `upsert_batch` return `Result<(), E>`, implying synchronous completion. No commit receipts, no ordering enforcement, no typestate machine exists yet.

## Desired State

### New file: `persistence/commit.rs` (~240 lines)

**Handle/receipt infrastructure:**
- `CommitReceipt` — marker trait (`Clone + Debug + Send + Sync + 'static`) for durable acknowledgement proofs
- `CommitHandle` — `#[must_use]` trait with `type Receipt: CommitReceipt`, `type Error`, and `fn wait(self) -> Result<Self::Receipt, Self::Error>` — the durable acknowledgement boundary
- `ReadyCommitHandle<R, E>` — immediate already-resolved handle for synchronous backends and tests, with `ok()`, `err()`, `from_result()` constructors

**Receipt types:**
- `FindingsCommitReceipt` — counts: `finding_count`, `occurrence_count`, `observation_count`
- `DoneLedgerCommitReceipt` — counts: `record_count`, `scanned_count`, `findings_count`
- `CheckpointCommitReceipt` — full scope: `tenant_id`, `run_id`, `shard_id`, `fence_epoch`, `cursor: Cursor`, `committed_items`, `checkpointed_at: LogicalTime`
- `ItemCommitReceipt` — composite: `PageCommitScope` + `FindingsCommitReceipt` + `DoneLedgerCommitReceipt` (proves durable findings + done-ledger)
- `PageCommitReceipt` — composite: `ItemCommitReceipt` + `CheckpointCommitReceipt` (proves full page durability)

All receipt types implement `CommitReceipt`.

### New file: `persistence/page_commit.rs` (~370 lines)

**Page scope:**
- `PageCommitScope` — scoped to one tenant/run/shard/fence epoch/cursor: `tenant_id`, `run_id`, `shard_id`, `fence_epoch`, `committed_items`, `checkpoint_cursor: Cursor`

**Validation:**
- `PageCommitValidationError` — 7 mismatch variants for receipt-vs-scope validation:
  - `LedgerItemCountMismatch` — done-ledger record_count != committed_items
  - `CheckpointTenantMismatch`, `CheckpointRunMismatch`, `CheckpointShardMismatch`, `CheckpointFenceMismatch` — scope field mismatches
  - `CheckpointItemCountMismatch`, `CheckpointCursorMismatch` — checkpoint field mismatches
- `CommitAdvanceError<E>` — `Wait(E) | Validation(PageCommitValidationError)` — combined wait/validation error

**Typestate markers:**
- `AwaitingFindings` — initial state, no durable findings yet
- `FindingsDurable` — findings durably persisted, done-ledger pending
- `ItemDurable` — findings + done-ledger durable, checkpoint pending
- `CheckpointDurable` — all three layers durable

**Typestate machine:**
- `PageCommit<S>` — `#[must_use]` generic struct with `scope: PageCommitScope` + `state: S`
- State transitions enforced at compile time:
  ```
  PageCommit<AwaitingFindings>
    → .record_findings(receipt) / .wait_findings(handle)
  PageCommit<FindingsDurable>
    → .record_done_ledger(receipt) / .wait_done_ledger(handle)
  PageCommit<ItemDurable>
    → .record_checkpoint(receipt) / .wait_checkpoint(handle)
  PageCommit<CheckpointDurable>
    → .into_page_commit_receipt()
  ```
- `record_done_ledger` validates `receipt.record_count() == scope.committed_items()`
- `record_checkpoint` validates all 6 scope fields match (tenant, run, shard, fence, items, cursor)

### Modifications to existing A1 files

**`done_ledger.rs` — `DoneLedger` trait changes:**
```rust
// A1 (current after gossip-8951.1):
pub trait DoneLedger: Send + Sync {
    type Error: Error + Send + Sync + 'static;
    fn batch_upsert(&self, records: &[DoneLedgerRecord]) -> Result<(), Self::Error>;
}

// A2 (updated):
pub trait DoneLedger: Send + Sync {
    type Error: Error + Send + Sync + 'static;
    type CommitHandle: CommitHandle<Receipt = DoneLedgerCommitReceipt, Error = Self::Error>;
    fn batch_upsert(&self, records: &[DoneLedgerRecord]) -> Result<Self::CommitHandle, Self::Error>;
}
```

**`findings.rs` — `FindingsSink` trait changes:**
```rust
// A1 (current after gossip-8951.1):
pub trait FindingsSink: Send + Sync {
    type Error: Error + Send + Sync + 'static;
    fn upsert_batch(&self, batch: FindingsUpsertBatch<'_>) -> Result<(), Self::Error>;
}

// A2 (updated):
pub trait FindingsSink: Send + Sync {
    type Error: Error + Send + Sync + 'static;
    type CommitHandle: CommitHandle<Receipt = FindingsCommitReceipt, Error = Self::Error>;
    fn upsert_batch(&self, batch: FindingsUpsertBatch<'_>) -> Result<Self::CommitHandle, Self::Error>;
}
```

**New import added:** `Cursor` from `crate::connector` (used by `CheckpointCommitReceipt` and `PageCommitScope`).

title: A3 — Root ObservationRecord identity in canonical ObservationId derivation
description:
## Context

This task makes policy-scoped observation identity explicit and tamper-evident. Currently (after A1), `ObservationRecord::new` accepts a caller-provided `ObservationId`, which means a caller could accidentally (or intentionally) supply an ID that does not match the canonical derivation from `(tenant, policy_hash, occurrence_id)`. A3 closes this gap by making `ObservationRecord::new` derive the ID internally and adding validation for the storage round-trip path.

The identity infrastructure already exists in the identity module — `ObservationIdInputs`, `derive_observation_id`, and golden vectors are all implemented at `identity/finding.rs:300-434`. A3 wires this into the persistence boundary so that no one can confuse "finding identity" with "policy-scoped detection event" in persistence code.

This task depends on A1 (`gossip-8951.1`) because it modifies `ObservationRecord` and `PersistenceInputError` introduced there. It also depends on A2 (`gossip-8951.2`) because the artifact assumes the commit-handle traits are in place and the `FindingsSink` trait doc is updated accordingly.

## Current State

After A1+A2, `ObservationRecord::new` accepts a caller-provided `ObservationId`:

```rust
// persistence/findings.rs — after A1
impl ObservationRecord {
    pub fn new(
        tenant_id: TenantId,
        observation_id: ObservationId, // <-- caller provides this
        occurrence_id: OccurrenceId,
        policy_hash: PolicyHash,
        ovid_hash: OvidHash,
        run_id: RunId,
        shard_id: ShardId,
        fence_epoch: FenceEpoch,
        seen_at: LogicalTime,
    ) -> Self { /* stores observation_id as-is */ }
}
```

There is no validation that the provided `observation_id` matches the canonical derivation `H(tenant, policy_hash, occurrence_id)`. No `from_persisted` path for storage round-trips. No batch-level identity validation.

The identity derivation infrastructure already exists:
- `ObservationIdInputs` at `identity/finding.rs:300-307` — struct with public fields `tenant: TenantId`, `policy: PolicyHash`, `occurrence: OccurrenceId`
- `derive_observation_id` at `identity/finding.rs:432` — BLAKE3 derive-key with `OBSERVATION_V1` domain
- Golden vectors and field-order tests at `identity/finding.rs:1013-1029`

## Desired State

### Modifications to `persistence/findings.rs`

**`ObservationRecord::new` — remove `observation_id` parameter, derive internally:**

```rust
impl ObservationRecord {
    /// Construct a policy-scoped observation record.
    ///
    /// The observation identity is derived canonically from
    /// `(tenant_id, policy_hash, occurrence_id)`. Callers do not provide an
    /// arbitrary `ObservationId`; that would allow the same policy-scoped event
    /// to be mislabeled as a different identity.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn new(
        tenant_id: TenantId,
        occurrence_id: OccurrenceId,    // observation_id removed
        policy_hash: PolicyHash,
        ovid_hash: OvidHash,
        run_id: RunId,
        shard_id: ShardId,
        fence_epoch: FenceEpoch,
        seen_at: LogicalTime,
    ) -> Self {
```

title: A4 — In-memory reference implementations under test-support feature
description:
## Context

This task adds deterministic in-memory reference implementations of the `DoneLedger` and `FindingsSink` traits, gated behind the existing `test-support` feature flag. These are **not toy mocks** — they enforce the same semantic invariants that production backends must uphold: monotonic lattice merges for done-ledger status, idempotent upserts, referential integrity between findings/occurrences/observations, and canonical observation identity validation. They also provide explicit fault injection hooks (fail submissions, fail commits, delay writes) for deterministic simulation testing.

This is the final Phase 1 task in the Boundary 5 persistence epic. After A4, the persistence module has enough infrastructure for simulation testing and conformance test harness development (future A5).

The existing codebase already has an `in_memory.rs` pattern in `gossip-coordination` (`crates/gossip-coordination/src/in_memory.rs`) that serves as the executable specification for that boundary's traits. A4 follows the same approach for persistence.

## Current State

After A1+A2+A3, the persistence module defines:
- `DoneLedger` trait with `batch_get` and `batch_upsert` methods
- `FindingsSink` trait with `upsert_batch` method
- `CommitHandle` trait with `wait()` for durable acknowledgement
- `DoneLedgerCommitReceipt`, `FindingsCommitReceipt` — durable receipt types
- `DoneLedgerRecord`, `FindingRecord`, `OccurrenceRecord`, `ObservationRecord` — record shapes
- `DoneLedgerStatus` monotonic lattice with `merge()` and `rank()` methods
- `ObservationRecord::validate_identity()` — canonical observation_id verification
- `FindingsUpsertBatch::validate()` — batch-level identity validation
- `PersistenceInputError` — validation error enum

The module doc has TODO comments at `persistence/mod.rs:1692-1698`:

```rust
// TODO(A4): add in-memory reference implementations with fault injection.
// TODO(A5): add backend-agnostic conformance tests covering:
// - idempotent done-ledger upserts
// - monotonic `DoneLedgerStatus` merge semantics
// - no duplicate findings / occurrences / observations under replay
// - no-early-ACK semantics for `CommitHandle::wait`
// - `PageCommit<S>` ordering and scope validation
```

There are no implementations of `DoneLedger` or `FindingsSink` yet. The `Cargo.toml` already has a `test-support` feature flag that gates `dep:proptest`. The crate has an existing pattern for conditional test-support compilation at `lib.rs:89-95`.

## Desired State

### New file: `crates/gossip-contracts/src/persistence/in_memory.rs`

A single 1309-line module providing:

**Public types:**

- `CompletionOrder` — enum `{ OldestFirst, NewestFirst }` for manual release ordering
- `InMemoryStoreKind` — enum `{ DoneLedger, Findings }` for fault injection and error reporting
- `PendingWriteId` — opaque u64 wrapper for pending operation tracking
- `InMemoryPersistenceError` — comprehensive error enum with variants:
  - `InjectedSubmissionFailure { store }` — submission rejected by fault injection
  - `InjectedCommitFailure { store }` — commit failed by fault injection
  - `Poisoned { store }` — mutex/condvar poisoned
  - `UnknownOperation { store, op_id }` — handle waited on nonexistent op
  - `MissingFinding { tenant_id, finding_id, occurrence_id }` — referential integrity violation
  - `MissingOccurrence { tenant_id, occurrence_id, observation_id }` — referential integrity violation
  - `FindingConflict { tenant_id, finding_id }` — immutable content mismatch
  - `OccurrenceConflict { tenant_id, occurrence_id }` — immutable content mismatch
  - `ObservationConflict { tenant_id, observation_id }` — identity field mismatch
  - `BatchValidation(PersistenceInputError)` — A3 identity validation failure
- `InMemoryDoneLedger` — `Clone`, `Default`, `Arc`-backed reference implementation of `DoneLedger`
- `InMemoryDoneLedgerHandle` — `CommitHandle` impl with condvar-based wait
- `InMemoryFindingsSink` — `Clone`, `Default`, `Arc`-backed reference implementation of `FindingsSink`
- `InMemoryFindingsHandle` — `CommitHandle` impl with condvar-based wait

**`InMemoryDoneLedger` public API:**

```rust
impl InMemoryDoneLedger {
    pub fn new() -> Self;
    pub fn with_auto_complete(auto_complete: bool) -> Self;
    pub fn set_auto_complete(&self, auto_complete: bool) -> Result<(), InMemoryPersistenceError>;
    pub fn delay_next_writes(&self, count: usize) -> Result<(), InMemoryPersistenceError>;
    pub fn fail_next_submissions(&self, count: usize) -> Result<(), InMemoryPersistenceError>;
    pub fn fail_next_commits(&self, count: usize) -> Result<(), InMemoryPersistenceError>;
    pub fn release_next(&self, order: CompletionOrder) -> Result<Option<PendingWriteId>, InMemoryPersistenceError>;
    pub fn release_specific(&self, op_id: PendingWriteId) -> Result<bool, InMemoryPersistenceError>;
    pub fn release_all(&self, order: CompletionOrder) -> Result<usize, InMemoryPersistenceError>;
    pub fn pending_count(&self) -> Result<usize, InMemoryPersistenceError>;
    pub fn pending_ids(&self) -> Result<Vec<PendingWriteId>, InMemoryPersistenceError>;
    pub fn get_record(&self, key: DoneLedgerKey) -> Result<Option<DoneLedgerRecord>, InMemoryPersistenceError>;
    pub fn snapshot(&self) -> Result<Vec<DoneLedgerRecord>, InMemoryPersistenceError>;
}
```

**`InMemoryFindingsSink` public API:**

```rust
impl InMemoryFindingsSink {
    pub fn new() -> Self;
    pub fn with_auto_complete(auto_complete: bool) -> Self;
    pub fn set_auto_complete(&self, auto_complete: bool) -> Result<(), InMemoryPersistenceError>;
    pub fn delay_next_writes(&self, count: usize) -> Result<(), InMemoryPersistenceError>;
    pub fn fail_next_submissions(&self, count: usize) -> Result<(), InMemoryPersistenceError>;
    pub fn fail_next_commits(&self, count: usize) -> Result<(), InMemoryPersistenceError>;
    pub fn release_next(&self, order: CompletionOrder) -> Result<Option<PendingWriteId>, InMemoryPersistenceError>;
    pub fn release_specific(&self, op_id: PendingWriteId) -> Result<bool, InMemoryPersistenceError>;
    pub fn release_all(&self, order: CompletionOrder) -> Result<usize, InMemoryPersistenceError>;
    pub fn pending_count(&self) -> Result<usize, InMemoryPersistenceError>;
    pub fn pending_ids(&self) -> Result<Vec<PendingWriteId>, InMemoryPersistenceError>;
    pub fn findings_snapshot(&self) -> Result<Vec<FindingRecord>, InMemoryPersistenceError>;
    pub fn occurrences_snapshot(&self) -> Result<Vec<OccurrenceRecord>, InMemoryPersistenceError>;
    pub fn observations_snapshot(&self) -> Result<Vec<ObservationRecord>, InMemoryPersistenceError>;
    pub fn get_finding(&self, tenant_id: TenantId, finding_id: FindingId) -> Result<Option<FindingRecord>, InMemoryPersistenceError>;
    pub fn get_occurrence(&self, tenant_id: TenantId, occurrence_id: OccurrenceId) -> Result<Option<OccurrenceRecord>, InMemoryPersistenceError>;
    pub fn get_observation(&self, tenant_id: TenantId, observation_id: ObservationId) -> Result<Option<ObservationRecord>, InMemoryPersistenceError>;
}
```

**Key semantic behaviors:**

1. **Done-ledger monotonic lattice merge**: when upserting an existing key, `DoneLedgerStatus::merge()` is used (higher rank wins). `bytes_scanned` and `findings_count` take `max()`. Provenance is chosen from whichever record has the higher status rank, or later `finished_at` on ties, or later `started_at` on ties. Error codes are cleared if merged status is scanned.

2. **Findings immutability**: findings and occurrences keyed by `(tenant_id, finding_id)` / `(tenant_id, occurrence_id)` are immutable once stored. Re-upserting the same key with identical content is idempotent. Re-upserting with different content returns `FindingConflict` / `OccurrenceConflict`.

3. **Observation merges**: observations are keyed by `(tenant_id, observation_id)`. Identity fields `(tenant_id, observation_id, occurrence_id, policy_hash, ovid_hash)` must agree; disagreement returns `ObservationConflict`. Non-identity provenance fields (`run_id`, `shard_id`, `fence_epoch`, `seen_at`, `location`) are merged by most-recent `seen_at`, with tie-breaking favoring records that have location data.

4. **Referential integrity**: occurrence submissions check that `finding_id` references a finding in the same batch or already durable. Observation submissions check that `occurrence_id` references an occurrence in the same batch or already durable. Violations return `MissingFinding` / `MissingOccurrence`.

5. **A3 identity validation**: observations are validated via `ObservationRecord::validate_identity()` before processing. Failures surface as `BatchValidation(PersistenceInputError)`.

6. **Staged write atomicity**: findings payload application clones durable state into staging maps, validates all records against staging, and only commits to durable state on full success.

7. **Auto-complete mode**: when enabled (default), submissions complete immediately — `CommitHandle::wait()` returns instantly. When disabled, submissions remain pending until explicitly released.

8. **Fault injection**: `fail_next_submissions(N)` causes the next N `batch_upsert`/`batch_get` calls to return `InjectedSubmissionFailure` before creating a handle. `fail_next_commits(N)` causes the next N durable commit applications to return `InjectedCommitFailure`. `delay_next_writes(N)` causes the next N submissions to remain pending regardless of auto-complete.

9. **Manual release**: `release_next(order)` releases one pending op in FIFO/LIFO order. `release_specific(op_id)` releases a specific op. `release_all(order)` drains all pending ops. Released ops wake blocked `CommitHandle::wait()` callers via condvar.

### Modifications to `crates/gossip-contracts/src/persistence/mod.rs`

Remove the `TODO(A4)` comment. Add conditional module declaration and re-exports:


## Testing Guidance

**DoneLedger invariants:**
- **Lattice monotonicity**: upserting the same key with a lower-ranked status does not downgrade the stored status
- **Lattice merge correctness**: `ScannedClean.merge(FailedRetryable) == ScannedClean`; `FailedRetryable.merge(ScannedWithFindings) == ScannedWithFindings`
- **Idempotent upsert**: upserting the same record twice produces identical durable state
- **`max()` aggregation**: `bytes_scanned` and `findings_count` take the max of existing and incoming
- **Provenance selection**: higher-status record's provenance wins; on ties, later `finished_at` wins
- **Error code clearing**: merged scanned status clears error_code regardless of incoming error_code

- **Observation merge**: identity fields must agree; provenance merges by most-recent `seen_at`
- **Referential integrity**: occurrence without corresponding finding returns `MissingFinding`; observation without corresponding occurrence returns `MissingOccurrence`
- **Same-batch references**: occurrence can reference a finding in the same batch (not yet durable)
- **A3 identity validation**: invalid `observation_id` returns `BatchValidation(ObservationIdMismatch)`

- **`fail_next_commits(1)`**: submission succeeds but `wait()` returns `InjectedCommitFailure`
- **`delay_next_writes(1)`**: submission succeeds, `pending_count()` increases, `release_next` completes it
- **Counters are saturating**: `fail_next_submissions(usize::MAX)` does not overflow

**CommitHandle invariants:**
- **Auto-complete mode**: `wait()` returns immediately with receipt when auto_complete is true
- **Manual release**: with auto_complete off, `wait()` blocks until `release_next` is called
- **FIFO/LIFO ordering**: `release_next(OldestFirst)` releases in submission order; `NewestFirst` reverses
- **`release_specific`**: releases exactly the targeted op; returns `false` for already-completed ops
- **`release_all`**: drains all pending ops; returns count

title: A5 — Backend-agnostic persistence conformance test harness
description:
## Context

This task adds a backend-agnostic persistence conformance test harness that every `DoneLedger` and `FindingsSink` implementation must pass. The conformance suite validates the semantic invariants that are specified in trait documentation but cannot be mechanically enforced by Rust's type system alone: idempotent upserts, monotonic lattice merges, referential integrity, no-duplicate guarantees under replay, and Debug redaction of sensitive types.

This is the final task in Phase 1 of the Boundary 5 persistence epic. After A5, the persistence module has its full contract surface: types (A1), commit protocol (A2), canonical identity (A3), and conformance harness (A5). The in-memory reference backends (formerly A4) now live in the separate `gossip-persistence-inmemory` crate (gossip-8961). Future phases add production backends — each must pass `run_conformance` before being accepted.

The existing codebase already has conformance test harnesses for the connector boundary (`crates/gossip-contracts/src/connector/conformance_tests.rs`) and the coordination boundary (`crates/gossip-coordination/src/conformance_tests.rs`). A5 follows the same pattern for persistence.

## Current State

After A1+A2+A3, the persistence module has:
- `DoneLedger` trait with `batch_get` and `batch_upsert` methods, documented monotonic lattice contract
- `FindingsSink` trait with `upsert_batch` method, documented idempotent upsert and referential integrity contract
- `CommitHandle` trait separating submission from durability
- Record types: `DoneLedgerRecord`, `FindingRecord`, `OccurrenceRecord`, `ObservationRecord`
- `DoneLedgerStatus` monotonic lattice with `merge()` and `rank()`
- `ObservationRecord::validate_identity()` canonical ID validation

The in-memory reference backends (`InMemoryDoneLedger`, `InMemoryFindingsSink`) currently live in `gossip-contracts::persistence::in_memory` behind a `test-support` feature gate. Task gossip-8961 will extract them into the `gossip-persistence-inmemory` crate before this task begins.

The `FindingsSink` trait is write-only by design. This is correct for production, but makes idempotency untestable: a backend could accept the same batch twice and silently duplicate storage while returning `Ok(())` both times. The conformance harness solves this with a small test-only read-side probe trait.

## Desired State

### New file: `crates/gossip-contracts/src/persistence/conformance.rs`

An ~815-line module providing the reusable conformance harness. **This module is NOT behind `cfg(test-support)` — it is a public module available to all consumers** so that external backend crates (`gossip-persistence-inmemory`, `gossip-persistence-postgres`, `gossip-persistence-scylla`) can run conformance tests against their implementations.

**Public types:**

- `DurableFindingsCounts` — value type with `findings`, `occurrences`, `observations` counts and `saturating_sub` for delta assertions
- `FindingsConformanceProbe` — test-only trait with `durable_counts() -> Result<DurableFindingsCounts, Self::Error>`
- `PersistenceConformanceReport` — aggregate report with `done_ledger_checks`, `findings_checks`, `redaction_checks` counts
- `PersistenceConformanceError` — comprehensive error enum covering fixture construction, submission, wait, lookup, invariant violations, probe failures, and redaction leaks

**Public functions:**

```rust
/// Run the full persistence conformance suite.
pub fn run_conformance<L, F>(
    done_ledger: &L,
    findings: &F,
) -> Result<PersistenceConformanceReport, PersistenceConformanceError>
where
    L: DoneLedger,
    F: FindingsSink + FindingsConformanceProbe;

/// Run only done-ledger conformance (3 checks).
pub fn run_done_ledger_conformance<L: DoneLedger>(
    done_ledger: &L,
) -> Result<u32, PersistenceConformanceError>;

/// Run only findings conformance (3 checks).
pub fn run_findings_conformance<F: FindingsSink + FindingsConformanceProbe>(
    findings: &F,
) -> Result<u32, PersistenceConformanceError>;

/// Run only redaction conformance (3 checks).
pub fn run_redaction_conformance() -> Result<u32, PersistenceConformanceError>;
```

**Done-ledger conformance cases (3 checks):**
1. Idempotent upsert — submit same record twice, read back, verify durable state unchanged
2. Failed-then-scanned — submit `FailedRetryable` then `ScannedWithFindings`, verify scanned dominates
3. Scanned-then-failed — submit in reverse order, verify scanned still dominates (out-of-order resilience)

**Findings conformance cases (3 checks):**
1. Idempotent replay — submit valid batch, replay exact same batch, verify durable counts unchanged via probe
2. Missing finding — submit occurrence without its finding, verify failure and no durable side effects
3. Missing occurrence — submit observation without its occurrence, verify failure and no durable side effects

**Redaction conformance cases (3 checks):**
1. `NormHash` Debug output does not contain raw hex bytes
2. `SecretHash` Debug output does not contain raw hex bytes
3. `FindingRecord` Debug output does not leak `SecretHash` raw bytes

### Conformance test using in-memory backends

After gossip-8961 extracts the in-memory backends to `gossip-persistence-inmemory`, the smoke test that runs conformance against the in-memory backends should live in ONE of these locations:

**Option A (preferred):** `crates/gossip-persistence-inmemory/tests/conformance.rs` — integration test in the in-memory crate that depends on `gossip-contracts` conformance harness.

**Option B:** `crates/gossip-contracts/src/persistence/conformance_tests.rs` with `gossip-persistence-inmemory` as a dev-dependency. This keeps conformance tests close to the harness but creates a circular-feeling dependency.

The test itself is simple:
```rust
use gossip_contracts::persistence::conformance::run_conformance;
use gossip_persistence_inmemory::{InMemoryDoneLedger, InMemoryFindingsSink};

#[test]
fn in_memory_backends_pass_persistence_conformance() {
    let done_ledger = InMemoryDoneLedger::new();
    let findings = InMemoryFindingsSink::new();
    let report = run_conformance(&done_ledger, &findings)
        .unwrap_or_else(|err| panic!("conformance failed: {err}"));
    assert_eq!(report.done_ledger_checks(), 3);
    assert_eq!(report.findings_checks(), 3);
    assert_eq!(report.redaction_checks(), 3);
}
```

### `FindingsConformanceProbe` implementation

The `FindingsConformanceProbe` impl for `InMemoryFindingsSink` lives in **`gossip-persistence-inmemory`**, not in `gossip-contracts`. The in-memory crate depends on `gossip-contracts` (for the `FindingsConformanceProbe` trait definition) and implements it:

```rust
// In gossip-persistence-inmemory
impl FindingsConformanceProbe for InMemoryFindingsSink {
    type Error = InMemoryPersistenceError;

    fn durable_counts(&self) -> Result<DurableFindingsCounts, Self::Error> {
        let guard = self.lock_state()?;
        Ok(DurableFindingsCounts::new(
            guard.durable_findings.len() as u64,
            guard.durable_occurrences.len() as u64,
            guard.durable_observations.len() as u64,
        ))
    }
}
```

### Modifications to `crates/gossip-contracts/src/persistence/mod.rs`

- Update module doc to include A5 scope section
- Add `pub mod conformance;` declaration (NOT behind cfg gate — public for all consumers)
- Add re-exports: `run_conformance`, `run_done_ledger_conformance`, `run_findings_conformance`, `run_redaction_conformance`, `DurableFindingsCounts`, `FindingsConformanceProbe`, `PersistenceConformanceError`, `PersistenceConformanceReport`

## Implementation Guidance

### Implementation Source

The complete A5 code is in the artifact directory:

- `tmp/gossip-project-artifacts/b5_persistence/phase1/a5/conformance_tests.rs` (17 lines) — smoke test

**NOTE:** The artifact `a5/in_memory.rs` assumes the in-memory impl stays in contracts. After gossip-8961, the `FindingsConformanceProbe` impl should be added to the `gossip-persistence-inmemory` crate instead.

### Files to Create / Modify

| `crates/gossip-persistence-inmemory/src/lib.rs` (or findings.rs) | Modify | Add `FindingsConformanceProbe` impl for `InMemoryFindingsSink` |
| `crates/gossip-persistence-inmemory/tests/conformance.rs` | **Create** | Integration test running conformance against in-memory backends |

### Patterns to Follow

| Pattern | Reference | Apply to |
|---------|-----------|----------|
| Conformance harness as public module | `crates/gossip-contracts/src/connector/conformance_tests.rs` | `persistence/conformance.rs` is public so external backend crates can run it |
| Seed-based deterministic fixtures | Connector conformance uses scripted fixtures | `sample_fixture(seed: u8)` constructs all identity types deterministically |
| Test-only probe trait | Not present in other boundaries but necessary here because `FindingsSink` is write-only | `FindingsConformanceProbe` — backend crates implement it |
| Redaction leak detection via Debug | Connector conformance checks `ToxicDigest` does not leak raw bytes | `assert_no_raw_hex` checks `NormHash`, `SecretHash`, `FindingRecord` Debug output |

### Blast Radius

| Consumer | Impact |
|----------|--------|
| `gossip-persistence-inmemory` | Adds `FindingsConformanceProbe` impl (~12 lines) and conformance integration test |
| `gossip-contracts` mod.rs | Additive — new module declaration, re-exports, doc section |
| Future `gossip-persistence-postgres` | Primary consumer — must implement `FindingsConformanceProbe` and call `run_conformance` |
| Future `gossip-persistence-scylla` | Same — must implement `FindingsConformanceProbe` and call `run_conformance` |

## Design Notes

**Why `FindingsConformanceProbe` instead of adding read methods to `FindingsSink`:**

The `FindingsSink` trait is intentionally write-only. Adding read methods would:
1. Force every production backend to expose internal counts that may be expensive to compute
2. Pollute the production trait surface with test-only concerns
3. Create a temptation to use the probe in non-test code paths

Instead, `FindingsConformanceProbe` is a separate trait that backend test suites implement. The in-memory backend naturally has the durable maps in memory, so the probe is trivial. For production backends (e.g., Postgres), the probe would issue a `SELECT COUNT(*)` — acceptable in tests but not in the production write path.

**Why the conformance module is NOT behind `cfg(test-support)`:**

External backend crates need to call `run_conformance` in their integration tests. If it were behind a feature gate on `gossip-contracts`, every backend crate would need to depend on `gossip-contracts` with `features = ["test-support"]` in `[dev-dependencies]`, which is possible but unnecessary. The conformance module has no runtime overhead — it is only invoked by tests.

title: Design PageCommit coordinator trait for cross-trait ordering
description:
## Context

The persistence module defines two independent traits: `FindingsSink` and
`DoneLedger`. When a scan produces findings, callers must persist them via
`FindingsSink::upsert_batch` BEFORE recording completion in
`DoneLedger::batch_upsert`. This ordering ensures that a done-ledger entry
with `ScannedWithFindings` always has its findings already durable.

Currently this ordering is documented (in `persistence/mod.rs`) but not
mechanically enforced. A `PageCommit` coordinator trait would enforce the
write ordering at the type level.

## Current State

- `persistence/mod.rs:22-27` documents the cross-trait ordering contract.
- No coordinator trait exists. Callers must manually call `FindingsSink`
  before `DoneLedger`.

## Desired State

A `PageCommit` (or similar) trait that:
1. Accepts both findings and done-ledger records for a single page/batch.
2. Enforces the correct write ordering internally.
3. Provides atomicity guarantees (all-or-nothing for the combined write).

## Implementation Guidance

- New file: `persistence/page_commit.rs` (or extend `mod.rs`).
- The trait should compose `FindingsSink` and `DoneLedger` rather than
  replacing them.
- Consider whether the coordinator owns a transaction or delegates to
  the backend's native transaction mechanism.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `PageCommit` trait defined with documented ordering guarantees
- [ ] Module docs updated to reference the new trait
- [ ] cargo fmt/check/clippy/test pass
close_reason: Superseded: PageCommit<S> typestate machine was already implemented in gossip-8951.2 (A2). The trait-level ordering enforcement described in this task is exactly what PageCommit<S> provides — findings -> done-ledger -> checkpoint ordering enforced at compile time via typestate markers (AwaitingFindings -> FindingsDurable -> ItemDurable -> CheckpointDurable).

title: Fix rank-fallback skew after byte-axis compaction in StreamingSplitEstimator
description:
## Context

Code review of `StreamingSplitEstimator` identified that the rank-based fallback
in `estimate_split_key` is weaker than the code and documentation suggest. When
the byte-weighted candidate lands on the first key (triggering the "avoid
degenerate first-item split" guard), the estimator falls back to searching the
retained samples on the rank axis. However, those samples were compacted on the
**byte axis**, so in streams with long flat byte plateaus the rank distribution
of retained samples becomes very skewed. The "rank fallback" can end up nowhere
near the actual midpoint rank.

This is not cosmetic — the code comment at line 498-502 promises midpoint-like
behavior for front-loaded streams, but the current single-sketch compaction
strategy undercuts that promise.

## Current State

When `estimate_split_key` detects the byte-weighted candidate is the first key,
it falls back to a rank-axis nearest-sample search on the same `self.samples`
vector that was compacted on the byte axis:

```rust
// crates/gossip-connectors/src/split_estimator.rs:503-531
pub(crate) fn estimate_split_key(&self) -> Option<&[u8]> {
    // ...
    let target_weight = self.total_bytes / 2;
    let candidate = Self::nearest_sample(&self.samples, SampleAxis::Bytes, target_weight)
        .or_else(|| Self::nearest_sample(&self.samples, SampleAxis::Rank, rank_target))?;

    // Keep split semantics aligned with existing connectors: avoid
    // degenerate "first item" splits when weight is front-loaded.
    if self
        .first_observed_key
        .as_ref()
        .is_some_and(|first| candidate == first.as_ref())
    {
        return Self::nearest_sample(&self.samples, SampleAxis::Rank, rank_target);
    }
    Some(candidate)
}
```

The compaction axis is chosen by `preferred_axis` (line 291), which picks
`SampleAxis::Bytes` whenever the first and last byte positions differ:

```rust
// crates/gossip-connectors/src/split_estimator.rs:291-299
fn preferred_axis(samples: &[Sample]) -> SampleAxis {
    let first = samples.first().expect("non-empty samples");
    let last = samples.last().expect("non-empty samples");
    if first.cumulative_bytes != last.cumulative_bytes {
        SampleAxis::Bytes
    } else {
        SampleAxis::Rank
    }
}
```

In a stream like: 1 huge file, then 10000 zero-byte files — the byte range is
non-degenerate (first=0, last=huge), so compaction uses the byte axis. But
after compaction most retained samples cluster near byte position 0 (the huge
file), with very few samples in the zero-byte tail. A rank-axis search on this
set will find its "nearest" sample far from the true rank midpoint.

## Desired State

The rank fallback should land near the true rank midpoint regardless of how
byte-axis compaction distributed the retained samples.

### Approach options (choose one)

**Option A — Plateau-aware compaction (minimal fix)**:
During `selected_sample_indices`, when the interpolated target falls inside an
equal-byte-position run, space interior picks by **rank** within the plateau
rather than collapsing them. This preserves rank diversity in flat regions
without adding a second data structure.

**Option B — Dual-sketch design (structural fix)**:
Maintain two independent sample sketches sharing a total memory budget:
one compacted on the byte axis, one on the rank axis. `estimate_split_key`
uses the byte-sketch for byte search and the rank-sketch for rank fallback.
Easier to reason about, but doubles the bookkeeping.

Option A is recommended as the first step since it is lower risk and does not
change the memory model. Option B can follow if accuracy requirements tighten.

## Implementation Guidance

### Files to Modify

| File | Change | Rationale |
|------|--------|-----------|
| `crates/gossip-connectors/src/split_estimator.rs` | Add plateau-aware spacing in `selected_sample_indices` (Option A) | Preserve rank diversity in flat byte runs |
| `crates/gossip-connectors/src/split_estimator_tests.rs` | Add regression test for front-loaded zero-tail fallback | Pin the fix |

### Patterns to Follow

The `selected_sample_indices` function already has axis-generic code. For Option A,
detect when multiple consecutive samples share the same axis position and
distribute picks among them by rank spacing instead. This can be done as a
local sub-loop within the main selection loop.

### Utilities to Reuse

| Utility | Location | Purpose |
|---------|----------|---------|
| `interpolated_position` | `split_estimator.rs:310` | Already used for target computation; can be reused for rank-space sub-interpolation within plateaus |
| `SampleAxis` | `split_estimator.rs:94` | Axis-generic position access |

### Blast Radius

Changes are internal to the compaction algorithm. No public API changes.
The `estimate_split_key` function itself does not need modification — the
improvement comes from better sample retention.

## Code References

```rust
// crates/gossip-connectors/src/split_estimator.rs:244-278 — main selection loop
for i in 0..cap {
    let target = interpolated_position(first, last, i, cap);
    while cursor + 1 < len && samples[cursor + 1].position(axis) < target {
        cursor += 1;
    }
    let mut pick = if cursor + 1 < len {
        let next = cursor + 1;
        let d_curr = samples[cursor].position(axis).abs_diff(target);
        let d_next = samples[next].position(axis).abs_diff(target);
        if d_next < d_curr { next } else { cursor }
    } else {
        cursor
    };
    // ... forward-progress and room constraints ...
}
```

```rust
// crates/gossip-connectors/src/split_estimator.rs:520-528 — rank fallback path
if self
    .first_observed_key
    .as_ref()
    .is_some_and(|first| candidate == first.as_ref())
{
    return Self::nearest_sample(&self.samples, SampleAxis::Rank, rank_target);
}
```

## Testing Strategy

Add a targeted regression test:

**`front_loaded_zero_tail_fallback_stays_near_rank_midpoint_after_compaction`**:
Feed a stream with 1 large file followed by N zero-byte files (N >> sample_cap,
so compaction fires). Trigger the first-key guard fallback. Assert the returned
split key is within a bounded distance of the true rank midpoint (e.g., within

title: Rename cumulative_bytes to recorded_byte_position and preferred_axis to compaction_axis
description:
## Context

Code review identified two naming issues in `split_estimator.rs` that create
unnecessary cognitive load when reasoning about the code:

1. **`cumulative_bytes` field name is misleading**: The field on `Sample`
   (line 117) is not always "cumulative bytes at this key." For byte-triggered
   samples it is the exact stride mark the file straddles; for rank-triggered
   samples it is the file's start position. The current name makes it harder
   to reason about what the value actually represents.

2. **`preferred_axis` function name is too broad**: The function (line 291) is
   only used for compaction/selection in `selected_sample_indices` (line 231),
   but the name suggests it governs all search decisions. Meanwhile,
   `estimate_split_key` (line 512) hard-codes byte search regardless of this
   function's return value. The naming muddies the relationship between
   compaction axis selection and estimation axis selection.

## Current State

### `cumulative_bytes`

```rust
// crates/gossip-connectors/src/split_estimator.rs:113-123
struct Sample {
    rank: u64,
    /// Cumulative byte position at which this sample was recorded.
    ///
    /// When sampled by the byte-stride trigger this is the exact byte-stride
    /// mark that the file straddles; otherwise it is the cumulative byte total
    /// at the start of the file (a rank-triggered fallback position).
    cumulative_bytes: u64,
    key: Box<[u8]>,
}
```

The doc comment correctly describes the dual meaning, but the field name
`cumulative_bytes` only reflects one of the two cases. Every reader has to
remember that "cumulative" is sometimes a misnomer.

### `preferred_axis`

```rust
// crates/gossip-connectors/src/split_estimator.rs:291-299
/// Choose the compaction/search axis: bytes when the range is non-degenerate,
/// rank otherwise.
fn preferred_axis(samples: &[Sample]) -> SampleAxis {
    let first = samples.first().expect("non-empty samples");
    let last = samples.last().expect("non-empty samples");
    if first.cumulative_bytes != last.cumulative_bytes {
        SampleAxis::Bytes
    } else {
        SampleAxis::Rank
    }
}
```

The doc says "compaction/search axis" but `estimate_split_key` does not use
this function — it always searches on `SampleAxis::Bytes` first (line 517),
falling back to `SampleAxis::Rank` (line 518/527). The "search" part of the
doc is misleading.

## Desired State

1. Rename `cumulative_bytes` to `recorded_byte_position` (or
   `sample_byte_position`). This accurately describes what the field stores
   without implying it is always a cumulative total.

2. Rename `preferred_axis` to `compaction_axis`. Update its doc comment to
   clarify it governs compaction spacing only, not estimation search.

3. Update all references, doc comments, and test assertions that mention the
   old names.

## Implementation Guidance

### Files to Modify

| File | Change | Rationale |
|------|--------|-----------|
| `crates/gossip-connectors/src/split_estimator.rs` | Rename `cumulative_bytes` field to `recorded_byte_position` | Accurate naming |
| `crates/gossip-connectors/src/split_estimator.rs` | Rename `preferred_axis` to `compaction_axis`, update doc | Scope clarity |
| `crates/gossip-connectors/src/split_estimator_tests.rs` | Update references to `cumulative_bytes` in debug view assertions | Keep tests aligned |

### Patterns to Follow

Use IDE-style rename (or `replaceAll` in edit tool) to catch all occurrences.
The field is accessed in:
- `Sample::new` (line 158)
- `Sample::position` (line 170)
- `Sample::fmt` Debug impl (line 150)
- `preferred_axis` / `compaction_axis` (line 294)
- `sample_debug_view` (line 599)
- Test assertions checking debug view tuples

### Blast Radius

Both names are `pub(crate)` or private. No cross-crate API changes. The
`sample_debug_view` test helper returns tuples `(rank, cumulative_bytes, key)`;
callers in tests access `.1` positionally so the field rename itself does not
break them, but any comments or variable names referencing `cumulative_bytes`
should be updated.

## Code References

```rust
// crates/gossip-connectors/src/split_estimator.rs:167-173 — position() uses the field
fn position(&self, axis: SampleAxis) -> u64 {
    match axis {
        SampleAxis::Rank => self.rank,
        SampleAxis::Bytes => self.cumulative_bytes,
    }
}
```

```rust
// crates/gossip-connectors/src/split_estimator_tests.rs:54-63 — test helper uses the field
fn assert_samples_sorted(estimator: &StreamingSplitEstimator) {
    let samples = estimator.sample_debug_view();
    // ...
    assert!(
        samples.windows(2).all(|window| window[0].1 <= window[1].1),
        "sample byte positions must remain non-decreasing: {samples:?}"
    );
}
```

## Related Work

| Task ID | Title | Relationship |
|---------|-------|-------------|
| gossip-8942 | Fix semantic mismatch in byte-sample doc comment (closed) | relates-to — prior doc fix for the same field |
| gossip-8945 | Migrate sample keys to ByteSlab | relates-to — that task will also touch Sample fields; coordinate naming |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `cumulative_bytes` renamed to `recorded_byte_position` everywhere
- [ ] `preferred_axis` renamed to `compaction_axis` with updated doc comment
- [ ] All doc comments referencing the old names are updated
- [ ] All existing tests pass: `cargo test -p gossip-connectors`
- [ ] `cargo fmt --all && cargo check && cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`
- [ ] `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps --all-features` passes

## Pointers

- `Sample` struct: `split_estimator.rs:112-123`
- `preferred_axis`: `split_estimator.rs:291-299`
- `estimate_split_key` hard-coded byte search: `split_estimator.rs:512-518`
- Prior doc fix: `gossip-8942`

title: Extract in-memory persistence backends from gossip-contracts into gossip-persistence-inmemory crate
description:
## Context

The `gossip-contracts` crate should contain only API surface: traits, types, and contracts. Currently it also houses ~1500 lines of concrete in-memory persistence implementations (`InMemoryDoneLedger`, `InMemoryFindingsSink`, their commit handles, error types, and fault injection machinery) behind a `#[cfg(any(test, feature = "test-support"))]` gate.

This violates the boundary principle that contracts define APIs and implementations live in their own crates. The coordination side already follows the correct pattern — `gossip-coordination/src/in_memory.rs` lives in the implementation crate, not in `gossip-contracts`.

With Postgres, ScyllaDB, and etcd backends planned, the in-memory persistence backends should be a peer crate alongside those production backends, not embedded in the contracts crate.

## Current State

In-memory persistence implementations live in `gossip-contracts`:
- `crates/gossip-contracts/src/persistence/in_memory.rs` (~1550 lines)
- `crates/gossip-contracts/src/persistence/in_memory_tests.rs`
- Feature-gated behind `test-support` in `crates/gossip-contracts/Cargo.toml:14`
- Re-exported from `crates/gossip-contracts/src/persistence/mod.rs:90-94`

Public types that need to move:
- `InMemoryDoneLedger` (implements `DoneLedger` trait)
- `InMemoryFindingsSink` (implements `FindingsSink` trait)
- `InMemoryDoneLedgerHandle` (implements `CommitHandle`)
- `InMemoryFindingsHandle` (implements `CommitHandle`)
- `InMemoryPersistenceError`
- `InMemoryStoreKind`
- `CompletionOrder`
- `PendingWriteId`

No downstream crates currently import these types — only `gossip-contracts` own tests use them. This makes the move low-risk if done now. Delay increases migration cost as downstream consumers start depending on the `test-support` re-exports.

The `test-support` feature on `gossip-contracts` also gates `test_util` (proptest strategies) and some coordination helpers — those stay.

## Desired State

A new workspace member `crates/gossip-persistence-inmemory` that:
1. Depends on `gossip-contracts` for trait definitions (`DoneLedger`, `FindingsSink`, `CommitHandle`, record types)
2. Contains the full in-memory implementation currently in `gossip-contracts/src/persistence/in_memory.rs`
3. Contains the tests currently in `gossip-contracts/src/persistence/in_memory_tests.rs`
4. Exports all public types currently re-exported from `gossip-contracts::persistence` under the `test-support` gate
5. Implements `FindingsConformanceProbe` (from A5 conformance harness) when that trait exists

The `gossip-contracts` crate:
1. Removes `in_memory.rs` and `in_memory_tests.rs`
2. Removes the in-memory re-exports from `persistence/mod.rs:90-94`
3. Keeps the `test-support` feature for proptest strategies and other test utilities
4. Keeps the conformance harness (`conformance.rs`) since that defines contract surface

Crate naming follows the planned backend structure:
- `gossip-persistence-inmemory` — reference/test backends (this task)
- `gossip-persistence-postgres` — future Postgres done-ledger + findings
- `gossip-persistence-scylla` — future ScyllaDB done-ledger
- `gossip-coordination-etcd` — future etcd coordination backend

## Implementation Guidance

### Files to Create

| File | Contents |
|------|----------|
| `crates/gossip-persistence-inmemory/Cargo.toml` | Workspace member, depends on `gossip-contracts` |
| `crates/gossip-persistence-inmemory/src/lib.rs` | Module root with re-exports |
| `crates/gossip-persistence-inmemory/src/done_ledger.rs` | `InMemoryDoneLedger` + handle + merge logic (extracted from `in_memory.rs:316-855`) |
| `crates/gossip-persistence-inmemory/src/findings.rs` | `InMemoryFindingsSink` + handle + apply logic (extracted from `in_memory.rs:857-end`) |
| `crates/gossip-persistence-inmemory/src/error.rs` | `InMemoryPersistenceError`, `InMemoryStoreKind`, `CompletionOrder`, `PendingWriteId` (extracted from `in_memory.rs:73-286`) |
| `crates/gossip-persistence-inmemory/src/pending.rs` | Shared `PendingState<R>`, `PendingOp<P, R>` internals (extracted from `in_memory.rs:288-314`) |

### Files to Modify

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `crates/gossip-contracts/src/persistence/mod.rs` | Remove `#[cfg(any(test, feature = "test-support"))] mod in_memory;` and corresponding re-exports |
| `crates/gossip-contracts/src/persistence/in_memory.rs` | Delete (moved to new crate) |
| `crates/gossip-contracts/src/persistence/in_memory_tests.rs` | Delete (moved to new crate) |
| `Cargo.toml` (workspace root) | Add `gossip-persistence-inmemory` to workspace members |

### Files to Update in Downstream (if any future consumers exist)

Any crate that currently enables `gossip-contracts/test-support` for the in-memory types would instead add `gossip-persistence-inmemory` as a dev-dependency. Currently no downstream crate imports these types, so this is a no-op today.

### Patterns to Follow

The coordination boundary already follows this pattern:
- Traits defined in `gossip-contracts::coordination` (`CoordinationBackend`, `RunManagement`)
- In-memory implementation in `gossip-coordination::in_memory` (separate crate)
- Production backend would be `gossip-coordination-etcd` (another separate crate)

### Considerations

- The `PendingState<R>` and `PendingOp<P, R>` internal types are shared between done-ledger and findings backends. Consider a shared `pending.rs` module in the new crate.
- The `validate_batch_tenant_consistency` function (`in_memory.rs:1303-1336`) is backend-specific validation. Move it with the findings impl.
- The `merge_done_ledger_records` function (`in_memory.rs:819-855`) encodes lattice merge semantics. This is arguably a contract concern (it uses `DoneLedgerStatus::merge`), but the implementation is backend-specific. Move it with the done-ledger impl.

## Code References

- Current in-memory module: `crates/gossip-contracts/src/persistence/in_memory.rs:1-1550`
- Current tests: `crates/gossip-contracts/src/persistence/in_memory_tests.rs`
- Module gating: `crates/gossip-contracts/src/persistence/mod.rs:66-67, 90-94`
- Feature flag: `crates/gossip-contracts/Cargo.toml:14`
- Coordination pattern to follow: `crates/gossip-coordination/src/in_memory.rs` (3320 lines, lives in impl crate)
- Trait definitions: `crates/gossip-contracts/src/persistence/done_ledger.rs`, `findings.rs`, `commit.rs`

## Related Work

| Task ID | Title | Relationship |
|---------|-------|-------------|
| gossip-8951 | Boundary 5 — Persistence epic | Parent epic (description needs update) |
| gossip-8951.4 | A4 — In-memory reference implementations | Closed task that created the code being moved |
| gossip-8951.5 | A5 — Conformance test harness | Open task that references modifying in_memory.rs in contracts (needs update) |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `crates/gossip-persistence-inmemory/` exists as a workspace member
- [ ] All in-memory persistence types (`InMemoryDoneLedger`, `InMemoryFindingsSink`, handles, errors) are exported from the new crate
- [ ] `crates/gossip-contracts/src/persistence/in_memory.rs` is deleted
- [ ] `crates/gossip-contracts/src/persistence/in_memory_tests.rs` is deleted
- [ ] `gossip-contracts::persistence` mod.rs no longer has any `#[cfg(test-support)]` module or re-exports for in-memory types
- [ ] All existing in-memory persistence tests pass from the new crate
- [ ] `gossip-contracts` `test-support` feature still works for proptest strategies and other test utilities
- [ ] `cargo fmt --all && cargo check && cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`
- [ ] `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps --all-features`

## Pointers

- In-memory implementation: `crates/gossip-contracts/src/persistence/in_memory.rs`
- Tests: `crates/gossip-contracts/src/persistence/in_memory_tests.rs`
- Trait definitions: `crates/gossip-contracts/src/persistence/{done_ledger,findings,commit}.rs`
- Coordination pattern: `crates/gossip-coordination/src/in_memory.rs`
- Feature flag: `crates/gossip-contracts/Cargo.toml:14`
