title: B0 — Create crate gossip-coordination-etcd
description:
## Context

This is the first subtask of Epic B (gossip-8968) — the etcd coordination persistence backend. B0 creates the `gossip-coordination-etcd` workspace crate, wires up a real etcd client connection, and exposes the final `EtcdCoordinator` backend type that implements `CoordinationBackend`, `RunManagement`, **and `ShardClaiming`**. The scope is intentionally narrow: prove connectivity and establish the crate structure. Real etcd persistence arrives in B1/B2.

During B0, all protocol semantics delegate to `InMemoryCoordinator` so the crate builds and can be wired into tests without lying about durability guarantees. This is a temporary bootstrap — B1 adds the keyspace/codec, and B2 replaces the delegation with real etcd transactions.

## Current State

No `gossip-coordination-etcd` crate exists. The coordination trait surface is stable in `gossip-coordination`:

```rust
// crates/gossip-coordination/src/facade.rs:457
pub trait CoordinationFacade: CoordinationBackend + RunManagement + ShardClaiming {}
```

The `InMemoryCoordinator` provides an executable reference backend:

```rust
// crates/gossip-coordination/src/in_memory.rs:532-543
pub struct InMemoryCoordinator {
    pub(crate) shards: AHashMap<TenantId, AHashMap<ShardKey, ShardRecord>>,
    pub(crate) total_shard_count: usize,
    pub(crate) runs: AHashMap<(TenantId, RunId), RunRecord>,
    pub(crate) run_shards: AHashMap<(TenantId, RunId), HashSet<ShardId, ahash::RandomState>>,
    pub(crate) default_lease_duration: u64,
    pub(crate) max_shards_per_tenant: usize,
    pub(crate) max_total_shards: usize,
    pub(crate) claim_cooldowns: AHashMap<WorkerId, LogicalTime>,
    pub(crate) claim_cooldown_interval: u64,
    pub(crate) slab: ByteSlab,
    pub(crate) claim_candidates_scratch: Vec<ShardId>,
}
```

Constructor: `InMemoryCoordinator::new(default_lease_duration: u64) -> Self` at `in_memory.rs:619`.

Reference implementation artifacts exist at `tmp/gossip-project-artifacts/b5_persistence/phase2/b0/`.

## Desired State

A new workspace member `crates/gossip-coordination-etcd` that:
1. Owns a live `etcd_client::Client` connection
2. Exposes `EtcdCoordinator` as the final backend type
3. Implements `CoordinationBackend`, `RunManagement`, **and `ShardClaiming`** (all delegating to `InMemoryCoordinator` until B1/B2)
4. Validates configuration (endpoints, namespace prefix)
5. Proves connectivity with a `status()` smoke test against a local etcd

## Implementation Guidance

### Files to Create
| File | Content | Rationale |
|------|---------|-----------|
| `crates/gossip-coordination-etcd/Cargo.toml` | Crate manifest with `gossip-coordination`, `etcd-client`, `tokio` deps | Workspace member |
| `crates/gossip-coordination-etcd/src/lib.rs` | Module declarations, `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`, re-exports | Crate root |
| `crates/gossip-coordination-etcd/src/backend.rs` | `EtcdCoordinator` struct, `CoordinationBackend` + `RunManagement` + `ShardClaiming` impls delegating to `InMemoryCoordinator` | Core type |
| `crates/gossip-coordination-etcd/src/config.rs` | `EtcdCoordinatorConfig` with endpoint/prefix validation | Configuration |
| `crates/gossip-coordination-etcd/src/error.rs` | `EtcdCoordinatorError`, `EtcdOperation` enum | Error types |
| `crates/gossip-coordination-etcd/src/runtime.rs` | `SyncRuntime` — private current-thread tokio runtime for sync/async bridge | Async bridge |
| `crates/gossip-coordination-etcd/src/tests.rs` | Config validation tests + ignored etcd connectivity smoke test | Testing |

### Files to Modify
| File | Change | Rationale |
|------|--------|-----------|
| `Cargo.toml` (root) | Add `gossip-coordination-etcd` to workspace members and workspace.dependencies | Workspace registration |

### Patterns to Follow

The `EtcdCoordinator` struct follows the same pattern as `InMemoryCoordinator`:

```rust
// tmp/gossip-project-artifacts/b5_persistence/phase2/b0/backend.rs:57-62
pub struct EtcdCoordinator {
    config: EtcdCoordinatorConfig,
    runtime: SyncRuntime,
    client: etcd_client::Client,
    protocol_delegate: InMemoryCoordinator,
    claim_candidates_scratch: Vec<ShardId>,  // REQUIRED for ShardClaiming delegation
}
```

**IMPORTANT — `ShardClaiming` implementation**: There is **no blanket impl** for `ShardClaiming` (confirmed at `facade.rs:422`). You must implement it explicitly. Delegate to the free function `default_claim_next_available`:

```rust
// crates/gossip-coordination/src/facade.rs:237-346
pub fn default_claim_next_available<'a, B: CoordinationBackend + RunManagement>(
    backend: &mut B,
    now: LogicalTime,
    tenant: TenantId,
    run: RunId,
    worker: WorkerId,
    out: &'a mut AcquireScratch,
    candidates: &mut Vec<ShardId>,  // caller-owned scratch
) -> Result<AcquireResultView<'a>, ClaimError>
```

The `ShardClaiming` impl pattern (follow InMemoryCoordinator's approach):

```rust
impl ShardClaiming for EtcdCoordinator {
    fn claim_next_available<'a>(
        &mut self,
        now: LogicalTime,
        tenant: TenantId,
        run: RunId,
        worker: WorkerId,
        out: &'a mut AcquireScratch,
    ) -> Result<AcquireResultView<'a>, ClaimError> {
        // Since we're delegating, forward to the protocol_delegate.
        // The delegate already has its own claim_candidates_scratch.
        self.protocol_delegate.claim_next_available(now, tenant, run, worker, out)
    }
}
```

Alternatively, if the delegated InMemoryCoordinator already implements ShardClaiming, just forward the call directly.

The sync/async bridge uses a private current-thread tokio runtime:

```rust
// tmp/gossip-project-artifacts/b5_persistence/phase2/b0/runtime.rs:12-30
pub(crate) struct SyncRuntime {
    inner: tokio::runtime::Runtime,
}
impl SyncRuntime {
    pub(crate) fn new() -> Result<Self, EtcdCoordinatorError> {
        let inner = tokio::runtime::Builder::new_current_thread()
            .enable_all()
            .build()
            .map_err(EtcdCoordinatorError::RuntimeBuild)?;
        Ok(Self { inner })
    }
    pub(crate) fn block_on<F>(&self, future: F) -> F::Output
    where F: Future { self.inner.block_on(future) }
}
```

Configuration validates endpoints and namespace prefix:

```rust
// tmp/gossip-project-artifacts/b5_persistence/phase2/b0/config.rs:19-23
pub struct EtcdCoordinatorConfig {
    endpoints: Vec<String>,
    namespace_prefix: String,
}
```

### Cargo.toml Dependencies

**IMPORTANT**: Use `etcd-client` version `0.18` (latest on crates.io). The B1/B2 artifacts reference `0.14` — this is stale. The `connect` API is identical between 0.14 and 0.18. Use `default-features = false` to avoid pulling in OpenSSL (etcd-client's default feature enables TLS via `tls` feature which pulls `openssl`).

```toml
[package]
name = "gossip-coordination-etcd"
version = "0.1.0"
edition.workspace = true
rust-version.workspace = true

[dependencies]
gossip-coordination.workspace = true
etcd-client = { version = "0.18", default-features = false }
tokio = { version = "1", features = ["rt", "time", "sync", "net"] }

[dev-dependencies]
gossip-coordination = { workspace = true, features = ["test-support"] }

[features]
test-support = ["gossip-coordination/test-support"]
```

The `test-support` feature gates test helpers that depend on `gossip-coordination/test-support` (which provides test construction helpers for `ShardRecord`, `RunRecord`, etc.). Integration tests use this for building sample records.

Tokio features are scoped to `["rt", "time", "sync", "net"]` rather than `["full"]` to minimize compile dependencies. These are the minimal features needed for the sync runtime bridge and etcd client.

### Utilities to Reuse
| Utility | Location | How to Reuse |
|---------|----------|-------------|
| `InMemoryCoordinator` | `gossip-coordination/src/in_memory.rs:532` | B0 delegation target — all trait methods forward to this |

| `default_claim_next_available` | `gossip-coordination/src/facade.rs:237` | ShardClaiming delegation helper |

title: B1 — etcd keyspace + versioned serialization
description:
## Context

This is the second subtask of Epic B (gossip-8968). B0 established the crate scaffold and etcd connectivity. B1 adds the two pillars that B2's real etcd persistence needs: a deterministic key layout (keyspace) and versioned record codecs. Without these, B2 cannot build/locate/encode/decode records in etcd.

The key layout defines where every coordination entity lives in etcd's key-value space. The codec provides explicit, deterministic, versioned serialization — not serde-derived, not protobuf, but hand-written binary encoding with a `v1` version prefix for forward compatibility.

## Current State

After B0 (gossip-8968.1), `gossip-coordination-etcd` exists as a workspace member with:
- `EtcdCoordinator` struct with live etcd client connection
- `CoordinationBackend` + `RunManagement` + `ShardClaiming` delegating to `InMemoryCoordinator`
- Configuration, error types, sync/async bridge

No keyspace or codec modules exist. The crate has no understanding of how records map to etcd keys or how records are serialized.

```rust
// crates/gossip-coordination-etcd/src/lib.rs (after B0)
mod backend;
mod config;
mod error;
mod runtime;
pub use backend::{EtcdCoordinator, EtcdEndpointStatus};
pub use config::{EtcdCoordinatorConfig, EtcdCoordinatorConfigError};
pub use error::{EtcdCoordinatorError, EtcdOperation};
```

## Desired State

Two new modules in `gossip-coordination-etcd`:

### 1. Keyspace Module (`keyspace.rs`)

A deterministic key builder producing ASCII etcd key paths:

```
{prefix}/tenants/{tenant_hex}/runs/{run_hex}                          -> RunRecord blob
{prefix}/tenants/{tenant_hex}/runs/{run_hex}/shards/{shard_hex}       -> ShardRecord blob
{prefix}/tenants/{tenant_hex}/runs/{run_hex}/shards/{shard_hex}/owner -> owner lease key
{prefix}/tenants/{tenant_hex}/runs_active/{run_hex}                   -> active-run index
{prefix}/tenants/{tenant_hex}/runs/{run_hex}/shards_active/{shard_hex} -> active-shard index
```

Key properties:
- `TenantId` = `[u8; 32]`, hex-encoded to 64 lowercase hex chars (via `TenantId::as_bytes()`)
- `RunId` = `u64`, zero-padded 16-digit lowercase hex (via `RunId::as_raw()`)
- `ShardId` = `u64`, zero-padded 16-digit lowercase hex (via `ShardId::as_raw()`)
- All keys are deterministic and prefix-scannable
- Active index keys enable efficient range queries for active runs/shards

**IMPORTANT — B2 dependency**: The keyspace must include a `shard_records_scan_prefix(tenant, run)` method that returns `{run_record_key}/shards/` (note trailing slash). This is critical because without the trailing slash, a prefix scan on `{run_record_key}/shards` would match both `/shards/{shard_hex}` (shard records) AND `/shards_active/{shard_hex}` (active indexes). B2's `scan_run_shards` method depends on this.

### 2. Codec Module (`codec.rs`)

Versioned blob encoding for `RunRecord` and `ShardRecord`:

- Every blob starts with `b"v1"` version prefix + 1-byte `BlobKind` tag
- Encoding is explicit and deterministic: hand-written `put_*`/`read_*` primitives for `u8`, `u32`, `u64`, `bool`, length-prefixed byte vectors, optional values
- All integers use **little-endian** encoding (`to_le_bytes` / `from_le_bytes`)
- Length prefixes use `u32` LE (via `put_len` / `read_len`)
- Owned intermediate types (`OwnedRunRecord`, `OwnedShardRecord`) bridge between the pooled runtime types and flat byte streams
- Invariant validation on decode: cross-field consistency checks reject corrupt blobs
- `ShardRecord` decode allocates pooled fields (`PooledShardSpec`, `PooledCursor`, `PooledSpawned`) into a caller-provided `ByteSlab`, with rollback on failure

### Updated Backend

`EtcdCoordinator` gains a `keyspace: EtcdKeyspace` field, constructed during `connect()`. Protocol semantics still delegate to `InMemoryCoordinator` — B2 will replace the delegation.

### Updated Dependencies

The crate adds `gossip-contracts` and `gossip-stdx` as dependencies (needed for identity types, `ByteSlab`, coordination types used by the codec).

## Implementation Guidance

### Files to Create
| File | Content | Rationale |
|------|---------|-----------|
| `crates/gossip-coordination-etcd/src/keyspace.rs` | `EtcdKeyspace` struct with key builder methods | Deterministic key layout |
| `crates/gossip-coordination-etcd/src/codec.rs` | `encode_run_record_v1`, `decode_run_record_v1`, `encode_shard_record_v1`, `decode_shard_record_v1`, `Decoder`, owned intermediate types | Versioned record encoding |

### Files to Modify
| File | Change | Rationale |
|------|--------|-----------|
| `crates/gossip-coordination-etcd/src/lib.rs` | Add `mod keyspace; mod codec;` and re-exports | Module registration |
| `crates/gossip-coordination-etcd/src/backend.rs` | Add `keyspace: EtcdKeyspace` field to `EtcdCoordinator`, construct in `connect()` | Backend gains keyspace awareness |
| `crates/gossip-coordination-etcd/src/error.rs` | Add `Keyspace(EtcdKeyspaceError)` variant, `From` impl | Error propagation |
| `crates/gossip-coordination-etcd/Cargo.toml` | Add `gossip-contracts.workspace = true`, `gossip-stdx.workspace = true`, update `test-support` feature | Codec dependencies |
| `crates/gossip-coordination-etcd/src/tests.rs` | Add keyspace path tests, round-trip codec tests | Testing |

### Patterns to Follow

**Keyspace hex encoding:**
```rust
// tmp/gossip-project-artifacts/b5_persistence/phase2/b1-artifacts/keyspace.rs:126-146
fn tenant_hex(tenant: TenantId) -> String { encode_hex(tenant.as_bytes()) }
fn run_hex(run: RunId) -> String { format!("{:016x}", run.as_raw()) }
fn shard_hex(shard: ShardId) -> String { format!("{:016x}", shard.as_raw()) }
fn encode_hex(bytes: &[u8]) -> String {
    const LUT: &[u8; 16] = b"0123456789abcdef";
    let mut out = String::with_capacity(bytes.len() * 2);
    for &b in bytes {
        out.push(LUT[(b >> 4) as usize] as char);
        out.push(LUT[(b & 0x0f) as usize] as char);
    }
    out
}
```

**Keyspace must include this method (missing from artifact, needed by B2):**
```rust
/// Scan prefix for all shard records under a run.
///
/// Returns `{run_record_key}/shards/` (with trailing slash) so prefix
/// queries do NOT accidentally match `shards_active/` keys.
pub fn shard_records_scan_prefix(&self, tenant: TenantId, run: RunId) -> String {
    format!("{}/", self.run_shards_prefix(tenant, run))
}
```

**Codec version header:**
```rust
const VERSION_PREFIX_V1: &[u8; 2] = b"v1";

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
#[repr(u8)]
pub enum BlobKind {
    RunRecord = 1,
    ShardRecord = 2,
}
```

### Codec Wire Format Specification

All blobs follow this structure: `[v1 prefix (2 bytes)] [BlobKind tag (1 byte)] [fields...]`

**Wire encoding primitives:**
| Type | Encoding | Size |
|------|----------|------|
| `u8` | raw byte | 1 |
| `bool` | `0x00` (false) or `0x01` (true), other values rejected | 1 |
| `u32` | little-endian 4 bytes | 4 |
| `u64` | little-endian 8 bytes | 8 |
| `TenantId` | raw 32 bytes (`as_bytes()`) | 32 |
| `Vec<u8>` / `&[u8]` | `u32 LE length` + `raw bytes` | 4 + len |
| `Option<Vec<u8>>` | `bool` presence flag + (if true) `u32 LE length` + `raw bytes` | 1 [+ 4 + len] |
| `Option<u64>` | `bool` presence flag + (if true) `u64 LE` | 1 [+ 8] |
| `Option<u32>` | `bool` presence flag + (if true) `u32 LE` | 1 [+ 4] |
| `Option<u8>` | `bool` presence flag + (if true) `u8` | 1 [+ 1] |

**RunRecord v1 field order:**
1. `tenant: TenantId` (32 bytes)
2. `run: RunId` (u64 LE)
3. `cursor_semantics: CursorSemantics` (u8)
4. `lease_duration: u64` (u64 LE, from `config.lease_duration.get()`)
5. `max_shard_retries: Option<u32>` (bool + u32 LE)
6. `status: RunStatus` (u8)
7. `created_at: LogicalTime` (u64 LE)
8. `completed_at: Option<u64>` (bool + u64 LE)
9. `root_shards: Vec<ShardId>` — `u32 LE count` + `count * u64 LE`
10. `op_log: Vec<RunOpLogEntry>` — `u32 LE count` + `count * entry`

**RunOpLogEntry field order (per entry):**
1. `op_id: OpId` (u64 LE)
2. `kind: RunOpKind` (u8)
3. `payload_hash: u64` (u64 LE)
4. `executed_at: LogicalTime` (u64 LE)
5. `result: RunOpResult` — tag byte + fields:
   - Tag `1` = `RegisteredShards`: `u32 LE count` + `count * u64 LE (ShardId)`
   - Tag `2` = `Ack`: no additional bytes

**ShardRecord v1 field order:**
1. `tenant: TenantId` (32 bytes)
2. `run: RunId` (u64 LE)
3. `shard: ShardId` (u64 LE)
4. `status: ShardStatus` (u8)
5. `park_reason: Option<u8>` (bool + u8 ParkReason)
6. `key_range_start: Vec<u8>` (len-prefixed)
7. `key_range_end: Vec<u8>` (len-prefixed)
8. `metadata: Vec<u8>` (len-prefixed)
9. `cursor_last_key: Option<Vec<u8>>` (bool + len-prefixed)
10. `cursor_token: Option<Vec<u8>>` (bool + len-prefixed)
11. `cursor_semantics: CursorSemantics` (u8)
12. `lease_owner: Option<u64>` (bool + u64 LE WorkerId)
13. `lease_deadline: Option<u64>` (bool + u64 LE LogicalTime)
14. `fence_epoch: FenceEpoch` (u64 LE)
15. `parent: Option<u64>` (bool + u64 LE ShardId)
16. `spawned: Vec<ShardId>` — `u32 LE count` + `count * u64 LE`
17. `op_log: Vec<OpLogEntry>` — `u32 LE count` + `count * entry`

**OpLogEntry field order (per entry):**
1. `op_id: OpId` (u64 LE)
2. `kind: OpKind` (u8)
3. `result: OpResult` (u8)
4. `payload_hash: u64` (u64 LE)
5. `executed_at: LogicalTime` (u64 LE)

### All Enum Variants and Tags (Complete)

The codec must encode/decode every variant. Here are the complete `repr(u8)` tags:

**`CursorSemantics`** (`gossip-contracts/src/coordination/shard_spec.rs:72`):
- `Completed = 0` — cursor marks last completed item
- `Dispatched = 1` — cursor marks last dispatched item

**`ShardStatus`** (`gossip-coordination/src/record.rs:99`):
- `Active = 0` — may be acquired by a worker
- `Done = 1` — completed successfully (terminal)
- `Split = 2` — replaced by children (terminal)
- `Parked = 3` — halted due to error (terminal)

**`RunStatus`** (`gossip-coordination/src/run.rs:84`):
- `Initializing = 0` — being set up, no shards yet
- `Active = 1` — shards being processed
- `Done = 2` — all shards completed (terminal)
- `Failed = 3` — some shards parked (terminal)
- `Cancelled = 4` — administratively cancelled (terminal)

**`ParkReason`** (`gossip-coordination/src/record.rs:181`):
- `PermissionDenied = 0`
- `NotFound = 1`
- `Poisoned = 2`
- `TooManyErrors = 3`
- `Other = 4`

**`OpKind`** (`gossip-coordination/src/lease.rs:352`):
- `Checkpoint = 0`
- `Complete = 1`
- `Park = 2`
- `SplitReplace = 3`
- `SplitResidual = 4`
- `Unpark = 5`

**`OpResult`** (`gossip-coordination/src/lease.rs:499`):
- `Completed = 0`
- `Error = 1`
- `Superseded = 2`

**`RunOpKind`** (`gossip-coordination/src/run.rs:276`):
- `RegisterShards = 0`
- `CompleteRun = 1`
- `FailRun = 2`
- `CancelRun = 3`

**`RunOpResult`** (`gossip-coordination/src/run.rs:334`) — NOT `repr(u8)`, use manual tags:
- Tag `1` = `RegisteredShards { shard_ids: Box<[ShardId]> }` — encode as u32 count + shard IDs
- Tag `2` = `Ack` — no payload

### Owned Intermediate Types

The codec needs these owned types to bridge pooled runtime types and flat bytes:

**`OwnedRunRecord`** — fields: `tenant`, `run`, `cursor_semantics`, `lease_duration` (u64), `max_shard_retries` (Option<u32>), `status`, `created_at`, `completed_at`, `root_shards` (Vec<ShardId>), `op_log` (Vec<OwnedRunOpLogEntry>)

**`OwnedRunOpLogEntry`** — fields: `op_id`, `kind` (RunOpKind), `payload_hash`, `executed_at`, `result` (OwnedRunOpResult)

**`OwnedRunOpResult`** — enum: `RegisteredShards { shard_ids: Vec<ShardId> }` (tag=1), `Ack` (tag=2)

**`OwnedShardRecord`** — fields: `tenant`, `run`, `shard`, `status`, `park_reason`, `key_range_start` (Vec<u8>), `key_range_end` (Vec<u8>), `metadata` (Vec<u8>), `cursor_last_key` (Option<Vec<u8>>), `cursor_token` (Option<Vec<u8>>), `cursor_semantics`, `lease_owner` (Option<u64>), `lease_deadline` (Option<u64>), `fence_epoch`, `parent` (Option<ShardId>), `spawned` (Vec<ShardId>), `op_log` (Vec<OwnedShardOpLogEntry>)

**`OwnedShardOpLogEntry`** — fields: `op_id`, `kind` (OpKind), `result` (OpResult), `payload_hash`, `executed_at`

### Key Constants for Validation

The codec validation must reference these constants:

| Constant | Value | Location |
|----------|-------|----------|
| `ShardRecord::OP_LOG_CAP` | 16 | `gossip-coordination/src/record.rs` |
| `RunRecord::OP_LOG_CAP` | 8 | `gossip-coordination/src/run.rs` |
| `MAX_KEY_SIZE` | 4096 | `gossip-contracts/src/coordination/cursor.rs:39` |
| `MAX_TOKEN_SIZE` | 16384 | `gossip-contracts/src/coordination/cursor.rs:42` |
| `MAX_METADATA_SIZE` | defined in `gossip-contracts/src/coordination/shard_spec.rs` |
| `MAX_SPAWNED_PER_SHARD` | defined in `gossip-contracts/src/coordination/split.rs` |

### Codec Invariant Validation (on decode)

**RunRecord validation rules:**
1. `created_at > LogicalTime::ZERO`
2. `lease_duration > 0`
3. Active run MUST have non-empty `root_shards`
4. Initializing run MUST have empty `root_shards`
5. `completed_at.is_some()` iff `status.is_terminal()`
6. If present, `completed_at >= created_at`
7. `op_log.len() <= RunRecord::OP_LOG_CAP` (8)
8. No duplicate `ShardId` in `root_shards`
9. No duplicate `OpId` in `op_log`
10. Timestamps in op_log must be non-decreasing
11. `RegisterShards` entries must have `RegisteredShards` result; others must have `Ack`
12. Each entry: `payload_hash != 0`, `executed_at > ZERO`

**ShardRecord validation rules:**
1. Parked shards MUST have `park_reason`; non-Parked MUST NOT
2. Terminal shards MUST NOT have a lease
3. Lease `owner` and `deadline` must be both-present or both-absent
4. If present, lease `deadline > LogicalTime::ZERO`
5. `fence_epoch >= FenceEpoch::INITIAL` (i.e., >= 1)
6. Token requires last_key (can't have token without key)
7. Split shards MUST have non-empty `spawned`
8. `parent.is_some()` iff `shard.is_derived()` (bit 63 set)
9. Spawned children must be derived (`is_derived()` is true)
10. `op_log.len() <= ShardRecord::OP_LOG_CAP` (16)
11. `spawned.len() <= MAX_SPAWNED_PER_SHARD`
12. No duplicate `OpId` in `op_log`
13. Each entry: `payload_hash != 0`, `executed_at > ZERO`

### ShardRecord Decode with Slab Rollback

The `into_record` method on `OwnedShardRecord` allocates into ByteSlab with strict rollback on failure:

```rust
fn into_record(self, slab: &mut ByteSlab) -> Result<ShardRecord, EtcdCodecError> {
    let spec_ref = ShardSpecRef::new(&self.key_range_start, &self.key_range_end, &self.metadata);
    let pooled_spec = PooledShardSpec::from_spec_ref(spec_ref, slab)
        .map_err(|e| EtcdCodecError::SlabFull(e))?;

    let cursor_update = CursorUpdate::from_parts(
        self.cursor_last_key.as_deref(),
        self.cursor_token.as_deref(),
    );
    let pooled_cursor = match PooledCursor::from_update(&cursor_update, slab) {
        Ok(cursor) => cursor,
        Err(err) => {
            pooled_spec.deallocate(slab);  // ROLLBACK spec on cursor failure
            return Err(EtcdCodecError::SlabFull(err));
        }
    };

    let pooled_spawned = match PooledSpawned::from_slice(&self.spawned, slab) {
        Ok(spawned) => spawned,
        Err(err) => {
            pooled_cursor.release_fields(slab);  // ROLLBACK cursor
            pooled_spec.deallocate(slab);         // ROLLBACK spec
            return Err(EtcdCodecError::SlabFull(err));
        }
    };
    // ... build ShardRecord from fields
}
```

### Design Notes

- **Why not serde?** The codec must be explicit and deterministic. Serde-derived serialization is non-deterministic across versions and doesn't provide cross-field invariant validation on decode. The hand-written codec ensures bitwise-identical round-trips and validates domain invariants during deserialization.
- **Why owned intermediate types?** `RunRecord` and `ShardRecord` use pooled/slab-backed fields (`PooledShardSpec`, `PooledCursor`). The owned intermediates provide heap-backed copies that can be constructed from flat bytes, validated, then converted back to pooled records with proper slab allocation.
- **v1 prefix for versioning**: If the schema evolves, a `v2` prefix can be introduced with a migration path. Decoders dispatch on the version prefix.
- **`RunConfig` field decomposition**: `RunRecord.config` is a `RunConfig` struct with `cursor_semantics`, `lease_duration` (NonZeroU64), and `max_shard_retries` (Option<u32>). The codec encodes these as individual fields, not nested — the owned intermediate flattens `RunConfig` into `cursor_semantics`, `lease_duration` (as u64), and `max_shard_retries`.

title: B2 — Lease + fencing enforcement (acquire/renew/checkpoint)
description:
## Context

This is the third subtask of Epic B (gossip-8968) and the most complex. B0 established crate connectivity, B1 added the keyspace and codec. B2 replaces the `InMemoryCoordinator` delegation with real etcd-backed coordination for the hot-path operations: `acquire_and_restore_into`, `renew`, and `checkpoint`. It also implements `create_run`, `register_shards`, the read-side queries, and `ShardClaiming`.

This is a correctness-critical task. Every hot-path mutation must be fenced via etcd transactions. The hard rule: **do not ACK a checkpoint unless the etcd txn commits**. A stale write that commits silently would violate single-writer invariants and cause data loss.

## Current State

After B1 (gossip-8968.2), `gossip-coordination-etcd` has:
- `EtcdCoordinator` with live etcd connection and `EtcdKeyspace`
- Versioned codec for `RunRecord` and `ShardRecord` (v1 format)
- All protocol semantics still delegated to `InMemoryCoordinator`

```rust
// crates/gossip-coordination-etcd/src/backend.rs (after B1)
pub struct EtcdCoordinator {
    config: EtcdCoordinatorConfig,
    keyspace: EtcdKeyspace,
    runtime: SyncRuntime,
    client: etcd_client::Client,
    protocol_delegate: InMemoryCoordinator,  // <-- B2 removes this
    claim_candidates_scratch: Vec<ShardId>,   // <-- B2 keeps this for ShardClaiming
}
```

## Desired State

`EtcdCoordinator` removes the `InMemoryCoordinator` delegation and implements coordination operations directly against etcd:

### New Struct Shape

```rust

    config: EtcdCoordinatorConfig,
    keyspace: EtcdKeyspace,
    runtime: SyncRuntime,
    client: etcd_client::Client,
    claim_candidates_scratch: Vec<ShardId>,  // retained for ShardClaiming
}
```

### Implemented Operations (B2 scope)
| Trait | Method | Implementation |
|-------|--------|---------------|
| `RunManagement` | `create_run` | etcd txn: compare-absent on run key, put RunRecord blob |
| `RunManagement` | `register_shards` | etcd txn: compare-absent on shard keys, put ShardRecord blobs + active indexes, update RunRecord to Active |
| `RunManagement` | `get_run` | etcd get + decode |
| `RunManagement` | `get_run_progress` | prefix scan shards, aggregate with `RunProgress::observe_shard()` |
| `RunManagement` | `list_shards_into` | prefix scan + filter with `ShardFilter::matches()` + sort |
| `RunManagement` | `collect_claim_candidates_into` | prefix scan, identify Active shards without live owners |
| `CoordinationBackend` | `acquire_and_restore_into` | etcd txn: bump fence_epoch, create owner key attached to etcd lease, update ShardRecord |
| `CoordinationBackend` | `renew` | etcd lease keep-alive + txn: update deadline in ShardRecord |
| `CoordinationBackend` | `checkpoint` | etcd txn: require fence match + owner key exists, update cursor in ShardRecord |
| `ShardClaiming` | `claim_next_available` | delegate to `default_claim_next_available` free function |

### Fail-Closed Operations (deferred to later Epic B items)

These methods MUST fail closed. Use a helper like `fail_unimplemented(method_name: &str) -> !` that panics with context:

| Method | Behavior |
|--------|----------|
| `complete` | `fail_unimplemented("complete")` |
| `park_shard` | `fail_unimplemented("park_shard")` |
| `split_replace` | `fail_unimplemented("split_replace")` |
| `split_residual` | `fail_unimplemented("split_residual")` |
| `complete_run` | `fail_unimplemented("complete_run")` |
| `fail_run` | `fail_unimplemented("fail_run")` |
| `cancel_run` | `fail_unimplemented("cancel_run")` |
| `unpark_shard` | `fail_unimplemented("unpark_shard")` |

### ShardClaiming Implementation

**IMPORTANT**: `ShardClaiming` has no blanket impl (`facade.rs:422`). You must implement it explicitly using the `default_claim_next_available` free function:

```rust
// Pattern from InMemoryCoordinator
impl ShardClaiming for EtcdCoordinator {
    fn claim_next_available<'a>(
        &mut self,
        now: LogicalTime,
        tenant: TenantId,
        run: RunId,
        worker: WorkerId,
        out: &'a mut AcquireScratch,
    ) -> Result<AcquireResultView<'a>, ClaimError> {
        let mut candidates = std::mem::take(&mut self.claim_candidates_scratch);
        let result = default_claim_next_available(
            self, now, tenant, run, worker, out, &mut candidates,
        );
        self.claim_candidates_scratch = candidates;
        result
    }
}
```

The free function `default_claim_next_available` is at `gossip-coordination/src/facade.rs:237`. It calls `collect_claim_candidates_into`, then iterates candidates starting at `worker.as_raw() % len` offset, trying `acquire_and_restore_into` on each.

### Fencing Protocol

Every hot-path mutation uses an etcd transaction with `Compare`s that enforce:
1. **Shard record mod_revision matches** — optimistic concurrency via `CompareOp::Equal` on `mod_revision`
2. **Owner key fencing** — owner key value matches expected `(worker, fence_epoch)` binding
3. **Owner key attached to etcd lease** — storage-layer liveness independent of logical lease deadline

**The acquire flow:**
1. Load shard record from etcd (`etcd_get` + `decode_shard_record_v1`)
2. Check status (must be `Active`), check no live owner (`!is_leased_at(now)`)
3. Load run record to get `lease_duration` from `RunConfig`
4. Grant a new etcd lease (`etcd_lease_grant(owner_lease_ttl_secs)`)
5. Bump `fence_epoch` via `record.advance_fence()` (`record.rs:908`)
6. Set new `LeaseHolder` with logical deadline (`now + lease_duration`)
7. Build txn: compare shard mod_revision + owner key state, put updated shard + owner key (with etcd lease attachment via `PutOptions::new().with_lease()`)
8. If txn fails (compare contention), revoke new lease via `best_effort_revoke_lease`, retry
9. Fill `AcquireScratch` (see pattern below), compute `CapacityHint`, return `AcquireResultView`

**The checkpoint flow:**
1. Load shard record from etcd
2. Check op-log idempotency via `check_op_idempotency(record, op_id, payload_hash)` (shard-level, `validation.rs:312`)
3. Validate lease via `validate_lease(now, tenant, lease, record)` (`validation.rs:114`)
4. Validate cursor via `validate_cursor_update_pooled(new_cursor, old_last_key, spec_start, spec_end)` (`validation.rs:209`)
5. Update cursor in slab, push `OpLogEntry` with `OpKind::Checkpoint`, `OpResult::Completed`
6. Build txn: compare shard mod_revision + owner present with matching value
7. **HARD RULE**: only ACK if txn commits; if txn fails, retry or return error

**The renew flow:**
1. Load shard record from etcd
2. Validate lease via `validate_lease(now, tenant, lease, record)` (`validation.rs:114`)
3. Verify owner key matches (`owner_matches_lease`)
4. Load run for `lease_duration`, compute `new_deadline = now + lease_duration`
5. Keep-alive etcd lease (NOT new grant — use `etcd_lease_keep_alive_once`)
6. Build txn: compare shard mod_revision + owner present, put updated shard with new deadline
7. Return `RenewResult { new_deadline, capacity }`

### AcquireScratch Fill Pattern

After a successful acquire, fill the `AcquireScratch` exactly like `InMemoryCoordinator` (`in_memory.rs:1126-1144`):

```rust
// 1. Reset scratch buffers
out.reset();

// 2. Write shard spec from slab-backed pooled fields
out.write_spec(
    record.spec.key_range_start(&slab),
    record.spec.key_range_end(&slab),
    record.spec.metadata(&slab),
);

// 3. Write cursor from slab-backed pooled fields
out.write_cursor(
    record.cursor.last_key(&slab),
    record.cursor.token(&slab),
);

// 4. Write spawned lineage
out.write_spawned_iter(record.spawned.iter(&slab));

// 5. Build snapshot view
let snapshot = out.view(record.status, record.cursor_semantics, record.parent);

// 6. Compute capacity hint
let capacity = self.count_available_for_run(now, tenant, key.run());

Ok(AcquireResultView { lease, snapshot, capacity })
```

The `AcquireScratch` type is at `gossip-coordination/src/error.rs:1519`. Methods: `reset()` (:1552), `write_spec()` (:1573), `write_cursor()` (:1594), `write_spawned_iter()` (:1624), `view()` (:1667).

### CapacityHint Computation

In the etcd backend, `CapacityHint` must be computed by prefix-scanning all shards in the run (unlike InMemoryCoordinator which iterates a HashMap). Follow `InMemoryCoordinator::count_available_for_run` at `in_memory.rs:2281-2354`:

```rust
fn count_available_for_run(&self, now: LogicalTime, tenant: TenantId, run: RunId) -> CapacityHint {
    let shards = self.scan_run_shards(tenant, run)?;  // prefix scan
    let mut available_count: u32 = 0;
    let mut earliest_deadline: Option<LogicalTime> = None;
    for persisted in &shards {
        if persisted.record.status != ShardStatus::Active { continue; }
        if persisted.owner_is_live_at(now) {
            // Track earliest deadline among leased shards
            let deadline = persisted.record.lease_deadline().unwrap();
            earliest_deadline = Some(match earliest_deadline {
                Some(prev) => core::cmp::min(prev, deadline),
                None => deadline,
            });
        } else {
            available_count += 1;
        }
    }
    CapacityHint { available_count, earliest_deadline }
}
```

### Idempotency: Run-Level vs Shard-Level

**Critical distinction** — there are TWO different idempotency mechanisms:

1. **Shard-level** (`check_op_idempotency` in `validation.rs:312`):
   - Used by: `checkpoint`, `complete`, `park_shard`, `split_replace`, `split_residual`
   - Operates on `ShardRecord.op_log: RingBuffer<OpLogEntry, 16>`
   - Returns `Result<Option<&OpLogEntry>, CoordError>`

2. **Run-level** (`RunRecord::check_op_idempotency` method in `run.rs:705`):
   - Used by: `register_shards`, `complete_run`, `fail_run`, `cancel_run`
   - Operates on `RunRecord.op_log: RingBuffer<RunOpLogEntry, 8>`
   - Returns `Result<Option<&RunOpLogEntry>, RunOpIdConflict>`
   - For `register_shards` replay: extract cached `shard_ids` from `RunOpResult::RegisteredShards`

**For `register_shards`** specifically:
```rust
let payload_hash = hash_register_shards_payload(shards);  // run.rs:1481
if let Some(entry) = record.check_op_idempotency(op_id, payload_hash)? {
    match entry.result() {
        RunOpResult::RegisteredShards { shard_ids } => {
            return Ok(IdempotentOutcome::Replayed(shard_ids.to_vec()));
        }
        RunOpResult::Ack => panic!("data corruption"),
    }
}
```

## Risk Analysis

- **Fencing correctness**: A bug in compare construction could allow stale writes. Mitigation: use `/dist-sys-auditor`, exhaustive integration tests, verify owner key binding matches after every mutation.
- **Lease cleanup on retry**: If acquire txn fails, the newly granted etcd lease must be revoked. Failure to clean up leaks etcd leases. Mitigation: `best_effort_revoke_lease()` in every retry path.
- **Retry budget exhaustion**: If compare contention doesn't converge within `optimistic_txn_retries`, the operation fails. This is correct behavior (fail closed), but operators need visibility. Mitigation: clear error messages with context.
- **Partial transaction semantics**: etcd transactions are atomic but the operation loads state with separate GETs before the txn. Another writer can interleave between the GET and the TXN. Mitigation: compare on mod_revision catches all interleavers — the txn fails and we retry.
- **`&mut self` on etcd client**: The etcd-client crate's sub-clients (`KvClient`, `LeaseClient`) take `&mut self`. Since `EtcdCoordinator` methods also take `&mut self`, this works directly. title: B3 — Split operations with bounded fanout
description:
## Context

This is the fourth subtask of Epic B (gossip-8968). B0-B2 established the crate scaffold, keyspace/codec, and hot-path fencing (acquire/renew/checkpoint). B3 adds the split operations (`split_replace` and `split_residual`) as atomic etcd transactions with enforced bounded fanout via `max_children_per_op`. These are the most structurally complex coordinator mutations — each involves multiple child shard creation, parent record mutation, owner key cleanup, and active-index updates in a single atomic transaction.

The correctness invariant: **under failure injection, partial child sets must never be published**. Either all children appear atomically or none do. The etcd transaction model guarantees this naturally, but the implementation must construct the transaction correctly.

## Current State

After B2 (gossip-8968.3), `gossip-coordination-etcd` has acquire/renew/checkpoint with full fencing, plus `create_run`, `register_shards`, and read-side queries. The split operations call `fail_unimplemented("split_replace")` / `fail_unimplemented("split_residual")`.

```rust
// crates/gossip-coordination-etcd/src/backend.rs (after B2)
fn split_replace(&mut self, ...) -> Result<IdempotentOutcome<SplitReplaceResult>, SplitReplaceError> {
    self.fail_unimplemented("split_replace")  // <-- B3 replaces this
}
fn split_residual(&mut self, ...) -> Result<IdempotentOutcome<SplitResidualResult>, SplitResidualError> {
    self.fail_unimplemented("split_residual")  // <-- B3 replaces this
}
```

## Desired State

Both split operations implemented as fenced etcd transactions with:
1. Bounded fanout enforcement via `config.max_children_per_op`
2. Deterministic child ID derivation via `derive_split_shard_id`
3. Atomic publication of all children (or none) via etcd txn
4. Idempotent replay returning cached child IDs from op-log/spawned list
5. Owner key cleanup on split_replace (parent becomes terminal)
6. Active-shard index management (remove parent on split_replace, add children/residual)

### split_replace Flow

1. Load shard record + owner key from etcd
2. Check tenant isolation
3. **Shard-level idempotency**: `check_op_idempotency(record, op_id, payload_hash)` — if replayed, extract cached child IDs from `parent.spawned` via `split_replace_replay_child_ids`
4. Check not terminal
5. Validate lease via `validate_lease`
6. Verify owner key matches lease binding
7. **Validate preconditions** via `split_replace_validate_preconditions`:
   - Backend child limit: `plan.children().len() > config.max_children_per_op` → `SplitValidationError::BackendChildLimitExceeded`
   - Per-child spec validity via `ShardSpec::validate_ref`
   - Coverage: children must collectively cover parent's `[start, end)` with no gaps/overlaps
   - Spawn capacity: `parent.spawned.len() + plan.children().len() <= MAX_SPAWNED_PER_SHARD`
8. Derive child IDs deterministically via `derive_split_shard_id(run, parent_shard, op_id, DerivedShardKind::Child, base_offset + i)`
9. Verify all child keys absent in etcd (compare-absent guards)
10. Build child `ShardRecord`s via `ShardRecord::new_split_child`
11. **Apply parent mutation** via `split_replace_apply_parent`:
    - Append child IDs to `parent.spawned` (via `allocate_appended_slot` + `install_slot`)
    - Transition parent to `ShardStatus::Split`
    - Clear parent's lease
    - Push `OpLogEntry(OpKind::SplitReplace, OpResult::Completed)`
12. **Atomic etcd txn**: compares on shard revision + owner present + all children absent; ops: put parent, delete owner key, delete parent active-shard index, put all child records, put all child active-shard index keys
13. On txn failure: retry (bounded by `optimistic_txn_retries`); on success: return `SplitReplaceResult { children }`

### split_residual Flow

1. Load shard record + owner key from etcd
2. Check tenant isolation
3. **Two-phase replay check** via `split_residual_check_replay`:
   - First: op-log idempotency (standard `check_op_idempotency`)
   - Second: scan `parent.spawned` for a derived residual matching the op_id via `find_replayed_residual`
4. Check not terminal
5. **Validate preconditions** via `split_residual_validate_preconditions`:
   - Validate lease
   - Per-spec validity for both parent_new_spec and residual_spec
   - Residual split bounds: `validate_residual_split_bounds` (parent=left partition, residual=right partition)
   - Cursor bounds: parent's cursor must fall within proposed new parent spec
   - Spawn capacity: `parent.spawned.len() + 1 <= MAX_SPAWNED_PER_SHARD`
6. Verify owner key matches
7. Derive residual ID via `derive_split_shard_id(run, parent_shard, op_id, DerivedShardKind::Residual, base_offset)`
8. Verify residual key absent in etcd
9. Build residual `ShardRecord` via `ShardRecord::new_split_child`
10. **Apply parent mutation** via `split_residual_apply_parent`:
    - Append residual ID to `parent.spawned`
    - Update parent spec via `spec.update_from_ref(parent_new_spec, slab)` (shrinks range)
    - Push `OpLogEntry(OpKind::SplitResidual, OpResult::Completed)`
    - Rollback spawned slot on spec update failure
11. **Atomic etcd txn**: compares on shard revision + owner present + residual absent; ops: put parent, put residual record, put residual active-shard index
12. Parent stays `Active` (NOT terminal) — worker retains lease and continues processing the shrunk range
13. On success: return `SplitResidualResult { residual }`

### New Config Field

`EtcdCoordinatorConfig` gains:
- `max_children_per_op: usize` — maximum children allowed in one atomic split operation (default: 8, validated > 0 and <= `MAX_SPLIT_CHILDREN`)
- New config errors: `ZeroMaxChildrenPerOp`, `MaxChildrenPerOpExceedsGlobalLimit { requested, global_max }`

- `split_replace_validate_preconditions(plan, record, slab, max_children_per_op)` — full precondition check, returns `SplitChildOrder`
- `split_residual_validate_preconditions(now, tenant, lease, record, slab, plan)` — validates lease, specs, bounds, capacity
- `split_residual_validate_cursor_bounds(record, slab, new_parent_start, new_parent_end)` — ensures cursor within new range

**Mutation helpers:**
- `split_replace_apply_parent(record, slab, child_ids, op_id, payload_hash, now)` — mutates parent: spawned append, Split status, clear lease, push op-log
- `split_residual_apply_parent(record, slab, residual_id, new_parent_spec, op_id, payload_hash, now)` — mutates parent: spawned append, spec shrink, push op-log (with rollback)

**Replay helpers:**
- `split_replace_replay_child_ids(record, slab, plan_len)` — extracts child IDs from `parent.spawned` tail
- `find_replayed_residual(record, slab, run, parent_shard, op_id)` — scans spawned for matching derived ID
- `split_residual_check_replay(record, op_id, payload_hash, slab, run, parent_shard)` — two-phase replay check

| `MAX_SPAWNED_PER_SHARD` | `gossip-contracts/src/coordination/limits.rs:20` | 1024 — max cumulative spawned |

### Design Notes

- **Why `SplitChildOrder`?** Coverage validation requires children sorted by `key_range_start`, but the plan preserves caller order for deterministic hashing. `SplitChildOrder` provides a sorted index mapping without reordering the plan. Uses `[u16; MAX_SPLIT_CHILDREN]` (512 bytes stack) — acceptable since MAX_SPLIT_CHILDREN is bounded at 256.
- **Derive child IDs deterministically**: `derive_split_shard_id` uses domain-separated BLAKE3 with `(run, parent, op_id, kind, index)`. The `index` parameter must be `parent.spawned.len() + child_offset` (base offset from existing spawned count). Bit 63 is forced set so `ShardId::is_derived()` returns true.
- **split_residual cursor preservation**: Unlike split_replace (where parent becomes terminal), split_residual keeps the parent `Active`. The parent's cursor is preserved and must fall within the proposed new parent spec range — validated by `split_residual_validate_cursor_bounds`.
- **Transaction size**: A split_replace with N children produces a transaction with ~(3 + 2N) operations: put parent + delete owner + delete parent-active-index + N puts for child records + N puts for child active-index keys. With `max_children_per_op=8` (default), this is 19 ops — well within etcd's per-txn limits.

### Skill Recommendations

- **Use `/dist-sys-auditor`** to review the transaction construction — verify atomicity guarantees, that partial child sets are impossible
- **Use `/safe-over-unsafe`** if any unsafe code appears (unlikely for this task)
- **Use `/doc-rigor`** on the helper functions — split validation logic needs precise documentation
- **Use `/deep-research "etcd transaction size limits and compare-and-swap scalability — maximum operations per transaction, performance with 20+ ops"` if concerned about transaction size with many children**

## Review Findings & Corrections (2026-03-07)

### Dependency Graph Correction
B3 now formally depends on B2 (gossip-8968.3) in addition to B1 (gossip-8968.2). B3 requires the etcd transaction infrastructure (helpers like `etcd_txn`, `etcd_get`, `etcd_put`, `etcd_delete`, `etcd_lease_grant`), fencing model (owner keys, lease bindings), and `EtcdOperation` enum expansion that B2 introduces. Without B2, the split operations have no transaction primitives to build on.

### Current State Clarification
The 'Current State' section describes the expected state AFTER B2 completes, not the literal current codebase. The live backend.rs (412 lines) delegates ALL operations to `InMemoryCoordinator` via `self.protocol_delegate`. There are NO `fail_unimplemented` stubs — B2 will replace the delegation pattern with real etcd RPCs for hot-path operations (acquire/renew/checkpoint, create_run, register_shards, read queries) and leave split operations either as `fail_unimplemented` or delegation stubs. The B3 implementing agent should work against the post-B2 codebase, not the current delegation shell.

### Line Number Corrections
Two references in the 'Key Types and Utilities to Reuse' table are off by ~16 lines:
- `validate_split_coverage_bounds`: claimed ~1340, **actual line 1324** in `shard_spec.rs`
- `validate_residual_split_bounds`: claimed ~1487, **actual line 1471** in `shard_spec.rs`
All other line references verified accurate (20/22 exact or within 2 lines).

### etcd Transaction Pattern Reference — CRITICAL CONTEXT
The B2 artifact establishes ALL the etcd transaction patterns that B3 must follow. The implementing agent should read the B2 artifact first:
- **Location**: `tmp/gossip-project-artifacts/b5_persistence/phase2/b2/crates/gossip-coordination-etcd/src/backend.rs`
- **Helper methods**: `etcd_get`, `etcd_put`, `etcd_delete`, `etcd_txn`, `etcd_lease_grant`, `etcd_lease_keep_alive_once`, `etcd_lease_revoke` — all defined as private methods on `EtcdCoordinator`
- **Compare constructors**: `compare_shard_revision(key, mod_rev)`, `compare_run_revision(key, mod_rev)`, `compare_absent(key)`, `compare_owner_present(key, value)` — static helper functions
- **Transaction idiom**: `Txn::new().when(compares).and_then(success_ops)` — `.or_else()` is NEVER used; all artifacts check `response.succeeded()` for CAS failure
- **Retry pattern**: `for _ in 0..self.config.optimistic_txn_retries() { load → validate → build_txn → execute → if !succeeded { continue } }` with idempotency check on each iteration and after exhaustion
- **Error pattern**: `self.etcd_txn(txn).unwrap_or_else(|err| self.fatal_storage_error(...))` — transport errors panic, only CAS failures retry
- **etcd-client API imports**: `use etcd_client::{Compare, CompareOp, DeleteOptions, GetOptions, PutOptions, Txn, TxnOp};`

The B3 reference artifact at `tmp/gossip-project-artifacts/b5_persistence/phase2/b3-artifacts/crates/gossip-coordination-etcd/src/backend.rs` (2042 lines) already follows these patterns. Use it as the primary reference.

### etcd max-txn-ops Concern — RESEARCH NEEDED
etcd 3.5 has a default `--max-txn-ops` limit of 128 operations per transaction. The split_replace transaction produces ~(3 + 2N) operations where N = number of children:
- `max_children_per_op=8` (default) → 19 ops — well within limit
- `max_children_per_op=32` → 67 ops — within limit
- `max_children_per_op=64` → 131 ops — EXCEEDS default limit
- `max_children_per_op=128` → 259 ops — far exceeds

The config validation should either:
(a) Cap `max_children_per_op` to a value that stays within etcd's default txn-ops limit (e.g., 62), OR
(b) Document that operators must increase `--max-txn-ops` on their etcd cluster when using large values, OR
(c) Add a config field for the etcd cluster's `max-txn-ops` and validate against it

**Recommendation**: Use `/deep-research "etcd --max-txn-ops limit: default value across versions, how to query the current cluster limit at runtime, best practices for large transactions, whether etcd-client 0.18 exposes this information"` to determine the best approach. The B3 artifact does not address this.

### EtcdOperation Enum
B2 expands the `EtcdOperation` enum from `{Connect, Status}` to include `{Get, Put, Delete, Txn, LeaseGrant, LeaseRevoke, LeaseKeepAlive}`. B3 does NOT need to modify `error.rs` — all needed variants will exist after B2.

- `tmp/.../b3-artifacts/.../config.rs` — 197 lines, includes `max_children_per_op`
- `tmp/.../b3-artifacts/.../tests.rs` — 453 lines, integration tests

title: B4 — Run lifecycle saga (Initializing → Active) + GC of partial runs
description:
## Context

This is the fifth and final subtask of Epic B (gossip-8968). B0-B3 established crate scaffold, keyspace/codec, hot-path fencing, and split operations. B4 completes the `EtcdCoordinator` by implementing run lifecycle management (`complete_run`, `fail_run`, `cancel_run`), shard unparking (`unpark_shard`), active-run index maintenance, and garbage collection of stale partial (Initializing) runs that were never fully registered.

The correctness invariant: **workers must only enumerate "active runs" via the active-run index, never discovering half-registered Initializing runs**. The GC mechanism cleans up orphaned Initializing runs (from crashed coordinators that started `create_run` but never completed `register_shards`).

After B4, the only remaining unimplemented operations are `complete` (shard-level terminal) and `park_shard` — these are explicitly out of B4 scope and remain fail-closed.

## Current State

After B3 (gossip-8968.4), `gossip-coordination-etcd` has:
- Full hot-path: acquire, renew, checkpoint, split_replace, split_residual
- Run setup: create_run, register_shards
- Read-side: get_run, get_run_progress, list_shards_into, collect_claim_candidates_into
- The following operations still call `fail_unimplemented(...)`:
  - `complete_run`, `fail_run`, `cancel_run` (run lifecycle transitions)
  - `unpark_shard` (shard recovery)
  - `complete`, `park_shard` (shard-level terminal operations — remain out of scope)

## Desired State

### Implemented Operations (B4 scope)

| Trait | Method | Implementation |
|-------|--------|---------------|
| `RunManagement` | `complete_run` | Fenced txn: transition Active → Done, remove active-run index |
| `RunManagement` | `fail_run` | Fenced txn: transition Active → Failed, remove active-run index |
| `RunManagement` | `cancel_run` | Fenced txn: transition Initializing/Active → Cancelled, remove active-run index |
| `RunManagement` | `unpark_shard` | Fenced txn: Parked → Active, bump fence, clear park_reason |
| N/A (public method) | `list_active_runs_into` | Prefix scan of active-run index keys |
| N/A (public method) | `gc_stale_initializing_runs_into` | Scan + delete orphaned Initializing runs older than cutoff |

### Still Fail-Closed After B4
| Method | Behavior | Reason |
|--------|----------|--------|
| `complete` (shard) | `fail_unimplemented("complete")` | Deferred to future epic |
| `park_shard` | `fail_unimplemented("park_shard")` | Deferred to future epic |

### Run Lifecycle State Machine

```
Initializing --register_shards--> Active   (active-run index PUBLISHED)
Initializing --cancel_run-------> Cancelled (active-run index was never published)
Active ------complete_run-------> Done      (active-run index REMOVED)
Active ------fail_run-----------> Failed    (active-run index REMOVED)
Active ------cancel_run---------> Cancelled (active-run index REMOVED)
```

Key invariant: The active-run index is published ONLY on `register_shards` (transition to Active) and removed ONLY on terminal transitions. Workers use `list_active_runs_into` to discover work — they never see Initializing or terminal runs.

### Shared Terminal Transition Implementation

All three terminal transitions (`complete_run`, `fail_run`, `cancel_run`) share a `transition_run_terminal` helper:

```rust
fn transition_run_terminal(
    &mut self,
    now: LogicalTime,
    tenant: TenantId,
    run: RunId,
    op_id: OpId,
    target_status: RunStatus,
    op_kind: RunOpKind,
    payload_hash: u64,
    require_active: bool,  // true for complete/fail, false for cancel
) -> Result<IdempotentOutcome<()>, RunTransitionError>
```

The flow (optimistic retry loop):
1. Load run record from etcd
2. Check tenant isolation
3. **Run-level idempotency**: `record.check_op_idempotency(op_id, payload_hash)` — if replayed, return `Replayed(())`
4. Check run is not already terminal → `RunTransitionError::RunTerminal { status }`
5. If `require_active`: check `status == Active` → `RunTransitionError::WrongStatus { status, target }`
6. Apply mutation via `apply_terminal_run_transition`:
   - Assert status transition is legal
   - Set `record.status = target_status`
   - Set `record.completed_at = Some(now)`
   - Push `RunOpLogEntry(op_id, op_kind, payload_hash, now, RunOpResult::Ack)`
7. Encode and build fenced txn:
   - Compare: run mod_revision
   - Compare: active-run index presence based on prior status (present if was Active, absent if was Initializing)
   - Ops: put updated run blob, delete active-run index key
8. On txn success: return `Executed(())`

### unpark_shard Implementation

Restores a Parked shard to Active status (admin operation, no lease required):

1. Load shard record + run record from etcd
2. Check tenant isolation, check run not terminal
3. **Shard-level idempotency** with manual error mapping:
   - `check_op_idempotency` returns `CoordError` variants
   - Must map `CoordError::OpIdConflict` → `UnparkError::OpIdConflict(RunOpIdConflict { ... })`
4. Verify shard is Parked → `UnparkError::NotParked { status }`
5. Apply mutation:
   - Bump fence epoch via `record.advance_fence()`
   - Clear `park_reason = None`
   - Set `status = Active`
   - Clear lease
   - Push `OpLogEntry(OpKind::Unpark, OpResult::Completed)`
6. Fenced txn:
   - Compare: shard mod_revision + run mod_revision + run-active-key present + owner-key absent
   - Ops: put updated shard, delete owner key (if exists), put active-shard index key
7. Return `Executed(())`

### GC of Stale Initializing Runs

```rust
pub fn gc_stale_initializing_runs_into(
    &mut self,
    tenant: TenantId,
    cutoff: LogicalTime,
    out: &mut Vec<RunId>,
) -> Result<(), EtcdCoordinatorError>
```

Flow:
1. `scan_tenant_runs(tenant)` — prefix scan all run records under the tenant
2. Filter: retain only `Initializing` runs with `created_at < cutoff`
3. Sort by `created_at` (oldest first)
4. For each candidate: fenced delete txn:
   - Compare: run mod_revision + active-run index absent (Initializing runs should never have one)
   - Ops: delete run key, delete active-run index key (safety), range-delete shard records prefix, range-delete active-shards prefix
5. Append deleted `RunId` to `out`

### Active-Run Index Enumeration

```rust
pub fn list_active_runs_into(
    &self,
    tenant: TenantId,
    out: &mut Vec<RunId>,
) -> Result<(), EtcdCoordinatorError>
```

Prefix-scans `{prefix}/tenants/{tenant_hex}/runs_active/`, parses `RunId` from each key's suffix (16 hex chars) via `parse_direct_run_id_from_key`.

### Payload Hash Functions

| Operation | Hash Function | Location |
|-----------|--------------|----------|
| `complete_run` | `hash_complete_run_payload()` | `gossip-coordination/src/run.rs:1513` — parameterless |
| `fail_run` | `hash_fail_run_payload()` | `gossip-coordination/src/run.rs:1519` — parameterless |
| `cancel_run` | `hash_cancel_run_payload()` | `gossip-coordination/src/run.rs:1525` — parameterless |
| `unpark_shard` | `hash_unpark_payload(key: &ShardKey)` | `gossip-coordination/src/run.rs:1534` — includes run + shard |

## Implementation Guidance

### Files to Modify
| File | Change | Rationale |
|------|--------|-----------|
| `crates/gossip-coordination-etcd/src/backend.rs` | Replace `fail_unimplemented` for `complete_run`/`fail_run`/`cancel_run`/`unpark_shard`; add `transition_run_terminal`, `apply_terminal_run_transition`, `scan_tenant_runs`, `list_active_runs_into`, `gc_stale_initializing_runs_into`, `parse_direct_run_id_from_key` | Core change (~500 lines) |
| `crates/gossip-coordination-etcd/src/lib.rs` | Update module doc to reflect B4 scope | Documentation |
| `crates/gossip-coordination-etcd/src/tests.rs` | Add 4 integration tests | End-to-end verification |

### Files NOT Modified
| File | Reason |
|------|--------|
| `codec.rs` | RunRecord codec already encodes all `RunOpKind` variants including `CompleteRun`, `FailRun`, `CancelRun` with `Ack` result |
| `keyspace.rs` | All needed key methods already exist (`run_record_key`, `run_active_index_key`, `runs_active_prefix`, `runs_prefix`) |
| `error.rs` | No new error variants needed |
| `config.rs` | No new config fields needed |

### Key Helper Functions

**`transition_run_terminal`** (private, ~85 lines):
- Shared by complete_run, fail_run, cancel_run
- Optimistic retry loop
- Handles both "was Active" (active-index present) and "was Initializing" (active-index absent) cases in compare construction

**`apply_terminal_run_transition`** (module-level pure function):
```rust
fn apply_terminal_run_transition(
    record: &mut RunRecord,
    now: LogicalTime,
    target_status: RunStatus,
    op_id: OpId,
    op_kind: RunOpKind,
    payload_hash: u64,
) {
    assert!(target_status.is_terminal());
    assert!(!record.status.is_terminal());
    record.status = target_status;
    record.completed_at = Some(now);
    record.op_log_push(RunOpLogEntry::new(op_id, op_kind, payload_hash, now, RunOpResult::Ack));
    // assert post-conditions
}
```

**`scan_tenant_runs`** (private):
- Prefix-scans `{prefix}/tenants/{tenant_hex}/runs/` for all run record keys
- Decodes each blob via `decode_run_record_v1`
- Returns `Vec<PersistedRun>` sorted by `run.as_raw()`

**`parse_direct_run_id_from_key`** (private):
- Strips the expected prefix from an etcd key
- Parses the remaining 16 hex chars as a `RunId`
- Returns `None` on parse failure

### Utilities to Reuse

| Utility | Exact Location | Usage |
|---------|---------------|-------|
| `RunRecord::check_op_idempotency` (run-level) | `gossip-coordination/src/run.rs:705` | Idempotency for terminal transitions |
| `check_op_idempotency` (shard-level) | `gossip-coordination/src/validation.rs:312` | Idempotency for unpark_shard |
| `hash_complete_run_payload` | `gossip-coordination/src/run.rs:1513` | complete_run hash (parameterless) |
| `hash_fail_run_payload` | `gossip-coordination/src/run.rs:1519` | fail_run hash (parameterless) |
| `hash_cancel_run_payload` | `gossip-coordination/src/run.rs:1525` | cancel_run hash (parameterless) |
| `hash_unpark_payload` | `gossip-coordination/src/run.rs:1534` | unpark_shard hash (includes ShardKey) |
| `RunTransitionError` | `gossip-coordination/src/run_errors.rs:273` | Error type for terminal transitions |
| `UnparkError` | `gossip-coordination/src/run_errors.rs:358` | Error type for unpark_shard |
| `RunOpIdConflict` | `gossip-coordination/src/run.rs:436` | Intermediate type for From impls |
| `ShardRecord::advance_fence` | `gossip-coordination/src/record.rs:908` | Fence bump in unpark |

### Duplication Prevention

- `transition_run_terminal` is the SINGLE implementation for all three terminal ops — do NOT write separate implementations for complete_run/fail_run/cancel_run
- `apply_terminal_run_transition` is a pure function — do NOT mix mutation with etcd I/O
- Reuse `RunRecord::check_op_idempotency` — do NOT reimplement run-level idempotency
- For unpark_shard: `check_op_idempotency` from `validation.rs:312` returns `CoordError` variants; you must manually map `CoordError::OpIdConflict` → `UnparkError::OpIdConflict(RunOpIdConflict { ... })` since there's no automatic `From` impl

### Design Notes

- **cancel_run accepts both Initializing and Active**: Unlike complete_run/fail_run (which require Active), cancel_run can cancel a run that hasn't been registered yet. The `require_active` flag controls this. For Initializing cancellation, the active-run index was never published, so the compare checks absence instead of presence.
- **GC is conservative**: Only deletes runs that are (a) still Initializing and (b) older than a caller-provided cutoff. This prevents deleting runs that are actively being registered (race between `create_run` and `register_shards` by another coordinator).
- **GC uses range-delete**: For shard records and active-shard indexes under a deleted run, uses etcd range-delete with prefix. This handles the (unlikely) case where some shards were partially created but the run never transitioned to Active.
- **Active-run index invariant**: The index is the source of truth for worker discovery. Workers MUST use `list_active_runs_into` instead of scanning all run records. This is enforced by the keyspace design — active-run index keys live under a separate `runs_active/` prefix.

### Skill Recommendations

- **Use `/dist-sys-auditor`** to review the GC safety — verify no race between GC and concurrent `register_shards`
- **Use `/doc-rigor`** on `transition_run_terminal` and `gc_stale_initializing_runs_into`
- **Use `/deep-research "etcd range delete semantics — prefix deletion, atomicity guarantees, interaction with watches and leases"` if ambiguity about etcd's range-delete behavior in transactions**

## Testing Strategy

1. **`active_run_index_hides_initializing_runs_and_unpublishes_terminal_runs`** (`#[ignore]`):
   - Create run (Initializing) — verify NOT in active index
   - Register shards (→ Active) — verify IN active index
   - Cancel a second Initializing run — verify never appears in active index
   - Complete the first run — verify REMOVED from active index

2. **`fail_run_removes_active_index_and_replays_idempotently`** (`#[ignore]`):
   - Create + register run
   - `fail_run` → verify removed from active index, status=Failed, completed_at set
   - Replay same `fail_run` with same op_id → verify `Replayed(())`

3. **`gc_stale_initializing_runs_deletes_only_old_orphans`** (`#[ignore]`):
   - Create 3 runs: run_old (Initializing, created at t=1), run_fresh (Initializing, created at t=100), run_active (registered at t=2)
   - GC with cutoff t=50 → only run_old deleted
   - Verify run_fresh and run_active still exist

4. **`unpark_seeded_parked_shard_round_trip_against_local_etcd`** (`#[ignore]`):
   - Seed a Parked shard (via `test_seed_shard_record`)
   - `unpark_shard` → verify Active status, bumped fence, cleared park_reason, preserved cursor
   - Replay → verify `Replayed(())`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `complete_run` transitions Active → Done, removes active-run index, supports idempotent replay
- [ ] `fail_run` transitions Active → Failed, removes active-run index, supports idempotent replay
- [ ] `cancel_run` transitions Initializing/Active → Cancelled, handles both index-present and index-absent cases

- [ ] All terminal transitions use shared `transition_run_terminal` (no code duplication)
- [ ] `complete` (shard) and `park_shard` remain fail-closed with `fail_unimplemented`

title: Add docker-compose.yml for local etcd testing
description:
## Context

The gossip-rs workspace is building an etcd-backed coordination backend (`gossip-coordination-etcd`). Integration tests need a local etcd instance. Currently, developers must manually start etcd before running `#[ignore]`-gated tests. No Docker infrastructure exists in the project. This task creates the foundational Docker Compose configuration that all other etcd testing infrastructure builds on.

The eventual deployment target is Kubernetes (KinD for local dev, deferred). Docker Compose serves as the stepping stone — the etcd configuration knowledge (env vars, health checks, network setup) carries over directly when KinD is adopted.

## Current State

No Docker infrastructure exists anywhere in the repository:
- No `docker-compose.yml`
- No `Dockerfile`
- No container orchestration scripts

The etcd integration tests assume a manually started etcd:

```rust
// crates/gossip-coordination-etcd/src/tests.rs:607-624
fn local_backend() -> EtcdCoordinator {
    let endpoints = env::var("ETCD_ENDPOINTS")
        .ok()
        .and_then(|raw| {
            let trimmed = raw.trim().to_owned();
            if trimmed.is_empty() { None } else { Some(trimmed) }
        })
        .unwrap_or_else(|| "http://127.0.0.1:2379".to_owned());

    let config = EtcdCoordinatorConfig::from_endpoints_csv(&endpoints, "/gossip/v1")
        .expect("test endpoint configuration should be valid");
    EtcdCoordinator::connect(config).expect("local etcd should be reachable")
}
```

The config module supports these defaults:

```rust
// crates/gossip-coordination-etcd/src/config.rs:21-30
pub(crate) const DEFAULT_CONNECT_TIMEOUT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(5);
pub(crate) const DEFAULT_OWNER_LEASE_TTL_SECS: i64 = 60;
pub(crate) const DEFAULT_OPTIMISTIC_TXN_RETRIES: usize = 8;
```

## Desired State

A `docker-compose.yml` at the project root (or `tests/docker-compose.yml`) that defines a single-node etcd service for local development and testing. The service should:

1. Use a **pinned** image tag (e.g., `bitnami/etcd:3.5` or `gcr.io/etcd-development/etcd:v3.5.17`) for reproducibility.
2. Expose port 2379 on localhost for client connections.
3. Disable authentication for test use (`ALLOW_NONE_AUTHENTICATION=yes` for bitnami, or appropriate flags for official image).
4. Configure `--listen-client-urls http://0.0.0.0:2379` so the container accepts connections from the Docker host.
5. Include a health check using `etcdctl endpoint health`.
6. Use Docker Compose v2 syntax (`docker compose`, NOT the deprecated `docker-compose` v1).
7. Disable auto-compaction for test stability (`--auto-compaction-mode=revision --auto-compaction-retention=0`).

### Example structure

```yaml
services:
  etcd:
    image: bitnami/etcd:3.5
    ports:
      - "2379:2379"
    environment:
      - ALLOW_NONE_AUTHENTICATION=yes
      - ETCD_ADVERTISE_CLIENT_URLS=http://localhost:2379
      - ETCD_LISTEN_CLIENT_URLS=http://0.0.0.0:2379
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "etcdctl", "endpoint", "health"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 10
      start_period: 5s
    tmpfs:
      - /bitnami/etcd/data
```

### Image choice decision

Research identified two viable options:

| Image | Pros | Cons |
|-------|------|------|
| `bitnami/etcd:3.5` | 100M+ pulls, env-var config, `ALLOW_NONE_AUTHENTICATION` | Larger image, Photon OS based |
| `gcr.io/etcd-development/etcd:v3.5.17` | Official, smaller, direct flag control | No convenience env vars |

Either is acceptable. bitnami is simpler for test configuration. The official image is leaner and closer to what runs in production k8s.

## Implementation Guidance

### Files to Create
| File | Content | Rationale |
|------|---------|-----------|
| `docker-compose.yml` (or `tests/docker-compose.yml`) | etcd service definition | Single-node etcd for local testing |

### Patterns to Follow
- sqlx project uses `tests/docker-compose.yml` as a "service catalog" with selective startup (launchbadge/sqlx GitHub).
- Pin container image tags for reproducibility (testcontainers design principles).
- Docker Compose v2 syntax only — v1 is deprecated and unavailable on modern GitHub Actions runners.

### Key Configuration Details
- `tmpfs` for etcd data directory prevents disk accumulation during test runs.
- Health check interval of 5s with start_period of 5s gives etcd time to initialize.
- `ETCD_LISTEN_CLIENT_URLS=http://0.0.0.0:2379` is essential — without it, etcd only listens on localhost inside the container, making it unreachable from the Docker host via port mapping.

## Code References

title: Add Justfile with dev recipes and etcd integration test orchestration
description:
## Context

The gossip-rs workspace has no task runner (no Justfile, no Makefile). Developers must remember and type multi-part cargo commands, Docker commands, and quality-gate pipelines manually. A Justfile provides one-command ergonomics for common development workflows, with a focus on etcd integration testing where the multi-step lifecycle (check Docker → start etcd → run tests → cleanup) benefits most from automation.

Justfile is the preferred task runner in the Rust ecosystem (used by testcontainers-rs-modules-community, many Rust projects). It has clean syntax, built-in `.env` loading, recipe parameters, and cross-platform support.

## Current State

No task runner exists:

```
$ ls Justfile Makefile 2>/dev/null
# (no output — neither file exists)
```

The CI workflow at `.github/workflows/ci.yml` defines the quality gates but there's no developer-facing equivalent:

```yaml
# .github/workflows/ci.yml — the quality gates developers should be able to run locally
# fmt → clippy → test → doc
```

The etcd integration tests are buried behind verbose commands:

```bash
# Current workflow to run etcd integration tests:
docker run -d --name etcd -p 2379:2379 ...  # manual etcd start
ETCD_ENDPOINTS=http://127.0.0.1:2379 cargo test -p gossip-coordination-etcd -- --ignored
docker stop etcd && docker rm etcd  # manual cleanup
```

## Desired State

A `Justfile` at the project root with these recipe categories:

### Core development recipes
| Recipe | Command | Description |
|--------|---------|-------------|
| `just check` | `cargo fmt --all && cargo check && cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` | Quick quality gate |
| `just test` | `cargo nextest run` | All unit tests (no Docker) |
| `just doc` | `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps --all-features` | Build docs with warnings as errors |
| `just dev` | check + test + doc | Full PR-ready gate |

### etcd integration testing recipes
| Recipe | Command | Description |
|--------|---------|-------------|
| `just etcd-up` | `docker compose up -d etcd` | Start local etcd |
| `just etcd-down` | `docker compose down` | Stop and remove etcd |
| `just etcd-status` | `docker compose ps` + `etcdctl endpoint health` | Check etcd health |
| `just test-etcd` | Start etcd if needed → run etcd tests → report | Full integration test cycle |
| `just test-integration` | Run all integration tests (etcd + future services) | Umbrella target |

### Prerequisite checks
| Recipe | Purpose |
|--------|---------|
| `_require-docker` | Fail-fast with helpful error if Docker is not running |
| `_require-etcd` | Fail-fast if etcd container is not healthy |

### Example Justfile structure

```just
# gossip-rs development recipes

set dotenv-load := true

# ── Core ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# Quick quality gate: format + check + clippy
check:
    cargo fmt --all
    cargo check
    cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings

# Run all unit tests (no Docker required)
test:
    cargo nextest run

# Build documentation with warnings as errors
doc:
    RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps --all-features

# Full PR-ready gate: check + test + doc
dev: check test doc

# ── etcd ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# Start local etcd for integration testing
etcd-up: _require-docker
    docker compose up -d etcd
    @echo "Waiting for etcd to be healthy..."
    @docker compose exec etcd etcdctl endpoint health --endpoints=http://localhost:2379 || \
        (echo "etcd not ready yet, retrying..." && sleep 2 && \
         docker compose exec etcd etcdctl endpoint health --endpoints=http://localhost:2379)
    @echo "etcd is ready at http://127.0.0.1:2379"

# Stop local etcd
etcd-down:
    docker compose down

# Check etcd health
etcd-status:
    @docker compose ps
    @docker compose exec etcd etcdctl endpoint health --endpoints=http://localhost:2379

# Run etcd integration tests
test-etcd: _require-docker
    @just etcd-up
    ETCD_ENDPOINTS=http://127.0.0.1:2379 cargo nextest run -p gossip-coordination-etcd -- --ignored
    @echo "etcd integration tests complete"

# Run all integration tests
test-integration: test-etcd

# ── Prerequisites ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────

[private]
_require-docker:
    @docker version > /dev/null 2>&1 || \
        (echo "Error: Docker is not running. Please start Docker Desktop." && exit 1)
```

### Key design decisions

1. **`_require-docker` prefix convention**: Private recipes (prefixed with `_`) for prerequisite checks. Fail-fast with clear error messages.
2. **`set dotenv-load := true`**: Automatically loads `.env` file if present (useful for `ETCD_ENDPOINTS` override).
3. **etcd-up does NOT auto-down**: Developer may want etcd running for multiple test iterations. `etcd-down` is explicit.
4. **test-etcd starts etcd**: The `test-etcd` recipe ensures etcd is running before tests. Idempotent if already up.
5. **Naming convention**: `test-<service>` for service-specific integration tests. `test-integration` as umbrella.

## Implementation Guidance

### Files to Create
| File | Content | Rationale |
|------|---------|-----------|
| `Justfile` | Development recipes as described above | Task runner for common workflows |

### Patterns to Follow
- Vector project's Makefile (`make test-integration-<service>` naming pattern)
- TiKV's `make dev` as the "must pass before PR" target
- testcontainers-rs-modules-community Justfile as Rust ecosystem example
- Docker prerequisite checking with fail-fast error messages (common cross-project pattern)

### Dependencies
This task depends on the docker-compose.yml being in place (gossip-8972). The `just etcd-up` recipe calls `docker compose up -d etcd`.

## Code References

```yaml
# .github/workflows/ci.yml:66-79 — the quality gates to mirror locally
fmt:
    name: Format
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - run: cargo fmt --all -- --check
```

```toml
# .config/nextest.toml:9-22 — nextest profiles already configured
[profile.default]
test-threads = "num-cpus"
fail-fast = true
retries = 1
slow-timeout = { period = "30s", terminate-after = 4 }
```

## Related Work
| Task ID | Title | Relationship |
|---------|-------|-------------|
| gossip-8972 | Add docker-compose.yml for local etcd testing | Blocks — Justfile etcd recipes depend on compose file |
| gossip-8971 | B5 — etcd backend conformance + simulation hooks | Relates-to — B5 tests will be runnable via justfile recipes |

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `just check` runs fmt + check + clippy successfully
- [ ] `just test` runs all unit tests via nextest
- [ ] `just dev` runs the full PR-ready gate (check + test + doc)
- [ ] `just etcd-up` starts etcd and waits for health check
- [ ] `just etcd-down` stops and removes etcd
- [ ] `just test-etcd` runs the full integration test cycle (start etcd → run tests)
- [ ] `just _require-docker` fails with helpful message when Docker is not running
- [ ] `just --list` shows all available recipes with descriptions

## Pointers
- just manual: https://just.systems/man/en/
- casey/just GitHub: https://github.com/casey/just
- Existing nextest config: `.config/nextest.toml`
- Existing CI workflow: `.github/workflows/ci.yml`
notes:
## Done-Ledger Postgres Recipes (from Epic C - gossip-9006)

When implementing this task, also add Postgres recipes alongside the etcd ones. The Postgres recipes follow the same naming pattern.

### Recipes to add:

```just
# ── Postgres ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# Start local Postgres for integration testing
pg-up: _require-docker
    docker compose up -d postgres
    @echo "Waiting for Postgres to be healthy..."
    @docker compose exec postgres pg_isready -U postgres || \
        (echo "Postgres not ready yet, retrying..." && sleep 2 && \
         docker compose exec postgres pg_isready -U postgres)
    @echo "Postgres is ready at 127.0.0.1:5432"

# Stop local Postgres
pg-down:
    docker compose down

# Check Postgres health
pg-status:
    @docker compose ps
    @docker compose exec postgres pg_isready -U postgres

# Run Postgres integration tests
test-postgres: _require-docker
    @just pg-up
    GOSSIP_POSTGRES_TEST_URL="host=127.0.0.1 user=postgres password=postgres dbname=gossip_test" \
        cargo nextest run -p gossip-done-ledger-postgres -- --ignored
    @echo "Postgres integration tests complete"
```

Update `test-integration` umbrella recipe to include `test-postgres`:

```just
# Run all integration tests
test-integration: test-etcd test-postgres
```
