title: Generify coordination test fixture helpers over CoordinationBackend
description:
## Context

The coordination conformance test suite (gossip-8975 epic) needs backend-agnostic execution. This first sub-task converts the concrete-typed test fixture helpers from \`InMemoryCoordinator\` to generic trait bounds, enabling any \`CoordinationBackend\` implementor to use them.

The fixture module already has one generic helper (\`claim_result<B: ShardClaiming>\` at test_fixtures.rs:204), proving the pattern works. This task extends it to the remaining 5 operation helpers.

## Current State

### Operation helpers typed to InMemoryCoordinator

\`\`\`rust
// crates/gossip-coordination/src/test_fixtures.rs:260
pub fn acquire_shard(coord: &mut InMemoryCoordinator, t: u64, worker_id: u64) -> Lease {
    let mut scratch = crate::error::AcquireScratch::new();
    let result = coord
        .acquire_and_restore_into(now(t), test_tenant(), test_key(), test_worker(worker_id), &mut scratch)
        .expect("acquire should succeed");
    result.lease
}
\`\`\`

Similar concrete typing on:
- \`checkpoint_ok(coord: &mut InMemoryCoordinator, ...)\` (line 278)
- \`complete_ok(coord: &mut InMemoryCoordinator, ...)\` (line 295)
- \`park_ok(coord: &mut InMemoryCoordinator, ...)\` (line 312)
- \`do_split_replace(coord: &mut InMemoryCoordinator, ...)\` (line 376)

### Already-generic helper (pattern to follow)

\`\`\`rust
// crates/gossip-coordination/src/test_fixtures.rs:204
pub fn claim_result<B: ShardClaiming + Sized>(
    backend: &mut B,
    now: LogicalTime,
    tenant: TenantId,
    run: RunId,
    worker: WorkerId,
) -> Result<AcquireFixture, ClaimError> { ... }
\`\`\`

### Factory helpers (NOT changed by this task)

These construct \`InMemoryCoordinator\` instances and stay concrete:
- \`seeded_coordinator() -> InMemoryCoordinator\` (line 119)
- \`seeded_coordinator_with_semantics(CursorSemantics) -> InMemoryCoordinator\` (line 124)
- \`coordinator_with_run_and_lease() -> (InMemoryCoordinator, Lease)\` (line 341)

## Desired State

Convert the 5 operation helpers to generic trait bounds:

\`\`\`rust
pub fn acquire_shard<B: CoordinationBackend>(coord: &mut B, t: u64, worker_id: u64) -> Lease { ... }
pub fn checkpoint_ok<B: CoordinationBackend>(coord: &mut B, t: u64, lease: &Lease, cursor_key: &[u8], op_id: u64) { ... }
pub fn complete_ok<B: CoordinationBackend>(coord: &mut B, t: u64, lease: &Lease, cursor_key: &[u8], op_id: u64) { ... }
pub fn park_ok<B: CoordinationBackend>(coord: &mut B, t: u64, lease: &Lease, reason: ParkReason, op_id: u64) { ... }
pub fn do_split_replace<B: CoordinationBackend>(coord: &mut B, lease: &Lease) { ... }
\`\`\`

All methods called by these helpers (\`acquire_and_restore_into\`, \`checkpoint\`, \`complete\`, \`park_shard\`, \`split_replace\`) are on \`CoordinationBackend\`, so that is the minimum bound.

### No caller changes required

Since \`InMemoryCoordinator\` implements \`CoordinationBackend\`, all existing callers that pass \`&mut InMemoryCoordinator\` compile unchanged. The compiler infers the generic parameter.

title: Add CI pipeline job for etcd integration tests
description:
## Context

The gossip-rs CI pipeline (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) runs fmt, clippy, unit tests, docs, and nightly extended tests (Miri, Kani, Loom, ASAN) — but has no integration testing against external services. As the `EtcdCoordinator` backend gains test coverage via testcontainers and conformance harnesses, CI must run these tests to prevent regressions.

Research confirms the consensus pattern: separate CI jobs for unit tests (no Docker) and integration tests (Docker required). GitHub Actions `services:` containers provide the most efficient etcd provisioning for CI — they start in parallel with checkout/setup steps and are automatically managed.

## Current State

```yaml
# .github/workflows/ci.yml:40-64 — current job structure
jobs:
  changes:     # Path filtering
  fmt:         # cargo fmt --check
  clippy:      # cargo clippy
  test:        # cargo nextest run (unit tests only)
  doc:         # cargo doc
  nightly:     # Miri, Kani, Loom, ASAN (scheduled)
```

No `services:` block. No Docker usage. No integration test job. The etcd integration tests are `#[ignore]` and never run in CI.

```toml
# .config/nextest.toml — no test groups for integration tests
[profile.default]
test-threads = "num-cpus"
fail-fast = true
retries = 1
```

## Desired State

### 1. New CI job: `test-etcd`

```yaml
test-etcd:
  name: etcd Integration Tests
  runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
  timeout-minutes: 15
  if: ${{ always() && !cancelled() && (github.event_name != 'pull_request' || needs.changes.outputs.rust == 'true') }}
  needs: [changes, clippy]  # only run if clippy passes
  services:
    etcd:
      image: bitnami/etcd:3.5
      ports:
        - 2379:2379
      env:
        ALLOW_NONE_AUTHENTICATION: "yes"
        ETCD_ADVERTISE_CLIENT_URLS: http://localhost:2379
        ETCD_LISTEN_CLIENT_URLS: http://0.0.0.0:2379
      options: >-
        --health-cmd "etcdctl endpoint health --endpoints=http://localhost:2379"
        --health-interval 5s
        --health-timeout 3s
        --health-retries 10
        --health-start-period 5s
  steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v4
    - uses: ./.github/actions/setup-rust
    - name: Run etcd integration tests
      run: |
        cargo nextest run \
          -p gossip-coordination-etcd \
          --features test-support \
          --run-ignored=all \
          --profile ci
      env:
        ETCD_ENDPOINTS: http://127.0.0.1:2379
```

### 2. Nextest test group for etcd tests

```toml
# .config/nextest.toml additions
[test-groups]
etcd-integration = { max-threads = 4 }

[[profile.default.overrides]]
filter = 'package(gossip-coordination-etcd) & test(/etcd|integration/)'
test-group = 'etcd-integration'

[[profile.ci.overrides]]
filter = 'package(gossip-coordination-etcd) & test(/etcd|integration/)'
test-group = 'etcd-integration'
retries = 3  # integration tests may be flaky due to container timing
```

### 3. Design decisions

- **GitHub Actions `services:` over Docker Compose in CI**: Services start before job steps, health checks gate the job, lifecycle is automatic. Research (4 agents corroborate) confirms this is faster and simpler than running `docker compose` in CI steps.
- **Separate job from unit tests**: The `test` job runs without Docker (fast, no service deps). `test-etcd` runs with etcd (slower, Docker required). This matches sqlx's CI pattern.
- **`needs: [clippy]`**: Don't waste CI minutes on integration tests if basic checks fail.
- **`--run-ignored=all`**: The existing `#[ignore]` tests run when etcd is available. No need for feature-flag gating in CI.
- **`--profile ci`** with 3 retries: Integration tests are inherently more flaky (container timing, network). Generous retries in CI.
- **Linux only**: GitHub Actions `services:` are Linux-only. This is fine — CI runs on `ubuntu-24.04`.

## Implementation Guidance

### Files to Modify
| File | Change | Rationale |
|------|--------|-----------|
| `.github/workflows/ci.yml` | Add `test-etcd` job with `services:` block | Run etcd integration tests in CI |
| `.config/nextest.toml` | Add `etcd-integration` test group | Rate-limit integration tests |

### Patterns to Follow

The existing CI structure at `.github/workflows/ci.yml`:

```yaml
# Lines 65-79 — fmt job structure to follow
fmt:
  name: Format
  runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
  timeout-minutes: 5
  if: ${{ always() && !cancelled() && (github.event_name != 'pull_request' || needs.changes.outputs.rust == 'true') }}
  needs: [changes]
```

The existing custom action at `.github/actions/setup-rust/action.yml` handles toolchain, caching, sccache, and system deps (including `protobuf-compiler` for etcd-client). Reuse this.

### Key considerations

1. **Health check on etcd service**: The `options:` field maps to `docker run` flags. `etcdctl endpoint health` is the standard health probe. The `--health-start-period` gives etcd time to initialize before health checks begin.
2. **`ETCD_ENDPOINTS` env var**: The existing `local_backend()` helper reads this. Setting it in the CI job connects tests to the service container.
3. **Image tag pinning**: Use `bitnami/etcd:3.5` (minor-version pin). This provides patch-level updates automatically while preventing major version drift. For stricter pinning, use a specific patch version.
4. **Timeout**: 15 minutes is generous for integration tests. The unit test job uses the default timeout. Adjust based on observed durations.

## Code References

```yaml
# .github/workflows/ci.yml:80-130 — test job to model from
test:
  name: Test
  runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
  timeout-minutes: 20
  if: ${{ always() && !cancelled() && (github.event_name != 'pull_request' || needs.changes.outputs.rust == 'true') }}
  needs: [changes]
  steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@...
    - uses: ./.github/actions/setup-rust
    - name: Run tests
      run: cargo nextest run --features test-support,perf-stats --profile ci
```

title: Create Claude Code skills for integration test workflows
description:
## Context

As the gossip-rs project adds Docker-dependent testing infrastructure (etcd via Docker Compose and testcontainers-rs), agents need repeatable workflows for running, debugging, and maintaining integration tests. Custom Claude Code skills can encode these workflows as invocable commands, reducing friction and ensuring consistency.

## Current State

No testing-focused skills exist. The current skills are oriented toward code quality (doc-rigor, review-dispatch, unsafe-review), performance (perf-regression, bench-compare, asm-forge), simulation (sim-run, sim-scaffold), and research (deep-research, design-tournament).

## Desired State

### Skill 1: `run-integration-tests`

**Trigger**: `/run-integration-tests [--service=etcd] [--all]`

**Workflow**:
1. Check Docker availability (`docker version`)
2. Start required services (`docker compose up -d <service>` or verify testcontainers)
3. Wait for health check (poll etcd endpoint)
4. Run integration tests (`cargo nextest run -p gossip-coordination-etcd --run-ignored=all`)
5. Report results (pass/fail counts, failing test names)
6. On failure, capture diagnostics:
   - Docker container logs (`docker compose logs etcd`)
   - etcd health status
   - Test output with failure details
7. Offer cleanup (`docker compose down`)

**Why a skill and not just a justfile recipe**: The skill adds diagnostic intelligence — when tests fail, it can read container logs, check if the issue is infrastructure (etcd not ready, port conflict) vs logic (test assertion failure), and suggest fixes. A justfile recipe just runs commands.

### Skill 2: `etcd-dev`

**Trigger**: `/etcd-dev [status|start|stop|shell|logs|reset]`

**Workflow**:
- `status`: Check if etcd is running, show endpoint, version, key count
- `start`: `docker compose up -d etcd`, wait for health
- `stop`: `docker compose down`
- `shell`: Open `etcdctl` shell against local etcd (show useful commands)
- `logs`: Show recent etcd container logs
- `reset`: Wipe all keys under test namespace, restart if needed

**Why a skill**: Quick reference for etcd operations during development. Agents frequently need to inspect etcd state when debugging coordination backend issues.

### Skill 3: `test-infra-check`

**Trigger**: `/test-infra-check`

**Workflow**:
1. Check Docker installed and running
2. Check Docker Compose v2 available (`docker compose version`)
3. Check etcd image available locally (`docker image inspect`)
4. Check port 2379 not already bound
5. Check nextest installed
6. Check testcontainers dependency in Cargo.toml
7. Verify `.config/nextest.toml` has etcd test group
8. Report readiness status with fix instructions for any issues

**Why a skill**: One-command environment validation. Prevents wasted time debugging infrastructure issues vs code issues.

## Implementation Guidance

### Files to Create
| File | Content | Rationale |
|------|---------|-----------|
| `.claude/skills/run-integration-tests/SKILL.md` | Skill definition with workflow steps | Integration test orchestration |
| `.claude/skills/etcd-dev/SKILL.md` | Skill definition with sub-commands | etcd developer utilities |
| `.claude/skills/test-infra-check/SKILL.md` | Skill definition with check steps | Environment validation |

### Patterns to Follow

Existing skills follow the pattern in `.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md`:
- Clear trigger description
- Step-by-step workflow
- Tool usage instructions (which tools to use at each step)
- Error handling guidance
- Output format specification

### Skill Design Principles

1. **Diagnostic over prescriptive**: When something fails, skills should gather diagnostic information before suggesting fixes. Don't assume the cause of failure.
2. **Idempotent**: Running a skill twice should be safe. `docker compose up -d` is idempotent. Health checks can be repeated.
3. **Fail-fast with context**: If Docker isn't installed, say so immediately with install instructions. Don't attempt Docker operations that will fail cryptically.
4. **Leverage existing infrastructure**: Skills should use the Justfile recipes and docker-compose.yml, not bypass them.

## Related Work
| Task ID | Title | Relationship |
|---------|-------|-------------|
| gossip-8972 | Add docker-compose.yml for local etcd testing | Prerequisite — skills use compose |
| gossip-8973 | Add Justfile with dev recipes | Prerequisite — skills wrap justfile recipes |
| gossip-8974 | Add testcontainers-rs integration | Relates-to — skill provides diagnostic wrapper |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `etcd-dev` skill defined in `.claude/skills/etcd-dev/SKILL.md`
- [ ] `test-infra-check` skill defined in `.claude/skills/test-infra-check/SKILL.md`

- [ ] Each skill has clear trigger conditions, workflow steps, and error handling
- [ ] Skills leverage existing Justfile recipes and docker-compose.yml

- Skill creator guide: `.claude/skills/examples/skill-creator/SKILL.md`

title: Add failure-injection wrapper around etcd_client operations
description:
## Context

The etcd coordination backend makes RPCs to etcd (Get, Put, Txn, LeaseGrant,
LeaseKeepAlive, LeaseRevoke) through thin wrapper methods on `EtcdCoordinator`.
There is no mechanism to inject failures into these RPC paths for testing
retry logic, lease cleanup, or error-handling branches without a live etcd
cluster and network-level fault injection.

## Current State

All etcd RPCs flow through six wrapper methods in `backend.rs`:

- `etcd_get` (line 654) — wraps `client.get(key, options)`
- `etcd_txn` (line 669) — wraps `client.txn(txn)`
- `etcd_lease_grant` (line 680) — wraps `client.lease_grant(ttl, None)`
- `etcd_lease_keep_alive_once` (line 695) — wraps `client.lease_keep_alive(id)`
- `etcd_lease_revoke` (line 719) — wraps `client.lease_revoke(id)`
- Direct `client.put` call in `sync_owner_key` (line 1535)

Each wrapper clones `self.client`, calls `self.runtime.block_on(...)`, and
maps errors into `EtcdCoordinatorError::Etcd { operation, source }`.

There is no failure-injection layer anywhere in the etcd crate. The simulation
harness in `gossip-coordination` uses `InMemoryCoordinator` and does not
exercise the etcd RPC path.

## Desired State

A trait (or closure-based hook) that sits between `EtcdCoordinator` and the
raw `etcd_client::Client`, allowing tests to:

1. Inject transient RPC failures on specific operations (e.g., fail the 2nd
   `Txn` call but succeed on the 3rd).
2. Inject permanent failures (e.g., all `LeaseGrant` calls fail).
3. Inject latency (sleep before returning).
4. Count invocations per operation type.

This enables testing of:
- CAS retry loop exhaustion and `on_exhaustion` paths.
- Lease cleanup when `etcd_txn` fails after `etcd_lease_grant` succeeds.
- Graceful degradation on `lease_keep_alive` failure during `renew`.

## Implementation Guidance

**Approach A — Trait-based:** Define an `EtcdRpc` trait with methods matching
the six wrappers. `EtcdCoordinator` becomes generic over `R: EtcdRpc`.
Production uses `RealEtcdRpc` (the current wrapper logic). Tests use
`FailableEtcdRpc` with configurable failure schedules.

**Approach B — Closure hooks:** Add optional `Arc<dyn Fn(EtcdOperation) ->
Result<(), etcd_client::Error>>` fields to `EtcdCoordinator` that the wrappers
call before forwarding to the real client. Simpler but less composable.

**Files to modify:**
- `crates/gossip-coordination-etcd/src/backend.rs` — extract RPC dispatch
- Possibly a new `rpc.rs` module for the trait and implementations
- `crates/gossip-coordination-etcd/src/tests.rs` — add failure-injection tests

**Patterns to follow:** The `claim_candidates_scratch` field (line 470) shows
the project's pattern for test-supporting internal state on `EtcdCoordinator`.

## Code References

```rust
// backend.rs:654-666 — etcd_get wrapper
fn etcd_get(
    &self,
    key: impl Into<Vec<u8>>,
    options: Option<GetOptions>,
) -> Result<etcd_client::GetResponse, EtcdCoordinatorError> {
    let mut client = self.client.clone();
    self.runtime
        .block_on(client.get(key, options))
        .map_err(|source| EtcdCoordinatorError::Etcd {
            operation: EtcdOperation::Get,
            source,
        })
}

// backend.rs:669-677 — etcd_txn wrapper
fn etcd_txn(&self, txn: Txn) -> Result<etcd_client::TxnResponse, EtcdCoordinatorError> {
    let mut client = self.client.clone();
    self.runtime
        .block_on(client.txn(txn))
        .map_err(|source| EtcdCoordinatorError::Etcd {
            operation: EtcdOperation::Txn,
            source,
        })
}
```

## Related Work

- gossip-8982: Track pending leases for cleanup on CAS failure (tests lease
  cleanup paths that this wrapper would enable)
- gossip-8999: Extract reusable OptimisticTransaction abstraction (the retry
  logic that failure injection would exercise)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Failure injection mechanism compiles behind `#[cfg(test)]` or a feature
      gate (no production overhead).
- [ ] At least one test demonstrates injecting a transient `Txn` failure and
      verifying the CAS retry loop recovers.
- [ ] At least one test demonstrates injecting a `LeaseGrant` failure and
      verifying the correct error propagates.
- [ ] `cargo test --all-targets --all-features` passes.
- [ ] `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` passes.

## Pointers

- Wrapper methods: `backend.rs` lines 654–730
- Direct put call: `backend.rs` line 1535 (`sync_owner_key`)
- `EtcdOperation` enum: `error.rs` lines 35–54
- CAS retry loop: `backend.rs` lines 596–610

title: Add integration tests for load_shard_record atomic prefix-range scan
description:
## Context

The `load_shard_record` method already performs an atomic prefix-range scan,
fetching both the shard record and its `/owner` child key in a single etcd
RPC. This task adds targeted regression tests proving the single-RPC
atomicity guarantee and covering key edge cases (missing record, expired
owner, never-acquired shard).

## Current State

`load_shard_record` (`backend/coordinator.rs` lines 496–581) performs a
single prefix-range GET to atomically fetch both the shard record KV and
the optional `/owner` child KV:

```rust
// backend/coordinator.rs:508-511
let response = self.etcd_get(
    shard_record_key.clone().into_bytes(),
    Some(GetOptions::new().with_prefix()),
)?;
```

A loop at lines 516–522 classifies the returned KVs by exact key
comparison:
- `kv.key() == shard_record_key.as_bytes()` → record KV
- `kv.key() == owner_key.as_bytes()` → owner KV

The method comment (lines 479–488) documents this design:
> "Uses a single prefix-range GET on the shard record key. Because shard IDs
> are fixed-width 16-char hex and the only child key is `/owner`, the prefix
> scan returns exactly the record KV and (optionally) the owner KV."

The test wrapper `test_load_shard_snapshot` (`test_support.rs:283-291`)
directly calls `load_shard_record` and returns an `EtcdTestShardSnapshot`.
However, the snapshot type currently does **not** expose the `owner` field —
it only exposes `ShardRecord` via `Deref`. This must be fixed before the
owner-field assertions can compile.

## Desired State

### Prerequisite: Add owner accessor to `EtcdTestShardSnapshot`

Add an `owner_worker()` method to `EtcdTestShardSnapshot` in
`test_support.rs` that exposes the owner binding loaded by the atomic
prefix-range scan:

```rust
/// Return the owner binding loaded atomically with the shard record by
/// the prefix-range scan, if the `/owner` child key was present.
pub fn owner_worker(&self) -> Option<(WorkerId, FenceEpoch)> {
    self.inner.owner.as_ref().map(|o| (o.binding.worker, o.binding.fence))
}
```

This avoids widening `PersistedOwner` visibility (it is `pub(super)`) by
returning `(WorkerId, FenceEpoch)` — both already public types.

### Test cases

1. **Active owner present**: Register a shard, acquire it (creates the
   `/owner` key), then call `test_load_shard_snapshot`. Assert the record
   fields are correct AND `owner_worker()` returns `Some((worker, fence))`
   with the expected values.

2. **Owner TTL-expired**: Use `test_coordinator_with_ttl(5)`, acquire a
   shard, sleep 8+ seconds for the etcd lease to expire, then call
   `test_load_shard_snapshot`. Assert the `ShardRecord` is still present
   (the record key is not TTL-gated) but `owner_worker()` returns `None`.
   **Note**: `ShardRecord.lease` may still contain the stale lease holder —
   only the etcd `/owner` key is TTL-deleted.

3. **Non-existent shard**: Call `test_load_shard_snapshot` with a
   `ShardKey` that was never registered. Assert `Ok(None)`.

4. **Registered but never acquired**: Register a shard without acquiring
   it. Call `test_load_shard_snapshot`. Assert the record is present and
   `owner_worker()` returns `None`.

### Dropped: prefix-range isolation test

The proptest at `tests.rs:693-811` already proves prefix isolation
structurally: fixed-width 16-char hex encoding guarantees no shard ID is a
proper prefix of another. An integration test against live etcd would only
re-test etcd well-established `with_prefix()` semantics and adds no value.

### Existing coverage note

Some scenarios are partially covered by existing tests (e.g.,
`acquire_checkpoint_and_renew_round_trip` at tests.rs:1046 exercises
`test_load_shard_snapshot` after acquire). The tests in this task are
specifically targeted at the `owner_worker()` accessor to prove the atomic
prefix-range scan returns both the record and owner in one RPC — coverage
existing tests do not provide because the owner field was previously
inaccessible.

## Implementation Guidance

**Files to modify:**
- `crates/gossip-coordination-etcd/src/backend/test_support.rs` — add
  `owner_worker()` accessor to `EtcdTestShardSnapshot` (lines 50-78).
- `crates/gossip-coordination-etcd/src/tests.rs` — add integration tests.

**Test entry point:**
Use `test_load_shard_snapshot` (`test_support.rs:283-291`) — it directly
wraps `load_shard_record` and returns the snapshot. Do NOT use
`get_run_progress` (that calls `scan_run_shards`, a different code path).

**TTL expiry tests:**
Use `test_coordinator_with_ttl(5)` (established pattern, see
`lease_expiry_rejects_stale_checkpoint` at tests.rs:2121). etcd enforces a
minimum lease TTL of ~5 seconds; sleep for `ttl + 3` seconds (8s total).
Use `std::thread::sleep`, not `tokio::time::sleep` (tests run on sync
coordinators, not async runtimes).

**Test annotation:**
All integration tests must be `#[ignore = "requires Docker or ETCD_ENDPOINTS"]`.

**Test helpers available:**
- `test_coordinator()` — default coordinator (from `crate::test_etcd`)
- `test_coordinator_with_ttl(secs)` — custom lease TTL
- `test_tenant()` / `other_tenant()` — stable tenant identities (tests.rs:1925-1933)
- `test_run()` / `other_run()` — distinct run IDs (tests.rs:1936-1943)
- `test_shard()` — stable shard ID (tests.rs:1946)
- `test_worker(id)` — worker identity (tests.rs:1949)
- `now(t)` — logical timestamp constructor (tests.rs:1956)

## Code References

```rust
// backend/coordinator.rs:496-581 — load_shard_record (sync, pub(super))
pub(super) fn load_shard_record(
    &self,
    tenant: TenantId,
    key: ShardKey,
) -> Result<Option<PersistedShard>, EtcdCoordinatorError> {
    let shard_record_key = self
        .keyspace
        .shard_record_key(tenant, key.run(), key.shard());
    let owner_key = shard_record_key.owner_key();
    let response = self.etcd_get(
        shard_record_key.clone().into_bytes(),
        Some(GetOptions::new().with_prefix()),
    )?;
    // ... classify response KVs by exact key comparison ...
}

// test_support.rs:283-291 — test_load_shard_snapshot
pub fn test_load_shard_snapshot(
    &self,
    tenant: TenantId,
    key: ShardKey,
) -> Result<Option<EtcdTestShardSnapshot>, EtcdCoordinatorError> {
    Ok(self.load_shard_record(tenant, key)?.map(|inner| EtcdTestShardSnapshot { inner }))
}

// test_support.rs:50-78 — EtcdTestShardSnapshot (needs owner_worker accessor)
pub struct EtcdTestShardSnapshot {
    inner: PersistedShard,
}
impl Deref for EtcdTestShardSnapshot {
    type Target = ShardRecord;
    fn deref(&self) -> &Self::Target { &self.inner.record }
}

// backend.rs:282-287 — PersistedOwner (pub(super))
struct PersistedOwner {
    binding: OwnerLeaseValue,
    lease_id: i64,
}

// codec.rs:129-132 — OwnerLeaseValue (pub)
pub struct OwnerLeaseValue {
    pub worker: WorkerId,
    pub fence: FenceEpoch,
}
```

## Related Work

- gossip-8994: Add tenant isolation integration tests (CLOSED — implemented
  5 tenant isolation tests for scan, acquire, candidate, run listing, and
  run lookup isolation)
- Prefix isolation proptest: `tests.rs:693-811`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `EtcdTestShardSnapshot` gains `owner_worker(&self) -> Option<(WorkerId, FenceEpoch)>` in `test_support.rs`.
- [ ] Integration test: register + acquire a shard, `test_load_shard_snapshot` returns record with `owner_worker() == Some((worker, fence))`.
- [ ] Integration test: `test_coordinator_with_ttl(5)`, acquire, sleep 8s, `test_load_shard_snapshot` → `owner_worker()` returns `None`, record still present.
- [ ] Integration test: `test_load_shard_snapshot` on non-existent shard key → `Ok(None)`.
- [ ] Integration test: register (no acquire), `test_load_shard_snapshot` → record present, `owner_worker()` returns `None`.
- [ ] All tests `#[ignore]`d with `"requires Docker or ETCD_ENDPOINTS"`.

title: Reuse HashMap/Vec scratch buffers in scan_run_shards
description:
## Context

`scan_run_shards` allocates a fresh `HashMap` and `Vec` on every call to
classify etcd prefix-scan results. These are WARM-path allocations (called
during `list_shards_into`, `get_run_progress`, and `collect_claim_candidates_into`)
that could be reused across calls via scratch buffers on `EtcdCoordinator`.

## Current State

`scan_run_shards` (backend.rs lines 902–962) allocates per-call:

```rust
// backend.rs:913-914
let mut owner_map = HashMap::<Vec<u8>, PersistedOwner>::new();
let mut record_kvs = Vec::<(Vec<u8>, Vec<u8>, i64)>::new();
```

The `owner_map` collects owner KVs keyed by their etcd key bytes. The
`record_kvs` collects non-owner KVs as `(key, value, mod_revision)` tuples.
Both are populated in a loop over `response.kvs()` (lines 916–923), then
consumed in a second loop (lines 926–949) that decodes shard records and
pairs them with their owners.

Each call to `record_kvs.push(...)` at line 921 also clones the etcd key and
value bytes into owned `Vec<u8>`s.

The project already uses the `mem::take` + shrink + restore pattern for
`claim_candidates_scratch` (backend.rs lines 470, 3241–3250).

## Desired State

Add `scan_owner_map_scratch` and `scan_record_kvs_scratch` fields to
`EtcdCoordinator`, reused across `scan_run_shards` calls via the same
`mem::take` / shrink / restore pattern used for `claim_candidates_scratch`.

## Implementation Guidance

**Files to modify:**
- `crates/gossip-coordination-etcd/src/backend.rs`

**Pattern to follow** (existing at lines 3241–3250):
```rust
let mut candidates = std::mem::take(&mut self.claim_candidates_scratch);
// ... use candidates ...
if candidates.capacity() > 1024 && candidates.len() < candidates.capacity() / 4 {
    candidates.shrink_to(candidates.len().max(256));
}
self.claim_candidates_scratch = candidates;
```

**Steps:**
1. Add two fields to `EtcdCoordinator` struct (line 463):
   - `scan_owner_map_scratch: HashMap<Vec<u8>, PersistedOwner>`
   - `scan_record_kvs_scratch: Vec<(Vec<u8>, Vec<u8>, i64)>`
2. Initialize both as empty in `connect()`.
3. In `scan_run_shards`, `mem::take` at entry, `.clear()` before use,
   and restore at exit with capacity shrink guard.
4. The HashMap's `clear()` retains its bucket allocation; `Vec::clear()`
   retains capacity. Both avoid re-allocation on subsequent calls.

**Allocation tier:** WARM (frequent read/query operations). Simplicity-first
is acceptable, but these are called in claim loops so reuse is worthwhile.

## Code References

```rust
// backend.rs:902-962 — scan_run_shards
fn scan_run_shards(
    &self,
    tenant: TenantId,
    run: RunId,
) -> Result<Vec<PersistedShard>, EtcdCoordinatorError> {
    let prefix = self.keyspace.shard_records_scan_prefix(tenant, run);
    let response = self.etcd_get(prefix.into_bytes(), Some(GetOptions::new().with_prefix()))?;

    let mut owner_map = HashMap::<Vec<u8>, PersistedOwner>::new();        // line 913
    let mut record_kvs = Vec::<(Vec<u8>, Vec<u8>, i64)>::new();            // line 914
    // ... populate from response.kvs() ...
}

// backend.rs:463-471 — struct with existing scratch
pub struct EtcdCoordinator {
    // ...
    claim_candidates_scratch: Vec<ShardId>,  // line 470
}
```

## Related Work

- gossip-8987: Pre-allocate owner key buffer in scan_run_shards (addresses
  per-shard String clone in the same method's inner loop)
- gossip-8989: Pool decode ByteSlab across operations (addresses per-shard
  slab allocation in the same method's inner loop)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `scan_owner_map_scratch` and `scan_record_kvs_scratch` fields added to
      `EtcdCoordinator`.
- [ ] `scan_run_shards` reuses both buffers via `mem::take` + clear + restore.
- [ ] Capacity shrink guard prevents unbounded growth.
- [ ] Existing integration tests pass unchanged.
- [ ] `cargo test --all-targets --all-features` passes.
- [ ] `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` passes.

## Pointers

- `scan_run_shards`: `backend.rs` lines 902–962
- Scratch reuse pattern: `backend.rs` lines 3241–3250
- `EtcdCoordinator` struct: `backend.rs` lines 463–471

title: Add clock regression detection in lease validation
description:
## Context

Lease validation compares the caller's `now` timestamp against persisted
deadlines to determine lease expiry. If the caller provides a `now` value
that is less than a previously provided value for the same shard, lease
operations may silently produce incorrect results. There is currently no
detection of caller-provided time regression.

**Note:** `LogicalTime` is explicitly *not* wall-clock time — it is an
abstract, monotonically increasing counter used for lease expiration,
Lamport timestamps, and deterministic simulation clocks
(`gossip-contracts/src/identity/coordination.rs:169-177`). The coordination
layer has no internal clock; `now` is always caller-provided through the
trait interface. This means "clock regression" is actually "the caller
passed a non-monotonic `now` value," not an NTP or VM-migration issue.

## Current State

### Lease validation

`validate_lease` (`validation.rs:114-180`) checks five conditions in priority
order: tenant isolation, terminal status, fence epoch, lease expiry, and
owner divergence. The only time-related checks are:

```rust
// validation.rs:122-125 — precondition
assert!(
    now > LogicalTime::ZERO,
    "validate_lease: now must be > ZERO"
);

// validation.rs:157-158 — expiry check
if now >= deadline {
    return Err(CoordError::LeaseExpired { deadline, now });
}
```

There is no check that `now >= previously_observed_now`.

### Deadline computation

Every lease-granting path (acquire and renew) computes the new deadline as:

```rust
let deadline = now
    .checked_add(lease_duration)
    .unwrap_or(LogicalTime::from_raw(u64::MAX));
```

This appears in:
- `InMemoryCoordinator::acquire_and_restore_into` (`in_memory.rs:1120-1122`)
- `InMemoryCoordinator::renew` (`in_memory.rs:1174-1176`)
- `EtcdCoordinator::acquire_and_restore_into` (`shard_coordination.rs:193-195`)
- `EtcdCoordinator::renew` (`shard_coordination.rs:375-377`)
- Async variants mirror the same formula.

### `visible_now` helper

`visible_now` (`backend.rs:572-586`) determines the effective observation
time for `ShardFilter` evaluation in `list_shards_into` and
`get_run_progress`. It is NOT part of the lease validation path and does
not need a regression guard:

```rust
fn visible_now(persisted: &PersistedShard, now: LogicalTime) -> LogicalTime {
    if persisted.owner_is_live_at(now) {
        now
    } else {
        persisted.record.lease_deadline().unwrap_or(now)
    }
}
```

`owner_is_live_at` is defined at `backend.rs:314-323`.

### `WorkerSession`

`WorkerSession` (`session.rs:178-207`) is the per-shard session wrapper.
Each session corresponds to exactly one shard. It holds:

```rust
pub struct WorkerSession<'b, B: CoordinationBackend> {
    backend:  &'b mut B,
    tenant:   TenantId,
    worker:   WorkerId,
    lease:    Lease,           // contains deadline, updated by renew()
    snapshot: SnapshotState,
    capacity: CapacityHint,
}
```

Six methods accept `now: LogicalTime`:
- `new` (line 241) — constructor, calls `acquire_and_restore_into`
- `renew` (line 482) — extends lease deadline
- `checkpoint` (line 531) — persists cursor progress
- `complete` (line 556) — terminal, marks shard `Done`
- `park` (line 583) — terminal, marks shard `Parked`
- `split_replace` (line 612) — terminal, replaces parent with children
- `split_residual` (line 663) — narrows parent key range

The session already asserts that `renew` produces a deadline after `now`
(`session.rs:486`):

```rust
assert!(result.new_deadline > now, "renewal deadline not after now");
```

But it does NOT track `now` across calls, so it cannot detect regression.

### How `now` enters the system

Every `now: LogicalTime` value is caller-provided through the trait
interface. The call chain is:

```
Application code
  -> WorkerSession::renew(now) / checkpoint(now) / ...   [session.rs]
    -> CoordinationBackend::renew(now, ...) / ...         [traits.rs]
      -> validate_lease(now, ...)                         [validation.rs]
```

All 7 methods on `CoordinationBackend` (traits.rs:265-596) and all 7 on
`AsyncCoordinationBackend` (traits.rs:644-702) accept `now: LogicalTime`
as their first real parameter. `ShardClaiming::claim_next_available`
(facade.rs:436) also accepts `now`.

## The Regression Scenario

1. Worker acquires shard at `now=100`, `lease_duration=60` → deadline=160.
2. Worker renews at `now=120` → `validate_lease` passes (120 < 160),
   new deadline = 120 + 60 = 180. Correct.
3. Caller provides regressed `now=105`.
4. Worker renews at `now=105` → `validate_lease` passes (105 < 180),
   new deadline = 105 + 60 = 165.

**Impact:** The deadline silently dropped from 180 to 165. The lease
lost 15 ticks of duration. Repeated regressions progressively erode the
lease, potentially causing premature expiry while the worker believes
it is safely renewed. The `validate_lease` check (`now < deadline`)
does not catch this because a regressed `now` is *more* likely to pass
the check, not less.

## Desired State

Detect when `now` regresses below a previously observed value for the
same shard, and either warn or error before the regression silently
corrupts deadline calculations.

## Implementation Guidance

### Recommended approach: `WorkerSession`-level high-water mark

Add a `last_observed_now: LogicalTime` field to `WorkerSession`. Check
monotonicity at the top of every `now`-accepting method.

**Why `WorkerSession` is the right level:**
- Each session = exactly one shard. No cross-shard false positives.
- Every `now`-accepting method goes through the session, so the guard
  applies to all operations (renew, checkpoint, complete, park, split).
- Works identically for all backends (InMemory, Etcd, future ones).
- The check happens BEFORE calling into the backend, catching regression
  early.

**What about callers that bypass `WorkerSession`?**
The module docs (session.rs:63) state that direct `CoordinationBackend`
usage is supported for multi-shard workers. Those callers bypass
`WorkerSession` and are responsible for their own correctness. A
`debug_assert` in `validate_lease` provides defense-in-depth for
direct callers in debug/test builds.

### Files to modify

**`crates/gossip-coordination/src/session.rs`:**
1. Add `last_observed_now: LogicalTime` field to `WorkerSession` (line 207).
2. Initialize to `now` in the `new` constructor (after line 250).
3. Initialize to `lease.deadline()` in `from_acquire_result` (this
   constructor does not receive `now`, but the deadline was computed
   from the acquire-time `now`, so it's a safe lower bound. Alternatively,
   use `LogicalTime::ZERO` and skip the first check).
4. Add a private helper method:
   ```rust
   fn check_time_monotonicity(&mut self, now: LogicalTime) {
       if now < self.last_observed_now {
           tracing::warn!(
               shard = %self.lease.shard_key(),
               worker = %self.worker,
               last_now = self.last_observed_now.as_raw(),
               current_now = now.as_raw(),
               "caller-provided LogicalTime regressed; \
                lease deadline computation may be incorrect"
           );
           debug_assert!(
               now >= self.last_observed_now,
               "WorkerSession: now ({now:?}) < last_observed_now ({:?})",
               self.last_observed_now,
           );
       }
       self.last_observed_now = now;
   }
   ```
5. Call `self.check_time_monotonicity(now)` at the top of: `renew`,
   `checkpoint`, `complete`, `park`, `split_replace`, `split_residual`.
   Do NOT call it in constructors (the constructor sets the initial value).

**`crates/gossip-coordination/src/validation.rs`:**
6. Add a `debug_assert!` in `validate_lease` as defense-in-depth for
   direct backend callers. This requires an optional `previous_now`
   parameter or a separate function. The simplest option is a standalone
   `debug_assert_time_monotonic(now, previous_now)` utility that
   backend implementations can call, but this is optional scope.

### Edge cases to handle

| Edge case | Expected behavior |
|-----------|-------------------|
| First call after `new()` | `now` from constructor sets baseline. First operation call cannot regress below it. |
| First call after `from_acquire_result()` | No `now` available at construction. Use `LogicalTime::ZERO` as baseline (no check fires on first operation). |
| `now == last_observed_now` (equal, not less) | NOT a regression. Same `now` is valid (e.g., checkpoint + complete in the same tick). Only `now < last_observed_now` triggers the guard. |
| Tests passing arbitrary `now` values | `debug_assert` will catch regressions in test builds. Tests that deliberately regress time (if any) need updating. |
| Simulation testing with deterministic clocks | Simulation clocks are monotonic by construction, so the guard should never fire. Compatible. |
| CAS retry loops in etcd backend | `now` is captured once at the start of each trait method call and reused across retries. No regression within a single operation. |
| `split_residual` (non-terminal, keeps session) | Same session continues. `last_observed_now` carries over naturally. |

### Behavioral choice: warn vs error

The recommended approach is **warn + debug_assert** (not a hard error):

- **`tracing::warn!`** in release builds — logs the regression for
  operational visibility without breaking the caller.
- **`debug_assert!`** in debug/test builds — panics, catching caller
  bugs early in development and CI.
- A hard `CoordError` variant is NOT recommended at this stage because:
  (a) it would require adding a new variant to `CoordError` and updating
  all 6 operation-specific error types that wrap it, and (b) the
  regression is a caller bug, not a protocol error — `assert` is the
  appropriate Rust idiom for precondition violations.

If a hard error is desired later, `CoordError` is `#[non_exhaustive]`
(error.rs:217), so a `TimeRegression` variant can be added without
breaking downstream match arms.

## Code References

```rust
// session.rs:178-207 — WorkerSession struct (add field here)
pub struct WorkerSession<'b, B: CoordinationBackend> {
    backend:  &'b mut B,
    tenant:   TenantId,
    worker:   WorkerId,
    lease:    Lease,
    snapshot: SnapshotState,
    capacity: CapacityHint,
    // ADD: last_observed_now: LogicalTime,
}

// session.rs:241-250 — new() constructor (initialize field here)
pub fn new(
    backend: &'b mut B,
    now: LogicalTime,
    tenant: TenantId,
    key: ShardKey,
    worker: WorkerId,
) -> Result<Self, AcquireError> {

// session.rs:316 — from_acquire_result (no `now` parameter)
pub fn from_acquire_result(backend: &'b mut B, acquired: AcquireResultView<'_>) -> Self {

// session.rs:482-495 — renew (add check here, before backend call)
pub fn renew(&mut self, now: LogicalTime) -> Result<RenewResult, RenewError> {
    let fence_before = self.lease.fence();
    let result = self.backend.renew(now, self.tenant, &self.lease)?;
    assert!(result.new_deadline > now, "renewal deadline not after now");
    // ...
}

// session.rs:486 — existing assert (checks deadline > now, not monotonicity)
assert!(result.new_deadline > now, "renewal deadline not after now");

// validation.rs:114-180 — validate_lease (defense-in-depth debug_assert)
pub fn validate_lease(
    now: LogicalTime,
    tenant: TenantId,
    lease: &Lease,
    record: &ShardRecord,
) -> Result<(), CoordError> {

// in_memory.rs:1174-1176 — deadline computation (affected by regression)
let deadline = now
    .checked_add(lease_duration)
    .unwrap_or(LogicalTime::from_raw(u64::MAX));

// shard_coordination.rs:375-377 — etcd deadline computation (same formula)
let new_deadline = now
    .checked_add(lease_duration)
    .unwrap_or(LogicalTime::from_raw(u64::MAX));

// identity/coordination.rs:169-179 — LogicalTime definition
/// Monotonic logical clock for lease expiration and ordering.
///
/// `LogicalTime` is not wall-clock time — it is an abstract, monotonically
/// increasing counter used for lease expiration, Lamport timestamps, and
/// deterministic simulation clocks.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash)]
pub struct LogicalTime(u64);

// error.rs:217 — CoordError (non_exhaustive, can add variants)
#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
#[non_exhaustive]
pub enum CoordError { ... }
```

## Related Work

- gossip-8996 (CLOSED): Infra-error propagation — already implemented.
  If a hard `CoordError::TimeRegression` variant is added in the future,
  the infrastructure for structured error propagation is already in place.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `WorkerSession` stores a `last_observed_now: LogicalTime` field.
- [ ] `WorkerSession::new` initializes `last_observed_now` to the
      constructor's `now` parameter.
- [ ] `WorkerSession::from_acquire_result` initializes `last_observed_now`
      to `LogicalTime::ZERO` (or the lease deadline as a conservative bound).
- [ ] Every `now`-accepting method on `WorkerSession` (`renew`,
      `checkpoint`, `complete`, `park`, `split_replace`, `split_residual`)
      calls `check_time_monotonicity(now)` before forwarding to the backend.
- [ ] `check_time_monotonicity` emits `tracing::warn!` when
      `now < last_observed_now`.
- [ ] `check_time_monotonicity` includes a `debug_assert!` that panics
      in debug builds on regression.
- [ ] Equal values (`now == last_observed_now`) do NOT trigger the guard.
- [ ] `last_observed_now` is updated to `now` on every call (even on
      regression, to avoid repeated warnings for the same baseline).
- [ ] Unit test: create a session, call `renew(now=100)`, then
      `checkpoint(now=90)`. Verify:
      - In debug builds: panics with a clear message.
      - If `debug_assert` is disabled: the warn log is emitted
        (use `tracing-test` or similar).
- [ ] Unit test: `renew(now=100)`, then `renew(now=100)` (equal values).
      Verify no warning or panic.
- [ ] Unit test: `renew(now=100)`, then `checkpoint(now=110)`, then
      `complete(now=120)`. Verify no warning or panic (monotonic sequence).
- [ ] `cargo check` across the entire workspace succeeds.
- [ ] `cargo test --all-targets --all-features` passes (no existing test
      regressions — check that no existing test passes non-monotonic `now`
      values to `WorkerSession` methods).
- [ ] `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` passes.
- [ ] `cargo fmt --all --check` passes.

title: Restrict codec exports to pub(crate)
description:
## Context

The codec module re-exports several types in `lib.rs` that are not used by any
crate outside `gossip-coordination-etcd`, with the exception of two fuzz targets.
Restricting visibility where possible narrows the public API surface.

## Current State

`lib.rs` (lines 69–72) re-exports:

```rust
pub use codec::{
    BlobKind, EtcdCodecError, OwnerLeaseValue, decode_owner_value, decode_run_record,
    decode_shard_record, encode_owner_value, encode_run_record, encode_shard_record,
};
```

All codec public items in `codec.rs`:
- `pub enum BlobKind` (line 103) — 3 variants
- `pub struct OwnerLeaseValue` (line 129) — 2 public fields (`worker`, `fence`)
- `pub enum EtcdCodecError` (line 141) — 11 error variants, `#[non_exhaustive]`
- `pub fn encode_run_record` (line 253)
- `pub fn encode_shard_record_into` (line 274) — not re-exported from `lib.rs`
- `pub fn encode_owner_value_into` (line 343) — not re-exported from `lib.rs`
- `pub fn decode_run_record` (line 366)
- `pub fn encode_shard_record` (line 384)
- `pub fn decode_shard_record` (line 411)
- `pub fn encode_owner_value` (line 424)
- `pub fn decode_owner_value` (line 434)

### Internal consumers (all via `use crate::codec::...`)

- `backend.rs:77-79` — `EtcdCodecError`, `OwnerLeaseValue`, `decode_owner_value`,
  `encode_owner_value`, `encode_shard_record`
- `backend/coordinator.rs:57` — `EtcdCodecError`, `decode_run_record`,
  `decode_shard_record`, `encode_run_record`
- `backend/run_management.rs:47` — `encode_run_record`, `encode_shard_record_into`
- `backend/shard_coordination.rs:64` — `encode_owner_value_into`,
  `encode_shard_record`, `encode_shard_record_into`
- `backend/test_support.rs:11` — `encode_run_record`, `encode_shard_record`
- `error.rs:24` — `EtcdCodecError`

### External consumers (fuzz targets)

- `fuzz/fuzz_targets/fuzz_decode_run_record.rs:3` —
  `use gossip_coordination_etcd::decode_run_record;`
- `fuzz/fuzz_targets/fuzz_decode_shard_record.rs:3` —
  `use gossip_coordination_etcd::decode_shard_record;`

These fuzz targets are separate compilation units that depend on the crate
externally, so the items they import must remain `pub` and re-exported
from `lib.rs`.

## Desired State

### Items that MUST stay `pub` + re-exported (fuzz target consumers)

| Item | Line | Reason |
|------|------|--------|
| `decode_run_record` | 366 | fuzz target `fuzz_decode_run_record` |
| `decode_shard_record` | 411 | fuzz target `fuzz_decode_shard_record` |

### Items to change to `pub(crate)` (no external consumers)

| Item | Line |
|------|------|
| `BlobKind` | 103 |
| `OwnerLeaseValue` | 129 |
| `OwnerLeaseValue.worker` field | 130 |
| `OwnerLeaseValue.fence` field | 131 |
| `EtcdCodecError` | 141 |
| `encode_run_record` | 253 |
| `encode_shard_record_into` | 274 |
| `encode_owner_value_into` | 343 |
| `encode_shard_record` | 384 |
| `encode_owner_value` | 424 |
| `decode_owner_value` | 434 |

### `lib.rs` re-export block

Replace the current 4-line re-export block with only the two fuzz-required items:

```rust
pub use codec::{decode_run_record, decode_shard_record};
```

## Implementation Guidance

**Files to modify:**
- `crates/gossip-coordination-etcd/src/lib.rs` — shrink codec re-exports to
  only `decode_run_record` and `decode_shard_record`
- `crates/gossip-coordination-etcd/src/codec.rs` — change the 11 items listed
  in the table above from `pub` to `pub(crate)`, including the two
  `OwnerLeaseValue` fields

**Steps:**
1. In `lib.rs`, replace lines 69–72 with:
   `pub use codec::{decode_run_record, decode_shard_record};`
2. In `codec.rs`, for each item in the "change to `pub(crate)`" table, replace
   `pub` with `pub(crate)`.
3. For `OwnerLeaseValue`, also change the field visibility:
   `pub worker` -> `pub(crate) worker`, `pub fence` -> `pub(crate) fence`.
4. Run `cargo check` across the full workspace to confirm no breakage.
5. Run `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`.

**Risk:** Low. The only external consumers are the two fuzz targets, and those
are preserved. All other consumers use `crate::codec::` internal paths.

## Code References

```rust
// lib.rs:69-72 — current re-exports (to be shrunk)
pub use codec::{
    BlobKind, EtcdCodecError, OwnerLeaseValue, decode_owner_value, decode_run_record,
    decode_shard_record, encode_owner_value, encode_run_record, encode_shard_record,
};

// fuzz/fuzz_targets/fuzz_decode_run_record.rs:3 — external consumer
use gossip_coordination_etcd::decode_run_record;

// fuzz/fuzz_targets/fuzz_decode_shard_record.rs:3 — external consumer
use gossip_coordination_etcd::decode_shard_record;

// backend.rs:77-79 — internal consumer
use crate::codec::{
    EtcdCodecError, OwnerLeaseValue, decode_owner_value, encode_owner_value, encode_shard_record,
};

// backend/coordinator.rs:57 — internal consumer
use crate::codec::{EtcdCodecError, decode_run_record, decode_shard_record, encode_run_record};

// backend/run_management.rs:47 — internal consumer
use crate::codec::{encode_run_record, encode_shard_record_into};

// backend/shard_coordination.rs:64 — internal consumer
use crate::codec::{encode_owner_value_into, encode_shard_record, encode_shard_record_into};

// backend/test_support.rs:11 — internal consumer
use crate::codec::{encode_run_record, encode_shard_record};

// error.rs:24 — internal consumer
use crate::codec::EtcdCodecError;
```

## Related Work

None found.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `decode_run_record` and `decode_shard_record` remain `pub` and are
      re-exported from `lib.rs`.
- [ ] All other codec types and functions are `pub(crate)`, not `pub`.
- [ ] `OwnerLeaseValue` fields (`worker`, `fence`) are `pub(crate)`.
- [ ] `lib.rs` re-exports only `decode_run_record` and `decode_shard_record`
      from the codec module.
- [ ] `cargo check` across the entire workspace succeeds.
- [ ] `cargo test --all-targets --all-features` passes.
- [ ] `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` passes.
- [ ] Fuzz targets compile: `cargo +nightly fuzz check` (if nightly available).

## Pointers

- `lib.rs` re-exports: lines 69–72
- `codec.rs` public items: lines 103, 129, 141, 253, 274, 343, 366, 384,
  411, 424, 434
- Internal consumers: `backend.rs:77`, `backend/coordinator.rs:57`,
  `backend/run_management.rs:47`, `backend/shard_coordination.rs:64`,
  `backend/test_support.rs:11`, `error.rs:24`
- Fuzz targets: `fuzz/fuzz_targets/fuzz_decode_run_record.rs`,
  `fuzz/fuzz_targets/fuzz_decode_shard_record.rs`

title: Enhance credential redaction in config Debug impl
Verify etcd_client::Client clone cost, document or optimize
description:
## Context

Every etcd RPC wrapper in `EtcdCoordinator` clones `self.client` before
calling async methods. If `etcd_client::Client::clone()` is expensive (deep
copy of connection state), this adds overhead on every RPC. If it's cheap
(Arc refcount bump), the current pattern is fine but should be documented.

## Current State

`EtcdCoordinator` stores the client directly (backend.rs line 467):

```rust
pub struct EtcdCoordinator {
    // ...
    client: etcd_client::Client,
    // ...
}
```

Every RPC wrapper clones before use:

```rust
// backend.rs:659 — etcd_get
let mut client = self.client.clone();
self.runtime.block_on(client.get(key, options))

// backend.rs:670 — etcd_txn
let mut client = self.client.clone();
self.runtime.block_on(client.txn(txn))

// backend.rs:684 — etcd_lease_grant
let mut client = self.client.clone();
self.runtime.block_on(client.lease_grant(ttl, None))
```

Clone sites: lines 557, 659, 670, 684, 696, 723, 1533.

The crate uses `etcd-client = "0.18"` (Cargo.toml line 19). The `etcd-client`
0.18 `Client` struct internally holds `Arc<Channel>` from tonic, making
`.clone()` an O(1) Arc refcount increment — NOT a deep copy. No new TCP
connections are created.

## Desired State

1. Add a code comment on the `client` field or near the first clone site
   documenting that `Client::clone()` is O(1) (Arc-based) and does not
   create new connections.
2. Optionally, verify this claim by checking `etcd-client` 0.18 source or
   docs and citing the relevant line/doc.

## Implementation Guidance

**Files to modify:**
- `crates/gossip-coordination-etcd/src/backend.rs` — add doc comment

**Minimal change:**
```rust
/// etcd gRPC client. Clone is O(1) — internally `Arc<Channel>` from tonic.
/// Each wrapper method clones to satisfy the `&mut self` requirement of
/// etcd-client's async methods while keeping `EtcdCoordinator` methods
/// callable with `&self`.
client: etcd_client::Client,
```

**Verification step:** Inspect `etcd-client` 0.18 source to confirm
`Client` contains `Arc<KvClient>` / `Arc<LeaseClient>` etc. Document the
specific field or struct.

## Code References

```rust
// backend.rs:463-471 — struct definition
pub struct EtcdCoordinator {
    config: EtcdCoordinatorConfig,
    keyspace: EtcdKeyspace,
    runtime: tokio::runtime::Runtime,
    client: etcd_client::Client,           // line 467
    claim_candidates_scratch: Vec<ShardId>,
}

// Cargo.toml:19
etcd-client = { version = "0.18", default-features = false }
```

## Related Work

None.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Doc comment on `client` field documents clone cost and rationale.
- [ ] Verification note cites the `etcd-client` source confirming Arc-based
      internals.
- [ ] No code behavior changes.
- [ ] `cargo test --all-targets --all-features` passes.
- [ ] `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` passes.

## Pointers

- `client` field: `backend.rs` line 467
- Clone sites: `backend.rs` lines 557, 659, 670, 684, 696, 723, 1533
- `etcd-client` version: `Cargo.toml` line 19

title: Pre-allocate owner key buffer in scan_run_shards
description:
## Context

Inside the `scan_run_shards` inner loop, each shard iteration clones the
record key `Vec<u8>` and appends `/owner` to construct the owner-key lookup.
This allocation can be avoided by pre-allocating a single owner-key buffer
and reusing it across iterations.

## Current State

In `scan_run_shards` (backend.rs lines 926–949), the inner loop at lines
935–937:

```rust
let mut owner_key = record_key.clone();        // line 935 — Vec<u8> clone per shard
owner_key.extend_from_slice(b"/owner");        // line 936 — extend
let owner = owner_map.remove(&owner_key);      // line 937 — HashMap lookup
```

`record_key` is a `Vec<u8>` from the etcd response. Each iteration clones
it (~100–150 bytes for a typical keyspace path), extends with 6 bytes, uses
it for a HashMap lookup, then drops it.

The keyspace module already provides `_into` variants that append to a
caller-owned buffer (keyspace.rs lines 385–394), but `scan_run_shards`
works with raw bytes from etcd responses, not keyspace-constructed strings.

## Desired State

Pre-allocate a single `Vec<u8>` before the loop and reuse it:

```rust
let mut owner_key_buf = Vec::with_capacity(256);
for (record_key, value, mod_revision) in record_kvs {
    owner_key_buf.clear();
    owner_key_buf.extend_from_slice(&record_key);
    owner_key_buf.extend_from_slice(b"/owner");
    let owner = owner_map.remove(&owner_key_buf[..]);
    // ...
}
```

## Implementation Guidance

**Files to modify:**
- `crates/gossip-coordination-etcd/src/backend.rs` — `scan_run_shards` method

**Steps:**
1. Before the decode loop (around line 926), allocate:
   `let mut owner_key_buf = Vec::with_capacity(256);`
2. Replace lines 935–937 with clear + extend + lookup using the buffer.
3. The `HashMap::remove` call needs `&Vec<u8>` or `&[u8]` — verify the
   HashMap key type allows lookup by slice. Since keys are `Vec<u8>`,
   `HashMap::remove` with `&[u8]` works because `Vec<u8>: Borrow<[u8]>`.

**Alternatively**, this buffer could be a scratch field on `EtcdCoordinator`
(combined with gossip-8980), but a local allocation is simpler and sufficient
since the capacity is small and the loop runs once per scan call.

**Allocation tier:** WARM — per-scan, not per-shard.

## Code References

```rust
// backend.rs:926-949 — inner loop
let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(record_kvs.len());
for (record_key, value, mod_revision) in record_kvs {
    let mut slab = Self::make_decode_slab(value.len());
    let record = decode_shard_record(&value, &mut slab).map_err(|source| { ... })?;

    let mut owner_key = record_key.clone();        // line 935
    owner_key.extend_from_slice(b"/owner");        // line 936
    let owner = owner_map.remove(&owner_key);      // line 937
    // ...
}
```

## Related Work

- gossip-8980: Reuse HashMap/Vec scratch buffers in scan_run_shards (addresses
  the outer-level allocations in the same method)
- gossip-8989: Pool decode ByteSlab across operations (addresses the per-shard
  slab allocation at line 927)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `record_key.clone()` removed from inner loop.
- [ ] Owner key constructed via reusable buffer.
- [ ] Existing integration tests pass unchanged.
- [ ] `cargo test --all-targets --all-features` passes.
- [ ] `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` passes.

## Pointers

- Inner loop: `backend.rs` lines 926–949
- Owner key clone: `backend.rs` lines 935–937
- HashMap key type: `HashMap<Vec<u8>, PersistedOwner>` at line 913

title: Batch large shard registrations into chunked transactions
description:
## Context

`register_shards` currently rejects batches exceeding 41 shards with
`ResourceExhausted`, forcing callers to pre-split large registrations. The
limit comes from etcd's default 128-op transaction budget: each shard
needs 3 ops (1 compare + 2 puts), plus 3 fixed ops for the run record.

## Current State

The check at backend.rs lines 2695–2699:

```rust
if shards.len() > MAX_SHARDS_PER_ETCD_TXN {
    return Err(RegisterShardsError::ResourceExhausted {
        resource: "etcd_txn_ops",
    });
}
```

`MAX_SHARDS_PER_ETCD_TXN = 41` (line 126), derived from:
- Fixed overhead: 3 ops (1 compare-run-revision + 1 put-run-record + 1 put-run-active-index)
- Per-shard: 3 ops (1 compare-absent + 1 put-shard-record + 1 put-active-index)
- Budget: `(128 - 3) / 3 = 41`

The method builds all comparisons and puts in a single transaction
(lines 2769–2815) and submits as one `etcd_txn` call.

An integration test at tests.rs lines 740–778 verifies the rejection:
```rust
fn register_shards_rejects_batch_exceeding_etcd_txn_limit() {
    // 42 shards exceed the MAX_SHARDS_PER_ETCD_TXN limit of 41.
}
```

## Desired State

Instead of rejecting large batches, chunk them into multiple transactions
of at most 41 shards each. The first chunk includes the run-record update;
subsequent chunks use the updated run revision as their CAS precondition.

## Implementation Guidance

**Files to modify:**
- `crates/gossip-coordination-etcd/src/backend.rs` — `register_shards` method
- `crates/gossip-coordination-etcd/src/tests.rs` — update rejection test,
  add chunked-registration test

**Key design decisions:**
1. **Atomicity:** Individual chunks are atomic (etcd txn), but the overall
   registration is NOT atomic across chunks. If chunk 2 fails after chunk 1
   committed, the run has partial shards. The method must either:
   - (a) Accept partial registration and return partial results, OR
   - (b) Attempt cleanup of committed chunks on failure (complex), OR
   - (c) Document that partial registration is possible and rely on
     `gc_stale_initializing_runs_into` to clean up.
2. **Run-record update:** Only the first chunk transitions the run from
   Initializing to Active and publishes the active-index marker. Subsequent
   chunks compare against the updated run revision.
3. **Shard-limit checks:** The total shard count must be checked against
   limits BEFORE chunking begins, not per-chunk.

**Transaction structure per chunk:**
- Chunk 1: compare run-revision + N shard compare-absent + put run + put active-index + 2N shard puts
- Chunk 2+: compare run-revision (updated) + M shard compare-absent + put run + 2M shard puts

**Ceiling division:** `num_chunks = (shards.len() + MAX_SHARDS_PER_ETCD_TXN - 1) / MAX_SHARDS_PER_ETCD_TXN`

## Code References

```rust
// backend.rs:126-141 — budget constants
const MAX_SHARDS_PER_ETCD_TXN: usize = 41;

// backend.rs:2695-2699 — current rejection
if shards.len() > MAX_SHARDS_PER_ETCD_TXN {
    return Err(RegisterShardsError::ResourceExhausted { resource: "etcd_txn_ops" });
}

// backend.rs:2769-2815 — single-txn construction
let mut txn_ops = Vec::with_capacity(1 + (shards.len() * 2) + 1);
let mut compares = Vec::with_capacity(1 + shards.len());
```

## Related Work

None.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `register_shards` accepts batches larger than 41 shards.
- [ ] Large batches are split into chunks of at most 41 shards per etcd txn.
- [ ] Shard-limit enforcement happens before chunking.
- [ ] Partial-failure behavior is documented (whether cleanup is attempted).
- [ ] Integration test: register 50+ shards in a single call, verify all
      created.
- [ ] Existing limit test updated or replaced.
- [ ] `cargo test --all-targets --all-features` passes.
- [ ] `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` passes.

## Pointers

- `register_shards`: `backend.rs` lines 2687–2863
- Budget constant: `backend.rs` line 126
- Existing rejection test: `tests.rs` lines 740–778
- `gc_stale_initializing_runs_into`: `backend.rs` lines 1169–1220

title: Pool decode ByteSlab across operations
description:
## Context

Every shard record decode allocates a fresh `ByteSlab`. In `scan_run_shards`,
this means N slab allocations for N shards. Since each `PersistedShard` owns
its slab (the slab outlives decode and is returned to the caller), pooling
requires a different strategy than simple reuse — but build-side slabs in
`split_replace` ARE discarded after encoding and could be pooled.

## Current State

`ByteSlab` allocations in backend.rs:

| Line | Method | Per-call? | Slab lifetime |
|------|--------|-----------|---------------|
| 867 | `load_shard_record` | 1 per call | Returned in `PersistedShard` |
| 927 | `scan_run_shards` loop | N per call | Returned in `Vec<PersistedShard>` |
| 1454 | `build_root_shard_blob` | 1 per shard | Dropped after encode |
| 2193 | `split_replace` loop | N per child | Dropped after encode |
| 2470 | `split_residual` | 1 per call | Dropped after encode |

The `make_decode_slab` helper (lines 620–626) sizes slabs heuristically:
```rust
fn make_decode_slab(blob_len: usize) -> ByteSlab {
    let cap = blob_len.saturating_mul(3).saturating_add(1024)
        .clamp(MIN_DECODE_SLAB_CAPACITY, MAX_DECODE_SLAB_CAPACITY);
    ByteSlab::with_capacity(cap)
}
```
- `MIN_DECODE_SLAB_CAPACITY = 4 KiB` (line 111)
- `MAX_DECODE_SLAB_CAPACITY = 256 KiB` (line 118)

Slabs used for **decode** (lines 867, 927) are owned by `PersistedShard` and
cannot be trivially pooled — the caller holds references to slab-backed
pooled fields (`PooledShardSpec`, `PooledCursor`, `PooledSpawned`).

Slabs used for **encode** (lines 1454, 2193, 2470) are temporary: the shard
record is encoded into a `Vec<u8>` blob, then the slab is dropped. These
ARE candidates for pooling via a `clear()` + reuse pattern.

## Desired State

Pool encode-side slabs where the slab is dropped after encoding:

1. Add a `build_slab_scratch: ByteSlab` field to `EtcdCoordinator`.
2. In `build_root_shard_blob`, `split_replace` child loop, and
   `split_residual`, reuse the scratch slab via `slab.clear()` before each
   use.
3. Leave decode-side slabs as-is (they must outlive the operation).

## Implementation Guidance

**Files to modify:**
- `crates/gossip-coordination-etcd/src/backend.rs`

**Pattern for encode-side reuse:**
```rust
// Before: fresh allocation per child
let mut child_slab = ByteSlab::with_capacity(cap);
let child_record = ShardRecord::new_split_child(..., &mut child_slab)?;
let blob = encode_shard_record(&child_record, &child_slab);
// child_slab dropped here

// After: reuse scratch
self.build_slab_scratch.clear();
if self.build_slab_scratch.capacity() < needed_cap {
    self.build_slab_scratch = ByteSlab::with_capacity(needed_cap);
}
let child_record = ShardRecord::new_split_child(..., &mut self.build_slab_scratch)?;
let blob = encode_shard_record(&child_record, &self.build_slab_scratch);
// scratch retained for next iteration
```

**Important:** `ByteSlab::clear()` resets the bump pointer and free list but
retains the underlying allocation. Verify this is the case in `byte_slab.rs`.

**Allocation tier:** The `split_replace` child loop is HOT-adjacent (called
during split operations which are frequent in steady state). The
`build_root_shard_blob` path is COLD (registration only).

## Code References

```rust
// backend.rs:620-626 — make_decode_slab
fn make_decode_slab(blob_len: usize) -> ByteSlab { ... }

// backend.rs:2193 — split_replace child loop
let mut child_slab = ByteSlab::with_capacity(
    Self::build_slab_capacity_for_spec_and_cursor(child.spec(), child.cursor()),
);

// gossip-stdx/src/byte_slab.rs — ByteSlab::clear()
```

## Related Work

- gossip-8980: Reuse HashMap/Vec scratch buffers in scan_run_shards
- gossip-8987: Pre-allocate owner key buffer in scan_run_shards

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Encode-side slab reuse implemented for `split_replace` child loop and
      `split_residual`.
- [ ] `build_root_shard_blob` optionally reuses scratch (COLD path, lower
      priority).
- [ ] Decode-side slabs remain per-operation (no change).
- [ ] `ByteSlab::clear()` behavior verified (retains capacity).
- [ ] Existing integration tests pass unchanged.
- [ ] `cargo test --all-targets --all-features` passes.
- [ ] `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` passes.

## Pointers

- Encode-side allocations: `backend.rs` lines 1454, 2193, 2470
- Decode-side allocations: `backend.rs` lines 867, 927
- `make_decode_slab`: `backend.rs` lines 620–626
- `ByteSlab`: `gossip-stdx/src/byte_slab.rs`
- Slab capacity constants: `backend.rs` lines 106–118

title: Add should_panic tests for unimplemented operations
description:
## Context

Two `CoordinationBackend` trait methods on `EtcdCoordinator` intentionally
panic because their etcd transaction semantics are not yet defined. These
panics should have `#[should_panic]` tests to document the expected behavior
and catch accidental implementations that change the panic message.

## Current State

The backend code is split across a `backend/` directory (not a single
`backend.rs` file). Relevant files:
- `backend/coordinator.rs` — `EtcdCoordinator` struct, `fail_unimplemented`
- `backend/shard_coordination.rs` — `CoordinationBackend` impl

Two methods panic unconditionally via `fail_unimplemented`:

```rust
// shard_coordination.rs:587-600 — complete
fn complete(
    &mut self, _now: LogicalTime, _tenant: TenantId, _lease: &Lease,
    _final_cursor: &CursorUpdate<'_>, _op_id: OpId,
) -> Result<IdempotentOutcome<()>, CompleteError> {
    self.fail_unimplemented("complete")
}

// shard_coordination.rs:602-615 — park_shard
fn park_shard(
    &mut self, _now: LogicalTime, _tenant: TenantId, _lease: &Lease,
    _reason: ParkReason, _op_id: OpId,
) -> Result<IdempotentOutcome<()>, ParkError> {
    self.fail_unimplemented("park_shard")
}
```

The panic helper (`coordinator.rs` lines 222–233):
```rust
pub(super) fn fail_unimplemented<T>(&self, operation: &'static str) -> T {
    panic!(
        "EtcdCoordinator::{operation} is not yet persisted to etcd; \
         this operation must be implemented before it is callable"
    );
}
```

There are also async variants on `AsyncEtcdCoordinator`
(`shard_coordination.rs` lines 1563–1583) with a similar panic message
(`"AsyncEtcdCoordinator::{operation}..."`), but testing those requires
async test infrastructure and is out of scope for this task.

There are currently **no** `#[should_panic]` tests anywhere in `tests.rs`.

Only `complete` and `park_shard` call `fail_unimplemented` — no other
methods use it.

## Desired State

Add `#[test]` `#[should_panic(expected = "is not yet persisted to etcd")]`
tests for both `complete` and `park_shard`. These tests:
1. Document that the methods are intentionally unimplemented.
2. Will fail when someone implements the methods (prompting test update).
3. Require etcd connectivity only for `EtcdCoordinator` construction (the
   panic fires before any etcd RPC).

## Implementation Guidance

**Files to modify:**
- `crates/gossip-coordination-etcd/src/tests.rs`

**New imports needed** (not currently in tests.rs imports at lines 38–60):
```rust
use gossip_coordination::Lease;
use gossip_contracts::identity::FenceEpoch;
```
Add `Lease` to the `gossip_coordination` import block and `FenceEpoch`
to the `gossip_contracts::identity` import block.

**Constructing a dummy Lease** (`Lease::new` is `pub`, defined at
`gossip-coordination/src/lease.rs` lines 190–214):
```rust
let lease = Lease::new(
    test_tenant(),
    test_run(),
    test_shard(),
    test_worker(1),
    FenceEpoch::INITIAL,        // from_raw(1), minimum valid epoch
    LogicalTime::from_raw(100), // any non-zero deadline
);
```
`FenceEpoch::INITIAL` is the minimum valid fence epoch (panics on zero).
`LogicalTime` deadline must be non-zero (panics on zero).

**Test structure:**
```rust
#[test]
#[should_panic(expected = "is not yet persisted to etcd")]
#[ignore = "requires Docker or ETCD_ENDPOINTS"]
fn complete_panics_as_unimplemented() {
    let mut backend = test_coordinator();
    let lease = Lease::new(
        test_tenant(),
        test_run(),
        test_shard(),
        test_worker(1),
        FenceEpoch::INITIAL,
        LogicalTime::from_raw(100),
    );
    let _ = backend.complete(
        now(1),
        test_tenant(),
        &lease,
        &CursorUpdate::new(b"x"),
        OpId::from_raw(1),
    );
}

#[test]
#[should_panic(expected = "is not yet persisted to etcd")]
#[ignore = "requires Docker or ETCD_ENDPOINTS"]
fn park_shard_panics_as_unimplemented() {
    let mut backend = test_coordinator();
    let lease = Lease::new(
        test_tenant(),
        test_run(),
        test_shard(),
        test_worker(1),
        FenceEpoch::INITIAL,
        LogicalTime::from_raw(100),
    );
    let _ = backend.park_shard(
        now(1),
        test_tenant(),
        &lease,
        ParkReason::WorkerError,
        OpId::from_raw(1),
    );
}
```

**Why `#[ignore]` is required:** `test_coordinator()` (defined at
`test_etcd.rs` lines 145–151) calls `EtcdCoordinator::connect()` which
requires a real etcd connection (Docker via testcontainers or
`ETCD_ENDPOINTS` env var). The panic itself fires before any etcd RPC,
but coordinator construction cannot be skipped.

**Placement:** Add these near the existing integration test section
(after line 826 where the integration tests begin).

## Code References

```rust
// coordinator.rs:222-233 — fail_unimplemented (sync, EtcdCoordinator)
// coordinator.rs:1822-1828 — fail_unimplemented (async, AsyncEtcdCoordinator)
// shard_coordination.rs:587-600 — complete (calls fail_unimplemented)
// shard_coordination.rs:602-615 — park_shard (calls fail_unimplemented)
// shard_coordination.rs:1563-1572 — async complete (calls fail_unimplemented)
// shard_coordination.rs:1574-1583 — async park_shard (calls fail_unimplemented)
// lease.rs:190-214 — Lease::new (pub constructor)
// test_etcd.rs:145-151 — test_coordinator()
// tests.rs:38-60 — current imports
```

## Related Work

None.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `#[should_panic]` test for `complete`.
- [ ] `#[should_panic]` test for `park_shard`.
- [ ] Both tests use `expected = "is not yet persisted to etcd"` to match
      the panic message.
- [ ] Both tests are `#[ignore = "requires Docker or ETCD_ENDPOINTS"]`.
- [ ] `Lease` and `FenceEpoch` imports added to tests.rs.
- [ ] `cargo test --all-targets --all-features` passes.
- [ ] `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` passes.

## Pointers

- `fail_unimplemented` (sync): `coordinator.rs` lines 222–233
- `fail_unimplemented` (async): `coordinator.rs` lines 1822–1828
- `complete` impl: `shard_coordination.rs` lines 587–600
- `park_shard` impl: `shard_coordination.rs` lines 602–615
- `Lease::new`: `gossip-coordination/src/lease.rs` lines 190–214
- `FenceEpoch::INITIAL`: `gossip-contracts/src/identity/` (minimum valid epoch, raw value 1)
- Test coordinator: `test_etcd.rs` lines 145–151 (requires etcd, 202 lines total)
- Tests.rs imports: lines 38–60 (need `Lease` and `FenceEpoch` added)
- Existing integration tests start at: `tests.rs` line 826

title: Add codec edge case tests (empty collections, boundary values)
description:
## Context

The codec test suite covers round-trip correctness via proptests and several
error paths, but specific edge cases around boundary values and empty
collections are not systematically covered. Adding these tests closes gaps
that proptests may not reliably reach.

## Current State

Existing edge-case coverage in `codec_tests.rs` (1708 lines):

**Already tested:**
- Zero fence epoch rejection (line 92: `owner_value_decode_rejects_zero_fence_epoch`)
- Wrong blob kind detection (line 102: `owner_value_rejects_wrong_blob_kind`
  and line 215: `decode_shard_record_rejects_wrong_blob_kind`)
- Invalid version prefix (line 162: `decode_run_record_rejects_wrong_version_prefix`)
- TrailingBytes for run records (line 177: `decode_run_record_rejects_trailing_bytes`)
- Truncated blob (line 192: `decode_run_record_rejects_truncated_blob`)
- Active run without root shards (line 201: `decode_run_record_rejects_active_without_root_shards`)
- Cursor token without last_key (line 231: `decode_shard_record_rejects_cursor_token_without_last_key`)
- SlabFull on exhausted slab (line 246: `decode_shard_record_rolls_back_on_slab_exhaustion`)
- Invalid bool tags (line 794: `decoder_read_bool_rejects_invalid`)
- Decoder u32 truncation (line 815: `decoder_read_u32_truncated`)
- Decoder u64 truncation (line 835: `decoder_read_u64_truncated`)
- Decoder vec truncated body (line 857: `decoder_read_vec_truncated_body`)
- FieldTooLarge on vec (line 871: `decoder_read_vec_rejects_too_large`)
- Decoder tenant truncation (line 910: `decoder_read_tenant_truncated`)
- Over op-log cap rejection (line 969: `shard_record_over_op_log_cap_rejected`)
- Max spawned at exact limit round-trip (line 1008: `shard_record_at_max_spawned_round_trips`)
- Over max spawned rejection (line 1056: `shard_record_over_max_spawned_rejected`)
- Cursor parse failure rollback (line 1496: `decode_shard_record_rolls_back_spec_on_cursor_parse_failure`)
- Oversized root shards (line 1538: `decode_run_record_rejects_oversized_root_shards`)
- Oversized registered shards (line 1570: `decode_run_record_rejects_oversized_registered_shards`)
- Non-monotonic op-log timestamps (line 1614: `decode_shard_record_rejects_non_monotonic_op_log_timestamps`)

**Error variants defined** (`codec.rs` lines 141–172):
- `Truncated` (line 143), `InvalidVersionPrefix` (line 145),
  `InvalidBlobKind` (line 147), `UnexpectedBlobKind` (line 149),
  `InvalidBool` (line 154), `InvalidEnum` (line 156),
  `InvalidSpec` (line 158), `InvalidCursor` (line 160),
  `SlabFull` (line 162), `TrailingBytes` (line 164),
  `InvariantViolation` (line 166), `FieldTooLarge` (line 171)

**Gaps identified (no existing test):**
1. Empty key-range strings (`key_start = ""`, `key_end = ""`) — the proptest
   strategy at line 637 generates `key_start` with range `1..=8` bytes
   (never empty), so this edge case is untested.
2. `u64::MAX` boundary values for WorkerId, ShardId, RunId, FenceEpoch —
   no dedicated deterministic unit test exists. Proptest may reach these
   but is not guaranteed to.
3. Maximum-length field values (exactly at `MAX_FIELD_SIZE` boundary) —
   the `decoder_read_vec_rejects_too_large` test (line 871) only tests the
   over-limit case. No test encodes at exactly the limit.
4. Zero-length metadata field in shard records.
5. TrailingBytes for **shard records** and **owner values** — the existing
   test (line 177) only covers run records. No TrailingBytes test exists
   for shard records or owner values.
6. Run record with empty `root_shards` collection (for Initializing status,
   where this is valid).
7. Shard record with zero op-log entries.
8. All-zeros binary payload (regression against off-by-one in length parsing).

## Desired State

Deterministic unit tests (not proptests) for each gap, covering both
successful decode and expected error cases at boundaries.

## Implementation Guidance

**Files to modify:**
- `crates/gossip-coordination-etcd/src/codec_tests.rs`

**Test naming convention:** Follow existing `snake_case_describes_scenario`
pattern. Examples from the file:
`owner_value_decode_rejects_zero_fence_epoch`,
`decode_run_record_rejects_trailing_bytes`,
`shard_record_at_max_spawned_round_trips`.

**Example tests to add:**

```rust
#[test]
fn trailing_bytes_after_valid_shard_record_rejected() {
    // Encode a valid shard record, append a byte, verify TrailingBytes.
    // (Run record variant exists at line 177; shard and owner do not.)
}

#[test]
fn trailing_bytes_after_valid_owner_value_rejected() {
    let encoded = encode_owner_value(WorkerId::from_raw(1), FenceEpoch::INITIAL);
    let mut with_extra = encoded.clone();
    with_extra.push(0xFF);
    let err = decode_owner_value(&with_extra).unwrap_err();
    assert!(matches!(err, EtcdCodecError::TrailingBytes { remaining: 1 }));
}

#[test]
fn shard_record_with_u64_max_ids_round_trips() {

}

    // key_start = b"", key_end = b"" — verify encode/decode succeeds
```
