title: Refactor SyncEtcdLike: split into transport layer, lift data-loading to default impls, drop RefCell
description:
## Context

The `SyncEtcdLike` trait in `backend/coordinator.rs` mixes two abstraction levels: narrow transport methods (`etcd_get`, `etcd_txn`, `etcd_lease_grant`, etc.) and high-level data-loading helpers (`load_run_record`, `load_shard_record`, `scan_run_shards`, `transition_run_terminal`, `count_available_lightweight`, etc.). This causes ~500 lines of data-loading logic to be duplicated between `EtcdCoordinator`'s and `SimEtcdCoordinator`'s `SyncEtcdLike` impls, since both implement the same logic over different transport implementations.

Additionally, `SimEtcdCoordinator` wraps `SimulatedEtcdKV` in `RefCell` because the trait's transport methods take `&self` (the real `EtcdCoordinator` uses interior mutability via Tokio runtime). This creates fragile borrow patterns and runtime panics on nested calls.

This task addresses three review findings (F2, F8, F9) as a single cohesive refactor.

## Current State

```rust
// crates/gossip-coordination-etcd/src/backend/coordinator.rs:77-103
pub(crate) trait SyncEtcdLike: Sized {
    fn config(&self) -> &EtcdCoordinatorConfig;
    fn keyspace(&self) -> &EtcdKeyspace;
    fn sync_logical_time(&self, _now: LogicalTime) {}
    fn refresh_cached_run_state(&mut self, ...) -> Result<(), ...> { Ok(()) }
    fn cas_retry_backoff(&self, attempt: usize) { std::thread::sleep(...); }
    fn on_gc_run(&mut self, _tenant: TenantId, _run: RunId) {}
    // Transport methods:
    fn etcd_get(&self, ...) -> Result<GetResponse, ...>;
    fn etcd_txn(&self, ...) -> Result<TxnResponse, ...>;
    fn etcd_lease_grant(&self, ...) -> Result<LeaseGrantResponse, ...>;
    fn etcd_lease_keep_alive_once(&self, ...) -> Result<(), ...>;
    fn etcd_lease_revoke(&self, ...) -> Result<LeaseRevokeResponse, ...>;
}
```

```rust
// crates/gossip-coordination-etcd/src/sim_coordinator.rs:41-48
pub struct SimEtcdCoordinator {
    // ...
    kv: RefCell<SimulatedEtcdKV>,          // fragile interior mutability
    expired_lease_buffer: RefCell<Vec<i64>>, // deferred invalidation buffer
    test_faults: RefCell<SimEtcdTestFaultState>,
}
```

Data-loading methods like `load_run_record`, `load_shard_record`, `scan_run_shards`, `transition_run_terminal` are free functions in `backend/coordinator.rs` (~200 lines) that take `&impl SyncEtcdLike`. Both impls call the same free functions, but `SimEtcdCoordinator` also has its own copies of `list_active_runs_into`, `gc_stale_initializing_runs_into`, and `count_persisted_shards_under_prefix`.

## Desired State

1. **Split `SyncEtcdLike` into two traits:**
   - `SyncEtcdTransport` — narrow trait with 5 RPC methods + `keyspace()`/`config()` accessors. Transport methods take `&mut self`.
   - `SyncEtcdLike: SyncEtcdTransport` — supertrait with default-impl data-loading methods that call through `SyncEtcdTransport`.

2. **Transport methods take `&mut self`** — `SimEtcdCoordinator` can own `SimulatedEtcdKV` directly (no `RefCell`), and `expired_lease_buffer`/`test_faults` can be plain `Vec`/struct.

3. **~500 lines of duplicated data-loading code** move from free functions into default impls on `SyncEtcdLike`, eliminating duplication between the two coordinators.

## Implementation Guidance

### Files to Modify
| File | Change | Rationale |
|------|--------|-----------|
| `backend/coordinator.rs` | Split trait, move data-loading into default impls | Core refactor |
| `sim_coordinator.rs` | Drop `RefCell` on `kv`, `test_faults`, `expired_lease_buffer`; simplify borrow patterns | Enabled by `&mut self` transport |
| `backend/shard_coordination.rs` | Update macro callers if trait method signatures change | Downstream of trait split |
| `backend/run_management.rs` | Same | Downstream of trait split |

### Patterns to Follow
- The existing `refresh_cached_run_state` and `on_gc_run` default impls (`coordinator.rs:86-103`) show how hooks with defaults work in the trait.
- `cas_retry` already takes `&mut self` on the coordinator, which is compatible.

### Blast Radius
- All CAS loops in `shard_coordination.rs` and `run_management.rs` call through `SyncEtcdLike` methods.
- `SimEtcdCoordinator` test helpers and `SimIntrospection` impl access `kv` via `borrow()`/`borrow_mut()` — all need updating.
- `backend/test_support.rs` fault injection touches `test_faults` RefCell.

## Code References

The free functions that should become default impls:
- `load_run_record` — `backend/coordinator.rs` (loads and decodes a run record from KV)
- `load_shard_record` — `backend/coordinator.rs` (loads and decodes a shard record + owner from KV)
- `scan_run_shards` — `backend/coordinator.rs` (prefix scan of all shards under a run)
- `transition_run_terminal` — `backend/coordinator.rs` (CAS for terminal run transitions)
- `count_available_lightweight` — `backend/coordinator.rs` (keys-only count of active shards)

## Related Work
| Task ID | Title | Relationship |
|---------|-------|-------------|
| gossip-9020.2 | Build SimEtcdCoordinator | predecessor (now closed) |
| gossip-9020.3 | Progressive fault injection | independent — does not touch trait structure |

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `SyncEtcdTransport` trait has exactly: `config`, `keyspace`, `etcd_get`, `etcd_txn`, `etcd_lease_grant`, `etcd_lease_keep_alive_once`, `etcd_lease_revoke` — all `&mut self`
- [ ] `SyncEtcdLike: SyncEtcdTransport` has default-impl data-loading methods
- [ ] `SimEtcdCoordinator` owns `SimulatedEtcdKV` directly, no `RefCell`
- [ ] `expired_lease_buffer` and `test_faults` are plain fields, no `RefCell`
- [ ] Zero duplicated data-loading code between `EtcdCoordinator` and `SimEtcdCoordinator`
- [ ] `cargo fmt --all && cargo check && cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`
- [ ] `cargo test -p gossip-coordination-etcd` passes (all 174+ tests)
- [ ] `cargo test -p gossip-coordination` passes

## Pointers
- `docs/gossip-coordination/boundary-2-coordination.md` — coordination protocol spec
- `docs/gossip-coordination/simulation-harness.md` — simulation architecture
- Read `backend/coordinator.rs` lines 77-300 for the full trait + free function surface

title: Add secondary index for O(K) shard cache invalidation on lease expiry in SimEtcdCoordinator
Differential oracle — compare SimEtcdCoordinator vs real EtcdCoordinator to detect model drift
description:
## Context

The gossip-rs simulation trust chain has a critical gap: **nothing validates
that `SimulatedEtcdKV` accurately models real etcd behavior**. The existing
test infrastructure validates coordination invariants (S1--S7) against two
backends:

- `InMemoryCoordinator` (reference model, always available)
- `SimEtcdCoordinator` (in-memory etcd model, always available)

gossip-9020.8 proposes a differential oracle comparing InMemory vs SimEtcd,
which catches model drift between those two in-memory implementations. But
that oracle only validates that `SimEtcdCoordinator` agrees with
`InMemoryCoordinator` -- it does NOT validate that `SimulatedEtcdKV` agrees
with real etcd. Since `SyncEtcdLike` shares all coordination logic above the
KV layer, bugs hiding in the KV model (revision numbering, lease expiry
coalescing, transaction semantics) are invisible to same-layer comparisons.

This task creates a **differential oracle at the CoordinationBackend boundary**
that runs identical operation sequences against both `SimEtcdCoordinator` and
real `EtcdCoordinator` (via Docker/testcontainers), comparing observable
results to detect KV-layer model drift.

### Research evidence

The design is grounded in established distributed systems testing literature:

1. **McKeeman's differential testing (1998)** -- two implementations of the
   same spec serve as cross-referencing oracles. `SimulatedEtcdKV` and real
   etcd are exactly this pairing: same spec, independent implementations.
2. **Fowler's Contract Tests** -- periodic slow-loop validation of test doubles
   against the real service catches model drift that accumulates over time.
3. **Dropbox Trinity/Heirloom pattern** -- fast simulation tests run every
   commit; slow real-backend differential tests run nightly. The cost/benefit
   tradeoff is accepted: fast CI gets >99% coverage, nightly catches KV drift.
4. **FoundationDB simulation principle (SIGMOD 2021)** -- shared code paths
   eliminate drift by construction. gossip-rs shares coordination logic via
   `SyncEtcdLike`, but the KV layer is entirely independent (`SimulatedEtcdKV`
   vs real etcd gRPC). This is the layer the oracle must validate.
5. **Jepsen output-only oracle approach** -- compare observable operation
   results without introspecting internal state. Sufficient for catching
   semantic divergence.
6. **DoneLedgerOracle pattern** -- existing codebase precedent for model-based
   differential testing at `gossip-persistence-inmemory/src/sim/oracle.rs`.
7. **proptest state machine** -- existing `arb_sim_op` strategy can drive both
   backends with identical operation sequences and automatic shrinking.

## Current State

### `SyncEtcdLike` trait -- shared coordination logic

Both `EtcdCoordinator` and `SimEtcdCoordinator` implement the `SyncEtcdLike`
trait, which provides a unified surface for all etcd-backed coordination. The
macro `impl_sync_coordination_backend!` generates the `CoordinationBackend`
impl for both types using identical logic:


## Desired State

A differential oracle test module that:

1. **Generates random `SimOp` sequences** via proptest, reusing `arb_sim_op`
   from `crates/gossip-coordination/src/sim/test_util.rs`.

2. **Executes each operation against BOTH backends**:
   - `SimEtcdCoordinator` (in-memory, SunnyDay faults disabled)
   - `EtcdCoordinator` (real etcd via Docker/testcontainers)

3. **Compares `CoordinationBackend` operation results** after each step:
   - Success/error variant matching (e.g., both return `AcquireOk` or both
     return `AlreadyLeased`)
   - Error kind matching (not error message strings)

4. **Compares observable state** after each step:
   - Sim side: `SimIntrospection` trait methods (`shards()`, `runs()`,
     `shard_lookup()`)
   - Etcd side: `test_load_shard_snapshot()` and `test_load_run_snapshot()`
   - Compare: shard status, fence epoch, cursor position, lease holder,
     run state

5. **Handles known fidelity gaps** with explicit allowlists:
   - Revision number differences (documented: sim starts at 0, real at 1;
     batch expiry revision inflation)
   - Lease expiry timing boundary differences (heartbeat-based vs exact-tick)
   - `lease_grant` revision bump difference

6. **Uses proptest shrinking** to minimize diverging sequences to the smallest
   reproduction case.

7. **Docker-dependent, feature-gated**: `#![cfg(feature = "test-support")]`
   and `#[ignore]` for CI cost. Runs nightly via the gossip-8976 CI pipeline.

## Design Notes

### Compare at CoordinationBackend result level (Jepsen pattern)

Do NOT compare raw KV contents or etcd revision numbers between backends.
Compare only the `CoordinationBackend` method return values and the observable
shard/run record state. This is the Jepsen output-only oracle approach --
internal state representation may differ as long as observable behavior matches.

### Disable fault injection on SimEtcdCoordinator

Use `SimEtcdFaultConfig::default()` (SunnyDay -- all PPM rates zero) so the
sim backend produces no injected faults. Real etcd also has no injected faults.
Both backends must see identical "clean" conditions for strict comparison.

### Long lease TTL on real etcd

Use `test_coordinator_with_ttl(300)` (5 minutes) so lease expiry does not
occur during the test due to wall-clock time. The sim uses logical time
(`AdvanceTime` ops), which has no real-time equivalent. By keeping TTL large,
no real-etcd lease expires spontaneously during the sequence.

### Handle `AdvanceTime` differently

- Sim: `AdvanceTime { ticks }` advances the logical clock, potentially
  expiring leases.
- Real etcd: Logical time advancement has no effect. Leases expire via
  wall-clock TTL.
- **Strategy**: Skip `AdvanceTime` ops for real etcd, or filter them from
  generated sequences entirely. Alternatively, use `AdvanceTime` as a no-op
  on the etcd side but still compare state after each non-time op.
- **Consequence**: Lease expiry paths are NOT covered by this oracle. That is
  acceptable -- lease expiry semantics are a known fidelity gap, and the
  InMemory-vs-SimEtcd oracle (gossip-9020.8) covers that path.

### Fresh namespace per proptest case

Each proptest case gets its own unique namespace prefix via `unique_namespace()`.
This provides full isolation between cases and prevents stale state from
previous cases leaking into subsequent ones.

### Runtime sequencing

`EtcdCoordinator::connect()` creates its own internal Tokio runtime. The
testcontainers `SyncRunner` also uses a Tokio runtime. Per the documented
pattern in `test_etcd.rs:16-22`, extract all container metadata as owned
values before constructing any `EtcdCoordinator` to avoid runtime overlap.

title: Behavioral conformance harness for real EtcdCoordinator via CoordinationBackend output oracle
description:
## Context

The coordination protocol has three backend implementations with unequal conformance coverage:

- **InMemoryCoordinator**: 16 conformance tests (`conformance_tests.rs`) verifying cross-cutting invariant interactions, boundary conditions, and run-level protocol behavior.
- **SimEtcdCoordinator**: Will receive the same 16 tests via gossip-8975.3 (pending gossip-8975.2 landing the `SimulationBackend`-generic harness).
- **Real EtcdCoordinator**: Zero conformance tests. Has 89 bespoke integration tests (`tests.rs`) covering config validation, keyspace construction, round-trip lifecycle, CAS contention, and fault injection, but NONE of the cross-cutting invariant interaction patterns from conformance_tests.rs.

The conformance tests (`conformance_tests.rs`) exercise protocol safety invariants like fence monotonicity across ownership transfers, cursor bounds enforcement after split-residual, idempotency-before-terminal-rejection ordering, and terminal irreversibility. These are exactly the kind of bugs that would manifest differently across backends due to CAS retry timing, etcd lease TTL semantics, and transaction atomicity boundaries.

**Why a separate behavioral layer?** The existing conformance tests (and the upcoming `run_coordination_conformance` harness from gossip-8975.2) require `SimulationBackend = CoordinationFacade + SimIntrospection`. Real `EtcdCoordinator` cannot implement `SimIntrospection` because it returns `&ShardRecord` references tied to internal slab storage owned by the in-memory coordinator. Instead, this task creates a behavioral conformance layer that tests the same protocol scenarios using only the public `CoordinationBackend` + `RunManagement` trait surface, with assertions based on operation return values and `test_support.rs` read-back methods.

**Evidence from distributed systems testing practice:**
- Jepsen treats systems as opaque boxes, validates linearizability of client-observed histories. No internal state introspection needed.
- Fowler's Contract Tests validate test doubles by periodically running the same operations against the real service and comparing observable results.
- The Erlang QuickCheck `postcondition(state, cmd, result)` pattern validates each operation's result against model expectations using output-only oracles.

## Current State

### The 16 conformance tests (`conformance_tests.rs:118-1053`)

**Group A: Cross-Cutting Invariant Interactions (6 tests)**

| Test | SimIntrospection usage | Classification |
|------|----------------------|----------------|
| `fence_monotonicity_across_full_lifecycle` (L119) | `shard_lookup()` to read `fence_epoch`, `status` | **Behavioral** (fence is in acquire return; status verifiable via test_load_shard_snapshot) |
| `cursor_monotonicity_combined_with_split_residual` (L160) | `shard_lookup()` + `cursor.last_key(coord.slab())` + `spec.key_range_start/end(coord.slab())` | **Behavioral** (test_load_shard_snapshot has its own slab via EtcdTestShardSnapshot) |
| `idempotency_before_terminal_state_rejection` (L216) | `shard_lookup()` + `cursor.last_key(coord.slab())` | **Behavioral** (can use operation results + test_load_shard_snapshot) |
| `split_residual_preserved_through_park_unpark` (L277) | `shard_lookup()` + `cursor.last_key(coord.slab())` + `spec.key_range_start/end(coord.slab())` | **Behavioral** (test_load_shard_snapshot has its own slab via EtcdTestShardSnapshot) |
| `owner_divergence_with_matching_fence` (L370) | `shard_lookup()` to verify fence/cursor/status unchanged | **Behavioral** (can use test_load_shard_snapshot) |
| `terminal_clears_lease` (L429) | `shard_lookup()` to verify lease_owner/deadline/fence/status | **Behavioral** (test_load_shard_snapshot exposes all these fields) |

**Group B: Boundary Conditions and Variant Coverage (5 tests)**

| Test | SimIntrospection usage | Classification |
|------|----------------------|----------------|
| `cursor_semantics_dispatched_through_coordinator` (L510) | `shard_lookup()` to read `cursor_semantics`, `status` | **Behavioral** (test_load_shard_snapshot) |
| `lease_deadline_at_exact_boundary` (L551) | None (purely operation results) | **Behavioral** |
| `split_coverage_key_range_partition` (L589) | `shard_lookup()` + `spec.key_range_start/end(coord.slab())` + `cursor.last_key(coord.slab())` | **Behavioral** (test_load_shard_snapshot has its own slab) |
| `oplog_eviction_then_replay` (L665) | None (purely operation results) | **Behavioral** |
| `same_worker_reacquire_bumps_fence` (L788) | None (purely operation results + fence from lease) | **Behavioral** |

**Group C: Run-Level Conformance (4 tests)**

| Test | SimIntrospection usage | Classification |
|------|----------------------|----------------|
| `run_terminal_irreversibility` (L846) | `get_run()` (RunManagement method, not SimIntrospection) | **Behavioral** |
| `register_shards_on_non_initializing_rejected` (L920) | `get_run()` | **Behavioral** |
| `run_completed_at_consistency` (L961) | `get_run()` | **Behavioral** |
| `unpark_after_run_terminal_rejected` (L1026) | `get_run()` | **Behavioral** |

### SimIntrospection methods used in conformance tests

```rust
// From crates/gossip-coordination/src/sim/backend.rs:70-171
pub trait SimIntrospection {
    fn shard_lookup(&self, tenant: &TenantId, key: &ShardKey) -> Option<&ShardRecord>;
    fn cursor_last_key<'a>(&'a self, record: &'a ShardRecord) -> Option<&'a [u8]>;
    fn spec_bounds<'a>(&'a self, record: &'a ShardRecord) -> (&'a [u8], &'a [u8]);
    // ... plus shards(), runs(), shard_count(), validate_record_invariants(), spawned_children()
}
```

The key insight: `EtcdTestShardSnapshot` (from `test_support.rs:52-73`) implements `Deref<Target=ShardRecord>` and carries its own `ByteSlab`, providing the equivalent of `shard_lookup` + slab access. This makes ALL 16 conformance tests classifiable as **Behavioral** because `test_load_shard_snapshot()` returns an owned snapshot with its own slab.

### EtcdCoordinator trait surface

`EtcdCoordinator` implements via macros in `shard_coordination.rs:117` and `run_management.rs:54`:
- `CoordinationBackend` (7 shard lifecycle methods)
- `RunManagement` (create_run, register_shards, get_run, get_run_progress, list_shards_into, collect_claim_candidates_into, complete_run, fail_run, cancel_run, unpark_shard, plus list_active_runs_into, gc_stale_initializing_runs_into)
- `ShardClaiming`

### test_support.rs read-back methods (`test_support.rs:82-355`)

```rust
impl EtcdCoordinator {
    pub fn test_load_shard_snapshot(&self, tenant: TenantId, key: ShardKey)
        -> Result<Option<EtcdTestShardSnapshot>, EtcdCoordinatorError>;
    pub fn test_load_run_snapshot(&self, tenant: TenantId, run: RunId)
        -> Result<Option<RunRecord>, EtcdCoordinatorError>;
    pub fn test_load_owner_binding(&self, tenant: TenantId, key: ShardKey)
        -> Result<Option<(WorkerId, FenceEpoch, i64)>, EtcdCoordinatorError>;
    pub fn test_load_tenant_shard_count(&self, tenant: TenantId)
        -> Result<Option<u64>, EtcdCoordinatorError>;
    pub fn test_active_shard_index_exists(&self, tenant: TenantId, key: ShardKey)
        -> Result<bool, EtcdCoordinatorError>;
    pub fn test_seed_shard_record(&self, record: &ShardRecord, slab: &ByteSlab)
        -> Result<(), EtcdCoordinatorError>;
    pub fn test_seed_run_record(&self, record: &RunRecord)
        -> Result<(), EtcdCoordinatorError>;
}
```

`EtcdTestShardSnapshot` (`test_support.rs:52-73`) wraps `PersistedShard` and provides:
- `Deref<Target=ShardRecord>` for accessing all record fields
- `slab()` method returning `&ByteSlab` for resolving pooled fields (cursor, spec)

### Existing etcd integration test coverage

89 test functions in `tests.rs`, covering:
- Config validation (pure, no etcd): 25 tests
- Keyspace path construction: 11 tests (including proptest)
- etcd integration (round-trip lifecycle): ~35 tests
- CAS contention (multi-threaded): ~8 tests
- Error paths and edge cases: ~10 tests

Notably absent: cross-cutting invariant interactions (Group A style), boundary condition combinations, run-level conformance patterns.

## Desired State

A behavioral conformance module that tests protocol scenarios equivalent to all 16 conformance tests from `conformance_tests.rs`, adapted to use only `CoordinationBackend` + `RunManagement` methods plus `test_load_shard_snapshot()` / `test_load_run_snapshot()` read-backs.

Since `EtcdCoordinator` owns the `test_load_*` methods as inherent methods (not via a trait), the behavioral conformance tests are best written directly against `EtcdCoordinator` rather than generic over a trait. The function signature:

```rust
/// Run all behavioral conformance scenarios against a real EtcdCoordinator.
///
/// Each scenario mirrors one of the 16 conformance tests from
/// conformance_tests.rs, adapted for output-only oracle assertions.
fn run_behavioral_conformance(backend: &mut EtcdCoordinator) { ... }
```

Or, as individual test functions in a dedicated module to allow selective test execution.

## Design Notes

- **Output-only oracle:** Compare operation results (return values, error variants), not internal state. Where internal state must be checked (e.g., "fence was preserved"), use `test_load_shard_snapshot()` which reads back from etcd and provides its own slab.
- **EtcdTestShardSnapshot is the key enabler:** It wraps the decoded `ShardRecord` with its own `ByteSlab`, so `record.cursor.last_key(snapshot.slab())` and `record.spec.key_range_start(snapshot.slab())` work identically to the conformance tests' `record.cursor.last_key(coord.slab())`.
- **All 16 tests are behaviorally testable:** Because `test_load_shard_snapshot` provides owned slab access, even tests like `cursor_monotonicity_combined_with_split_residual` that read spec bounds and cursor positions can be translated.
- **Docker-dependent:** Tests require a real etcd. They run with the existing etcd integration test infrastructure (testcontainers or ETCD_ENDPOINTS). The CI pipeline from gossip-8976 handles Docker provisioning.
- **This is a COMPLEMENT, not a replacement:** The sim conformance harness (gossip-8975.2/8975.3) validates with richer invariant checking via `SimIntrospection`. This behavioral layer catches model-drift bugs where the real backend diverges from the simulated one.
- **LogicalTime works identically:** Real `EtcdCoordinator` also uses `LogicalTime` as an input (time is never read from a clock), so the same timing patterns from conformance_tests.rs work directly.

title: Build SimEtcdCoordinator implementing CoordinationBackend + SimIntrospection over SimulatedEtcdKV
description:
## Context

With SimulatedEtcdKV providing an in-memory etcd model (gossip-9020.1), the
next step is building a coordinator that exercises the real etcd backend
validation and mutation logic against the simulated KV, implementing
CoordinationBackend + SimIntrospection so it plugs directly into the existing
CoordinationSim harness.

This is the core enabler: once this exists, running
`CoordinationSim::with_backend(seed, level, SimEtcdCoordinator::new(...))` gives
full S1-S9 invariant checking against etcd-specific code paths (CAS retry loops,
mod_revision guards, dual-key ownership, owner binding with lease TTL).

## Current State

CoordinationSim<B> at `sim/harness.rs:821` is generic over
`B: SimulationBackend`. The `with_backend()` constructor at
`sim/harness.rs:1113` accepts any SimulationBackend. Only InMemoryCoordinator
implements SimulationBackend today.

The etcd coordinator uses a dual-key model:
- `/shard` record key: stores ShardRecord + ByteSlab serialized
- `/owner` key: attached to an etcd lease for TTL-based ownership

EtcdCoordinator implements AsyncCoordinationBackend (async) and wraps it
in a sync block_on for EtcdCoordinator. It does NOT implement
SimIntrospection (the read-only GAT-based observation trait).

## Desired State

A `SimEtcdCoordinator` struct that:

1. Wraps SimulatedEtcdKV as its storage layer
2. Implements `CoordinationBackend` (sync) — reuses the etcd backend's
   validation logic (CAS retry, revision guards, owner binding) but calls
   SimulatedEtcdKV instead of real etcd RPCs
3. Implements `SimIntrospection` — provides GAT iterators over decoded
   shard records for invariant checking
4. Uses the same `EtcdKeyspace` for key path construction
5. Uses the same binary codec for serialization/deserialization
6. Automatically satisfies `SimulationBackend` via the blanket impl

The key design: maintain a **decoded record cache** alongside the raw KV store.
After every mutation, update the cache. SimIntrospection reads from the cache.
This tests the full codec round-trip while providing efficient introspection.

## Implementation Guidance

### Files to Create
| File | Content |
|------|---------|
| `crates/gossip-coordination-etcd/src/sim_coordinator.rs` | SimEtcdCoordinator struct + CoordinationBackend + SimIntrospection impls |

### Files to Modify
| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `crates/gossip-coordination-etcd/src/lib.rs` | Add `pub mod sim_coordinator` behind `test-support` |
| `crates/gossip-coordination-etcd/Cargo.toml` | Add gossip-coordination/test-support dep for SimIntrospection |

### Patterns to Follow
- Follow InMemoryCoordinator's SimIntrospection impl at `in_memory.rs:2787+`
  for GAT iterator patterns
- Reuse `EtcdKeyspace` from `keyspace.rs` for key construction
- Reuse `PersistedShard` codec from `backend/mod.rs` for serialization
- The decoded record cache pattern: `HashMap<(TenantId, ShardKey), ShardRecord>`
  updated atomically with every KV mutation

### Key Design Decision
The SimEtcdCoordinator should NOT simply wrap InMemoryCoordinator. It must
exercise the etcd-specific code paths:
- CAS retry loop with revision-based compare predicates
- Dual-key ownership model (shard record + owner key with lease)
- Transaction budget constraints (128 ops max)
- Keyspace path encoding/decoding

This means the SimEtcdCoordinator reimplements CoordinationBackend by
calling SimulatedEtcdKV using the same transaction patterns as the real
etcd coordinator, just synchronously and without gRPC.

- [ ] CAS retry logic exercised (at least one test where CAS fails and retries)
- [ ] Dual-key ownership model exercised (owner key created with lease)
- [ ] Binary codec round-trip verified (encode to KV, decode for introspection)

title: Add progressive fault injection to SimulatedEtcdKV (CAS contention, uncertain commits, lease races)
description:
## Context

SimulatedEtcdKV (gossip-9020.1) provides an in-memory etcd model and
SimEtcdCoordinator (gossip-9020.2) plugs it into CoordinationSim. This task
adds progressive fault injection at the simulated etcd layer (Level 1) so
the coordinator's retry and error handling logic is exercised transparently.

Following TigerBeetle's VOPR pattern: faults are injected at the storage
layer, not the application layer. The coordinator code doesn't know it's
being tested — it sees CAS failures, lease expirations, and timeouts exactly
as it would in production.

## Current State

The coordination sim has 3 fault levels (sim/mod.rs:182-280) with PPM-based
rates for time jumps, lease expiry, and worker pauses. These are
coordination-level faults. No etcd-level faults exist (CAS contention,
uncertain commits, lease TTL races).

## Desired State

SimulatedEtcdKV gains fault injection hooks driven by FaultLevel:

| Fault | SunnyDay | Stormy | Radioactive |
|-------|----------|--------|-------------|
| CAS compare failure (simulated contention) | 0% | 10% | 30% |
| Uncertain commit (txn succeeds but client sees error) | 0% | 2% | 10% |
| Lease TTL expiry between read and write | 0% | 5% | 15% |
| cas_retry budget exhaustion | 0% | 1% | 5% |

Uncertain commit is the critical fault: the CAS succeeds server-side but the
client observes a timeout. On retry with the same op_id, the coordinator must
detect the replayed operation and return the cached result. This exercises
the idempotency logic that is currently only tested via direct method calls.

## Implementation Guidance

### Files to Modify
| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `sim_etcd_kv.rs` | Add `SimEtcdFaultConfig` with PPM rates; inject faults in `txn()` and `lease_keep_alive()` |
| `sim_coordinator.rs` | Pass FaultLevel to SimulatedEtcdKV at construction |

### Fault Injection Points
1. **CAS compare failure**: Before evaluating compares, roll dice. If hit, return
   `TxnResponse { succeeded: false }` even though compares would pass. Models
   concurrent writer contention.
2. **Uncertain commit**: After successfully applying the txn internally, return an
   error to the caller. The state has changed but the caller doesn't know.
   On retry, the op_id-based idempotency check should detect the replay.
3. **Lease TTL race**: In `tick()`, expire a lease mid-operation by injecting an
   extra tick between the coordinator's read and write phases.
4. **Retry exhaustion**: After N-1 successful CAS retries, force the Nth to fail
   permanently. Tests the coordinator's exhaustion handling path.

### Patterns to Follow
- FaultConfig::for_level() at sim/mod.rs for PPM rate definitions
- PPM dice roll pattern: `rng.gen_range(0..1_000_000) < rate_ppm`

## Related Work
gossip-9020: Parent epic
gossip-9020.1: Depends-on (SimulatedEtcdKV)
gossip-9020.2: Depends-on (SimEtcdCoordinator)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] SimEtcdFaultConfig with PPM rates for each fault type
- [ ] CAS contention injection works (S1-S9 still pass — faults cause rejections, not violations)
- [ ] Uncertain commit injection triggers idempotent replay detection
- [ ] Lease TTL race injection triggers StaleFence/LeaseExpired rejections
- [ ] Retry exhaustion injection triggers appropriate error handling
- [ ] All faults are seeded via ChaCha8Rng for reproducibility
- [ ] SunnyDay level has zero faults (regression safety)
- [ ] Clean build (fmt + check + clippy + doc)

## Pointers
- FaultConfig: `sim/mod.rs:182-280`
- Idempotency check: op_id matching in ShardRecord::op_log
- CAS retry: `coordinator.rs:246-263`
- TigerBeetle storage fault injection: storage.zig fault_config

title: Done-ledger lattice property tests — verify merge commutativity, associativity, idempotence via proptest
description:
## Context

The done-ledger uses a join-semilattice for merge semantics:
DoneLedgerStatus has a total order by rank (FailedRetryable < FailedPermanent
< Skipped < ScannedClean < ScannedWithFindings). The existing conformance
suite tests specific orderings (fail-then-scan, scan-then-fail) but does NOT
verify the algebraic properties (commutativity, associativity, idempotence)
for arbitrary orderings. Bugs that only manifest under specific merge
permutations go undetected.

From lattice theory (Shapiro et al., INRIA 2011): any CRDT merge must satisfy
commutativity, associativity, and idempotence. Property-based testing can
verify these exhaustively for finite lattices.

## Current State

DoneLedgerRecord::merge at `done_ledger.rs:570-643` composes multiple lattice
joins: status (max by rank), bytes_scanned (max), findings_count (status-aware
max), provenance (winner-takes-all), error_code (cleared on scan).

Conformance suite at `conformance.rs` has 4 checks. InMemory tests have
`batch_dedup_then_merge_agrees_with_two_phase_semantics` verifying InMemory
matches Postgres ON CONFLICT semantics. But no test generates N records and
verifies all N! orderings converge.

## Desired State

Proptest-based lattice property verification:

1. **Commutativity**: `a.merge(b) == b.merge(a)` for all a, b
2. **Associativity**: `(a.merge(b)).merge(c) == a.merge(b.merge(c))` for all a, b, c
3. **Idempotence**: `a.merge(a) == a` for all a
4. **Monotonicity**: `a.merge(b).status.rank() >= a.status.rank()` for all a, b
5. **No downgrade**: If `a.status.is_scanned()`, then `a.merge(b).status.is_scanned()` for all b
6. **Convergence under permutation**: For N records (2-8) with the same key,
   applying all records in any order produces the same final state
7. **Provenance consistency**: The winner's fields are coherent (error_code matches
   status, findings_count matches status)

## Implementation Guidance

### Files to Create
| File | Content |
|------|---------|
| `crates/gossip-contracts/src/persistence/lattice_property_tests.rs` | Proptest strategies + property tests |

### Files to Modify
| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `crates/gossip-contracts/src/persistence/mod.rs` | Add `#[cfg(test)] mod lattice_property_tests;` |

### Proptest Strategy
Generate `DoneLedgerRecord` with:
- Fixed key (tenant, policy, ovid) for merge testing
- Random status from all 5 variants
- Random bytes_scanned, findings_count
- Random timestamps (started_at, finished_at)
- Random error codes (Some/None, matching status constraints)
- Random locations, observations

### Patterns to Follow
- Existing proptest usage in `gossip-contracts` (already has `proptest` dep)
- proptest_state_machine pattern from `proptest_state_machine_tests.rs`

## Related Work
gossip-9020: Parent epic

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All 7 lattice properties verified via proptest
- [ ] Permutation convergence tested for 2-8 records per key
- [ ] At least 1000 test cases per property
- [ ] Tests run fast (< 10 seconds in default cargo test)
- [ ] Clean build (fmt + check + clippy + doc)

## Pointers

- DoneLedgerStatus rank: `done_ledger.rs:137-220`
- Conformance harness: `conformance.rs`
- Shapiro et al. CRDT properties: commutativity, associativity, idempotence

title: Build CompositionSim harness — coordinator + done-ledger + scan-driver with cross-component invariants C1-C4
description:
## Context

Individual components have strong testing in isolation, but no simulation
covers the boundaries where distributed systems bugs cluster. From post-mortem
analysis (Yuan et al. OSDI 2014), error handling paths at component
boundaries are the highest-value test targets. A composition simulation
wires coordinator + done-ledger + scan-driver into a single harness with
cross-component invariant checking.

The distributed runtime at `gossip-scanner-runtime/src/distributed.rs`
defines `DistributedCoordinator` which composes acquire_shard + is_shard_done
+ mark_shard_done — this is the natural composition seam.

## Current State

The three components are tested in complete isolation:
- CoordinationSim tests coordination protocol with S1-S9
- InMemoryDoneLedger tests persistence with conformance suite + unit tests
- ScanDriver is a trait with no simulation

No test exercises scenarios like:
- Coordinator marks shard complete but done-ledger write fails
- Fence epoch mismatch between coordinator and done-ledger provenance
- Scan driver retries with stale lease after coordinator reassigns shard
- Worker crashes between marking done in coordinator and writing done-ledger

## Desired State

A `CompositionSim` harness that tests the full lifecycle:

```
create_run → register_shards → claim → (scan → checkpoint)* → complete →
mark_done_in_ledger → verify_cross_component_invariants
```

Components:
- Coordinator: InMemoryCoordinator (or SimEtcdCoordinator when available)
- DoneLedger: InMemoryDoneLedger (with fault injection hooks)
- ScanDriver: SimulatedScanDriver (deterministic scan outcomes)

Shared infrastructure:
- Single SimContext (clock + PRNG)
- FaultConfig extended with cross-component faults (done-ledger failure
  after coordinator complete, stale lease in scan driver)

New cross-component invariants:
- **C1 (DoneLedger-Coordinator consistency)**: If done-ledger has terminal
  status for a shard, the coordinator's shard record must be in terminal state
- **C2 (Complete-then-mark ordering)**: mark_shard_done never called without
  preceding shard completion in coordinator
- **C3 (Fence propagation)**: Fence epoch from acquire_shard is carried
  through scan driver to complete_shard (no stale fences cross boundaries)
- **C4 (No scan after done)**: A shard marked done in the done-ledger is
  never assigned for scanning in subsequent claim operations

## Implementation Guidance

### Files to Create
| File | Content |
|------|---------|
| `crates/gossip-coordination/src/sim/composition.rs` | CompositionSim harness |
| `crates/gossip-coordination/src/sim/composition_invariants.rs` | C1-C4 cross-component invariant checker |
| `crates/gossip-coordination/src/sim/composition_tests.rs` | Test suite for composition sim |
| `crates/gossip-coordination/src/sim/scan_driver_sim.rs` | SimulatedScanDriver |

### Files to Modify
| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `crates/gossip-coordination/src/sim/mod.rs` | Add composition module |
| `crates/gossip-coordination/Cargo.toml` | Add gossip-persistence-inmemory/test-support dep |

### Patterns to Follow
- CoordinationSim three-stage model (harness.rs) for the coordination portion
- InMemoryDoneLedger fault injection hooks (fail_next_commits, delay_next_writes)
- SimulatedScanDriver can be minimal: given a shard assignment, produce a
  deterministic ScanReport after N simulated ticks

### Key Design Decisions
1. **Shared clock**: All components use the same LogicalTime from SimContext.
   The composition harness advances time between operations.
2. **Sequential execution**: Single-threaded, one operation at a time.
   Cross-component invariants checked after each step.
3. **Fault injection at boundaries**: New fault types for the composition:
   - DoneLedger write failure after coordinator completion
   - Stale lease passed from coordinator to scan driver
   - Scan driver crash between checkpoint and done-ledger write

## Related Work

gossip-9020.2: Optional dependency (can use SimEtcdCoordinator for etcd composition testing)
gossip-9020.6: Relates-to (done-ledger sim provides the persistence layer)

title: Differential oracle — compare InMemory vs SimEtcd coordinator and InMemory vs Postgres done-ledger
description:
## Context

The InMemoryCoordinator and SimEtcdCoordinator must produce identical
observable behavior for the same operation sequences. Similarly, the
InMemoryDoneLedger and DoneLedgerPg must converge to the same state for
the same workloads. A differential oracle applies the same randomized
workload to both backends and asserts equivalent results.

This catches "mock drift" — the primary risk identified by all 5 research
agents: a simulation that passes because the simulated backend diverges from
the production backend's actual semantics.

## Current State

No differential testing exists between any pair of backends. The conformance
suite runs independently against each backend but doesn't compare results of
the same randomized workload.

## Desired State

1. **Coordinator differential oracle**: Generate random operation sequences
   (using the existing SimOp generation from proptest_state_machine_tests.rs).
   Execute against both InMemoryCoordinator and SimEtcdCoordinator. After
   each operation, compare:
   - Operation result (success/rejection/error kind)
   - Shard record state (status, fence, cursor, lease)
   - Run record state

2. **DoneLedger differential oracle**: Generate random batch_upsert sequences.
   Execute against both InMemoryDoneLedger and DoneLedgerPg. Compare final
   state via batch_get for all written keys.

The done-ledger oracle requires Docker (for Postgres) and is `#[ignore]`'d.
The coordinator oracle is in-memory and can run in normal CI.

## Implementation Guidance

### Files to Create
| File | Content |
|------|---------|

### Patterns to Follow
- proptest_state_machine_tests.rs for operation sequence generation
- The scanner sim runner's differential oracle pattern (sim_scanner/runner.rs)
- Conformance test fixture isolation (per-seed unique keys)

## Related Work

gossip-9020.5: Relates-to (lattice property tests verify merge correctness)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] DoneLedger oracle: 100+ random batch sequences compared between InMemory and Postgres
- [ ] Any divergence produces a clear reproduction command (seed + op sequence)

title: DoneLedger persistence fault simulation harness
description:
## Context

The coordination subsystem has a mature deterministic simulation harness
(CoordinationSim) that verifies protocol invariants S1-S9 via seeded PRNG,
fault injection, and per-step invariant checking. The persistence
subsystem's InMemoryDoneLedger has production-quality fault injection
(three-counter model: submit failure, delay, commit failure) and
conformance tests, but lacks an orchestration harness. This creates a gap:
persistence failure scenarios (connection drops, commit failures, delayed
writes, out-of-order completion) cannot be systematically tested under
randomized fault injection with invariant verification.

Deep research across FoundationDB, TigerBeetle VOPR, sled, CockroachDB,
and Dropbox Nucleus confirms that deterministic in-process simulation
catches more bugs per CPU-hour than any other approach, and that the
existing InMemoryDoneLedger infrastructure is 80% of what is needed. The
missing 20% is the orchestration layer.

## Current State

### Existing Infrastructure (use these, don't reinvent)

| Component | Location | Purpose |
|-----------|----------|---------|
| InMemoryDoneLedger | gossip-persistence-inmemory/src/done_ledger.rs | Reference impl with fault injection |
| InMemoryStoreCore\<B\> | gossip-persistence-inmemory/src/store.rs:211 | Generic three-counter fault model |
| fail_next_submissions(n) | store.rs:279 | Reject next N submissions (pre-handle) |
| fail_next_commits(n) | store.rs:293 | Fail at commit time (handle.wait errors) |
| delay_next_writes(n) | store.rs:307 | Pending ops requiring manual release |
| release_specific(id) | store.rs:360 | Release a specific delayed op |
| release_all(order) | store.rs:394 | Release all pending ops (FIFO/LIFO) |
| CompletionOrder | store.rs:56 | OldestFirst / NewestFirst enum |
| DoneLedger trait | gossip-contracts/src/persistence/done_ledger.rs:663 | batch_get, batch_upsert, CommitHandle |
| DoneLedgerRecord::merge | gossip-contracts/src/persistence/done_ledger.rs:599 | Lattice merge (status promotion, GREATEST) |
| run_done_ledger_conformance | gossip-contracts/src/persistence/conformance.rs | Backend-agnostic invariant checks |
| CoordinationSim | gossip-coordination/src/sim/harness.rs | Proven sim pattern to follow |
| SimContext (ChaCha8Rng) | gossip-coordination/src/sim/mod.rs:85 | Deterministic PRNG + logical time |
| InvariantChecker | gossip-coordination/src/sim/invariants.rs | Per-step safety verification (S1-S9) |
| FaultInjectingIntrospector | gossip-coordination/src/sim/fault_injector.rs | Wrapper composition pattern for fault injection |
| UPSERT_SQL | gossip-done-ledger-postgres/src/schema.rs:101 | SQL ON CONFLICT with 6 CASE arms |
| DoneLedgerPg | gossip-done-ledger-postgres/src/backend.rs:92 | Production Postgres backend |

### The Gap

No harness drives InMemoryDoneLedger through randomized fault sequences
with invariant checking. The coordination sim tests coordination protocol
invariants (S1-S9) but has no persistence dimension. The conformance tests
verify static properties but not dynamic behavior under failures.

## Desired State

A DoneLedgerSim harness in gossip-persistence-inmemory that:

1. Generates random batch_upsert/batch_get operation sequences via
   seeded ChaCha8Rng (deterministic, reproducible).
2. Injects persistence faults at configurable rates via FaultLevel
   escalation (SunnyDay/Stormy/Radioactive) using the existing
   InMemoryDoneLedger fault injection API.
3. Verifies 10 persistence invariants (I1-I10) after every operation:
   - I1: StatusMonotonicity (status.rank() never decreases per key)
   - I2: BytesScanMonotonicity (bytes_scanned never decreases per key)
   - I3: CommitDurability (after Ok(receipt), batch_get returns record)
   - I4: SubmitRollback (after batch_upsert Err, no records applied)
   - I5: CommitRollback (after wait() Err, no records applied)
   - I6: LatticeConvergence (after all pending ops drain, state equals
     join of all committed records regardless of commit order)
   - I7: MergeConsistency (Rust merge == SQL ON CONFLICT for same inputs)
   - I8: ProvenanceFidelity (provenance from single source, no mixing)
   - I9: ReceiptAccuracy (receipt counts match deduplicated applied batch)
   - I10: IdempotentUpsert (re-upserting identical record is no-op)
4. Runs safety phase (random faults, verify no violations) followed by
   liveness phase (drain all pending ops, verify convergence) — following
   TigerBeetle VOPR pattern already used in CoordinationSim.
5. Exercises the 'swizzle-clogging' pattern: submit N batches with
   delay_next_writes, release in random order via release_specific,
   verify lattice convergence (I6). This is the highest-value test
   pattern and requires zero new fault injection API.
6. Maintains a model-based oracle (separate HashMap applying
   DoneLedgerRecord::merge) as the authoritative reference for
   convergence verification.
7. Provides integration hooks (PersistenceSim trait) for future
   composition with CoordinationSim.

Additionally, a SQL/Rust merge parity proptest in
gossip-done-ledger-postgres verifies that the 6 duplicated CASE arms in
UPSERT_SQL produce identical results to DoneLedgerRecord::merge for
randomly generated record pairs. This addresses the highest-severity
risk identified by research: merge parity drift between the SQL and
Rust implementations.

## Implementation Guidance

### Architecture (follows CoordinationSim pattern)

New module: gossip-persistence-inmemory/src/sim/

| File | Contents |
|------|----------|
| sim/mod.rs | DoneLedgerSimOp, DoneLedgerSimEvent, PersistenceSim trait, re-exports |
| sim/invariants.rs | DoneLedgerInvariantChecker, DoneLedgerInvariantViolation |
| sim/oracle.rs | DoneLedgerOracle (HashMap-based model tracking committed state) |
| sim/harness.rs | DoneLedgerSim, DoneLedgerSimReport, DoneLedgerFaultConfig |
| sim/tests.rs | Seed sweep tests, swizzle-clog tests, proptest state machine |

### Key Design Decisions (evidence-backed)

1. Use InMemoryDoneLedger as sim backend — the DoneLedger trait is the
   abstraction boundary, not the postgres driver (postgres::GenericClient
   is sealed and cannot be mocked at driver level).

2. Create persistence-local SimContext/FaultConfig rather than depending
   on gossip-coordination — avoids circular dependency. Reuse ChaCha8Rng
   and PPM-based fault rates pattern.

3. Exercise both auto-complete mode (mimics DoneLedgerPg synchronous
   commit) and delayed mode (exercises commit-handle protocol and
   out-of-order completion). DoneLedgerPg conflates submit and commit
   into a single synchronous call (ReadyCommitHandle returned after
   tx.commit), so auto-complete mode models this fidelity.

4. The swizzle-clogging pattern exercises order-independent lattice
   merge: delay_next_writes(N) then release_specific in random order.
   The existing InMemoryDoneLedger API supports this directly with zero
   new infrastructure (release_specific at store.rs:360, pending_ids
   at done_ledger.rs:193).

5. DoneLedgerOracle maintains committed state separately from the
   InMemoryDoneLedger. After liveness phase, oracle.committed must
   match ledger snapshot for every key. This catches merge bugs that
   per-step checks cannot detect.

6. SQL/Rust merge parity test uses proptest to generate random record
   pairs, inserts existing record, upserts incoming record, reads back,
   and compares all fields against DoneLedgerRecord::merge output. Gates
   behind #[ignore] since it requires Postgres.

### Submit/Commit Asymmetry

DoneLedgerPg has submit=commit (synchronous). InMemoryDoneLedger
separates them. The sim must exercise both:
- auto_complete=true: models PG synchronous path
- auto_complete=false: exercises delayed-write protocol, swizzle-clog

### Dependency Graph

Steps 1-3 (invariant checker, oracle, op types) → Step 4 (harness core)
→ Steps 5-6 (swizzle-clog, seed sweep). Step 7 (merge parity) is
independent. Step 8 (integration hooks) is trivial.

## Risk Register

| Risk | Severity | Mitigation |
|------|----------|------------|
| SQL/Rust merge parity drift (6 CASE arms) | Critical | I7 invariant + proptest merge parity (Step 7) |
| Asymmetric commit model (PG vs InMemory) | High | Both modes exercised in sim |
| Stale/broken PG connection | Medium | Documented as integration test target, not sim |
| Missing batch_get fault injection | Medium | Deferred; add fail_next_reads later |

## Acceptance Criteria

- gossip-persistence-inmemory/src/sim/ module exists with invariant
  checker, oracle, harness, op/event types, and PersistenceSim trait
- DoneLedgerSim::run(safety_ops, liveness_ops) returns SimReport
  with zero violations for SunnyDay level
- Stormy sweep: 100 seeds x 500 ops, zero invariant violations
- Swizzle-clog sweep: 100 seeds x 10 batches, zero I6 violations
- Radioactive sweep: 50 seeds x 1000 ops, zero violations (#[ignore])
- All 10 invariants (I1-I10) have at least one test that would detect
  violation (inject artificial divergence, verify checker catches it)
- SQL/Rust merge parity proptest: 1000 cases, field-by-field equality
  (requires Postgres, #[ignore])
- DoneLedgerSimReport::event_counts shows all DoneLedgerSimEventKind
  variants exercised across seed sweep (no dead op types)
- cargo fmt --all && cargo check && cargo clippy --all-targets
  --all-features -- -D warnings clean

## Related Work

- gossip-9010: DoneLedgerPg concurrent ops and boundary value tests
  (companion task for integration-level Postgres testing)
- CoordinationSim: gossip-coordination/src/sim/ (pattern to follow)
- run_done_ledger_conformance: gossip-contracts/src/persistence/conformance.rs

## Pointers

- CoordinationSim harness pattern: gossip-coordination/src/sim/harness.rs
- InvariantChecker pattern: gossip-coordination/src/sim/invariants.rs
- InMemoryStoreCore fault injection: gossip-persistence-inmemory/src/store.rs:152-174
- InMemoryDoneLedger release controls: gossip-persistence-inmemory/src/done_ledger.rs:193-218
- DoneLedgerRecord::merge: gossip-contracts/src/persistence/done_ledger.rs:599-643
- UPSERT_SQL 6 CASE arms: gossip-done-ledger-postgres/src/schema.rs:133-194
- TigerBeetle VOPR storage.zig: reference for fault-injecting storage sim
- FoundationDB simulation docs: apple.github.io/foundationdb/testing.html
close_reason: All 3 children complete. Sim module (invariant checker, oracle, harness, tests) delivered in gossip-persistence-inmemory/src/sim/. SQL/Rust merge parity proptest delivered in gossip-done-ledger-postgres. 32 tests total covering all 10 invariants, swizzle-clog, seed sweeps, and merge parity.

title: DoneLedgerSim harness core: invariant checker, oracle, ops, and harness driver
description:
## Context

This is sub-task A of the DoneLedger persistence fault simulation harness
epic (gossip-9021). It builds the core infrastructure: the invariant
checker, model oracle, op/event types, harness driver, and integration
trait. Sub-task B (test suite) and sub-task C (merge parity) depend on
or complement this work.

## Current State

The InMemoryDoneLedger (gossip-persistence-inmemory/src/done_ledger.rs)
has production-quality fault injection via InMemoryStoreCore (store.rs):
- fail_next_submissions(n) at store.rs:279
- fail_next_commits(n) at store.rs:293
- delay_next_writes(n) at store.rs:307
- release_specific(id) at store.rs:360
- release_all(order) at store.rs:394
- CompletionOrder (OldestFirst/NewestFirst) at store.rs:56
- set_auto_complete(bool) for toggling delayed mode
- pending_ids() at done_ledger.rs:193 for enumerating pending ops

No sim module exists in gossip-persistence-inmemory. No orchestration
harness drives the fault injection with invariant verification.

The CoordinationSim pattern to follow lives at:
- gossip-coordination/src/sim/harness.rs (harness driver)
- gossip-coordination/src/sim/invariants.rs (invariant checker)
- gossip-coordination/src/sim/mod.rs (SimContext, SimOp, FaultLevel)
- gossip-coordination/src/sim/backend.rs (SimulationBackend trait)

## Desired State

A new sim module at gossip-persistence-inmemory/src/sim/ containing:

### 1. Invariant Checker (sim/invariants.rs)

DoneLedgerInvariantChecker struct maintaining per-key history maps for
temporal monotonicity checks. Verifies I1-I6, I8-I10 after every step:

- I1: StatusMonotonicity — status.rank() never decreases for any key
  after a committed operation. Track prev_status: HashMap<DoneLedgerKey, u8>.
- I2: BytesScanMonotonicity — bytes_scanned never decreases per key.
  Track prev_bytes: HashMap<DoneLedgerKey, u64>.
- I3: CommitDurability — after CommitHandle::wait() returns Ok(receipt),
  batch_get for every key in that batch returns Some(record).
- I4: SubmitRollback — after batch_upsert returns Err, batch_get for
  every key in the attempted batch returns the pre-submission state.
- I5: CommitRollback — after wait() returns Err (InjectedCommitFailure),
  batch_get for every key returns the pre-submission state.
- I6: LatticeConvergence — checked in liveness phase only. After all
  pending ops drain, the ledger state for every key equals the oracle's
  expected state (join of all committed records).
- I8: ProvenanceFidelity — after merge, provenance fields come from a
  single source record (the status-rank winner, or finished_at tiebreak
  winner if equal rank).
- I9: ReceiptAccuracy — DoneLedgerCommitReceipt record_count,
  scanned_count, and findings_count match the deduplicated batch.
- I10: IdempotentUpsert — upserting an identical record produces no
  state change in batch_get result.

DoneLedgerInvariantViolation enum with a variant per invariant. The
check_after_upsert and check_after_get methods accept the operation
context (keys involved, result) and return Vec<Violation>.

Pattern to follow: gossip-coordination/src/sim/invariants.rs
InvariantChecker::check_all (checks S1-S9 after every op).

### 2. Model Oracle (sim/oracle.rs)

DoneLedgerOracle struct maintaining:
- committed: HashMap<DoneLedgerKey, DoneLedgerRecord> — the expected
  durable state. Only records that have been committed (handle.wait()
  returned Ok) are merged here using DoneLedgerRecord::merge.
- pending: HashMap<PendingWriteId, Vec<DoneLedgerRecord>> — records
  submitted but not yet committed.

Methods:
- submit(op_id, records) — register a batch as pending
- commit(op_id) — merge pending batch into committed state
- abort(op_id) — discard pending batch (submit or commit failed)
- expected_state(key) -> Option<&DoneLedgerRecord> — oracle lookup
- verify_convergence(ledger) -> Vec<Violation> — for I6

The oracle applies DoneLedgerRecord::merge (done_ledger.rs:599) to
the committed map, so its logic is structurally identical to what
InMemoryDoneLedger does internally.

### 3. SimOp and SimEvent Types (sim/mod.rs)

DoneLedgerSimOp enum:
- BatchUpsert { records: Vec<DoneLedgerRecord> }
- BatchGet { tenant, policy, ovid_hashes }
- ReleaseOldest
- ReleaseNewest
- ReleaseSpecific { op_id }
- ReleaseAll { order: CompletionOrder }
- InjectSubmitFailure { count }
- InjectCommitFailure { count }
- InjectDelay { count }

DoneLedgerSimEvent enum (mirrors outcomes):
- UpsertOk { op_id, receipt }
- UpsertPending { op_id }
- UpsertSubmitFailed
- GetOk { results }
- Released { op_id }
- ReleasedAll { count }
- CommitOk { op_id, receipt }
- CommitFailed { op_id }
- FaultConfigured

DoneLedgerSimEventKind enum (for counting in report).

Pattern to follow: CoordinationSim SimOp variants at harness.rs:167-283.

### 4. Harness Driver (sim/harness.rs)

DoneLedgerSim struct composing:
- context: persistence-local SimContext (ChaCha8Rng + monotonic counter)
- ledger: InMemoryDoneLedger
- oracle: DoneLedgerOracle
- checker: DoneLedgerInvariantChecker
- fault_config: DoneLedgerFaultConfig
- tenant/policy: fixed identity for record generation
- ovid_pool: Vec<OvidHash> — shared key pool for overlapping writes
- ops_executed: usize

DoneLedgerFaultConfig with PPM-based fault rates:
- submit_fail_ppm: u32
- commit_fail_ppm: u32
- delay_ppm: u32
Preset levels: SunnyDay (all 0), Stormy (~100k each), Radioactive (~200k).

Core method: step(op) -> (DoneLedgerSimEvent, Vec<Violation>)
1. Execute the op against InMemoryDoneLedger
2. Update oracle (submit/commit/abort)
3. Run invariant checker against affected keys
4. Return event + any violations

Run method: run(safety_ops, liveness_ops) -> DoneLedgerSimReport
1. Safety phase: generate weighted random ops using PRNG, inject
   faults based on fault_config PPM rates, call step() for each.
2. Liveness phase: disable all fault injection, release all pending
   writes, run additional ops without faults, verify I6 convergence.

Weighted op generation: BatchUpsert (high weight, varying batch sizes
1-50 with overlapping keys from ovid_pool), BatchGet (medium weight),
fault injection ops (weight proportional to fault_config).

Exercise both auto_complete modes:
- true during some safety sub-phases (models DoneLedgerPg synchronous)
- false during delay/release sub-phases (exercises commit-handle protocol)

### 5. Integration Trait (sim/mod.rs)

PersistenceSim trait:
  fn step(&mut self, op: Self::Op) -> (Self::Event, Vec<Self::Violation>);

DoneLedgerSim implements PersistenceSim. This is a hook for future
CoordinationSim composition — no consumers yet.

### DoneLedgerSimReport

pub struct DoneLedgerSimReport {
    pub seed: u64,
    pub ops_executed: usize,
    pub violations: Vec<DoneLedgerInvariantViolation>,
    pub event_counts: BTreeMap<DoneLedgerSimEventKind, usize>,
    pub converged: bool,
}

## Implementation Guidance

- Follow CoordinationSim pattern exactly for structure. Key files to
  reference:
  - harness.rs:1182-1238 for run() three-phase structure
  - invariants.rs for per-step checking pattern
  - mod.rs:85-120 for SimContext
  - harness.rs:167-283 for SimOp pattern
  - harness.rs:494-526 for event coverage tracking

- Create persistence-local SimContext/FaultConfig rather than depending
  on gossip-coordination. This avoids circular dependency. Reuse the
  ChaCha8Rng + PPM pattern but don't import from coordination crate.

- The InMemoryDoneLedger is cloneable (Arc-based). The harness owns
  one instance and passes it to the invariant checker for reads.

- For record generation: use the ovid_pool (fixed set of ~50 OvidHash
  values) so that batch_upsert calls naturally create overlapping keys.
  Vary status, bytes_scanned, findings_count, and provenance per record
  using the PRNG. Use test_util helpers (tenant, policy, ovid) from
  gossip-contracts for identity construction.

- Basic unit tests in this task should verify that each invariant
  checker variant fires correctly (inject artificial divergence, verify
  detection). Full seed-sweep tests are in sub-task B.

## Acceptance Criteria

- gossip-persistence-inmemory/src/sim/ module exists with mod.rs,
  invariants.rs, oracle.rs, harness.rs
- DoneLedgerSim::new(seed, level) constructs successfully
- DoneLedgerSim::step(op) executes and returns (event, violations)
- DoneLedgerSim::run(100, 50) completes for SunnyDay with zero violations
- Each invariant (I1-I6, I8-I10) has at least one unit test that
  verifies the checker detects artificial violations
- Oracle verify_convergence correctly detects injected divergence
- DoneLedgerSimReport tracks event counts for all event kinds
- PersistenceSim trait exists and DoneLedgerSim implements it
- cargo fmt --all && cargo check && cargo clippy --all-targets
  --all-features -- -D warnings clean
close_reason: Implemented DoneLedgerSim harness core with invariant checker (I1-I6, I8-I10), model oracle, op/event types, harness driver with safety/liveness phases, and PersistenceSim trait. All tests pass, clippy clean.

title: DoneLedgerSim test suite: swizzle-clog pattern and seed-sweep tests
description:
## Context

Sub-task B of the DoneLedger persistence fault simulation harness epic
(gossip-9021). Depends on gossip-9021.1 (harness core). Builds the test
suite that exercises the harness across seeds and fault levels.

## Current State

After gossip-9021.1, the DoneLedgerSim harness exists with step(),
run(), invariant checker (I1-I10), oracle, and fault configuration.
Basic unit tests verify invariant detection. What is missing: systematic
seed-sweep tests and the swizzle-clogging pattern.

## Desired State

### 1. Swizzle-Clog Test Pattern (sim/harness.rs or sim/tests.rs)

A run_swizzle_clog method on DoneLedgerSim:
1. Disable auto-complete (set_auto_complete(false)).
2. Submit N batches (e.g., 10), each with overlapping keys from the
   ovid_pool and varying status ranks per batch (thread 1 writes
   FailedRetryable, thread 2 writes ScannedWithFindings for same keys).
3. Inject some commit failures (fail_next_commits) on a subset.
4. Release batches in a random permutation via release_specific,
   seeded from SimContext PRNG.
5. After all released (or failed), verify I6 (LatticeConvergence):
   oracle committed state equals ledger snapshot for all keys.

This is the highest-value test pattern identified by research:
FoundationDB calls it 'swizzle-clogging' — staggered partial-failure-
partial-recovery that exercises order-independent lattice merge. The
InMemoryDoneLedger API supports it directly:
- delay_next_writes(n) at store.rs:307
- release_specific(id) at store.rs:360
- pending_ids() at done_ledger.rs:193

### 2. Seed-Sweep Tests (sim/tests.rs)

Following the mega_sim_tests pattern from CoordinationSim:

a) done_ledger_sim_sunny_day
   Single seed, SunnyDay level, 200 ops. Zero violations.
   Fast sanity check.

b) done_ledger_sim_stormy_sweep
   100 seeds x Stormy x 500 ops. Zero violations.
   Main regression suite.

c) done_ledger_sim_swizzle_clog_sweep
   100 seeds x 10 batches x random release order. Zero I6 violations.
   The core convergence test.

d) done_ledger_sim_radioactive
   50 seeds x Radioactive x 1000 ops. Zero violations.
   Mark #[ignore] — heavy test for CI.

e) Proptest state machine test
   Following the proptest_state_machine_tests.rs pattern from the
   coordination sim. Generate arbitrary DoneLedgerSimOp sequences,
   shrink on failure. This provides automatic minimization of failing
   inputs.

### 3. Coverage Analysis

DoneLedgerSimReport::event_counts verification: after the stormy sweep,
assert that every DoneLedgerSimEventKind variant has fired at least
once across all seeds. Zero-count variants indicate a generation weight
bug or unreachable op.

Pattern to follow: CoordinationSim coverage tracking at harness.rs:494-526.

## Implementation Guidance

- Reference mega_sim_tests.rs in gossip-coordination for seed-sweep
  test structure.
- Reference proptest_state_machine_tests.rs for proptest integration.
- The swizzle-clog pattern should generate batches with different
  status ranks for overlapping keys:
  - Batch 1: keys [A,B,C] with FailedRetryable
  - Batch 2: keys [B,C,D] with ScannedWithFindings
  - Batch 3: keys [A,D,E] with ScannedClean
  This creates interesting merge scenarios when release order varies.
- Use #[ignore] for radioactive tests — they are expensive.
- Proptest config: 256 cases, max shrink iters 1000.
- Test time budget: stormy sweep should complete in <10s. If it
  exceeds this, reduce ops_per_seed or increase batch efficiency.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Swizzle-clog sweep: 100 seeds x 10 batches, zero I6 violations
- Stormy sweep: 100 seeds x 500 ops, zero invariant violations
- SunnyDay single-seed test passes
- Radioactive sweep: 50 seeds x 1000 ops, zero violations (#[ignore])
- Proptest state machine: 256 cases, shrinks on failure
- Event coverage: all DoneLedgerSimEventKind variants exercised
- Stormy sweep completes in <10s
- cargo fmt/check/clippy clean

title: SQL/Rust merge parity proptest for DoneLedgerPg UPSERT_SQL
description:
## Context

Sub-task C of the DoneLedger persistence fault simulation harness epic
(gossip-9021). Independent of gossip-9021.1 and gossip-9021.2 — can
run in parallel.

Deep research identified SQL/Rust merge parity drift as the highest-
severity risk in the done-ledger subsystem: the UPSERT_SQL statement
(schema.rs:101-236) contains 6 duplicated CASE arms for provenance
winner selection that must remain in exact parity with
DoneLedgerRecord::merge (done_ledger.rs:599-643). The SQL comment at
schema.rs:141-144 explicitly warns: 'All 6 CASE arms MUST use the
identical condition... Edits to one CASE branch must be mirrored in
all others.'

No existing test verifies field-by-field parity between the SQL merge
and Rust merge for arbitrary inputs. The existing test
upsert_sql_case_branches_use_correct_scanned_discriminants
(migrations.rs:503) only checks discriminant values, not full merge
semantics across all provenance fields.

## Current State

File: crates/gossip-done-ledger-postgres/src/tests.rs (747 lines)
File: crates/gossip-done-ledger-postgres/src/schema.rs (UPSERT_SQL)
File: crates/gossip-contracts/src/persistence/done_ledger.rs (merge)

The UPSERT_SQL ON CONFLICT clause (schema.rs:133-194):
- Status: GREATEST(EXCLUDED.status, table.status) — promotes to higher rank
- bytes_scanned: GREATEST(EXCLUDED, table) — monotonic
- findings_count: status-dependent CASE (reset for ScannedClean, floor for
  ScannedWithFindings, max otherwise)
- 6 provenance columns (run_id, shard_id, fence_epoch, started_at,
  finished_at, error_code): each has an identical CASE expression selecting
  the winner based on status rank comparison, then finished_at tiebreak,
  then started_at tiebreak

DoneLedgerRecord::merge (done_ledger.rs:599-643):
- Picks winner by status rank, then finished_at, then started_at
- Applies same GREATEST/reset/floor logic for counters
- Returns merged record with winner's provenance

Both implementations should produce identical results for the same inputs.
A divergence means the in-memory reference backend and the production PG
backend silently produce different merge results — data corruption that
no existing test catches.

## Desired State

A proptest-driven cross-implementation merge parity test in
crates/gossip-done-ledger-postgres/src/tests.rs that:

1. Generates random (existing, incoming) DoneLedgerRecord pairs with:
   - Same key (tenant, policy, ovid)
   - Varying DoneLedgerStatus (all 5 variants)
   - Varying bytes_scanned (0, small, large, near-i64::MAX boundary)
   - Varying findings_count (0, small, i32::MAX boundary, status-valid)
   - Varying provenance timestamps (equal, different, crossed)
   - Varying error_codes (None, Some for error statuses)
   Records must satisfy DoneLedgerRecord::try_new and validate()
   invariants (ScannedClean requires findings_count=0, error statuses
   require error_code, etc.).

2. For each pair:
   a. Compute Rust merge: existing.merge(&incoming)
   b. Insert 'existing' into a fresh test database
   c. Upsert 'incoming' via batch_upsert (triggers SQL ON CONFLICT)
   d. Read back the merged row via batch_get
   e. Assert field-by-field equality between Rust merge result and
      SQL merge result:
      - status
      - bytes_scanned
      - findings_count
      - provenance (run_id, shard_id, fence_epoch, started_at,
        finished_at)
      - error_code

3. Test both merge directions: (A merge B) and (B merge A) to verify
   commutativity holds in SQL as well as Rust.

## Implementation Guidance

- Use proptest with a custom strategy for generating valid DoneLedgerRecord
  pairs. The strategy must respect cross-field invariants:
  - ScannedClean: findings_count == 0, error_code == None
  - ScannedWithFindings: findings_count >= 1, error_code == None
  - FailedRetryable/FailedPermanent: error_code.is_some()
  - Skipped: error_code == None
  - started_at <= finished_at
  - bytes_scanned fits in i64 (< i64::MAX for PG bigint)
  - findings_count fits in i32 (< i32::MAX for PG integer)

- For inserting the 'existing' record: use the try_insert helper
  (tests.rs:568) with RowOverrides to bypass batch_upsert and insert
  directly (avoids double-merge). OR use batch_upsert on a clean table.

- For each proptest case, use truncate_all_for_tests() to start clean,
  then insert existing, then upsert incoming.

- Mark test as #[ignore = "requires Docker or GOSSIP_POSTGRES_TEST_URL"]
  since it requires a running Postgres instance.

- proptest config: 1000 cases. The test will be slow (real PG per case)
  so consider #[ignore] and running in CI only.

- Alternatively, batch the proptest: generate 100 pairs, run them
  sequentially within one test function to amortize PG connection cost.

- File: crates/gossip-done-ledger-postgres/src/tests.rs

- Existing helpers to reuse:
  - done_record() at tests.rs:206 for constructing records
  - provenance() at tests.rs:186 for constructing provenance
  - test_client() at test_postgres.rs:147 for PG connection
  - truncate_all_for_tests() at backend.rs:168 for table cleanup
  - DoneLedgerRecord::merge at done_ledger.rs:599

## Acceptance Criteria

- Proptest with 1000 cases: all pass with field-by-field merge parity
- Both merge directions tested (A merge B, B merge A)
- All 5 DoneLedgerStatus variants appear in generated pairs
- Test covers the provenance tiebreak paths:
  - Higher status wins
  - Equal status, later finished_at wins
  - Equal status and finished_at, later started_at wins
- Test marked #[ignore] (requires Postgres)
- cargo fmt/check/clippy clean

## Related Work

- gossip-9021: Parent epic
- gossip-9021.1: Harness core (independent)
- gossip-9021.2: Test suite (independent)
- gossip-9010: DoneLedgerPg concurrent ops and boundary value tests

## Pointers

- UPSERT_SQL: gossip-done-ledger-postgres/src/schema.rs:101-236
- DoneLedgerRecord::merge: gossip-contracts/src/persistence/done_ledger.rs:599-643
- SQL parity warning comment: schema.rs:141-144
- Existing discriminant test: migrations.rs:503
- try_insert helper: tests.rs:568
- test_client: test_postgres.rs:147
