title: Extract shared migration runner into gossip-pg-common
description:
## Context

The forward-only embedded migration runner is duplicated wholesale across two
Postgres backend crates: `gossip-findings-postgres` and `gossip-done-ledger-postgres`.
Both crates contain structurally identical copies of `EmbeddedMigration`, 10 runner
functions, SQL-generation helpers, checksum verification logic, the migration error
type (3 variants each), and the corresponding unit test suites. The only differences
are the error type name, the history table name, and the advisory lock key.

This duplication was an intentional short-term decision (noted in gossip-9012.3:
"defined locally to avoid coupling"), but with two consumers now stable, the
extraction is justified.

## Current State

Two near-identical migration modules exist:

```rust
// crates/gossip-findings-postgres/src/migrations.rs:88-128 — EmbeddedMigration (findings copy)
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
pub struct EmbeddedMigration {
    version: &'static str,
    sql: &'static str,
}

impl EmbeddedMigration {
    pub const fn new(version: &'static str, sql: &'static str) -> Self {
        Self { version, sql }
    }
    pub const fn version(self) -> &'static str { self.version }
    pub const fn sql(self) -> &'static str { self.sql }
    pub fn checksum(self) -> Hash { blake3::hash(self.sql.as_bytes()) }
}
```

```rust
// crates/gossip-done-ledger-postgres/src/migrations.rs:85-125 — EmbeddedMigration (done-ledger copy)
// Structurally identical to the findings version.
```

The runner function (`apply_migrations`) is duplicated at:
- `crates/gossip-findings-postgres/src/migrations.rs:206-237`
- `crates/gossip-done-ledger-postgres/src/migrations.rs:217-254`

The migration error types are duplicated at:
- `crates/gossip-findings-postgres/src/error.rs:57-131` (`FindingsPgMigrationError`)
- `crates/gossip-done-ledger-postgres/src/error.rs:36-107` (`DoneLedgerPgMigrationError`)

Both error types have identical structure: `Postgres`, `ChecksumMismatch`, `CorruptedHistoryRecord`.

The shared crate `gossip-pg-common` already hosts `MigrationOperation` (the only
piece previously extracted):

```rust
// crates/gossip-pg-common/src/migration.rs:14-32
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum MigrationOperation {
    Connect, Configure, HistoryTable, AdvisoryLock,
    ApplyMigration, QueryMigration, RecordMigration, Commit,
}
```

The two parameterization points that differ between crates:

```rust
// crates/gossip-findings-postgres/src/schema.rs:40-46
pub const SCHEMA_MIGRATIONS_TABLE: &str = "findings_schema_migrations";
pub const MIGRATION_ADVISORY_LOCK_KEY: i64 = 0x47465047_4d494731; // "GFPGMIG1"

// crates/gossip-done-ledger-postgres/src/schema.rs:17,46
pub const SCHEMA_MIGRATIONS_TABLE: &str = "done_ledger_schema_migrations";
pub const MIGRATION_ADVISORY_LOCK_KEY: i64 = 0x4753444c_50474d31; // "GSDLPGM1"
```

## Desired State

A single `gossip_pg_common::migration` module that owns:

1. `EmbeddedMigration` struct (one copy)
2. `PgMigrationError` enum (single concrete error type replacing both crate-specific copies)
3. `apply_migrations(client, migrations, lock_timeout, config)` core runner
4. `apply_all_migrations(client, migrations, config)` convenience wrapper
5. SQL helpers: `create_migrations_table_sql`, `select_migration_checksum_sql`, `insert_migration_sql`
6. `verify_stored_checksum` function
7. All shared unit tests (checksum determinism, mismatch, corrupted record, etc.)

`MigrationConfig` (or direct parameters) carries the two per-crate values:
- `history_table: &'static str`
- `advisory_lock_key: i64`

Each backend crate reduces to:
- A `MIGRATIONS` const with `include_str!` entries
- A thin `apply_all_migrations` that calls the shared runner with its config
- A `connect_and_apply_migrations` test helper (if `test-utils` feature)
- Crate-specific domain tests (golden checksums, SQL content assertions)

## Implementation Guidance

### Files to Modify

| File | Change | Rationale |
|------|--------|-----------|
| `crates/gossip-pg-common/Cargo.toml` | Add `postgres = "0.19"`, `blake3 = "1.8"` deps | Runner needs DB client and checksum |
| `crates/gossip-pg-common/src/migration.rs` | Add `EmbeddedMigration`, `PgMigrationError`, runner fns, SQL helpers, `verify_stored_checksum`, unit tests | Central extraction target |
| `crates/gossip-pg-common/src/lib.rs` | Update module doc table, add re-exports | Public API surface |
| `crates/gossip-findings-postgres/src/migrations.rs` | Replace 10 functions + struct with delegation to `gossip_pg_common::migration` | Deduplication |
| `crates/gossip-findings-postgres/src/error.rs` | Remove `FindingsPgMigrationError`, re-export `PgMigrationError` (or alias) | Single error type |
| `crates/gossip-findings-postgres/src/lib.rs` | Update re-exports | Point at new locations |
| `crates/gossip-done-ledger-postgres/src/migrations.rs` | Same reduction as findings | Deduplication |
| `crates/gossip-done-ledger-postgres/src/error.rs` | Remove `DoneLedgerPgMigrationError`, re-export `PgMigrationError` | Single error type |
| `crates/gossip-done-ledger-postgres/src/lib.rs` | Update re-exports | Point at new locations |
| `crates/gossip-done-ledger-postgres/src/backend.rs` | Update call sites (lines 58, 127, 160) | Caller uses new shared API |
| `crates/gossip-done-ledger-postgres/src/tests.rs` | Update imports, error pattern matches (lines 31, 48, 49, 75, 83) | Test compatibility |
| `crates/gossip-done-ledger-postgres/src/test_postgres.rs` | Update `apply_all_migrations` import (line 150) | Test compatibility |

### Patterns to Follow

The existing `gossip_pg_common::types` module demonstrates the sharing pattern:
types are defined in `gossip-pg-common`, then re-exported via `pub use` in each
backend crate's `types.rs`. Follow the same approach for migration types.

### Utilities to Reuse

`MigrationOperation` at `crates/gossip-pg-common/src/migration.rs:14-32` is already
shared and should be used directly by the new runner code.

### Blast Radius

| Caller/Dependent | File | Impact |
|------------------|------|--------|
| `DoneLedgerPg::apply_migrations` | `done-ledger-postgres/src/backend.rs:158-161` | Import path changes |
| `DoneLedgerPg::connect_and_migrate` | `done-ledger-postgres/src/backend.rs:127-131` | Import path changes |
| Integration tests | `done-ledger-postgres/src/tests.rs:31,48,49,75,83` | Error variant names may change |
| Test helper | `done-ledger-postgres/src/test_postgres.rs:150` | Import path changes |
| Crate root re-exports | `findings-postgres/src/lib.rs:56-57` | Re-export source changes |
| Crate root re-exports | `done-ledger-postgres/src/lib.rs:79-80` | Re-export source changes |
| Error re-exports | Both crates `error.rs` | Already re-export `MigrationOperation` from pg-common |

## Design Notes

**Error type strategy**: Define a single concrete `PgMigrationError` in
`gossip-pg-common` rather than a generic trait. Both existing error types are
structurally identical, and the project's "one code path per behavior" mandate
favors a single type. Each backend crate can re-export or type-alias it.

**Dependency impact**: Adding `postgres` and `blake3` to `gossip-pg-common` changes
it from zero-runtime-dependency to two dependencies. This is appropriate because the
migration runner is inherently coupled to PostgreSQL. The `types` module remains
dependency-free.

**Public API preservation**: Both crates re-export `EmbeddedMigration`,
`apply_all_migrations`, `apply_migrations`, and `connect_and_apply_migrations`. These
re-exports should be preserved (pointing at `gossip-pg-common`) so that callers in
`backend.rs`, `tests.rs`, and `test_postgres.rs` require only import path updates,
not API changes.

## Code References

```rust
// crates/gossip-findings-postgres/src/migrations.rs:50-61 — SQL helper (duplicated)
fn create_migrations_table_sql() -> String {
    format!(
        r#"
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS {table} (
    version      TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    checksum     BYTEA NOT NULL CHECK (octet_length(checksum) = 32),
    applied_at   TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);
"#,
        table = SCHEMA_MIGRATIONS_TABLE
    )
}
```

```rust
// crates/gossip-findings-postgres/src/migrations.rs:258-283 — apply_or_verify (duplicated)
fn apply_or_verify_migration(
    tx: &mut Transaction<'_>,
    migration: EmbeddedMigration,
    select_sql: &str,
    insert_sql: &str,
) -> Result<(), FindingsPgMigrationError> {
    let expected_checksum = migration.checksum();
    let version = migration.version();
    let row = tx.query_opt(select_sql, &[&version])
        .map_err(|e| FindingsPgMigrationError::postgres(MigrationOperation::QueryMigration, e))?;
    if let Some(row) = row {
        let found_checksum: Vec<u8> = row.try_get(0).map_err(|e| {
            FindingsPgMigrationError::postgres(MigrationOperation::QueryMigration, e)
        })?;
        verify_stored_checksum(version, expected_checksum, &found_checksum)?;
        return Ok(());
    }
    tx.batch_execute(migration.sql())
        .map_err(|e| FindingsPgMigrationError::postgres(MigrationOperation::ApplyMigration, e))?;
    let checksum_bytes: &[u8] = expected_checksum.as_bytes();
    tx.execute(insert_sql, &[&version, &checksum_bytes])
        .map_err(|e| FindingsPgMigrationError::postgres(MigrationOperation::RecordMigration, e))?;
    Ok(())
}
```

```rust
// crates/gossip-findings-postgres/src/error.rs:57-94 — FindingsPgMigrationError
#[derive(Debug)]
pub enum FindingsPgMigrationError {
    Postgres { operation: MigrationOperation, source: postgres::Error },
    ChecksumMismatch { version: &'static str, expected_hex: String, found_hex: String },
    CorruptedHistoryRecord { version: &'static str, found_len: usize },
}
```

```rust
// crates/gossip-pg-common/Cargo.toml:12-13 — currently no runtime deps
[dependencies]
# Pure Rust types and inline conversion functions — no runtime dependencies.
```

## Related Work

| Task ID | Title | Relationship |
|---------|-------|-------------|
| gossip-9012.3 | D1.3 — SQL migration file and forward-only migration runner | relates-to (currently in_progress; acknowledged duplication as intentional) |
| gossip-9012.4 | D1.4 — Test infrastructure and Postgres integration tests | relates-to (will consume migration runner API) |
| gossip-9012 | D1 — Findings Postgres schema, migrations, and row projections | relates-to (parent epic) |
| gossip-9006.1 | C1.1 — Postgres done-ledger crate scaffold, schema, migrations | relates-to (closed; originally created the done-ledger migration pattern) |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `EmbeddedMigration`, `PgMigrationError`, and all runner functions live in `gossip-pg-common::migration`
- [ ] `gossip-findings-postgres::migrations` contains only `MIGRATIONS` const, thin wrappers, and domain-specific tests
- [ ] `gossip-done-ledger-postgres::migrations` contains only `MIGRATIONS` const, thin wrappers, and domain-specific tests
- [ ] No duplicated function bodies remain across the two backend crates
- [ ] All existing tests pass: `cargo test -p gossip-pg-common -p gossip-findings-postgres -p gossip-done-ledger-postgres`
- [ ] Code compiles clean: `cargo fmt --all && cargo check && cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`
- [ ] `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps --all-features` passes

## Pointers

- `crates/gossip-pg-common/src/types.rs` — existing sharing pattern to follow for re-exports
- `crates/gossip-pg-common/src/lib.rs:1-30` — module doc table that needs updating
- `crates/gossip-done-ledger-postgres/src/tests.rs` — integration tests that pattern-match on error variants (most fragile call sites)

Extract proptest infrastructure from tests.rs into merge_parity_proptest.rs
description:
## Context

`gossip-done-ledger-postgres/src/tests.rs` is ~1,700 lines mixing four distinct
test categories: migration runner, DoneLedger backend behavior, schema constraint
enforcement, and SQL/Rust merge parity proptests. The proptest infrastructure
alone (~630 lines) has its own types, strategies, helpers, and coverage-tracking
machinery that is logically independent of the other three categories.

Extracting the proptest infrastructure into a dedicated submodule reduces
cognitive load when navigating the file and makes the proptest code independently
reviewable.

## Current State

All proptest infrastructure lives inline in a single file:

```rust
// crates/gossip-done-ledger-postgres/src/tests.rs:271-end
// Contains:
//   - Constants: PG_BIGINT_MAX, PG_INTEGER_MAX, proptest_case_count(), VALID_ERROR_CODES, ALL_STATUSES
//   - Types: MergeScenario, MergeParityCase
//   - Strategies: arb_status(), arb_provenance(), arb_record_for_status(), arb_merge_parity_case()
//   - Assertion helper: assert_sql_merge_matches_rust_merge()
//   - Test function: sql_on_conflict_merge_matches_rust_merge_proptest()
//   - Coverage tracking: seen_statuses, saw_higher_status, saw_later_finished, etc.
```

The file also contains ~900 lines of non-proptest tests (migration, backend
behavior, schema constraints, COALESCE coverage) that would remain in `tests.rs`.

## Desired State

```
crates/gossip-done-ledger-postgres/src/tests.rs           (~900 lines, non-proptest tests)
crates/gossip-done-ledger-postgres/src/tests/
    mod.rs                                                  (re-exports, shared helpers)
    merge_parity_proptest.rs                               (~630 lines, all proptest infra)
```

Alternatively, if the existing `tests.rs` structure makes a `tests/` directory
awkward, use `#[path = "..."]` module inclusion from within `tests.rs`.

## Implementation Guidance

title: Fuse projection and dedup in findings backend for memory efficiency
description:
## Context

The PostgreSQL findings backend currently uses a two-pass approach: first project all records
from contracts types to row types, then deduplicate via HashMap. This doubles peak memory
because both the projected Vec and the HashMap exist simultaneously.

## Current State

- `project_and_dedupe` in `crates/gossip-findings-postgres/src/backend.rs` projects all rows
  into Vecs, then passes them to `dedupe_*_rows` functions that build HashMap + order Vec.
- `drain_in_order` helper reconstructs insertion order from the HashMap.
- At max batch size (~10k records), peak memory is ~20MB (projected Vec + HashMap).

## Desired State

- Single-pass approach: project each record and insert directly into `HashMap<Key, usize>`
  indexing into an output Vec.
- Eliminates `drain_in_order` entirely (it becomes unnecessary when output Vec IS the order).
- Halves peak memory from ~20MB to ~10MB at max batch size.
- `merge_observation_rows` can take owned params (enables String moves instead of clones).

## Implementation Guidance

- Replace `dedupe_findings_rows`, `dedupe_occurrence_rows`, `dedupe_observation_rows` with
  fused project-and-dedupe functions.
- Use `HashMap<Key, usize>` where usize indexes into the output Vec.
- Delete `drain_in_order` helper.
- Change `merge_observation_rows` signature to take owned `ObservationRow` params.
- Files to modify: `crates/gossip-findings-postgres/src/backend.rs`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Single-pass projection+dedup with HashMap<Key, usize> indexing
- [ ] `drain_in_order` deleted
- [ ] `merge_observation_rows` takes owned params
- [ ] All existing tests pass
- [ ] cargo fmt/check/clippy/doc clean

title: Extract coordination conformance harness over SimulationBackend
description:
## Context

gossip-8975 was reviewed and split into three sub-tasks (A->B->C). This is sub-task B: extract the 15 conformance test bodies from `conformance_tests.rs` into a reusable harness function generic over `SimulationBackend`, and call it from the existing test module with `InMemoryCoordinator`.

This follows the proven persistence conformance pattern where the harness lives in the shared crate and backend crates call it from their test suites.

## Current State

### 15 conformance tests hardcoded to InMemoryCoordinator

The conformance tests at `crates/gossip-coordination/src/conformance_tests.rs` (1053 lines, 15 tests) use:

- **`shard_lookup`** -- 21 calls. This method is on `SimIntrospection` (line 131 of `sim/backend.rs`), not on `CoordinationBackend`. Both `InMemoryCoordinator` and `SimEtcdCoordinator` implement it.
- **`.slab()`** -- 16 calls (lines: 177, 178, 179, 260, 303, 308, 313, 332, 337, 342, 358, 407, 611, 647, 759, 774). This is an `InMemoryCoordinator`-specific inherent method. Must be replaced with `SimIntrospection::cursor_last_key` and `SimIntrospection::spec_bounds`.
- **`seeded_coordinator`** -- factory calls that construct InMemoryCoordinator. The harness must accept a pre-constructed backend, not construct one internally.

### Trait hierarchy (ground truth from code)

SimulationBackend = CoordinationFacade + SimIntrospection (sim/backend.rs:187)
CoordinationFacade = CoordinationBackend + RunManagement + ShardClaiming (facade.rs:481)

Types implementing SimulationBackend:
- InMemoryCoordinator -- all four leaf traits
- SimEtcdCoordinator -- all four leaf traits (via macros + explicit impl)

EtcdCoordinator does NOT implement SimIntrospection and cannot be a conformance target.

### Full trait surface used by conformance tests

From CoordinationBackend: acquire_and_restore_into, checkpoint, complete, split_replace, split_residual, park_shard, renew

From RunManagement: create_run, register_shards, complete_run, cancel_run, fail_run, get_run, unpark_shard

From SimIntrospection: shard_lookup (21 calls), cursor_last_key (will replace slab cursor reads), spec_bounds (will replace slab spec reads)

### slab replacement mapping (mechanical)

Every .slab() call follows one of two patterns:

Pattern 1 - cursor read (10 occurrences):
  BEFORE: rec.cursor.last_key(coord.slab())
  AFTER:  coord.cursor_last_key(rec)

Pattern 2 - spec range read (6 occurrences):
  BEFORE: rec.spec.key_range_start(coord.slab()) / rec.spec.key_range_end(coord.slab())
  AFTER:  let (start, end) = coord.spec_bounds(rec);

### The 15+1 test functions to extract

1. fence_monotonicity_across_full_lifecycle (line 119)
2. cursor_monotonicity_combined_with_split_residual (line 160)
3. idempotency_before_terminal_state_rejection (line 216)
4. split_residual_preserved_through_park_unpark (line 277)
5. owner_divergence_with_matching_fence (line 370)
6. terminal_clears_lease (line 429)
7. cursor_semantics_dispatched_through_coordinator (line 510) -- uses Dispatched semantics
8. lease_deadline_at_exact_boundary (line 551)
9. split_coverage_key_range_partition (line 589)
10. oplog_eviction_then_replay (line 665)
11. unpark_lifecycle_fence_and_cursor_preserved (line 735)
12. same_worker_reacquire_bumps_fence (line 788)
13. run_terminal_irreversibility (line 846) -- rstest with 3 cases (Done, Failed, Cancelled)
14. register_shards_on_non_initializing_rejected (line 920)
15. run_completed_at_consistency (line 961)
16. unpark_after_run_terminal_rejected (line 1026)

### Test 7 needs special handling

cursor_semantics_dispatched_through_coordinator calls seeded_coordinator_with_semantics(Dispatched) instead of seeded_coordinator(). The harness factory must accept CursorSemantics so the caller constructs the backend with the right semantics.

## Desired State

### New module: conformance.rs in gossip-coordination

```rust
// crates/gossip-coordination/src/conformance.rs
use crate::sim::backend::SimulationBackend;
use gossip_contracts::coordination::shard_spec::CursorSemantics;

/// Run all coordination conformance tests against a backend factory.
///
/// The factory is called once per test to create a fresh backend.
/// Most tests use CursorSemantics::Completed; one test uses Dispatched.
pub fn run_coordination_conformance<B, F>(mut factory: F)
where
    B: SimulationBackend,
    F: FnMut(CursorSemantics) -> B,
{
    // calls each test function with factory(semantics)
}
```

### Compile-time guards stay in conformance_tests.rs

The compile-time allocation-contract guards (lines 54-98) are InMemoryCoordinator-specific and MUST remain in conformance_tests.rs, not in the generic harness.

### Updated conformance_tests.rs

Keeps compile-time guards and imports. Replaces 15 test bodies with calls to the harness. Can either be a single test or individual test functions calling harness sub-functions for granularity.

### Module exposed under test-support

```rust
// lib.rs
#[cfg(any(test, feature = "test-support"))]
pub mod conformance;
```

## Implementation Guidance

### Files to modify

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| crates/gossip-coordination/src/conformance.rs | NEW -- harness functions generic over SimulationBackend |
| crates/gossip-coordination/src/conformance_tests.rs | Remove test bodies, keep compile-time guards, call harness |
| crates/gossip-coordination/src/lib.rs | Add pub mod conformance under test-support gate |

### Factory pattern

The harness takes FnMut(CursorSemantics) -> B:
- 14 tests call it with CursorSemantics::Completed
- 1 test calls it with CursorSemantics::Dispatched

For InMemoryCoordinator: |semantics| seeded_coordinator_with_semantics(semantics)

### rstest test handling

run_terminal_irreversibility uses #[case] with 3 variants. In the harness, this becomes a loop or 3 explicit calls.

### Design decision: panic-based assertions

Use standard assert!/assert_eq! panics, not a report struct. Rationale: better error messages, stack traces, simpler, standard #[test] compatible. The persistence conformance harness uses a report struct but coordination tests are all sync and simpler.

## Code References

- conformance_tests.rs:1-1053 -- full conformance test module
- sim/backend.rs:70-171 -- SimIntrospection trait
- sim/backend.rs:173-188 -- SimulationBackend definition
- facade.rs:481-484 -- CoordinationFacade definition
- persistence/conformance.rs:333-346 -- persistence harness pattern
- in_memory.rs:2787 -- impl SimIntrospection for InMemoryCoordinator
- sim_coordinator.rs:430 -- impl SimIntrospection for SimEtcdCoordinator

## Related Work

- gossip-8975 -- parent task
- gossip-9041 (Sub-task A) -- prerequisite
- Sub-task C -- depends on this

## Risks

### SimEtcdCoordinator behavioral differences

- Lease TTL mapping: InMemoryCoordinator uses LogicalTime ticks directly. SimEtcdCoordinator maps logical time to etcd lease TTLs.
- Op-log capacity: Both use OP_LOG_CAP == 16, but etcd serializes the op-log differently.
- Time model: SimEtcdCoordinator uses logical time (like InMemoryCoordinator), so time-dependent tests should work.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. cargo test -p gossip-coordination --features test-support passes with zero regressions
2. cargo fmt --all && cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings clean
3. No .slab() calls remain in the harness function body
4. The harness is pub and gated behind cfg(any(test, feature = "test-support"))
5. Compile-time allocation guards remain in conformance_tests.rs, not in the harness
6. The harness function uses SimulationBackend as the trait bound
7. The factory accepts CursorSemantics parameter
8. cargo test -p gossip-coordination (without test-support) still compiles

title: Wire SimEtcdCoordinator through coordination conformance harness
description:
## Context

## Current State

### Conformance harness exists (after sub-task B)

After sub-task B completes, `crates/gossip-coordination/src/conformance.rs` exposes:

```rust
pub fn run_coordination_conformance<B, F>(factory: F)
where
    B: SimulationBackend,
    F: FnMut(CursorSemantics) -> B,
```

This is called from `conformance_tests.rs` with `InMemoryCoordinator`. No etcd backend calls it yet.

### SimEtcdCoordinator implements SimulationBackend

SimEtcdCoordinator (at `crates/gossip-coordination-etcd/src/sim_coordinator.rs:39`) implements:
- CoordinationBackend via `impl_sync_coordination_backend!(SimEtcdCoordinator)` (shard_coordination.rs)

These compose into SimulationBackend via the blanket impl.

### SimEtcdCoordinator construction

```rust
// crates/gossip-coordination-etcd/src/sim_coordinator.rs:58
impl SimEtcdCoordinator {
    pub fn new(config: EtcdCoordinatorConfig, seed: u64) -> Result<Self, EtcdCoordinatorError> {
        Self::with_kv(config, SimulatedEtcdKV::new(seed))
    }
}
```

No Docker or network needed -- SimEtcdCoordinator uses an in-memory simulated etcd KV store. This is a purely deterministic, in-process backend.

### Existing etcd test infrastructure

The test_etcd.rs module (crates/gossip-coordination-etcd/src/test_etcd.rs) provides testcontainers-based EtcdCoordinator factories for integration tests. These are NOT needed here -- SimEtcdCoordinator is self-contained.

### gossip-8974 (testcontainers integration) is already closed

The dependency on gossip-8974 noted in the original task is satisfied -- testcontainers infrastructure exists. However, this sub-task uses SimEtcdCoordinator (no Docker needed), so the dependency is actually irrelevant.

## Desired State

### New test file in gossip-coordination-etcd

```rust
            "http://unused:2379",  // SimEtcdKV ignores endpoint
            "/conformance/test",
        ).unwrap();
        // Config needs appropriate lease duration and cursor semantics
        // to match the harness expectations
        SimEtcdCoordinator::new(config, 42).unwrap()
    });
}
```

### Factory must match InMemory harness expectations

The conformance harness calls factory(CursorSemantics) and expects:
- A backend seeded with one run (test_run) containing one shard [a,z)
- Using the provided CursorSemantics
- With LEASE_DURATION = 100 ticks

The SimEtcdCoordinator factory must replicate the seeded_coordinator_with_semantics setup:
1. Create SimEtcdCoordinator with appropriate config
2. create_run with the given semantics and LEASE_DURATION
3. register_shards with test_shard [a,z)

This mirrors what seeded_coordinator_with_semantics does for InMemoryCoordinator.

## Implementation Guidance

### Files to create/modify

The etcd crate already has test-support features:

```toml

    "gossip-coordination/test-support",
    "gossip-contracts/test-support",

```

And gossip-coordination is already a dependency with test-support:

```toml

```

The conformance module is gated behind cfg(any(test, feature = "test-support")), so it should be accessible from the etcd crate tests.

### SimEtcdCoordinator config construction

SimEtcdCoordinator::new takes (EtcdCoordinatorConfig, seed). The config needs:
- An endpoint string (can be anything for SimEtcdKV -- it is not used)
- A namespace prefix (unique per test invocation to avoid cross-contamination)
- Appropriate lease TTL mapping for LEASE_DURATION compatibility

Check EtcdCoordinatorConfig construction to understand how logical time maps to lease TTLs. The conformance tests use LogicalTime ticks (LEASE_DURATION = 100). SimEtcdCoordinator should handle this correctly since it operates on LogicalTime like InMemoryCoordinator.

### Potential behavioral differences to watch for

1. **Lease TTL**: SimEtcdCoordinator maps logical time to etcd lease TTLs. Verify lease_deadline_at_exact_boundary test passes.
2. **Op-log serialization**: Etcd serializes the op-log as part of the shard record KV value. Verify oplog_eviction_then_replay test passes.
3. **CAS retry behavior**: SimEtcdCoordinator may inject CAS failures. Use SimEtcdCoordinator::new (no fault injection) for conformance, not with_fault_config.
4. **Shard limits**: EtcdCoordinatorConfig may have default shard limits that differ from InMemoryCoordinator. Ensure the config matches.

title: Task 1.1 — Add shared connector common contract module
description:
## Context

The connector redesign (Epic gossip-9044) replaces the old `ScanDriver`-based source abstraction with a family-based connector model. Before family-specific traits can be defined, the shared **paging vocabulary** must exist. This task creates the foundational types that all connector families will use to produce and validate enumeration pages.

Currently, connectors have no formal paging contract in `gossip-contracts`. The existing `Cursor` and `Budgets` types handle progression and limits, but there is no `PageBuf` (typed page container), no `PageState` (page completion status), no `PagingCapabilities` (capability flags specific to paging behavior), no `KeyedPageItem` (trait for items that participate in paged enumeration), and no page validation helpers. The connector-internal `KeyedEntry` trait in `gossip-connectors/src/common.rs` serves a similar role but is `pub(crate)` and not available at the contract boundary.

## Current State

**No paging types exist.** The connector contract surface in `gossip-contracts/src/connector/` currently contains:

- `types.rs` (1219 lines) — `ScanItem`, `ItemKey`, `ItemRef`, `Cursor`, `Budgets`, toxic-byte wrappers
- `api.rs` (326 lines) — `EnumerateError`, `ReadError`, `ConnectorCapabilities`
- `mod.rs` (68 lines) — re-exports

The `ScanItem` struct (`crates/gossip-contracts/src/connector/types.rs:996`) is the closest existing type to what a `KeyedPageItem` implementation would look like:

```rust
// crates/gossip-contracts/src/connector/types.rs:996-1004
pub struct ScanItem {
    item_key: ItemKey,
    item_ref: ItemRef,
    stable_item_id: StableItemId,
    version: VersionId,
    size_hint: Option<u64>,
    content_hints: Option<ContentHints>,
    location: Option<Location>,
}
```

The existing `ConnectorCapabilities` (`crates/gossip-contracts/src/connector/api.rs:294-322`) is the model for `PagingCapabilities`:

```rust
// crates/gossip-contracts/src/connector/api.rs:294-322
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct ConnectorCapabilities {
    pub seek_by_key: bool,
    pub token_resume: bool,
    pub range_read: bool,
    pub split_hints: bool,
}
```

The internal `KeyedEntry` trait (`crates/gossip-connectors/src/common.rs:111-113`) is the predecessor of `KeyedPageItem`:

```rust
// crates/gossip-connectors/src/common.rs:111-113
pub(crate) trait KeyedEntry {
    fn key_bytes(&self) -> &[u8];
}
```

## Desired State

A new `common.rs` submodule under `crates/gossip-contracts/src/connector/` containing:

1. **`PageBuf<T>`** — A generic typed page container holding a `Vec<T>` of items with a `PageState` describing whether the page is terminal or has more data. Enforces non-empty invariant on construction for filled pages. Provides item count, iteration, and destructuring.

2. **`PageState`** — An enum representing the page completion status:
   - `HasMore { cursor: Cursor }` — more pages follow; includes the cursor for the next request.
   - `Complete` — this is the final page for the current enumeration scope.

3. **`PagingCapabilities`** — Feature flags for paging behavior (similar pattern to `ConnectorCapabilities`). Fields include:
   - `ordered_keys: bool` — items are emitted in lexicographic key order.
   - `resumable: bool` — enumeration can resume from a cursor.
   - `splittable: bool` — the source supports dynamic shard splitting.
   - Default is all `false` (conservative profile).

4. **`KeyedPageItem`** — A trait that items must implement to participate in paged enumeration. Required methods:
   - `fn item_key(&self) -> &ItemKey` — ordered key for cursor progression.
   - `fn size_hint(&self) -> Option<u64>` — optional byte-size estimate for budget tracking.

5. **`PageShapeError`** — A dedicated error type for page validation failures (empty page, unsorted keys, duplicate keys, key outside shard bounds).

6. **`validate_filled_page(items, shard_start, shard_end)`** — A validation helper that checks:
   - Page is non-empty.
   - Items are sorted by `item_key` (lexicographic).
   - No duplicate keys.
   - All keys fall within the shard bounds `[start, end)`.

## Implementation Guidance

### Files to Modify

| File | Change | Rationale |
|------|--------|-----------|
| `crates/gossip-contracts/src/connector/common.rs` | **NEW** — all new paging types and validation | Keeps paging vocabulary separate from existing `types.rs` (item boundary types) and `api.rs` (error classification) |
| `crates/gossip-contracts/src/connector/common_tests.rs` | **NEW** — unit tests for paging types | Follows the `#[path]` test file pattern used by `types_tests.rs` and `api_tests.rs` |
| `crates/gossip-contracts/src/connector/mod.rs` | Add `mod common;` declaration and re-exports | Consistent with existing `mod api; mod types;` pattern |

### Patterns to Follow

- **Validation via `try_new` constructors** — follow the `Budgets::try_new` pattern (`crates/gossip-contracts/src/connector/types.rs:1166-1182`). Use `Result<Self, PageShapeError>` for fallible construction.
- **Capability flags struct** — mirror `ConnectorCapabilities` exactly (`crates/gossip-contracts/src/connector/api.rs:294-322`): `#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]` with all-`bool` fields.
- **Test style** — use `rstest` parameterized tests as in `types_tests.rs` and `api_tests.rs`. Include `proptest` property tests for ordering and validation invariants.
- **Module inclusion** — use `#[cfg(test)] #[path = "common_tests.rs"] mod tests;` at the bottom of `common.rs`.
- **Re-export in mod.rs** — add a focused `pub use common::{...};` block after the existing `pub use api` and `pub use types` blocks.

### Utilities to Reuse

| Utility | Location | How to Reuse |
|---------|----------|-------------|
| `ItemKey` (ordered toxic bytes) | `connector/types.rs:606-624` | `KeyedPageItem` returns `&ItemKey`; page validation compares keys via `ItemKey::as_bytes()` |
| `Cursor` | `connector/types.rs:672-803` | `PageState::HasMore` holds a `Cursor` for next-page progression |
| `ConnectorCapabilities` | `connector/api.rs:294-322` | Structural model for `PagingCapabilities` |
| `ConnectorInputError` | `connector/types.rs:202-233` | Reference for error design; `PageShapeError` is intentionally separate since it validates page shape, not input boundaries |

### Blast Radius

This task introduces **new** types only. No existing code changes. The blast radius is zero — downstream tasks (1.2, 1.3) will consume these types.

Future consumers:
- `connector/ordered.rs` (Task 1.2) — ordered family trait will return `PageBuf<ScanItem>`
- `connector/git.rs` (Task 1.2) — git family trait will return `PageBuf<GitRepoTarget>`
- `gossip-connectors` concrete implementations will implement `KeyedPageItem` for their item types

## Code References

```rust
// crates/gossip-contracts/src/connector/types.rs:1141-1182 — Budgets pattern (try_new + NonZero)
pub struct Budgets {
    max_items: NonZeroUsize,
    max_bytes: NonZeroU64,
    deadline: Option<Instant>,
}

impl Budgets {
    pub fn try_new(
        max_items: usize, max_bytes: u64, deadline: Option<Instant>,
    ) -> Result<Self, ConnectorInputError> {
        let max_items = NonZeroUsize::new(max_items)
            .ok_or(ConnectorInputError::ZeroBudget { field: "Budgets.max_items" })?;
        let max_bytes = NonZeroU64::new(max_bytes)
            .ok_or(ConnectorInputError::ZeroBudget { field: "Budgets.max_bytes" })?;
        Ok(Self { max_items, max_bytes, deadline })
    }
}
```

```rust
// crates/gossip-contracts/src/connector/api.rs:294-322 — ConnectorCapabilities pattern
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct ConnectorCapabilities {
    pub seek_by_key: bool,
    pub token_resume: bool,
    pub range_read: bool,
    pub split_hints: bool,
}
```

```rust
// crates/gossip-connectors/src/common.rs:111-125 — KeyedEntry trait + binary search
pub(crate) trait KeyedEntry {
    fn key_bytes(&self) -> &[u8];
}

pub(crate) fn lower_bound<T: KeyedEntry>(items: &[T], key: &[u8]) -> usize {
    items.partition_point(|item| item.key_bytes() < key)
}
```

```rust
// crates/gossip-contracts/src/connector/types.rs:996-1026 — ScanItem (future KeyedPageItem implementor)
pub struct ScanItem {
    item_key: ItemKey,
    item_ref: ItemRef,
    stable_item_id: StableItemId,
    version: VersionId,
    size_hint: Option<u64>,
    content_hints: Option<ContentHints>,
    location: Option<Location>,
}
```

```rust
// crates/gossip-contracts/src/connector/mod.rs:59-68 — module structure + re-exports
mod api;
mod types;

pub use api::{ConnectorCapabilities, EnumerateError, ErrorClass, ReadError};
pub use types::{
    Budgets, ConnectorInputError, ContentHints, Cursor, ItemKey, ItemRef, Location,
    MAX_ITEM_KEY_SIZE, MAX_ITEM_REF_SIZE, MAX_LOCATION_DISPLAY_SIZE, MAX_LOCATION_URL_SIZE,
    MAX_TOKEN_SIZE, PooledByteSlab, ScanItem, TokenBytes, ToxicDigest, VersionId,
};
```

## Testing Strategy

Unit tests in `common_tests.rs` should cover:

| Category | Tests |
|----------|-------|
| `PageBuf` construction | Empty page rejected; single-item page OK; multi-item page OK; state preserved |
| `PageState` round-trip | `HasMore` carries cursor; `Complete` is terminal |
| `PagingCapabilities` | Default is all-false; each field independently settable |
| `KeyedPageItem` for `ScanItem` | `ScanItem` implements `KeyedPageItem` correctly |
| `validate_filled_page` | Sorted page passes; unsorted rejected; duplicates rejected; out-of-bounds rejected; empty rejected |
| Property tests | `proptest` for sorted-page validation with arbitrary `ItemKey` sequences |

## Related Work

| Task ID | Title | Relationship |
|---------|-------|-------------|
| gossip-9044 | Epic 1 — Replace old contract surface | Parent epic |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `PageBuf<T>`, `PageState`, `PagingCapabilities`, `KeyedPageItem`, `PageShapeError`, `validate_filled_page` compile and are re-exported from `gossip_contracts::connector`
- [ ] `ScanItem` implements `KeyedPageItem`
- [ ] Future `GitRepoTarget` (Task 1.3) can implement `KeyedPageItem` (verified by trait bounds, not by concrete impl in this task)
- [ ] `validate_filled_page` has unit tests covering: empty page, sorted page, unsorted page, duplicate keys, out-of-bounds keys
- [ ] `PagingCapabilities::default()` returns all-false
- [ ] `PageBuf` with `PageState::HasMore` preserves the cursor
- [ ] All existing tests pass: `cargo test -p gossip-contracts`
- [ ] Code compiles clean: `cargo fmt --all && cargo check && cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`

## Pointers

- Reference design (artifacts): `tmp/gossip-project-artifacts/connector-redesign/gossip-connectors/src/common.rs` — existing `KeyedEntry` trait and binary search helpers
- Existing test patterns: `crates/gossip-contracts/src/connector/types_tests.rs`, `api_tests.rs`
- `Budgets` validation pattern: `crates/gossip-contracts/src/connector/types.rs:1141-1215`
- `ConnectorCapabilities` pattern: `crates/gossip-contracts/src/connector/api.rs:294-322`

title: Epic 1 — Replace old contract surface and rip out old design
description:
## Context

The current source abstraction is built around `ScanDriver` / `ConnectorKind` / `AssignmentSource` / `ScanSourceFactory` in the `gossip-scan-driver` crate, with concrete implementations in `gossip-connectors`. This design couples enumeration, execution, and paging into monolithic driver types that are hard to extend to new source families (SaaS APIs, cloud storage, etc.) without replicating the full driver scaffold.

This epic replaces the old contract surface with a family-based connector model:
- A shared paging vocabulary (`PageBuf`, `PageState`, `PagingCapabilities`, `KeyedPageItem`) in `gossip-contracts`.
- Family-specific contract modules (`connector/ordered.rs`, `connector/git.rs`) with per-family traits and types.
- Git family shared types (`RepoKey`, `RepoLocator`, `GitRepoTarget`, etc.) in the contracts layer.

Once the new surface is in place, the old abstraction roots are deleted.

## Current State

The source abstraction lives across two crates:

- `gossip-scan-driver` — `ConnectorKind`, `AssignmentSource`, `ScanDriver` trait, `ScanSourceFactory` trait
- `gossip-connectors` — `scan_driver.rs` dispatch, per-source implementations

## Desired State

1. New shared contract modules in `gossip-contracts/src/connector/`
2. `gossip-scan-driver` crate deleted
3. `gossip-connectors/src/scan_driver.rs` removed
4. Runtime dispatch through `ConnectorKind` / `AssignmentSource` / `ScanDriver` gone
5. All imports compile against new contract vocabulary only

## Exit Criteria

- Old source abstraction (`ScanDriver`, `ConnectorKind`, `AssignmentSource`) fully removed
- Repo builds cleanly against new contract surface only
- No new work can accidentally land on `ScanDriver`

title: Task 1.2 — Add ordered-content contract module
description:
## Context

This is the second task in Epic gossip-9045 (Replace old contract surface). Task 1.1 (gossip-9044) adds the shared paging vocabulary (`PageBuf`, `PageState`, `PagingCapabilities`, `KeyedPageItem`, `PageShapeError`, `validate_filled_page`). This task defines the first real **family trait** on top of that vocabulary: `OrderedContentSource`, for connectors that enumerate key-ordered content items and expose readable bytes.

All three current connectors (filesystem, git, in-memory) share identical inherent method surfaces (`caps`, `choose_split_point`, `open`, `read_range`) but have no unifying trait. The ordered-content module promotes these ad-hoc method signatures into a formal contract that lives in `gossip-contracts`, proving that the shared common layer from Task 1.1 is sufficient.

## Current State

The three connectors expose identical method shapes as **inherent methods** (no trait):

```rust
// crates/gossip-connectors/src/filesystem.rs:341 (identical pattern on git.rs:390, in_memory.rs:279)
pub fn caps(&self) -> ConnectorCapabilities { ... }

// crates/gossip-connectors/src/filesystem.rs:351 (identical on git.rs:400, in_memory.rs:290)
pub fn choose_split_point(
    &mut self,
    shard: &ShardSpec,
    cursor: &Cursor,
    budgets: Budgets,
) -> Result<Option<ItemKey>, EnumerateError> { ... }

// crates/gossip-connectors/src/filesystem.rs:365 (identical on git.rs:412, in_memory.rs:307)
pub fn open(
    &mut self,
    item_ref: &ItemRef,
    _budgets: Budgets,
) -> Result<Box<dyn io::Read + Send>, ReadError> { ... }

// crates/gossip-connectors/src/filesystem.rs:376 (identical on git.rs:424, in_memory.rs:318)
pub fn read_range(
    &mut self,
    item_ref: &ItemRef,
    offset: u64,
    dst: &mut [u8],
    budgets: Budgets,
) -> Result<usize, ReadError> { ... }
```

There is **no** `enumerate_page` / `fill_page` method today. The old `ScanDriver` trait (`crates/gossip-scan-driver/src/lib.rs:417`) bundles enumeration and detection into a monolithic `run()` call:

```rust
// crates/gossip-scan-driver/src/lib.rs:417-427
pub trait ScanDriver: Send {
    fn run(
        &mut self,
        engine: Arc<scanner_engine::Engine>,
        cfg: &ScanExecutionConfig,
        out: &dyn EventOutput,
        commit: &dyn CommitSink,
        cancel: &CancellationToken,
    ) -> Result<ScanReport>;
    fn checkpoint_hint(&self) -> Option<CursorUpdate> { None }
    fn debug_output(&self) -> Option<String> { None }
}
```

The existing `ConnectorCapabilities` (`crates/gossip-contracts/src/connector/api.rs:294-322`) advertises connector features:

```rust
// crates/gossip-contracts/src/connector/api.rs:294-322
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct ConnectorCapabilities {
    pub seek_by_key: bool,
    pub token_resume: bool,
    pub range_read: bool,
    pub split_hints: bool,
}
```

And the scan-driver-level `SourceCapabilities` (`crates/gossip-scan-driver/src/lib.rs:276-288`):

```rust
// crates/gossip-scan-driver/src/lib.rs:276-288
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct SourceCapabilities {
    pub supports_checkpoint_hints: bool,
    pub supports_cooperative_cancel: bool,
}
```

Neither of these captures ordered-content-specific capability semantics.

## Desired State

A new `ordered.rs` submodule under `crates/gossip-contracts/src/connector/` containing:

1. **`OrderedContentCapabilities`** — A capability struct specific to the ordered-content family. Follows the `ConnectorCapabilities` pattern (`#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]`, all-`bool` fields, conservative default). Fields capture what matters for ordered-content sources:
   - `range_read: bool` — supports byte-range reads of item content.
   - `split_hints: bool` — can emit split-point suggestions for dynamic re-sharding.
   - `token_resume: bool` — supports opaque token-based page resumption (in addition to key-based).

2. **`OrderedContentSource`** trait — The formal contract for connectors that enumerate key-ordered content items. Requires `Send`. Methods:

   | Method | Signature | Purpose |
   |--------|-----------|---------|
   | `capabilities` | `&self -> OrderedContentCapabilities` | Advertise family-specific features |
   | `fill_page` | `&mut self, shard: &ShardSpec, cursor: &Cursor, budgets: Budgets -> Result<PageBuf<ScanItem>, EnumerateError>` | Fill a page of key-ordered items within shard bounds, resuming from cursor |
   | `choose_split_point` | `&mut self, shard: &ShardSpec, cursor: &Cursor, budgets: Budgets -> Result<Option<ItemKey>, EnumerateError>` | Suggest a split key for dynamic re-sharding |
   | `open` | `&mut self, item_ref: &ItemRef, budgets: Budgets -> Result<Box<dyn io::Read + Send>, ReadError>` | Open an item for streaming read |
   | `read_range` | `&mut self, item_ref: &ItemRef, offset: u64, dst: &mut [u8], budgets: Budgets -> Result<usize, ReadError>` | Read a byte range from an item |

## Implementation Guidance

### Files to Modify

| File | Change | Rationale |
|------|--------|-----------|
| `crates/gossip-contracts/src/connector/ordered.rs` | **NEW** — `OrderedContentCapabilities` struct + `OrderedContentSource` trait | First family-specific contract module |
| `crates/gossip-contracts/src/connector/mod.rs` | Add `pub mod ordered;` declaration | Expose as public submodule (not flat re-export — family modules are namespaced) |

### Patterns to Follow

- **Capability struct** — mirror `ConnectorCapabilities` exactly: `#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]` with `pub` bool fields and conservative all-`false` default (`crates/gossip-contracts/src/connector/api.rs:294-322`).
- **Trait with `Send` bound** — the old `ScanDriver: Send` pattern ensures connectors can be moved across threads (`crates/gossip-scan-driver/src/lib.rs:417`).
- **Method signatures** — align with the inherent methods already on all three connectors. The `fill_page` method is new; all others (`choose_split_point`, `open`, `read_range`) match existing shapes.
- **Module as namespace** — use `pub mod ordered;` (not flat re-export) so consumers write `connector::ordered::OrderedContentSource`, keeping family modules namespaced.
- **No `#[path]` test file needed** — this module defines a trait and a struct with no complex logic to test. Compilation is the test. If any validation logic is added, a `#[cfg(test)]` block at the bottom suffices.

### Utilities to Reuse

| Utility | Location | How to Reuse |
|---------|----------|-------------|
| `PageBuf<T>` | `connector/common.rs` (from Task 1.1) | Return type of `fill_page` |
| `ScanItem` | `connector/types.rs:996` | The item type that `PageBuf` contains for ordered-content |
| `Cursor` | `connector/types.rs:672` | Input param for resume in `fill_page` and `choose_split_point` |
| `Budgets` | `connector/types.rs:1152` | Budget control for all methods |
| `ItemKey` | `connector/types.rs:606` | Return type of `choose_split_point` |
| `ItemRef` | `connector/types.rs:626` | Input param for `open` and `read_range` |
| `ShardSpec` | `coordination/shard_spec.rs:388` | Input param for `fill_page` and `choose_split_point` |
| `EnumerateError` | `connector/api.rs:233` | Error type for `fill_page` and `choose_split_point` |
| `ReadError` | `connector/api.rs:251` | Error type for `open` and `read_range` |

### Blast Radius

title: Task 1.3 — Add Git family contract module
description:
## Context

This is the third task in Epic gossip-9045 (Replace old contract surface). Tasks 1.1 (gossip-9044) and 1.2 (gossip-9045.1) add the shared paging vocabulary and the ordered-content family trait respectively. This task creates the **Git family contract module** — the first explicit exception to the one-trait-fits-all model.

Git repositories are fundamentally different from ordered-content sources: execution is whole-repo (commit walk, tree diff, pack scan), not item-by-item open/read. The current codebase reflects this by giving git a dedicated execution path (`execute_git_assignment` in `scan_driver.rs`) that bypasses `ScanDriver::run`. But the types that describe git work-units (repo identity, selection, mirror state, execution limits, outcome) are scattered across `gossip-connectors`, `scanner-git`, and `gossip-scan-driver` with no clean contract boundary.

This task moves the Git-specific boundary types into `gossip-contracts` so they are shareable across crates without pulling in `scanner-git` or `gix-*` dependencies.

**Reference material:** `tmp/gossip-project-artifacts/connector-redesign/gossip-connectors/` contains the target state for `gossip-connectors` after the epic. Key observations from the reference code:
- `scan_driver.rs` is absent — it is deleted in the target state.
- `lib.rs` has no `gossip-scan-driver` dependency — `ConnectorKind`, `connector_tag_for_kind()`, and all scan-driver re-exports are removed.
- The individual connector files (`git.rs`, `filesystem.rs`, `in_memory.rs`) keep their inherent method surfaces unchanged.
- This confirms the Git family contract types belong in `gossip-contracts`, not `gossip-connectors`.

## Current State

Git-related types are spread across three crates with no unified contract:

**Repository identity** — a bare `PathBuf` threaded through:
```rust
// crates/gossip-scan-driver/src/lib.rs:115
pub enum AssignmentSource {
    Git { repo_root: PathBuf },
    // ...
}
```

**Execution configuration** — lives in `gossip-connectors` tied to `scanner-git` types:
```rust
// crates/gossip-connectors/src/scan_driver.rs:103-126
pub struct GitExecutionConfig {
    pub repo_id: u64,
    pub scan_mode: GitScanMode,       // from scanner-git
    pub merge_diff_mode: MergeDiffMode, // from scanner-git
    pub pack_exec_workers: Option<usize>,
    pub scan_binary: bool,
    pub enrich_identities: bool,
    pub debug_level: GitDebugLevel,
    pub tree_delta_cache_mb: Option<u32>,
    pub engine_chunk_mb: Option<u32>,
}
```

**Execution outcome** — `ScanReport` + `Option<CursorUpdate>` + `Option<String>` tuple:
```rust
// crates/gossip-connectors/src/scan_driver.rs:925-932
pub fn execute_git_assignment(
    assignment: &Assignment,
    engine: Arc<scanner_engine::Engine>,
    cfg: &ScanExecutionConfig,
    git_cfg: &GitExecutionConfig,
    out: &dyn GitEventOutput,
    cancel: &CancellationToken,
) -> Result<(ScanReport, Option<CursorUpdate>, Option<String>)>
```

**Error taxonomy** — 14-variant `GitScanError` in `scanner-git` tied to pipeline stages:
```rust
// crates/scanner-git/src/runner.rs:813-844
pub enum GitScanError {
    RepoOpen(RepoOpenError),
    CommitPlan(CommitPlanError),
    TreeDiff(TreeDiffError),
    // ... 11 more stage-specific variants
    ConcurrentMaintenance,
}
```

**Ref selection** — `StartSetConfig` in `scanner-git`:
```rust
// crates/scanner-git/src/start_set.rs
pub enum StartSetConfig {
    DefaultBranchOnly,
    AllRemoteBranches { remote: Option<Vec<u8>> },
    BranchesAndTags { include_remote_branches: bool, remote: Option<Vec<u8>> },
    ExplicitRefs { refs: Vec<Vec<u8>> },
}
```

**No mirror/clone concepts exist anywhere** — the entire codebase assumes repos are already locally available.

**The reference `git.rs`** (`tmp/gossip-project-artifacts/connector-redesign/gossip-connectors/src/git.rs`) keeps the `GitConnector` file-level connector unchanged. This confirms that `GitConnector` is an `OrderedContentSource` (Task 1.2), while the *Git family traits* defined here address repo-level execution — a separate concern.

## Desired State

A new `git.rs` submodule under `crates/gossip-contracts/src/connector/` containing:

### Shared Git types

1. **`RepoKey`** — Canonical repo work-unit key. Wraps a validated identifier that uniquely identifies a repository within the system. Replaces the ad-hoc `repo_id: u64` scattered through `GitExecutionConfig`, `GitScanConfig`, and `FinalizeInput`.

2. **`RepoLocator`** — Describes where a repository can be found. Replaces the bare `PathBuf` in `AssignmentSource::Git`. Supports local paths now with extensibility for URLs later.

3. **`GitRepoTarget`** — A single repository work-unit for discovery/enumeration pages. Bundles `RepoKey` + `RepoLocator` + optional metadata. **Implements `KeyedPageItem`** so git repos can be paged through `PageBuf<GitRepoTarget>`.

4. **`GitSelection`** — Describes what subset of a repository to scan: which refs, scan mode, merge strategy. Contract-level analog of `StartSetConfig` + `GitScanMode` + `MergeDiffMode` without depending on `scanner-git` types.

5. **`LocalMirror`** — Represents a local clone/mirror of a repository ready for execution. Contains the local path and optional freshness metadata. Formalizes the implicit "repo is already local" assumption.

6. **`GitExecutionLimits`** — Resource limits and configuration for a git scan execution. Contract-level analog of `GitExecutionConfig` fields that don't depend on `scanner-git` types (worker count, cache sizes, binary scanning, identity enrichment).

7. **`GitRunOutcome`** — Describes what a completed git execution produced: counts and timing. Replaces the ad-hoc `(ScanReport, Option<CursorUpdate>, Option<String>)` tuple.

8. **`GitRunError`** — Contract-level error for git execution failures. Carries an `ErrorClass` (retryable vs permanent) and a diagnostic message, following the `EnumerateError`/`ReadError` pattern from `crates/gossip-contracts/src/connector/api.rs:114-231`. `ConcurrentMaintenance` maps to retryable; structural failures map to permanent.

### Git family traits

9. **`GitRepoDiscoverySource`** — Trait for discovering repository targets. Returns `PageBuf<GitRepoTarget>`.

10. **`GitMirrorManager`** — Trait for acquiring/refreshing local mirrors. Accepts a `RepoLocator`, produces a `LocalMirror`.

11. **`GitRepoExecutor`** — Trait for executing a git scan on a prepared local mirror. Accepts `LocalMirror` + `GitSelection` + `GitExecutionLimits`, returns `Result<GitRunOutcome, GitRunError>`. **No `open`/`read_range` methods** — git execution is whole-repo, not item-by-item.

## Implementation Guidance

### Files to Modify

| File | Change | Rationale |
|------|--------|-----------|
| `crates/gossip-contracts/src/connector/git.rs` | **NEW** — all git family types and traits | First family-specific contract module that breaks from the ordered-content model |
| `crates/gossip-contracts/src/connector/mod.rs` | Add `pub mod git;` declaration | Expose as namespaced public submodule |

### Patterns to Follow

- **Error type** — follow the `define_connector_error!` macro pattern from `crates/gossip-contracts/src/connector/api.rs:114-231`. `GitRunError` should carry `ErrorClass`, `message: String`, `retry_after_ms: Option<u64>`, with named constructors `retryable()`, `permanent()`, `concurrent_maintenance()`. Consider reusing the macro directly.
- **Capability/config structs** — follow `ConnectorCapabilities` pattern: `#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]` with public fields.
- **Trait with `Send` bound** — matches `OrderedContentSource: Send` from Task 1.2.
- **`KeyedPageItem` impl** — `GitRepoTarget` must implement the `KeyedPageItem` trait from Task 1.1, returning its `RepoKey`-derived `ItemKey`.
- **No `scanner-git` dependencies** — `gossip-contracts` must remain a leaf crate with only `blake3`, `subtle`, `gossip-stdx` (see `crates/gossip-contracts/Cargo.toml`).

### Utilities to Reuse

| Utility | Location | How to Reuse |
|---------|----------|-------------|
| `KeyedPageItem` | `connector/common.rs` (from Task 1.1) | `GitRepoTarget` implements this trait |
| `PageBuf<T>` | `connector/common.rs` (from Task 1.1) | Return type of `GitRepoDiscoverySource::discover_page` |
| `ItemKey` | `connector/types.rs:606` | Used by `KeyedPageItem` impl for `GitRepoTarget` |
| `ErrorClass` | `connector/api.rs:49` | Used by `GitRunError` for retry classification |
| `EnumerateError` | `connector/api.rs:233` | Error type for `GitRepoDiscoverySource` methods |
| `Budgets` | `connector/types.rs:1152` | Budget control for discovery paging |
| `Cursor` | `connector/types.rs:672` | Resume state for discovery paging |
| `define_connector_error!` macro | `connector/api.rs:114` | Structural model for `GitRunError` |

### Blast Radius

This task introduces **new** types only. No existing code changes. Zero blast radius. The reference code at `tmp/gossip-project-artifacts/connector-redesign/gossip-connectors/src/git.rs` confirms that `GitConnector` keeps its inherent methods unchanged — it will be wired to `OrderedContentSource` in a separate task, not modified here.

## Code References

```rust
// crates/gossip-scan-driver/src/lib.rs:111-118 — AssignmentSource::Git (being replaced by RepoLocator)
pub enum AssignmentSource {
    Filesystem { root: PathBuf },
    Git { repo_root: PathBuf },
    InMemory { dataset_id: String },
}
```

```rust
// crates/gossip-connectors/src/scan_driver.rs:103-126 — GitExecutionConfig (being replaced by GitExecutionLimits)
pub struct GitExecutionConfig {
    pub repo_id: u64,
    pub scan_mode: GitScanMode,
    pub merge_diff_mode: MergeDiffMode,
    pub pack_exec_workers: Option<usize>,
    pub scan_binary: bool,
    pub enrich_identities: bool,
    pub debug_level: GitDebugLevel,
    pub tree_delta_cache_mb: Option<u32>,
    pub engine_chunk_mb: Option<u32>,
}
```

```rust
// crates/scanner-git/src/runner.rs:813-844 — GitScanError (contract-level analog is GitRunError)
pub enum GitScanError {
    RepoOpen(RepoOpenError),
    CommitPlan(CommitPlanError),
    // ... 12 more stage-specific variants
    ConcurrentMaintenance,
}
```

```rust
// tmp/gossip-project-artifacts/connector-redesign/gossip-connectors/src/lib.rs — target state (no scan_driver)
mod common;
#[cfg(unix)]
pub mod filesystem;
pub mod git;
pub mod in_memory;
mod split_estimator;

pub use common::{
    FILESYSTEM_CONNECTOR_TAG, GIT_CONNECTOR_TAG, IN_MEMORY_CONNECTOR_TAG, path_buf_from_bytes,
};
// NOTE: no gossip-scan-driver imports, no ConnectorKind, no scan_driver re-exports
```

```rust
// crates/gossip-contracts/src/connector/api.rs:114-231 — define_connector_error! macro (model for GitRunError)
macro_rules! define_connector_error {
    ($(#[$meta:meta])* $name:ident) => {
        #[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
        pub struct $name {
            class: ErrorClass,
            message: String,
            retry_after_ms: Option<u64>,
        }
        // constructors: retryable(), rate_limited(), permanent()
        // accessors: class(), message(), retry_after_ms(), is_retryable()
    };
}
```

## Design Notes

- **`GitRunError` classifies, not enumerates.** The 14-variant `GitScanError` depends on stage-local error types. The contract-level `GitRunError` uses `ErrorClass` (retryable/permanent) + message, matching the `EnumerateError`/`ReadError` pattern. Conversion from `GitScanError` to `GitRunError` happens in the runtime crate.
- **No `open`/`read_range` on git traits.** The reference code at `tmp/gossip-project-artifacts/connector-redesign/gossip-connectors/src/git.rs` keeps `GitConnector`'s file-level `open`/`read_range` methods. These are `OrderedContentSource` methods (Task 1.2). The Git family traits here address repo-level execution — a separate concern.
- **`RepoKey` is canonical but not yet integrated with frontier.** Integration with `gossip-frontier` key encoding is deferred.
- **`LocalMirror` is a new concept.** The reference code confirms repos are still `PathBuf`-based today. `LocalMirror` formalizes this and creates a seam for future remote-mirror support.

title: Task 1.5 — Cut runtime compile surface to new family vocabulary
description:
## Context

This is the fifth task in Epic gossip-9045 (Replace old contract surface). Tasks 1.1–1.4 add the new contract modules and rebuild the public API surface. This task **cuts the runtime compile surface** so that `gossip-scanner-runtime` and `gossip-worker` no longer import any old abstraction types (`ConnectorKind`, `AssignmentSource`, `ScanDriver`, `ScanSourceFactory`, `Assignment`, `ScanExecutionConfig`, `ScanReport`, `CursorUpdate`, `CommitSink`, `FindingRecord`, `FindingsBatch`, `ItemMeta`, `NoOpCommitSink`).

This must happen before the old crates/files can be deleted (Task 1.6) because you cannot safely remove `gossip-scan-driver` or `gossip-connectors/src/scan_driver.rs` while runtime code still imports from them.

This task does **not** implement the family runtime loops. It only changes the compile surface and dispatch shape, introducing placeholder paths where the old driver invocations lived. A follow-up task (gossip-9045.7) tracks implementing the actual family dispatch bodies.

**Reference material:** `tmp/gossip-project-artifacts/connector-redesign/gossip-rs-task1.6-delete-driver-stack 2/crates/gossip-connectors/src/lib.rs` shows the target `gossip-connectors` with `scan_driver.rs` deleted and no `gossip-scan-driver` dependency. The corresponding target `Cargo.toml` at `tmp/gossip-project-artifacts/connector-redesign/gossip-rs-task1.6-delete-driver-stack 2/crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/Cargo.toml` shows both `gossip-scan-driver` and `gossip-connectors` dependencies removed. The runtime must be cut over first before that deletion can happen.

## Current State

The runtime has deep coupling to old abstraction types across 8 files in 2 crates (~65 old-type references):

### `gossip-scanner-runtime` (8 files with old-type references)

**`lib.rs`** — the primary dispatch hub:
```rust
// crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/lib.rs:42-53
use gossip_connectors::{
    FilesystemScanSourceFactory, GitDebugLevel, GitExecutionConfig, execute_git_assignment,
};
use gossip_connectors::{...};  // all imports are scan-driver-dependent re-exports
use gossip_scan_driver::{
    Assignment, AssignmentSource, CancellationToken, CommitSink, ConnectorKind, CursorUpdate,
    NoOpCommitSink, ScanExecutionConfig, ScanReport, ScanSourceFactory,
};
```

Key functions using old types:
- `ScanBudgets::to_execution_config_with_workers()` (line 187) — constructs and returns `ScanExecutionConfig` with embedded `FilesystemExecutionConfig`
- `build_assignment()` (line 831) — constructs `Assignment` with `ConnectorKind` + `AssignmentSource`
- `execute_assignment_with_config()` (line 786) — dispatches on `assignment.connector_kind` match, takes `ScanExecutionConfig` param
- `scan_fs_with_runtime()` (line 680) — calls `FilesystemScanSourceFactory.driver_for_assignment()` → `ScanDriver::run()`, sets fields on `ScanExecutionConfig.filesystem`
- `scan_git_with_runtime()` (line 732) — calls `execute_git_assignment()` with `GitExecutionConfig`
- `scan_fs_direct()` (line 644) — uses `NoOpCommitSink` directly
- `ScanRuntimeError::UnsupportedConnectorKind(ConnectorKind)` variant (line 524)
- `AssignmentOutcome` struct (line 614) — holds `ScanReport`, `Option<CursorUpdate>`

**`commit_sink.rs`** — identity-chain persistence:
```rust
// crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/commit_sink.rs:17,24
use gossip_scan_driver::{CommitSink, FindingRecord, FindingsBatch, ItemMeta};
pub use gossip_scan_driver::NoOpCommitSink as CliNoOpCommitSink;
```
`DurableCommitSink` implements `CommitSink` trait. `FindingRecord`, `FindingsBatch`, and `ItemMeta` are used in `DurableCommitSink::derive_identity_record` and in the `CommitSink` trait impl. The `CliNoOpCommitSink` is a re-export. The test module at line 190 also imports `FindingsBatch` and `ItemMeta`.

**`distributed.rs`** — distributed worker loop:
```rust
// crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/distributed.rs:40-42
use gossip_scan_driver::{Assignment, CancellationToken, CursorUpdate, ScanReport};
use gossip_connectors::GitExecutionConfig;
```
Calls `execute_assignment_with_config()` which dispatches on `ConnectorKind`.

**Key local types defined in target-state `lib.rs`:**

- Runs `parallel_scan_dir()` from `scanner-scheduler` with a channel-based event bridge
- If `persist_findings` is enabled, wires a `ChannelStoreProducer` for commit-sink forwarding
- Converts the scheduler's `LocalReport` into the local `ScanReport`
- Returns the report

Replace `OrderedContentRuntime::execute_source()` with a generic paging loop:
- Calls `source.fill_page(shard, cursor, budgets)` in a loop until `PageState::Complete`
- Drives scanner engine on each page of items
- Updates cursor from page results
- Emits events through the event sink

title: Extract decode_fixed_32 to gossip-pg-common
description:
## Context

Two PostgreSQL backend crates contain identical `decode_fixed_32` helper functions
that convert `BYTEA` column values into fixed `[u8; 32]` identity arrays. This
duplication violates the single-source-of-truth principle and risks silent drift
if one copy is updated without the other.

## Current State

The findings backend has its own copy:

```rust
// crates/gossip-findings-postgres/src/backend.rs:705-719
fn decode_fixed_32(bytes: Vec<u8>, column: &'static str) -> Result<[u8; 32], FindingsPgError> {
    let actual = bytes.len();
    if actual != 32 {
        return Err(FindingsPgError::InvalidByteLength {
            column,
            expected: 32,
            actual,
        });
    }
    Ok(bytes
        .try_into()
        .expect("decode_fixed_32 length check guarantees 32 bytes"))
}
```

The done-ledger backend has its own copy:

```rust
// crates/gossip-done-ledger-postgres/src/backend.rs:558-570
fn decode_fixed_32(bytes: Vec<u8>, field: &'static str) -> Result<[u8; 32], DoneLedgerPgError> {
    bytes.try_into().map_err(|bytes: Vec<u8>| {
        DoneLedgerPgConversionError::InvalidByteLength {
            field,
            expected: 32,
            actual: bytes.len(),
        }
        .into()
    })
}
```

Both do the same thing — validate length and convert — but return different
crate-local error types and use different parameter names (`column` vs `field`).

## Desired State

A single `decode_fixed_32` function in `gossip-pg-common/src/types.rs` returning
`Result<[u8; 32], PgByteaLengthError>`, with each backend adding a `From` impl
so `?` works transparently. This mirrors the existing `PgU64ConversionError`
sharing pattern.

## Implementation Guidance

### Files to Modify

| File | Change | Rationale |
|------|--------|-----------|
| `crates/gossip-pg-common/src/types.rs` | Add `PgByteaLengthError` error type and `decode_fixed_32` function | Central shared location, mirrors `PgU64ConversionError` |
| `crates/gossip-pg-common/src/lib.rs` | Add `pub use types::{PgByteaLengthError, decode_fixed_32}` | Expose through crate root |
| `crates/gossip-findings-postgres/src/types.rs` | Add `PgByteaLengthError, decode_fixed_32` to existing `pub use gossip_pg_common::types::{...}` | Re-export pattern already established |
| `crates/gossip-findings-postgres/src/backend.rs` | Delete local `decode_fixed_32` (line 706-719), import from `crate::types` | Remove duplicate |
| `crates/gossip-findings-postgres/src/error.rs` | Add `From<PgByteaLengthError> for FindingsPgError` mapping to `InvalidByteLength` | Error wiring for `?` |
| `crates/gossip-done-ledger-postgres/src/backend.rs` | Delete local `decode_fixed_32` (line 561-570), import from shared | Remove duplicate |
| `crates/gossip-done-ledger-postgres/src/types.rs` | Add `PgByteaLengthError, decode_fixed_32` to re-exports | Re-export pattern |
| `crates/gossip-done-ledger-postgres/src/error.rs` | Add `From<PgByteaLengthError>` for done-ledger error chain | Error wiring for `?` |

### Patterns to Follow

Model `PgByteaLengthError` after the existing `PgU64ConversionError` at
`crates/gossip-pg-common/src/types.rs:32-68`:
- `#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]`
- Fields: `field: &'static str`, `expected: usize`, `actual: usize`
- `Display` and `Error` impls

Use `field` (not `column`) as the parameter name to match `PgU64ConversionError`
precedent. The findings backend currently uses `column` — rename call sites.

The done-ledger error already has a `U64Conversion(PgU64ConversionError)` variant
at `crates/gossip-done-ledger-postgres/src/error.rs:29`. Add a parallel
`ByteaLength(PgByteaLengthError)` variant, replacing the inline `InvalidByteLength`
variant at line 30-35.

For the findings backend, wire `From<PgByteaLengthError>` to the existing
`FindingsPgError::InvalidByteLength` variant (mapping `field` -> `column` field name
in the variant, or rename the variant's field from `column` to `field` for consistency).

### Utilities to Reuse

| Utility | Location | How to Reuse |
|---------|----------|--------------|
| `PgU64ConversionError` | `gossip-pg-common/src/types.rs:32-68` | Mirror structure for `PgByteaLengthError` |
| Re-export block | `gossip-findings-postgres/src/types.rs:16-19` | Extend with new items |
| `From<PgU64ConversionError>` impls | `gossip-findings-postgres/src/error.rs:248-252`, `gossip-done-ledger-postgres/src/error.rs:75-79` | Mirror for `PgByteaLengthError` |

### Blast Radius

| Caller | File | Relationship |
|--------|------|--------------|
| `count_observations_by_tenant_policy` | `crates/gossip-findings-postgres/src/backend.rs:377-378` | Calls `decode_fixed_32` for `tenant_id`, `policy_hash` |
| `list_findings_needing_triage` | `crates/gossip-findings-postgres/src/backend.rs:424-439` | Calls `decode_fixed_32` for 6 identity columns |
| `decode_row` | `crates/gossip-done-ledger-postgres/src/backend.rs:489-492` | Calls `decode_fixed_32` for `tenant_id`, `policy_hash`, `ovid_hash` |
| Unit tests | `crates/gossip-findings-postgres/src/backend.rs:750-772` | 2 tests for accept/reject; move core tests to `gossip-pg-common`, keep error-wiring tests in backends |

## Code References

See Current State section above for the two `decode_fixed_32` implementations.

Existing shared error pattern to mirror:

```rust
// crates/gossip-pg-common/src/types.rs:32-51
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub enum PgU64ConversionError {
    OrderedOutOfRange {
        field: &'static str,
        value: u64,
    },
    NegativeStoredValue {
        field: &'static str,
        value: i64,
    },
}
```

Existing re-export pattern:

```rust
// crates/gossip-findings-postgres/src/types.rs:16-19
pub use gossip_pg_common::types::{
    PgU64ConversionError, pg_bigint_nonnegative_to_u64, pg_bigint_to_u64_bits,
    u64_to_pg_bigint_bits, u64_to_pg_bigint_checked,
};
```

## Design Notes

- **`PgByteaLengthError` should be a struct, not an enum** — there is only one
  failure mode (wrong length), unlike `PgU64ConversionError` which has two variants.
  A struct with `field`, `expected`, `actual` fields is simpler.
- **Rename findings variant field from `column` to `field`** for consistency with
  the shared type and the done-ledger convention. This is a breaking change but
  the project has no backwards-compatibility obligations.
- **Move core tests to `gossip-pg-common`** — test accept/reject at the shared
  level. Keep one error-wiring smoke test in each backend.

## Related Work

| Task ID | Title | Relationship |
|---------|-------|--------------|
| gossip-9015.1 | D4.1 -- Read-path result types, SQL queries, and read methods | relates-to |
| gossip-9026 | Extract shared embedded-migration runner into gossip-pg-common | relates-to (precedent) |
| gossip-9032 | Extract shared testcontainers lifecycle into gossip-pg-common | relates-to (precedent) |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Single `decode_fixed_32` in `gossip-pg-common/src/types.rs` returning `Result<[u8; 32], PgByteaLengthError>`
- [ ] `PgByteaLengthError` struct with `Display` + `Error` impls, carrying `field`, `expected`, `actual`
- [ ] Both backend crates import the shared function; no local `decode_fixed_32` remains
- [ ] `From<PgByteaLengthError>` impls in both backend error modules
- [ ] Core accept/reject unit tests live in `gossip-pg-common`
- [ ] `cargo test -p gossip-pg-common -p gossip-findings-postgres -p gossip-done-ledger-postgres` passes
- [ ] `cargo fmt --all && cargo check && cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` clean
- [ ] `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps --all-features` clean

## Pointers

- `gossip-pg-common/src/types.rs` — existing shared conversion helpers and errors
- `gossip-pg-common/src/lib.rs` — crate root re-exports
- `crates/gossip-findings-postgres/src/error.rs` and `crates/gossip-done-ledger-postgres/src/error.rs` — error variant definitions and `From` impls to wire up
