title: Epic 2 — Commit protocol and runtime durability model
description:
## Goal

Freeze and implement the shared commit protocol before any family-specific runtime path lands.

This is where the old Epic E work starts. The point is to ensure Epic 3 and Epic 4 both build on the same runtime durability model.

## Tasks

1. Define the committed unit and receipt model
   - define CompletedUnit
   - define CommitReceipt
   - define runtime-facing commit request shape
   - define what the checkpoint aggregator consumes
2. Implement ResultCommitter
   - derive IDs
   - write to FindingsSink
   - write to DoneLedger
   - return receipt
   - make retry idempotent
3. Wire checkpointing to committed receipts only
   - checkpoint advancement is driven only by receipts
   - no cursor movement from scan completion alone
   - define prefix-commit semantics explicitly
4. Add bounded commit/backpressure pipeline
   - bounded channel between execution and commit stage
   - commit stage is the only place that authoritatively finishes work
   - scanning pauses when sinks slow down
5. Define shared write context for data-plane fencing
   - include (run_id, shard_id, fence_epoch) in commit/write context
   - thread this through runtime APIs even if all stores do not yet enforce it
6. Add receipt/order tests at the runtime-primitive layer
   - crash after findings write, before ledger write
   - crash after ledger write, before checkpoint
   - prefix commit ordering
   - no checkpoint without receipt

## Deliverables

- shared runtime commit model
- ResultCommitter
- receipt-driven checkpoint aggregator
- bounded commit pipeline
- write-context/fence metadata shape

## Dependencies

- Epic 1 (gossip-9045)

## Exit criteria

- no runtime path can advance checkpoint without a receipt
- findings → done-ledger → checkpoint ordering is enforced by runtime structure
- ordered content and Git can both build on the same commit model

title: EP2.1 — Freeze the family-neutral commit model
description:
## Context

Epic 2 establishes the shared commit protocol and runtime durability model that
both ordered-content (Epic 3) and Git/repo-frontier (Epic 4) execution paths must
build on. Before any family-specific runtime path lands, the shared vocabulary and
type contracts must be frozen so both families compose identically through the
commit pipeline.

The current codebase has a well-structured receipt hierarchy (`FindingsCommitReceipt`
→ `DoneLedgerCommitReceipt` → `CheckpointCommitReceipt` composing into
`ItemCommitReceipt` → `PageCommitReceipt`) and a `PageCommit<S>` typestate
machine enforcing findings → done-ledger → checkpoint ordering. However:

1. The checkpoint boundary is cursor-only and page-oriented — it does not
   distinguish ordered-content frontiers from repo-frontier progress.
2. There is no runtime-level `CompletedUnit` concept representing the smallest
   durable work unit.
3. There is no `CommitRequest` shape for the future `ResultCommitter`.
4. The `checkpoint_hint` field on `AssignmentOutcome` is always `None` — it is
   a dormant field waiting for the commit protocol to give it meaning.
5. The checkpoint aggregator input is undefined — nothing enforces that checkpoint
   advancement is driven solely by durable receipts.

## Current State

### Persistence receipt hierarchy — `crates/gossip-contracts/src/persistence/commit.rs:136-367`
```rust
// Leaf receipts
pub struct FindingsCommitReceipt { finding_count, occurrence_count, observation_count }
pub struct DoneLedgerCommitReceipt { record_count, scanned_count, findings_count }
pub struct CheckpointCommitReceipt { scope: PageCommitScope, checkpointed_at: LogicalTime }

// Composite receipts
pub struct ItemCommitReceipt { scope: Arc<PageCommitScope>, findings, done_ledger }
pub struct PageCommitReceipt { item_commit: ItemCommitReceipt, checkpoint: CheckpointCommitReceipt }
```

### Existing `PageCommitScope` — `crates/gossip-contracts/src/persistence/page_commit.rs:90-161`
```rust
pub struct PageCommitScope {
    tenant_id: TenantId,
    run_id: RunId,
    shard_id: ShardId,
    fence_epoch: FenceEpoch,
    committed_items: u64,
    checkpoint_cursor: Cursor,
}
```
No `CheckpointBoundary` enum — the scope uses a bare `Cursor`, which is semantically
ambiguous between ordered-content and repo-frontier progress.

### `checkpoint_hint` always `None` — `crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/lib.rs:678-687`
```rust
pub struct AssignmentOutcome {
    pub report: ScanReport,
    pub checkpoint_hint: Option<ScanCheckpoint>,
    pub debug_output: Option<String>,
}
```

### `ScanCheckpoint` (dormant hint shape) — `crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/lib.rs:576-581`
```rust
pub struct ScanCheckpoint {
    pub cursor: Cursor,
    pub committed_items: u64,
}
```

### No `commit_model` module exists
The `gossip-scanner-runtime` crate has no `commit_model.rs`. The runtime-level
commit vocabulary (`CompletedUnit`, `CommitRequest`, `UnitCommitReceipt`,
`CheckpointAggregatorInput`) does not exist yet.

### Existing `CommitReceipt` marker trait — `crates/gossip-contracts/src/persistence/commit.rs:52`
```rust
pub trait CommitReceipt: Clone + fmt::Debug + Send + Sync + 'static {}
```
This trait is implemented by `FindingsCommitReceipt`, `DoneLedgerCommitReceipt`,
`CheckpointCommitReceipt`, `ItemCommitReceipt`, and `PageCommitReceipt`. It
serves as the supertrait bound on `CommitHandle::Receipt`.

## Desired State

After this task, the codebase has a frozen family-neutral commit vocabulary:

1. **`CheckpointBoundary` enum** in `gossip-contracts/src/persistence/page_commit.rs`:
   A tagged enum (`OrderedContent(Cursor)` | `RepoFrontier(Cursor)`) that carries
   the semantic domain of the frontier position. Both families reduce to a monotonic
   `Cursor` at the persistence boundary, but the tag keeps family semantics explicit.
   **No `From<Cursor>` impl** — callers must explicitly choose
   `CheckpointBoundary::ordered_content(cursor)` or
   `CheckpointBoundary::repo_frontier(cursor)` to prevent silent mis-tagging.

2. **`CheckpointBoundaryKind` enum** — `OrderedContent` | `RepoFrontier` —
   a Copy tag without the cursor payload, for pattern matching on the domain.

3. **`CommitScope` (replacing `PageCommitScope`)** in the same file:
   Carries `(tenant_id, run_id, shard_id, fence_epoch, committed_units,
   checkpoint_boundary: CheckpointBoundary)`. The field rename from
   `committed_items` to `committed_units` makes the type family-neutral.
   **No type alias** — rename `PageCommitScope` to `CommitScope` in one pass
   across all call sites (per no-versioning policy). Provide a
   `committed_items()` accessor alias delegating to `committed_units()` to
   avoid breaking callers that use the old accessor name.

4. **`CompletedUnit`** in `gossip-scanner-runtime/src/commit_model.rs`:
   The smallest runtime work unit that can yield an authoritative durable receipt.
   Carries `(sequence_no: u64, checkpoint_boundary: CheckpointBoundary)`.
   Convenience constructors for ordered-content and repo-frontier variants.
   `sequence_no = 0` is valid (zero-indexed). Sequences must be monotonically
   increasing within a shard but need not be contiguous.

5. **`CommitRequest<'a>`** in the same module:
   Runtime-facing input to the future `ResultCommitter`. Carries
   `(completed_unit: CompletedUnit, findings: FindingsUpsertBatch<'a>,
   done_ledger: &'a [DoneLedgerRecord])`. Borrows payloads so the runtime keeps
   buffer ownership outside the commit stage. Both findings and done-ledger may
   be empty (valid: a completed unit that scanned but found nothing). The future
   `ResultCommitter` must still produce a receipt for ordering purposes.
   **Note:** `WriteContext` is introduced in EP2.5; `CommitRequest` in this task
   does NOT include it.

6. **`UnitCommitReceipt`** (runtime-level) in the same module:
   Durable per-unit proof wrapping `(completed_unit: CompletedUnit,
   durable: ItemCommitReceipt)`. Does NOT imply checkpoint advancement.
   Named `UnitCommitReceipt` to avoid collision with the contracts-level
   `CommitReceipt` marker trait. The `CompletedUnit::checkpoint_boundary`
   and `ItemCommitReceipt::scope().checkpoint_boundary()` must be equivalent;
   the constructor should include a `debug_assert_eq!` validating this.

7. **`CheckpointAggregatorInput`** in the same module:
   Newtype wrapper around `UnitCommitReceipt` that makes explicit: the checkpoint
   stage must never look at raw scan completion signals. Checkpoint advancement
   is driven solely by durable receipts.

### Key invariant
No new runtime type uses `checkpoint_hint` or `ScanCheckpoint` as an
authoritative progress signal. The `checkpoint_hint` field on
`AssignmentOutcome` remains dormant until a later EP2 task wires it through
committed receipts.

## Implementation Guidance

### Files to Modify
| File | Change | Rationale |
|------|--------|-----------|
| `crates/gossip-contracts/src/persistence/page_commit.rs` | Add `CheckpointBoundaryKind` enum, `CheckpointBoundary` enum (no `From<Cursor>` impl), rename `PageCommitScope` to `CommitScope` with `checkpoint_boundary` field and `committed_units` field, add `committed_items()` accessor alias | Family-neutral boundary type |
| `crates/gossip-contracts/src/persistence/commit.rs` | Update `CheckpointCommitReceipt` and `ItemCommitReceipt` to use `CommitScope` instead of `PageCommitScope` | One-pass rename |
| `crates/gossip-contracts/src/persistence/mod.rs` | Add `CheckpointBoundary`, `CheckpointBoundaryKind`, `CommitScope` to the `pub use page_commit::` re-export block; remove `PageCommitScope` | Public surface |
| `crates/gossip-contracts/src/persistence/conformance.rs` | Update any `PageCommitScope` references to `CommitScope` | One-pass rename |
| `crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/commit_model.rs` | **New file**: `CompletedUnit`, `CommitRequest`, `UnitCommitReceipt`, `CheckpointAggregatorInput` with `#[must_use]` on all types, tests including cross-family boundary inequality test | Runtime commit vocabulary |
| `crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/lib.rs` | Add `pub mod commit_model;` alongside existing module declarations at lines 69-76 | Module re-export |
| `diagrams/08-pagecommit-typestate.md` | Update to reflect `CommitScope`, `CheckpointBoundary`, family-neutral terminology | Design doc accuracy |

### Rename Migration: `PageCommitScope` → `CommitScope`
All call sites must be updated in one pass. Grep for `PageCommitScope` in:
- `crates/gossip-contracts/src/persistence/page_commit.rs` (definition + tests)
- `crates/gossip-contracts/src/persistence/commit.rs` (receipt fields)
- `crates/gossip-contracts/src/persistence/mod.rs` (re-exports)
- Any test files referencing the type

The rename also changes:
- Field: `checkpoint_cursor: Cursor` → `checkpoint_boundary: CheckpointBoundary`
- Field: `committed_items: u64` → `committed_units: u64`
- Accessor: `checkpoint_cursor()` → `checkpoint_cursor()` (new: accessor on `CheckpointBoundary` via `cursor()`)
- Accessor alias: retain `committed_items()` delegating to `committed_units()`

### Constructor Migration
`CommitScope::new(...)` changes its last parameter from `checkpoint_cursor: Cursor`
to `checkpoint_boundary: CheckpointBoundary`. All call sites (primarily in
page_commit.rs tests) must be updated to pass
`CheckpointBoundary::ordered_content(cursor)` explicitly.

### Patterns to Follow
- **Typestate pattern**: Follow the existing `PageCommit<S>` pattern in
  `crates/gossip-contracts/src/persistence/page_commit.rs:332-337` for any
  state machines.
- **Receipt composition**: Follow the existing receipt hierarchy pattern in
  `crates/gossip-contracts/src/persistence/commit.rs:136-367` where leaf
  receipts compose into composite receipts.
- **`#[must_use]` on proof types**: All receipts and proof objects carry
  `#[must_use]` per the existing convention. Apply to `CompletedUnit`,
  `CommitRequest`, `UnitCommitReceipt`, and `CheckpointAggregatorInput`.
- **`into_parts()` destructors**: Follow the existing pattern of providing
  `into_parts()` methods on data types for zero-cost decomposition.

### Utilities to Reuse
| Utility | Location | How to Reuse |
|---------|----------|-------------|
| `CommitHandle` trait | `crates/gossip-contracts/src/persistence/commit.rs:64-76` | Reuse directly; already generic over `Receipt` |
| `ReadyCommitHandle<R, E>` | `crates/gossip-contracts/src/persistence/commit.rs:86-120` | Zero-cost adapter for synchronous backends |
| `CommitReceipt` marker trait | `crates/gossip-contracts/src/persistence/commit.rs:52` | Apply to any new contracts-level receipt types (NOT the runtime `UnitCommitReceipt`) |
| `Cursor` | `crates/gossip-contracts/src/connector/types.rs:686-689` | Wrapped inside `CheckpointBoundary` variants |
| `ItemCommitReceipt` | `crates/gossip-contracts/src/persistence/commit.rs:277-324` | Wrapped by the runtime-level `UnitCommitReceipt` |
| `FindingsUpsertBatch<'a>` | `crates/gossip-contracts/src/persistence/findings.rs` | Borrowed by `CommitRequest` |

### Blast Radius
**Files this task directly modifies** (gossip-contracts persistence module):
- `page_commit.rs`, `commit.rs`, `mod.rs` — all in `crates/gossip-contracts/src/persistence/`
- All `PageCommitScope` references within these files renamed to `CommitScope`

**Crates NOT modified by this task** (type alias removed, but these crates
do not reference `PageCommitScope` directly — confirmed by grep):
- `crates/gossip-persistence-inmemory/` — uses `CommitHandle` and receipt types, not `PageCommitScope`
- `crates/gossip-done-ledger-postgres/` — uses `ReadyCommitHandle`, not `PageCommitScope`
- `crates/gossip-findings-postgres/` — uses `ReadyCommitHandle`, not `PageCommitScope`

**Documentation needing updates**:
- `diagrams/08-pagecommit-typestate.md` — documents current typestate machine

## Code References

### CommitHandle trait — `crates/gossip-contracts/src/persistence/commit.rs:64-76`
```rust
#[must_use = "durability is not established until wait() returns a receipt"]
pub trait CommitHandle: Send + 'static {
    type Receipt: CommitReceipt;
    type Error: Error + Send + Sync + 'static;
    fn wait(self) -> Result<Self::Receipt, Self::Error>;
}
```

### PageCommit typestate struct — `crates/gossip-contracts/src/persistence/page_commit.rs:332-337`
```rust
#[must_use = "page commits must be driven to a durable receipt or explicitly dropped"]
pub struct PageCommit<S> {
    scope: Arc<PageCommitScope>,
    state: S,
}
```

### FindingsSink trait — `crates/gossip-contracts/src/persistence/findings.rs:735-758`
```rust
pub trait FindingsSink: Send + Sync {
    type Error: Error + Send + Sync + 'static;
    type CommitHandle: CommitHandle<Receipt = FindingsCommitReceipt, Error = Self::Error>;
    fn upsert_batch(&self, batch: FindingsUpsertBatch<'_>) -> Result<Self::CommitHandle, Self::Error>;
}
```

### DoneLedger trait — `crates/gossip-contracts/src/persistence/done_ledger.rs:727-767`
```rust
pub trait DoneLedger: Send + Sync {
    type Error: Error + Send + Sync + 'static;
    type CommitHandle: CommitHandle<Receipt = DoneLedgerCommitReceipt, Error = Self::Error>;
    fn batch_upsert(&self, records: &[DoneLedgerRecord]) -> Result<Self::CommitHandle, Self::Error>;
}
```

### Coordination checkpoint — `crates/gossip-coordination/src/traits.rs:370-377`
```rust
fn checkpoint(
    &mut self, now: LogicalTime, tenant: TenantId, lease: &Lease,
    new_cursor: &CursorUpdate<'_>, op_id: OpId,
) -> Result<IdempotentOutcome<()>, CheckpointError>;
```

## Design Notes

**Why `CheckpointBoundary` is an enum, not a trait:**
Both currently planned families (ordered-content and repo-frontier) reduce to a
monotonic `Cursor` at the persistence boundary. An enum with two variants is
simpler, cheaper, and pattern-matchable.

**No `From<Cursor> for CheckpointBoundary`:**
All callers must explicitly choose `CheckpointBoundary::ordered_content(cursor)` or
`CheckpointBoundary::repo_frontier(cursor)`. An implicit `From<Cursor>` that
defaults to `OrderedContent` would silently mis-tag repo-frontier code paths.
Explicit construction prevents this class of bug at the cost of ~8 call site
updates (all currently in test code within `page_commit.rs`).

**Why `CommitRequest` borrows payloads:**
The runtime should keep buffer ownership outside the commit stage. Borrowing
`FindingsUpsertBatch<'a>` and `&'a [DoneLedgerRecord]` prevents unnecessary
cloning on the hot path and lets the caller reuse buffers across commit cycles.

**Why `CheckpointAggregatorInput` is a newtype, not a type alias:**
A newtype prevents accidental construction from raw scan signals. The checkpoint
stage must consume only durable receipts; the newtype enforces this at the type
level.

**Name collision avoidance — `UnitCommitReceipt` vs `CommitReceipt`:**
The contracts crate exports `pub trait CommitReceipt` as a marker trait for
durable acknowledgements. The runtime-level `UnitCommitReceipt` is a composite
wrapper (not a durable acknowledgement itself), so it intentionally does NOT
implement the `CommitReceipt` trait. The name `UnitCommitReceipt` avoids import
collisions between `gossip_contracts::persistence::CommitReceipt` (trait) and
`gossip_scanner_runtime::commit_model::UnitCommitReceipt` (struct).

**Scope equality is semantically strengthened:**
Two `CommitScope` values with identical cursor bytes but different
`CheckpointBoundaryKind` tags (`OrderedContent` vs `RepoFrontier`) are NOT
equal. This is intentional — it prevents cross-family receipt mix-ups at the
typestate validation level.

**`CompletedUnit` boundary must match `ItemCommitReceipt` scope boundary:**
When constructing `UnitCommitReceipt`, the `CompletedUnit::checkpoint_boundary`
and `ItemCommitReceipt::scope().checkpoint_boundary()` must be equivalent. A
`debug_assert_eq!` in the constructor validates this invariant. Mismatches
indicate a programming error (e.g., a receipt from a different family's
pipeline was paired with the wrong completed unit).

## Reference Material

The directory `tmp/gossip-project-artifacts/commit-protocol/2_1/` contains
proposed implementations that serve as a jumping-off point:
- `gossip-contracts/src/persistence/commit.rs` — enhanced receipt types
- `gossip-contracts/src/persistence/page_commit.rs` — `CheckpointBoundary` enum,
  `CommitScope`, `CheckpointBoundaryKind`
- `gossip-contracts/src/persistence/mod.rs` — updated re-exports
- `gossip-scanner-runtime/src/commit_model.rs` — `CompletedUnit`, `CommitRequest`,
  `CommitReceipt` (rename to `UnitCommitReceipt`), `CheckpointAggregatorInput` with tests
- `gossip-scanner-runtime/src/lib.rs` — module re-export

**Key differences from reference artifacts:**
- Remove `From<Cursor> for CheckpointBoundary` — require explicit construction
- Remove `PageCommitScope = CommitScope` type alias — rename in one pass
- Rename `CommitReceipt` struct → `UnitCommitReceipt` to avoid marker trait collision
- Add `debug_assert_eq!` in `UnitCommitReceipt::new` for boundary match validation
- Add `#[must_use]` on all four new types

## Follow-up Consumers

These types are vocabulary-only in this task. They become wired by:
- **EP2.2** — `ResultCommitter` implements the commit pipeline using `CommitRequest`
  and producing `UnitCommitReceipt`
- **EP2.3** — Checkpoint aggregator consumes `CheckpointAggregatorInput`
- **EP2.5** — `WriteContext` with `(run_id, shard_id, fence_epoch)` is threaded
  through `CommitRequest`

## Related Work
| Task ID | Title | Relationship |
|---------|-------|-------------|
| gossip-9065 | Epic 2 — Commit protocol and runtime durability model | parent-epic |
| gossip-9045 | Epic 1 — Replace old contract surface and rip out old design | blocks (transitive via epic) |
| gossip-9045.8 | Add execution context for connector-mode family loops | relates-to — will consume this commit model |
| gossip-8951.2 | A2 — Implement commit-handle/receipt boundary and page-commit typestate | relates-to — created the existing receipt hierarchy this task extends |
| gossip-8951 | Boundary 5 — Persistence contracts, backends, and commit protocol | relates-to — established the persistence boundary this task modifies |

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `CheckpointBoundary` enum exists with `OrderedContent(Cursor)` and `RepoFrontier(Cursor)` variants, no `From<Cursor>` impl
- [ ] `CheckpointBoundaryKind` enum exists with `OrderedContent` and `RepoFrontier` variants
- [ ] `CommitScope` replaces `PageCommitScope` everywhere (no type alias — one-pass rename)
- [ ] `CommitScope` provides `committed_items()` accessor alias delegating to `committed_units()`
- [ ] `CompletedUnit` struct exists in `gossip-scanner-runtime/src/commit_model.rs` with `sequence_no` and `checkpoint_boundary`
- [ ] `CommitRequest<'a>` struct exists with borrowed findings and done-ledger payloads (no `WriteContext` — that is EP2.5)
- [ ] `UnitCommitReceipt` wraps `CompletedUnit + ItemCommitReceipt` with `debug_assert_eq!` on boundary match
- [ ] `CheckpointAggregatorInput` newtype wraps only `UnitCommitReceipt`
- [ ] All four new types carry `#[must_use]` attributes
- [ ] A test verifies `CheckpointBoundary::OrderedContent(c) != CheckpointBoundary::RepoFrontier(c)` for the same cursor
- [ ] Ordered-content and repo-frontier can both express "item durable" and "boundary durable" using the same model (demonstrated by tests)
- [ ] `static_assertions::assert_impl_all!(CheckpointAggregatorInput: Send, Sync)` or equivalent compile-time check
- [ ] No new runtime type uses `checkpoint_hint` as an authoritative progress signal
- [ ] All existing tests pass: `cargo test`
- [ ] Code compiles clean: `cargo fmt --all && cargo check && cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`
- [ ] `diagrams/08-pagecommit-typestate.md` updated to reflect `CommitScope`, `CheckpointBoundary`, and family-neutral terminology

## Pointers
- `crates/gossip-contracts/src/persistence/` — all persistence contract types
- `crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/` — runtime crate where commit_model.rs will live
- `diagrams/08-pagecommit-typestate.md` — typestate diagram to update

title: EP2.2 — Define and thread shared write context
description:
## Context

Epic 2 requires all runtime persistence writes to carry a shared fencing
and routing metadata object so downstream backends can enforce stale-writer
rejection without every call site threading five individual scalars. Currently
`ObservationRecord::new()` takes 8 positional arguments (5 of which are write
context), `DoneLedgerProvenance::new()` takes 5 (3 are write context), and
`DurableCommitSink` is missing `policy_hash`, `run_id`, and `fence_epoch`
entirely. There is no single source of truth for provenance.

This task introduces `WriteContext` as a small `Copy` struct and threads it
through runtime commit APIs and persistence record constructors, creating one
authoritative provenance shape used by both findings and done-ledger writes.

EP2.1 (gossip-9065.1) introduces `CommitRequest` and the commit model types
that this task extends with `WriteContext`.

## Current State

### `ObservationRecord::new()` — 8 scalar args (`crates/gossip-contracts/src/persistence/findings.rs:327-354`)
```rust
pub fn new(
    tenant_id: TenantId,
    occurrence_id: OccurrenceId,
    policy_hash: PolicyHash,
    ovid_hash: OvidHash,
    run_id: RunId,
    shard_id: ShardId,
    fence_epoch: FenceEpoch,
    seen_at: LogicalTime,
) -> Self
```
5 of 8 parameters are write-context fields (`tenant_id`, `policy_hash`,
`run_id`, `shard_id`, `fence_epoch`). The remaining 3 (`occurrence_id`,
`ovid_hash`, `seen_at`) are per-observation values.

### `DoneLedgerProvenance::new()` — 5 scalar args (`crates/gossip-contracts/src/persistence/done_ledger.rs:378-396`)
```rust
pub fn new(
    run_id: RunId,
    shard_id: ShardId,
    fence_epoch: FenceEpoch,
    started_at: LogicalTime,
    finished_at: LogicalTime,
) -> Self
```
3 of 5 parameters are write-context fields. The remaining 2 (`started_at`,
`finished_at`) are per-item timestamps. Note: `tenant_id` and `policy_hash`
live on `DoneLedgerKey`, not on provenance.

### `DurableCommitSink` — missing fencing fields (`crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/commit_sink.rs:92-98`)
```rust
pub struct DurableCommitSink {
    shard_id: Arc<str>,
    recorder: Arc<dyn CoordinationEventRecorder>,
    tenant_id: TenantId,
    tenant_secret_key: TenantSecretKey,
    in_flight_meta: Mutex<BTreeMap<Vec<u8>, ItemMeta>>,
}
```
Missing `policy_hash`, `run_id`, `fence_epoch`. Uses `Arc<str>` for `shard_id`
(string label for event routing) — distinct from `ShardId` (u64 numeric identity).

### `CommitProgressRecord` — no provenance (`crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/coordination_sink.rs:34-44`)
```rust
pub enum CommitProgressRecord {
    Begin { item_key: Vec<u8>, size_hint: Option<u64> },
    Finish { item_key: Vec<u8> },
}
```

### `IdentityChainRecord` — no provenance (`crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/coordination_sink.rs:51-70`)
Pure identity chain fields only — no routing/fencing metadata.

### No `WriteContext` or `ShardLease` types exist
Grep for both across the codebase returns zero hits.

### `PageCommitScope` — 4-field overlap (`crates/gossip-contracts/src/persistence/page_commit.rs:90-97`)
```rust
pub struct PageCommitScope {
    tenant_id: TenantId,
    run_id: RunId,
    shard_id: ShardId,
    fence_epoch: FenceEpoch,
    committed_items: u64,
    checkpoint_cursor: Cursor,
}
```
Shares `(tenant_id, run_id, shard_id, fence_epoch)` with `WriteContext`.
`PageCommitScope` is page-scoped (includes committed_items and cursor);
`WriteContext` is shard-scoped (includes policy_hash, no page fields).
They are complementary — see Design Notes.

## Desired State

1. **`WriteContext`** in `crates/gossip-contracts/src/persistence/write_context.rs`:
   A small `#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]` struct carrying
   `(tenant_id: TenantId, policy_hash: PolicyHash, run_id: RunId,
   shard_id: ShardId, fence_epoch: FenceEpoch)`. 88 bytes total, safe for
   `Copy`. All accessors are `const fn`. A single `new()` constructor.
   Include `const_assert!(size_of::<WriteContext>() == 88)` to catch size regressions.

2. **`ObservationRecord::from_write_context()`** — new convenience constructor
   that accepts `WriteContext` plus per-observation fields (`occurrence_id`,
   `ovid_hash`, `seen_at`). The existing `new()` (8 scalar args) is retained
   for the read/deserialization path (`from_persisted()`, Postgres row decode).
   Runtime write-path code should prefer `from_write_context()`.

3. **`DoneLedgerProvenance::from_write_context()`** — new convenience
   constructor that accepts `WriteContext` plus per-item timestamps
   (`started_at`, `finished_at`). Extracts only `(run_id, shard_id,
   fence_epoch)` from `WriteContext` — `tenant_id` and `policy_hash` are
   intentionally not stored on provenance (they live on `DoneLedgerKey`).
   Document this partial extraction in the doc comment. Existing `new()`
   retained for read path.

4. **`ObservationRecord::write_context()`** — accessor that reconstructs
   `WriteContext` from the observation's stored fields (round-trip verification).

5. **`DoneLedgerRecord::write_context()`** — accessor that reconstructs
   `WriteContext` by combining `tenant_id`/`policy_hash` from `self.key` with
   `run_id`/`shard_id`/`fence_epoch` from `self.provenance`. Document that
   reconstruction spans two sub-structs.

6. **`DurableCommitSink`** refactored to store `write_context: WriteContext`
   instead of individual `tenant_id` field. Constructor takes `WriteContext`
   plus `tenant_secret_key` (retained as separate field). The `shard_id:
   Arc<str>` field is renamed to `recorder_shard_label: Arc<str>` to
   distinguish it from `WriteContext.shard_id: ShardId` (numeric).
   Identity derivation uses `self.write_context.tenant_id()` for
   `FindingIdInputs.tenant`.

7. **`CommitProgressRecord`** gains `write_context: WriteContext` on both
   `Begin` and `Finish` variants. `DurableCommitSink` passes its stored
   context when constructing these.

8. **`IdentityChainRecord`** gains `write_context: WriteContext` field.

9. **`CommitRequest<'a>`** gains `write_context: WriteContext` field (EP2.1
   creates this type without it; this task adds the field). Update constructor,
   accessor, and `into_parts()`.

10. **`ShardLease`** — **new struct** in `crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/distributed.rs`:
    Bundles a scan `Assignment` with `write_context: WriteContext`,
    `shard_id: Arc<str>` (string label for event routing), and
    `tenant_secret_key: TenantSecretKey`. One lease corresponds to one shard
    from the coordination layer. Include a `debug_assert_eq!` validating that
    `assignment.policy_hash == write_context.policy_hash()`.

11. **Re-exports**: `WriteContext` added to
    `crates/gossip-contracts/src/persistence/mod.rs` public surface.

### Key invariant
Every done-ledger write and every observation write emitted by the runtime
uses the same `WriteContext` instance. The `WriteContext` is constructed once
at shard lease acquisition time and threaded through all downstream APIs.

### Implementation checkpoints
The changes are mechanical but span multiple crates. Land incrementally:

2. Then: Thread through runtime types (`DurableCommitSink`, `CommitProgressRecord`,
   `IdentityChainRecord`, `ShardLease`, `CommitRequest`). Verify:

## Design Notes

**Why `WriteContext` is `Copy`:**
At 88 bytes (two 32-byte hashes + three 8-byte IDs), `WriteContext` is small
enough for stack passing. It is constructed once per shard lease and threaded
by value. The per-finding copy (into `ObservationRecord::from_write_context()`)
is dwarfed by the BLAKE3 identity derivation that follows. A compile-time size
assertion prevents accidental regression.

**Why existing constructors are retained:**
`ObservationRecord::new()` and `DoneLedgerProvenance::new()` are used by the
read/deserialization path (Postgres `decode_row()`, `from_persisted()`) where
a pre-assembled `WriteContext` is not available. Runtime write-path code uses
`from_write_context()`. This is not a compatibility shim (no-versioning policy)
— the two constructors serve fundamentally different data flows.

**`DoneLedgerProvenance::from_write_context()` partial extraction:**
`DoneLedgerProvenance` stores only `(run_id, shard_id, fence_epoch)`.
`WriteContext` carries 5 fields. The constructor extracts only the 3 relevant
fields. `tenant_id` and `policy_hash` are not discarded — they live on
`DoneLedgerKey` (which is constructed separately from the same `WriteContext`).
The round-trip accessor `DoneLedgerRecord::write_context()` reconstructs
the full `WriteContext` by combining `key.tenant_id()`/`key.policy_hash()`
with `provenance.run_id()`/`provenance.shard_id()`/`provenance.fence_epoch()`.

**Relationship to `CommitScope`/`PageCommitScope`:**
`CommitScope` (from EP2.1, replacing `PageCommitScope`) carries
`(tenant_id, run_id, shard_id, fence_epoch, committed_units,
checkpoint_boundary)`. It overlaps with `WriteContext` on the first 4 fields
but is page-scoped (includes committed_units and boundary). `WriteContext` is
shard-scoped (includes `policy_hash`, no page fields). They are complementary.
Extracting a shared sub-struct (e.g., `ScopeIdentity`) is a possible future
refactor but not required now — the overlap is 4 scalar fields, and adding
composition would change both types' constructors simultaneously. Document
the overlap explicitly.

**Dual shard identity — `Arc<str>` vs `ShardId`:**
`DurableCommitSink` retains `recorder_shard_label: Arc<str>` for the
`CoordinationEventRecorder` trait interface (which takes `&str`). The numeric
`ShardId` inside `WriteContext` is the coordination-layer shard identity used
for fencing. These are distinct: the string label routes telemetry events,
the numeric ID gates lease ownership. `CoordinationEventRecorder` methods
receive the shard identity twice (as `&str` parameter and inside
`WriteContext.shard_id`); the `WriteContext.shard_id` is authoritative for
fencing, the `&str` is for routing/logging.

title: EP2.3 — Build deterministic result-to-persistence translation
description:
## Context

Epic 2 establishes the shared commit protocol and runtime durability model.
Before any family-specific runtime path can commit scan results to persistence,
the translation logic that converts raw scan output into durable records must be
frozen. This translation sits between the scan engine (which produces
`FsFindingRecord` values) and the commit pipeline (which writes to `FindingsSink`
and `DoneLedger`). Currently, identity derivation logic lives inside
`DurableCommitSink::derive_identity_record` (`crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/commit_sink.rs:129-176`),
but that code outputs `IdentityChainRecord` for event recording — not the
real persistence records (`FindingRecord`, `OccurrenceRecord`,
`ObservationRecord`, `DoneLedgerRecord`) that downstream commit stages require.

EP2.3 extracts and formalizes this translation as a pure, deterministic function
that the future `ResultCommitter` (EP2.4) will invoke to produce persistence
payloads before writing to sinks.

## Current State

### Identity derivation in DurableCommitSink — `crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/commit_sink.rs:129-176`
```rust
fn derive_identity_record(&self, item_key: &ItemKey, meta: &ItemMeta,
    finding: &FindingRecord) -> Result<IdentityChainRecord> {
    let norm_hash = NormHash::from_digest(finding.norm_hash);
    let secret_hash = key_secret_hash(&self.tenant_secret_key, &norm_hash);
    let finding_id = derive_finding_id(&FindingIdInputs {
        tenant: self.tenant_id, item: meta.stable_item_id,
        rule: rule_fingerprint_from_rule_id(finding.rule_id), secret: secret_hash,
    });
    // ... outputs IdentityChainRecord, NOT persistence records
}
```
This method performs correct BLAKE3-based identity derivation but targets the
coordination event recording surface, not real persistence records.

**Type name note:** The `FindingRecord` parameter above refers to
`commit_sink::FindingRecord` (fields: `rule_id`, `start`, `end`, `norm_hash`,
`confidence_score` — defined at `commit_sink.rs:36-47`). This is a different
type from `gossip_contracts::persistence::FindingRecord` (the persistence record).
The translation module uses neither of these as input — it takes
`scanner_scheduler::FsFindingRecord` (from `store.rs:41-57`) and produces
`gossip_contracts::persistence::FindingRecord` as output.

### `rule_fingerprint_from_rule_id` (private) — `crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/commit_sink.rs:234-238`
```rust
fn rule_fingerprint_from_rule_id(rule_id: u32) -> RuleFingerprint {
    let mut bytes = [0u8; 32];
    bytes[..4].copy_from_slice(&rule_id.to_le_bytes());
    RuleFingerprint::from_bytes(bytes)
}
```
This helper expands a numeric rule ID into the 32-byte fingerprint shape.
Currently private to `commit_sink.rs`.

### No `result_translation` module exists
The `gossip-scanner-runtime` crate has no `result_translation.rs`. Module
declarations in `crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/lib.rs:69-76`:
```rust
pub mod cli;
pub mod commit_sink;
pub mod coordination_sink;
pub mod distributed;
pub mod event_sink;
pub mod parity;
```

### Persistence record constructors already exist
- `FindingRecord::new()` in `crates/gossip-contracts/src/persistence/findings.rs:75-98` —
  derives `FindingId` internally from `(tenant, item, rule, secret)`.
- `OccurrenceRecord::try_new()` in `crates/gossip-contracts/src/persistence/findings.rs:185-201` —
  validates non-zero span length, derives `OccurrenceId`.
- `ObservationRecord::from_write_context()` (from EP2.2) in
  `crates/gossip-contracts/src/persistence/findings.rs` — constructs observation
  from `WriteContext` plus per-observation fields.
- `DoneLedgerRecord::try_new()` in `crates/gossip-contracts/src/persistence/done_ledger.rs:465-496` —
  validates status/findings_count consistency.
- `derive_ovid_hash()` in `crates/gossip-contracts/src/persistence/ovid.rs:52-57`.
- `key_secret_hash()` in `crates/gossip-contracts/src/identity/finding.rs:327-335`.

### `FsFindingRecord` input type — `crates/scanner-scheduler/src/store.rs:41-57`
```rust
pub struct FsFindingRecord {
    pub rule_id: u32,
    pub root_hint_start: u64,
    pub root_hint_end: u64,
    pub span_start: u64,
    pub span_end: u64,
    pub norm_hash: NormHash,  // [u8; 32] alias from engine
    pub confidence_score: i8,
}
```

### `ScanItem` — `crates/gossip-contracts/src/connector/types.rs:996-1004`
```rust
pub struct ScanItem {
    item_key: ItemKey,
    item_ref: ItemRef,
    stable_item_id: StableItemId,
    version: VersionId,
    size_hint: Option<u64>,
    content_hints: Option<ContentHints>,
    location: Option<Location>,
}
```

## Desired State

After this task, the codebase has a `result_translation` module in
`gossip-scanner-runtime` that provides a single pure entry point for converting
one completed item's scan results into the full set of persistence records:

1. **`ScanTiming`** — logical timing metadata carrying `started_at` and
   `finished_at` as `LogicalTime` values. Both are threaded into done-ledger
   provenance; `finished_at` doubles as the observation `seen_at` timestamp.
   Constructor includes `debug_assert!` for monotonicity.

2. **`ItemResult<'a>`** — terminal outcome enum:
   - `Scanned { findings: &'a [FsFindingRecord] }` — successful scan, findings
     may be empty.
   - `FailedRetryable { error_code: DoneLedgerErrorCode }` — transient failure.
   - `FailedPermanent { error_code: DoneLedgerErrorCode }` — permanent failure.
   - `Skipped { error_code: DoneLedgerErrorCode }` — intentional skip.

   Provides `done_ledger_status()` mapping and `error_code()` accessor. Only
   the `Scanned` branch produces findings, occurrences, and observations.

3. **`PersistenceTranslation`** — output bundle owning:
   - `ovid_hash: OvidHash`
   - `findings: Vec<FindingRecord>` (persistence `FindingRecord`, not `commit_sink::FindingRecord`)
   - `occurrences: Vec<OccurrenceRecord>`
   - `observations: Vec<ObservationRecord>`
   - `done_ledger: DoneLedgerRecord`

   Provides `findings_batch() -> FindingsUpsertBatch<'_>` for zero-copy
   borrowing by the commit stage, plus `finding_count()`, `occurrence_count()`,
   `observation_count()` accessors.

4. **`ResultTranslationError`** — error enum:
   - `InvalidFindingSpan { index, start, end }` — empty or inverted span.
   - `TooManyDistinctFindings { count }` — distinct finding count does not fit
     in `u32` (the done-ledger `findings_count` field type). Use
     `u32::try_from(distinct_count).map_err(...)` for the check.
   - `Persistence(PersistenceInputError)` — delegated constructor/validator rejection.

5. **`translate_item_result()`** — top-level pure translation function:
   ```rust
   pub fn translate_item_result(
       write_context: WriteContext,
       tenant_secret_key: &TenantSecretKey,
       item: &ScanItem,
       bytes_scanned: u64,
       timing: ScanTiming,
       result: ItemResult<'_>,
   ) -> Result<PersistenceTranslation, ResultTranslationError>
   ```
   Deterministic: no wall-clock reads, no random values, no backend state.
   Same inputs always produce the same persistence IDs and done-ledger key.

6. **`translate_findings()`** — internal helper that iterates `FsFindingRecord`
   slices and produces deduplicated `(findings, occurrences, observations)`
   tuples. Deduplication is by `FindingId`, `OccurrenceId`, and `ObservationId`
   respectively using `HashSet` tracking. Each `ObservationRecord` receives
   `item.location().cloned()` via `.with_location()` when the item carries a
   `Location`.

7. **`rule_fingerprint_from_rule_id()`** — extracted as `pub(crate)` so both
   `result_translation` and `commit_sink` can use it without duplication.

### Key invariants
- Input finding order is preserved.
- Stable findings are deduplicated by `FindingId`.
- Occurrences are deduplicated by `OccurrenceId`.
- Observations are deduplicated by `ObservationId`.
- The done-ledger `findings_count` is the number of distinct stable findings,
  not the number of raw engine emissions.
- `span_start`/`span_end` from `FsFindingRecord` are the version-specific
  occurrence span. `root_hint_*` fields do not enter persistence identity
  derivation.
- Post-translation validation runs `FindingsUpsertBatch::validate_observation_identity()`
  and `validate_referential_integrity()` before returning.
- No raw secret bytes appear in the output records, logs, or `Debug` output.

## Implementation Guidance

### Files to Modify
| File | Change | Rationale |
|------|--------|-----------|
| `crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/result_translation.rs` | **New file**: `ScanTiming`, `ItemResult`, `PersistenceTranslation`, `ResultTranslationError`, `translate_item_result()`, `translate_findings()`, `rule_fingerprint_from_rule_id()`, unit tests | Core translation module |
| `crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/lib.rs` | Add `pub mod result_translation;` at line ~68 alongside existing module declarations | Module registration |
| `crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/commit_sink.rs` | Change private `rule_fingerprint_from_rule_id()` to import from `result_translation` (or make `pub(crate)` and have result_translation import it) | Eliminate duplication per policy |

### Type disambiguation
Three different `FindingRecord` types exist in the codebase:
- `scanner_scheduler::FsFindingRecord` (`store.rs:41-57`) — **input** to translation
- `gossip_contracts::persistence::FindingRecord` (`findings.rs:75`) — **output** of translation
- `commit_sink::FindingRecord` (`commit_sink.rs:36-47`) — NOT used by translation

Use explicit `use` paths or aliases to avoid confusion. The `result_translation`
module should import `scanner_scheduler::FsFindingRecord` and
`gossip_contracts::persistence::FindingRecord` (the latter via the
`gossip_contracts::persistence::` path).

### Location threading
Each `ObservationRecord` produced by `translate_findings()` should carry the
item's location. After constructing the observation via
`ObservationRecord::from_write_context(...)`, apply the item's location:
```rust
let location = item.location().cloned();
// ... in the loop:
let mut obs = ObservationRecord::from_write_context(write_context, occurrence_id, ovid_hash, seen_at);
if let Some(loc) = location.clone() {
    obs = obs.with_location(loc);
}
```
`ScanItem::location()` returns `Option<&Location>`.

- **Pure translation functions**: The translation has no side effects, no I/O,
  no clock reads. Follow the same pattern as `derive_ovid_hash()` in
  `crates/gossip-contracts/src/persistence/ovid.rs:52-57`.
- **Persistence record constructors**: Use existing `FindingRecord::new()`,
  `OccurrenceRecord::try_new()`, `ObservationRecord::from_write_context()`,

- **`FindingsUpsertBatch` validation**: Follow the pattern in

## Design Notes

**Why the translation is a free function, not a method on a struct:**
The translation is stateless and pure — it takes all inputs as parameters and
produces all outputs as a return value. A struct would add lifetime complexity
and imply retained state. A free function makes the purity explicit and
simplifies testing.

**Why `PersistenceTranslation` owns Vecs:**
The commit stage (future `ResultCommitter`) needs to borrow
`FindingsUpsertBatch<'_>` and `&[DoneLedgerRecord]`. Owning the vectors in
the translation result lets the commit stage borrow without worrying about
intermediate lifetime juggling. The translation allocates once per item (WARM
tier), which is acceptable.

**`FsFindingRecord.norm_hash` type bridging:**
The engine uses `type NormHash = [u8; 32]` (a raw byte array alias). The
contracts crate has `NormHash` as a proper newtype. The bridge is
`NormHash::from_digest(finding.norm_hash)`. This must happen at the
translation boundary, not inside persistence constructors.

**`rule_fingerprint_from_rule_id` duplication strategy:**
The reference implementation defines its own copy in `result_translation.rs`.
Per the duplication-prevention policy, the preferred approach is to make the
existing function in `commit_sink.rs` `pub(crate)` and import it in
`result_translation.rs`, OR move it to `result_translation.rs` as `pub(crate)`
and import from `commit_sink.rs`. Choose whichever direction minimizes diff.

**Span semantics:**
`FsFindingRecord.span_start` / `span_end` are the version-specific occurrence
span (byte offsets within the scanned content). `root_hint_start` / `root_hint_end`
are deduplication aids for the scanner pipeline and do NOT enter persistence
identity derivation. Only `span_start` and `(span_end - span_start)` flow
into `OccurrenceRecord::try_new()`.

**`ScanItem.version` is non-optional:**
Unlike `DurableCommitSink::derive_identity_record` which handles
`ItemMeta.version: Option<VersionId>` with a fallback to
`ObjectVersionId::from_version_bytes(item_key.as_bytes())`, the
`translate_item_result()` function takes `&ScanItem` where
`ScanItem.version()` returns `VersionId` (non-optional, see
`crates/gossip-contracts/src/connector/types.rs:1079`).
`VersionId::object_version_id()` extracts `ObjectVersionId` from both
`Strong` and `Weak` variants without fallback. No optional handling is needed.

**Post-translation validation:**
`FindingsUpsertBatch::validate_observation_identity()` checks that every
observation's `observation_id` is deterministically derivable from its stored
fields. `validate_referential_integrity()` checks that every occurrence
references a finding in the batch, and every observation references an
occurrence. Both are called before returning the translation result to catch
implementation bugs early.

title: EP2.4 — Implement ResultCommitter
description:
## Context

Epic 2 establishes the shared commit protocol and runtime durability model.
EP2.1 froze the commit vocabulary (`CommitRequest`, `CompletedUnit`,
`UnitCommitReceipt`), EP2.2 threaded `WriteContext` through all persistence
APIs, and EP2.3 built the deterministic translation from scan results into
persistence records. EP2.4 is the authoritative write stage that takes the
translated records and commits them to durable sinks in the correct order.

Without EP2.4, there is no runtime-level service that enforces the
findings → done-ledger ordering invariant. The `PageCommit<S>` typestate
machine in `gossip-contracts` encodes this ordering at the type level, but
no runtime module drives it through a real commit cycle yet.

## Current State

### `PageCommit<S>` typestate machine — `crates/gossip-contracts/src/persistence/page_commit.rs:332-346`
```rust
#[must_use = "page commits must be driven to a durable receipt or explicitly dropped"]
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct PageCommit<S> {
    scope: Arc<PageCommitScope>,
    state: S,
}
```
Three state transitions: `AwaitingFindings` → `FindingsDurable` → `ItemDurable`
(→ optionally `CheckpointDurable`). EP2.4 drives the first two transitions
and extracts `ItemCommitReceipt` at `ItemDurable`.

### `PageCommit::new` + `wait_findings` — `page_commit.rs:348-383`
```rust
impl PageCommit<AwaitingFindings> {
    pub fn new(scope: PageCommitScope) -> Self {
        Self { scope: Arc::new(scope), state: AwaitingFindings }
    }
    pub fn wait_findings<H>(self, handle: H) -> Result<PageCommit<FindingsDurable>, H::Error>
    where H: CommitHandle<Receipt = FindingsCommitReceipt> { ... }
}
```

### `PageCommit::wait_done_ledger` → `ItemDurable` — `page_commit.rs:424-435`
```rust
pub fn wait_done_ledger<H>(self, handle: H)
    -> Result<PageCommit<ItemDurable>, CommitAdvanceError<H::Error>>
where H: CommitHandle<Receipt = DoneLedgerCommitReceipt> {
    let receipt = handle.wait().map_err(CommitAdvanceError::Wait)?;
    self.record_done_ledger(receipt).map_err(CommitAdvanceError::Validation)
}
```

### `PageCommit<ItemDurable>::into_item_commit_receipt` — `page_commit.rs:446-449`
```rust
pub fn into_item_commit_receipt(self) -> ItemCommitReceipt {
    self.state.item_commit
}
```

### `CommitHandle` trait — `crates/gossip-contracts/src/persistence/commit.rs:63-76`

```rust
#[must_use = "durability is not established until wait() returns a receipt"]
pub trait CommitHandle: Send + 'static {
    type Receipt: CommitReceipt;
    type Error: Error + Send + Sync + 'static;
    fn wait(self) -> Result<Self::Receipt, Self::Error>;
}
```

### `FindingsSink` trait — `crates/gossip-contracts/src/persistence/findings.rs:735-758`

```rust
    type Error: Error + Send + Sync + 'static;

        -> Result<Self::CommitHandle, Self::Error>;
}
```

### `DoneLedger` trait — `crates/gossip-contracts/src/persistence/done_ledger.rs:727-767`

```rust
    type Error: Error + Send + Sync + 'static;

        -> Result<Self::CommitHandle, Self::Error>;

```

### `CommitAdvanceError<E>` — `crates/gossip-contracts/src/persistence/page_commit.rs:199-228`

```rust
    Wait(E),
    Validation(PageCommitValidationError),
}
```

### No `result_committer` module exists
The `gossip-scanner-runtime` crate has no `result_committer.rs`. Module
declarations in `crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/lib.rs:69-76`:
```rust

pub mod coordination_sink;
pub mod distributed;
pub mod event_sink;
pub mod parity;
```

### `gossip-persistence-inmemory` not in dev-deps
`crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/Cargo.toml` dev-dependencies only include
`rstest` and `tempfile`. The InMemory backends needed for EP2.4 tests are
not available.

### InMemory test infrastructure
`InMemoryFindingsSink` and `InMemoryDoneLedger` provide:
- `with_auto_complete(false)` — delayed completion for ordering tests
- `fail_next_submissions(count)` — inject submission failures
- `fail_next_commits(count)` — inject durability wait failures
- `release_next(CompletionOrder)` — manually advance pending writes
- `pending_count()` — observe in-flight writes
- `findings_snapshot()` / `snapshot()` — observe persisted state
- `InMemoryPersistenceError` with `InjectedSubmissionFailure { store }` and
  `InjectedCommitFailure { store }` variants, `InMemoryStoreKind` enum

## Desired State

After this task, the codebase has a `result_committer` module in
`gossip-scanner-runtime` that provides the authoritative item-level durable
commit stage:

1. **`ResultCommitRequestError`** — deterministic validation errors for
   invalid commit requests (programming errors, not transient failures):
   - `DoneLedgerRecordCount { actual }` — not exactly one done-ledger row.
   - `FindingsBatch(PersistenceInputError)` — batch invariant violation.
   - `FindingTenantMismatch { expected, actual }` — finding row tenant differs.
   - `OccurrenceTenantMismatch { expected, actual }` — occurrence row tenant differs.
   - `ObservationWriteContextMismatch { index }` — observation write-context differs.
   - `ObservationOvidMismatch { index, expected, actual }` — observation OVID differs
     from done-ledger key.
   - `DoneLedgerWriteContextMismatch { expected, actual }` — done-ledger write-context differs.
   - `FindingsPresentForUnscannedStatus { status }` — findings payload on
     non-scanned terminal status.
   - `FindingsCountMismatch { expected, actual }` — done-ledger `findings_count`
     disagrees with distinct stable findings.
   - `DistinctFindingsOverflow { count }` — exceeds `u32` capacity.

2. **`ResultCommitError<FindingsError, DoneLedgerError>`** — runtime commit
   error enum preserving backend-specific error types:
   - `InvalidRequest(ResultCommitRequestError)` — pre-write validation failure.
   - `FindingsSubmit(FindingsError)` — sink rejected submission.
   - `FindingsWait(FindingsError)` — durability wait failed.
   - `DoneLedgerSubmit(DoneLedgerError)` — ledger rejected submission.
   - `DoneLedgerAdvance(CommitAdvanceError<DoneLedgerError>)` — ledger
     durability or typestate validation failed.

3. **`ResultCommitter<F, D>`** — thin generic struct parameterized over
   `F: FindingsSink` and `D: DoneLedger`:
   - `new(findings_sink, done_ledger)` constructor.
   - `findings_sink()` and `done_ledger()` accessors.
   - `commit_item(request: CommitRequest<'_>)` — primary entry point:
     validates request, constructs scope, drives `PageCommit` through
     `AwaitingFindings` → `FindingsDurable` → `ItemDurable`, extracts
     `ItemCommitReceipt`, wraps in runtime `CommitReceipt`.
   - `commit_translation(write_context, completed_unit, &PersistenceTranslation)` —
     convenience bridge from EP2.3 translation output to `commit_item`.
   - `commit(request)` — backwards-compatible alias for `commit_item`.

4. **`validate_request()`** — internal validation before any write:
   - `FindingsUpsertBatch::validate_observation_identity()`
   - `FindingsUpsertBatch::validate_referential_integrity()`
   - Exactly one done-ledger row
   - All findings/occurrences match `write_context.tenant_id()`
   - All observations match the request-level `WriteContext`
   - All observations match the done-ledger key's `ovid_hash`
   - Done-ledger row's `WriteContext` matches request-level `WriteContext`
   - Findings-count consistency for scanned status
   - No findings payload for non-scanned terminal status
   - `DoneLedgerRecord` error-code invariants (`MissingErrorCode`,
     `UnexpectedErrorCode`) are enforced at record construction time (by
     `DoneLedgerRecord::try_new()`). `validate_request()` relies on
     construction-time validation for these and does not re-check them.

5. **`distinct_findings_count()`** — free function counting unique `FindingId`
   values via `HashSet`, returning `u32` or `DistinctFindingsOverflow`.

### Key invariants
- **No early ACK**: The only way to obtain a `CommitReceipt` is after both
  `FindingsSink::upsert_batch().wait()` and `DoneLedger::batch_upsert().wait()`
  have returned. The `PageCommit` typestate machine enforces this at
  compile time.
- **Findings before done-ledger**: `DoneLedger::batch_upsert` is not called
  until `wait_findings` returns. If findings durability fails, the
  done-ledger is never written.
- **Retry safety**: Retrying the same `CommitRequest` is safe because sink
  contracts are idempotent on deterministic IDs (same `FindingId`,
  `OccurrenceId`, `ObservationId` produce upserts, not duplicates).
- **`committed_units = 1`**: Each `CommitRequest` carries exactly one
  done-ledger row. The scope is constructed with `committed_units = 1`,
  matching the done-ledger receipt's `record_count`.
- **Request validation before writes**: All consistency checks run before
  any sink call. Invalid requests never touch persistence.
- **Concurrent safety**: Multiple `commit_item` calls may execute
  concurrently. Each creates an independent `PageCommit` instance, so the
  findings→done-ledger ordering invariant holds per-call. No cross-call
  ordering is guaranteed or required.

### Commit flow
```
CommitRequest ──► validate_request()
                     │
                     ▼
              scope_for(write_context, completed_unit) (from EP2.2)
                     │
                     ▼
              PageCommit::new(scope)        [AwaitingFindings]
                     │
                     ▼
              findings_sink.upsert_batch()  → handle
              page.wait_findings(handle)    [FindingsDurable]
                     │
                     ▼
              done_ledger.batch_upsert()    → handle
              page.wait_done_ledger(handle) [ItemDurable]
                     │
                     ▼
              page.into_item_commit_receipt()
                     │
                     ▼
              CommitReceipt::new(completed_unit, item_receipt)
```

## Design Notes

**Why `ResultCommitter` is generic over `F` and `D`, not trait objects:**
Using trait object parameters (`&dyn FindingsSink<...>`) would require boxing
the `CommitHandle` associated type, adding heap allocation on every commit.
Generic parameters let the compiler monomorphize, preserving zero-cost
handle wait. This is consistent with how the conformance test harness uses
the sink traits.

**Why `committed_units = 1`:**
Each `CommitRequest` commits exactly one completed item. The scope is
constructed with `committed_units = 1`, and the `PageCommit` typestate
machine validates that `DoneLedgerCommitReceipt.record_count` matches
`scope.committed_items()` (via `PageCommitValidationError::LedgerItemCountMismatch`).
Multi-item batching is a future concern for the bounded pipeline.

**Why EP2.4 stops at `ItemDurable`, not `CheckpointDurable`:**
The `ResultCommitter` is responsible for per-item durability only. Checkpoint
advancement is a separate concern driven by the checkpoint aggregator, which
consumes `CommitReceipt` values and advances the cursor. EP2.4 returns
`CommitReceipt` wrapping `ItemCommitReceipt`, not `PageCommitReceipt`.

**`commit_translation()` vs `commit_item()`:**
`commit_translation()` is a convenience bridge from EP2.3's
`PersistenceTranslation` to `commit_item()`. It constructs a `CommitRequest`
by borrowing `translation.findings_batch()` and
`std::slice::from_ref(translation.done_ledger())`. Callers that already
have a `CommitRequest` (e.g., the bounded pipeline) use `commit_item()` directly.

**`DurableCommitSink` coexistence:**
EP2.4 does NOT replace `DurableCommitSink`. They serve different purposes:
- `DurableCommitSink` implements the `CommitSink` trait for the scan-driver
  pipeline, producing `IdentityChainRecord` for coordination event recording.
- `ResultCommitter` is the authoritative durable commit stage producing real
  persistence records with receipt-gated ordering.
Both may coexist until the old event-recording path is retired.

**Error shape preserves backend types:**
`ResultCommitError<FindingsError, DoneLedgerError>` is dual-generic to
preserve backend-specific error information without type erasure. This is
consistent with `CommitHandle::Error` and `CommitAdvanceError<E>` in the
contracts crate.

**Validation boundary — `DoneLedgerRecord` invariants:**
`DoneLedgerRecord::try_new()` enforces `MissingErrorCode` and
`UnexpectedErrorCode` consistency at construction time
(`crates/gossip-contracts/src/persistence/error.rs:37-40`).
`validate_request()` relies on construction-time validation for these
error-code invariants and does not re-check them. The committer's validation
focuses on cross-field consistency between the findings batch, done-ledger
row, and write context — invariants that span multiple records and cannot
be checked at individual record construction time.

title: EP2.5 — Implement receipt-driven prefix checkpoint aggregator
description:
## Context

Epic 2 establishes the shared commit protocol and runtime durability model.
EP2.1 froze the commit vocabulary, EP2.2 threaded `WriteContext`, EP2.3 built
result translation, and EP2.4 implemented the per-item `ResultCommitter`. The
missing piece is the checkpoint stage that consumes durable per-unit receipts
and advances a contiguous committed prefix.

The plan is explicit: checkpoint advancement is driven only by receipts. No
cursor movement from scan completion alone. The connector boundary plan is
explicit that empty-page semantics and cursor movement rules must be encoded
and tested, not inferred from side effects.

## Current State

### `PageCommit<ItemDurable>` — `crates/gossip-contracts/src/persistence/page_commit.rs:437-509`
```rust
impl PageCommit<ItemDurable> {
    pub fn item_commit_receipt(&self) -> &ItemCommitReceipt { ... }     // borrow
    pub fn into_item_commit_receipt(self) -> ItemCommitReceipt { ... }  // consuming
    pub fn record_checkpoint(self, receipt: CheckpointCommitReceipt)
        -> Result<PageCommit<CheckpointDurable>, PageCommitValidationError> { ... }
}
impl PageCommit<CheckpointDurable> {
    pub fn into_page_commit_receipt(self) -> PageCommitReceipt { ... }
}
```
The typestate machine supports `ItemDurable` → `CheckpointDurable` via
`record_checkpoint()`, which validates `receipt.scope() == self.scope()`.

### `CheckpointCommitReceipt::new()` — `crates/gossip-contracts/src/persistence/commit.rs:247-255`

```rust
    Self { scope, checkpointed_at }
}
```

```rust
pub enum PageCommitValidationError {
    LedgerItemCountMismatch { expected: u64, actual: u64 },
    CheckpointScopeMismatch,
}
```
`CheckpointScopeMismatch` fires when `record_checkpoint()` detects scope
disagreement. The aggregator uses this for retry semantics.

- `FindingsCommitReceipt` (`commit.rs:137-141`): `finding_count`, `occurrence_count`, `observation_count`
- `DoneLedgerCommitReceipt` (`commit.rs:194-198`): `record_count`, `scanned_count`, `findings_count`

```rust
    -> Result<PageCommit<ItemDurable>, PageCommitValidationError> {
    let expected = self.scope.committed_items();
    let actual = receipt.record_count();
    if expected != actual {
        return Err(PageCommitValidationError::LedgerItemCountMismatch { expected, actual });
    }
```

### No `checkpoint_aggregator` module exists

## Desired State

After this task, the codebase has a `checkpoint_aggregator` module in
`gossip-scanner-runtime` implementing the receipt-driven committed-prefix
checkpoint aggregation pattern:

1. **`ReceiptRecordOutcome`** — enum: `Buffered`, `DuplicateBuffered`,
   `AlreadyCheckpointed`. Reports the result of recording one receipt.

2. **`PendingPrefixCheckpoint`** — prepared contiguous prefix ready for
   checkpoint persistence. Carries `first_sequence_no`, `last_sequence_no`,
   and the checkpoint-ready `PageCommit<ItemDurable>` (reconstructed from
   aggregate receipts). Provides accessors for `committed_units()`,
   `checkpoint_boundary()`, `checkpoint_boundary_kind()`,
   `checkpoint_cursor()`, `scope()`, `item_commit_receipt()`,
   `page_commit()`, `into_page_commit()`.

3. **`ReceiptOwner`** — `Copy` struct carrying
   `(tenant_id, run_id, shard_id, fence_epoch)` for receipt ownership
   validation. Constructed from `WriteContext` or `CommitScope`.

4. **`PrefixCheckpointAggregator`** — shard-local, single-family aggregator:
   - `new(write_context, next_sequence_no)` — fresh aggregator.
   - `record_receipt(input)` — accept `CheckpointAggregatorInput`, buffer
     in `BTreeMap<u64, CommitReceipt>` reorder buffer. Validates ownership,
     per-unit receipt, boundary kind consistency. Returns
     `ReceiptRecordOutcome`.
   - `prepare_checkpoint()` — find contiguous prefix from
     `next_sequence_no`, reconstruct aggregate `PageCommit<ItemDurable>`
     from summed receipt counts. Returns `PendingPrefixCheckpoint` or `None`.
     Returns `None` if no receipt exists at `next_sequence_no` (including
     when the buffer is empty). If a pending prefix already exists, returns
     it without widening.
   - `acknowledge_checkpoint(CheckpointCommitReceipt)` — finalize the
     pending prefix after checkpoint write is durable. Validates receipt
     scope matches pending scope. On success: releases consumed receipts,
     advances `next_sequence_no` (via `checked_add`, returns
     `CounterOverflow` on overflow), increments `checkpointed_units`,
     records `last_checkpoint_key`. Returns `PageCommitReceipt`.
   - `observe(input)` — convenience: `record_receipt` + `prepare_checkpoint`.
   - Accessors: `write_context()`, `next_sequence_no()`,
     `checkpointed_units()`, `checkpoint_boundary_kind()`,
     `buffered_receipt_count()`, `pending_checkpoint()`.

5. **`PrefixCheckpointError`** — 13-variant error enum covering:
   ownership mismatch, receipt boundary mismatch, missing progress key,
   per-unit receipt expected, boundary kind mismatch, conflicting receipt,
   boundary regression, count overflow, invalid prepared checkpoint,
   no pending checkpoint, invalid checkpoint receipt, counter overflow.

6. **Internal helpers:**
   - `validate_receipt()` — check ownership, per-unit, boundary match,
     progress key presence.
   - `strip_checkpoint_token()` — drop connector token from checkpoint
     boundary, preserving only `last_key` for durable progress.
   - `checked_add()` — arithmetic with overflow detection.

### Aggregate receipt reconstruction

`build_pending_checkpoint()` iterates the contiguous receipt range and sums
6 distinct count fields across all receipts:

**From `FindingsCommitReceipt`**: `finding_count`, `occurrence_count`,
`observation_count`

**From `DoneLedgerCommitReceipt`**: `record_count`, `scanned_count`,
`findings_count`

The aggregate `DoneLedgerCommitReceipt::record_count()` must equal the
aggregate `committed_items` in the scope — both are set to the total number
of receipts in the prefix. This is validated by `record_done_ledger()` via
`LedgerItemCountMismatch`.

### Aggregate scope construction

The aggregate `CommitScope` (or `PageCommitScope`) is constructed from:
- **Identity fields**: `tenant_id`, `run_id`, `shard_id`, `fence_epoch` — from the aggregator's `WriteContext`
- **`committed_items`**: sum of per-receipt `committed_items()` (each is 1, so equals the number of receipts in the prefix)
- **`checkpoint_cursor`/`checkpoint_boundary`**: token-stripped cursor from the *last* receipt in the contiguous prefix, built via `Cursor::with_last_key(last_key)`

### Token stripping
Checkpoint boundaries carry both `last_key` (progress) and `token`
(connector resume state). Tokens are connector-specific and must not leak
into durable checkpoint state. The aggregator strips tokens before
computing the prepared prefix, preserving only key-based progress.

### Boundary kind freezing
The first receipt accepted by an aggregator instance pins its
`CheckpointBoundaryKind` (`OrderedContent` or `RepoFrontier`). All
subsequent receipts must match. This prevents cross-family receipt mixing
within a single shard.

### Failed checkpoint retry
If `acknowledge_checkpoint()` receives a mismatched
`CheckpointCommitReceipt`, the pending prefix is restored (not discarded)
and the error is returned. The caller can retry with the correct receipt.

## Implementation Guidance

### Files to Modify

| `crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/checkpoint_aggregator.rs` | **New file**: all types listed in Desired State, ~550 lines impl + ~500 lines tests | Core aggregator module |

### Patterns to Follow
- **Reorder buffer**: `BTreeMap<u64, CommitReceipt>` for O(log n) insert
  and contiguous prefix scan via iteration from lowest key.
- **Typestate reuse**: Reconstruct aggregate `PageCommit<ItemDurable>` by
  driving the same `new → record_findings → record_done_ledger` transitions.
- **Two-phase checkpoint**: `prepare_checkpoint()` creates the pending prefix;
  `acknowledge_checkpoint()` finalizes it after the checkpoint write is durable.
- **Retry on mismatch**: `acknowledge_checkpoint()` restores the pending
  prefix on `CheckpointScopeMismatch` so the caller can retry.

### Utilities to Reuse
| Utility | Location | How to Reuse |
|---------|----------|-------------|
| `PageCommit<S>` | `crates/gossip-contracts/src/persistence/page_commit.rs` | Reconstruct aggregate ItemDurable |
| `PageCommit::record_checkpoint()` | `page_commit.rs:462-475` | Finalize checkpoint in `acknowledge_checkpoint` |
| `CheckpointCommitReceipt::new()` | `commit.rs:247-255` | Created by caller, consumed by aggregator |
| `FindingsCommitReceipt::new(finding_count, occurrence_count, observation_count)` | `commit.rs:141-147` | Aggregate receipt construction |
| `DoneLedgerCommitReceipt::new(record_count, scanned_count, findings_count)` | `commit.rs:198-204` | Aggregate receipt construction |
| `CommitScope::from_write_context()` | EP2.2 deliverable | Aggregate scope construction |
| `Cursor::with_last_key()` | `types.rs:710-716` | Token-stripped cursor construction |

### Blast Radius
| Entity | File | Impact |
|--------|------|--------|
| `PageCommit<ItemDurable>` | `page_commit.rs` | Second runtime consumer (after EP2.4) |
| Future bounded commit pipeline | N/A | Will feed receipts into the aggregator |
| Coordination checkpoint | `crates/gossip-coordination/src/traits.rs:370-377` | Future consumer of `PageCommitReceipt` |

## Design Notes

**Why `&mut self`, not `&self`:**
The aggregator maintains mutable state (receipt buffer, pending prefix,
sequence counter). It is shard-local and single-threaded. Using `&mut self`
makes ownership explicit and avoids internal locking.

**Why `BTreeMap`, not `HashMap`:**
The reorder buffer is iterated from the lowest key to find contiguous
prefixes. `BTreeMap` provides sorted iteration.

**Why pending prefix is not widened after preparation:**
If `prepare_checkpoint()` is called again after a prefix is prepared but
before `acknowledge_checkpoint()`, it returns the same prefix. This
prevents the prepared prefix from silently growing while a checkpoint
write is in-flight.

**Why tokens are stripped:**
Connector tokens encode opaque resume state (e.g., pagination cursors). They
must not enter durable checkpoint storage because they may expire or become
invalid across restarts.

**Buffer growth:**
The reorder buffer is bounded in practice by the maximum in-flight units per
shard, which is controlled by the bounded commit pipeline (future task).
If a unit permanently fails and its receipt never arrives, the buffer retains
all later receipts. Cap enforcement and gap eviction are the responsibility
of the orchestrator layer — the aggregator is a pure data structure that does
not implement timeouts. This separation is intentional: the aggregator's
correctness guarantees (contiguous prefix only) must not be weakened by
timeout-based gap skipping.

**Boundary regression detection:**
Within a contiguous prefix, each receipt's `last_key` must be >= the
previous receipt's `last_key`. A regression indicates a programming error.

## Testing Strategy

|------|------------------|
| `prefix_checkpoint_waits_for_contiguous_receipts` | Out-of-order → gap-close → prepare → acknowledge lifecycle |
| `prefix_commit_drops_resume_token_but_preserves_last_key` | Token stripping semantics |
| `duplicate_and_already_checkpointed_receipts_are_idempotent` | Duplicate buffered + post-checkpoint replay |
| `conflicting_duplicate_sequence_is_rejected` | Different receipt for same sequence |
| `mismatched_write_scope_is_rejected` | Ownership validation |
| `checkpoint_scope_mismatch_keeps_pending_for_retry` | Failed ack preserves pending, retry succeeds |
| `cannot_ack_checkpoint_without_pending_prefix` | NoPendingCheckpoint error |
| `boundary_kind_is_frozen_from_first_receipt` | Single-family enforcement |
| `boundary_regression_is_rejected_when_building_prefix` | Key monotonicity within prefix |
| `observe_convenience_method_records_then_prepares` | Combined record+prepare shortcut |

title: EP2.6 — Add a bounded execution → commit pipeline
description:
## Goal

Implement the bounded execution → commit pipeline for the Epic 2 runtime durability model.

## Scope

Runtime pipeline structure and backpressure between scan execution and durable commit.

## Deliverables

1. Bounded channel between execution and commit stages
2. Commit stage owns authoritative completion
3. Scanning blocks or pauses when the queue is full or sinks are slow
4. Lease-loss behavior stops new work quickly rather than letting stale work dribble onward

## Pattern

Bounded producer/consumer pipeline with backpressure using sync_channel.

## Why This Matters

Epic 2 explicitly calls for a bounded commit pipeline and scanning pause under slow sinks. Phase VI already treats 'commit blocked' and commit queue backlog as operational stall signals, so this stage should expose queue/backlog state cleanly.

## Sub-tasks

1. Implement bounded commit pipeline core (types + pipeline + worker)
2. Add commit pipeline backpressure and correctness tests
3. Add lease-loss / cancellation to commit pipeline

## Acceptance Criteria

- No unbounded in-memory buffering
- Slow sinks cause pause, not memory blowup
- Commit stage is the only place that marks work finished
- Workers pause rather than outrunning durability
- Lease-loss stops new work quickly

## Dependencies

- EP2.1 (commit vocabulary types)
- EP2.2 (WriteContext)
- EP2.3 (result translation)
- EP2.4 (ResultCommitter)

title: EP2.6.1 — Implement bounded commit pipeline core (types + pipeline + worker)
description:
## Context

Epic 2 establishes the shared commit protocol and runtime durability model.
EP2.1 froze the commit vocabulary, EP2.2 threaded WriteContext, EP2.3 built
result translation, and EP2.4 implemented the per-item ResultCommitter. The
runtime needs one structural choke point between scan execution and durable
commit so that slow sinks pause scanning instead of letting memory usage drift
upward unboundedly.

This task implements the bounded producer/consumer boundary as a single commit
worker backed by `std::sync::mpsc::sync_channel`. Execution threads enqueue
owned work items; they do not write sinks directly. The commit worker is the
only place where runtime work becomes authoritatively durable.

**Scope boundary:** This task covers types, pipeline, worker, and module wiring
only. Tests are delivered in EP2.6.2. Cargo.toml dev-dependency changes for
test infrastructure (`gossip-persistence-inmemory`, `scanner-scheduler`) belong
to EP2.6.2 as well.

## Current State

### No commit_pipeline module exists

Module declarations in `crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/lib.rs:69-76`:
```rust
pub mod cli;
pub mod commit_sink;
pub mod coordination_sink;
pub mod distributed;
pub mod event_sink;
pub mod git_repo;
pub mod ordered_content;
pub mod parity;
```

There is no `commit_pipeline.rs` or bounded execution-to-commit queue in the
runtime crate. The `commit_model`, `result_translation`, and `result_committer`
modules will be delivered by EP2.1-EP2.4 before this task starts.

### ResultCommitter (EP2.4 deliverable) — `crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/result_committer.rs`
```rust
pub struct ResultCommitter<F, D> {
    findings_sink: F,
    done_ledger: D,
}

impl<F, D> ResultCommitter<F, D>
where
    F: FindingsSink,
    D: DoneLedger,
{
    pub fn new(findings_sink: F, done_ledger: D) -> Self { ... }

    pub fn commit_translation(
        &self,
        write_context: WriteContext,
        completed_unit: CompletedUnit,
        translation: &PersistenceTranslation,
    ) -> Result<CommitReceipt, ResultCommitError<F::Error, D::Error>> { ... }
}
```

### CompletedUnit (EP2.1 deliverable) — `crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/commit_model.rs`
```rust
pub struct CompletedUnit {
    sequence_no: u64,
    checkpoint_boundary: CheckpointBoundary,
}
```
Accessors: `sequence_no()`, `checkpoint_boundary()`, `checkpoint_cursor()`.
Convenience constructors: `ordered_content(seq, cursor)`, `repo_frontier(seq, cursor)`.

### CheckpointAggregatorInput (EP2.1 deliverable) — `crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/commit_model.rs`
```rust
pub struct CheckpointAggregatorInput {
    receipt: CommitReceipt,
}

impl CheckpointAggregatorInput {
    pub fn from_receipt(receipt: CommitReceipt) -> Self { ... }
    pub fn receipt(&self) -> &CommitReceipt { ... }
    pub fn into_receipt(self) -> CommitReceipt { ... }
}
```

### CommitReceipt (EP2.1 deliverable, runtime-level) — `crates/gossip-scanner-runtime/src/commit_model.rs`

```rust
pub struct CommitReceipt {
    completed_unit: CompletedUnit,
    durable: ItemCommitReceipt,

```
Accessors: `completed_unit()`, `durable()`, `into_parts()`.

```rust
pub struct WriteContext {
```

```rust
    type Error: Error + Send + Sync + 'static;
    type CommitHandle: CommitHandle<Receipt = FindingsCommitReceipt, Error = Self::Error>;
    fn upsert_batch(&self, batch: FindingsUpsertBatch<'_>) -> Result<Self::CommitHandle, Self::Error>;
```
